author: karanshukla
body:
Adds GIF (and sticker) insertion straight from Gboard's keyboard pickers, with alt text on both paths.

## Why the composer couldn't do this

Gboard only shows its GIF/sticker tabs when the focused editor advertises image MIME types in `EditorInfo.contentMimeTypes`. Compose's opt-in for that is `Modifier.contentReceiver`, but its own docs are explicit: *"only the `TextFieldState` override of the text field supports being a content receiver"* — the legacy `BasicTextField(value: TextFieldValue, …)` path never sets `contentMimeTypes` at all. The composer needs `TextFieldValue` to render its styled links (BTF2 has no styled-text equivalent short of an `OutputTransformation` rewrite), so migrating it was out of scope.

Instead the platform text input session is intercepted. `InterceptPlatformTextInput` sits above the text field, amends the `EditorInfo` the field publishes, and wraps the returned `InputConnection` to catch `commitContent`. The legacy adapter routes through `establishTextInputSession` → `startInputMethod`, so this works with the composer's existing `BasicTextField` untouched.

## How a committed image gets posted

The keyboard's content URI is only readable while the grant it hands over is held (it dies with the input connection), so the bytes are copied into the app's cache eagerly rather than at post time.

What happens next depends on whether the keyboard supplied a public `linkUri`:

- **With a URL** (Gboard passes the Tenor link for GIFs) → an `app.bsky.embed.external` card pointing straight at the animated file, which is how the Bluesky app posts GIFs. This matters: image blobs are re-encoded to a still frame by the CDN, so an uploaded GIF would not animate. The thumb blob is fetched from that URL by the existing post pipeline, so no data-layer changes were needed. Heron's timeline already renders `.gif`-suffixed external embeds animated.
- **Without one** — stickers, and keyboards that pass no link — the image is attached and uploaded like any other picked photo, subject to the same 10-photo limit.

## Alt text

Seeded from the keyboard's own description of the image (Gboard sends the GIF's description in the `ClipDescription` label) and editable either way:

- attached images keep using the existing ALT sheet;
- GIFs get an ALT chip on the embed preview opening a new sheet, which writes the `Alt: ` / `ALT: ` prefixed description that the Bluesky app writes and parses back.

## Changes

| Area | What |
|---|---|
| `ui/media` | New `KeyboardMedia` + `expect KeyboardMediaReceiver`; Android actual does the interception, iOS/desktop are a no-op |
| `feature/compose` | `EditMedia.AddKeyboardMedia` / `EditMedia.UpdateGifAltText`, the GIF-vs-attachment decision, the ALT chip and GIF alt sheet; the alt sheet body was extracted so both sheets share it |
| `data/models` | `ExternalEmbed.isGif` / `gifAltText` / `gifDescription` — the `.gif` URL check moved out of `PostExternal` so timeline and composer share one definition |
| `data/files` | `RestrictedFile.photo` takes an optional `altText` |

## Testing

**This was never built, and no CI will build it.** Actions are disabled on this fork — zero workflow runs repo-wide — so `check-style` never fires on the PR. And the authoring session's egress policy blocks Google's Maven (`dl.google.com` → 403 through the proxy), so no Gradle task could run there either. **Please run `./gradlew spotlessCheck :androidApp:assembleDebug` locally before trusting this.**

What *was* verified, from artifacts reachable on Maven Central:

- **Syntax**: the full diff parses clean under a standalone `kotlinc` 2.4.10 (the pinned version). Every remaining diagnostic is an unresolved reference or a cascade from one — no parse errors.
- **`InterceptPlatformTextInput` / `PlatformTextInputInterceptor`**: confirmed present with the expected shape in `org.jetbrains.compose.ui:ui-desktop:1.12.0-rc01`, the pinned CMP build. The interceptor is a genuine SAM interface, so the lambda conversion is valid.
- **FileKit**: `cacheDir`, `div`, `write(ByteArray)`, `createDirectories(mustCreate)`, `exists()` all check out against `filekit-core:0.15.0`.

Not verified, because androidx is published only to Google's Maven: full type resolution across the diff, and the Android actual of `PlatformTextInputMethodRequest.createInputConnection(EditorInfo)` (read from the androidx sources; stable since Compose 1.7, but not machine-checked here).

Two things only a device can settle:

1. Whether Gboard actually populates `linkUri` for Tenor GIFs. The implementation handles both cases, but if it turns out to be null in practice, GIFs fall back to the static-image path and the animated path is dead code worth revisiting.
2. Whether the intercepted `EditorInfo` surfaces the GIF tab across Gboard versions.

author: joaomarcos44
body: Fixes #92004 ## Summary - Every existing cost/usage view (web insights dashboard, session search, ad-hoc `state.db` inspection) reads exactly one `sessions` row per conversation. Delegate subagent usage lives in separate rows linked only by `parent_session_id`, and nothing walks that tree to sum it — see #92004 for the full architectural writeup and code references. - Adds `SessionDB.get_delegation_tree_usage(session_id)`: resolves the conversation root via the existing `get_conversation_root` (which already walks up through both compression rotation and delegate/branch edges), then walks back down `parent_session_id` to sum tokens/cost across every session in the tree. - Purely additive — no existing call site changed. ## Measured impact (from #92004) A 10-subagent delegation fan-out, read from only the root session: | metric | root only | root + 10 children (real) | |---|---|---| | input_tokens | 3,660,292 | 8,619,077 (2.35x) | | cache_read_tokens | 86,864,384 | 185,599,488 (2.14x) | ## Architecture ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'dark', 'themeVariables': { 'primaryColor': '#00f0ff', 'mainBkg': '#0a0a16', 'primaryTextColor': '#ffffff', 'primaryBorderColor': '#ff007f', 'lineColor': '#00f0ff'}}}%% graph TD A[🔒 Root Session Row] -->|parent_session_id| B[⚡ Delegate Child 1] A -->|parent_session_id| C[⚡ Delegate Child 2] A -->|parent_session_id| D[⚡ Delegate Child N] B -->|parent_session_id| E[⚡ Nested Subagent] subgraph Before["🩸 Before: every view stops here"] F[Web Insights Dashboard] -.->|reads A only| A G[Session Search] -.->|stops at delegate edge| A end subgraph After["🚀 After: get_delegation_tree_usage"] H[get_conversation_root] -->|resolves| A H --> I[walk parent_session_id DOWN] I --> A I --> B I --> C I --> D I --> E I --> J[⚔️ Summed totals: input/output/cache/cost] end ``` ## Test plan - [x] `pytest tests/hermes_state/test_delegation_tree_usage.py` — 6 new tests: standalone session, parent+3 delegate children, root resolution from a child, nested subagent-of-subagent, cost/cache column summation, cyclic-parent-link defensive guard - [x] `pytest tests/hermes_state/test_conversation_root.py` — no regression on the existing root-walk this builds on - [x] `python -c "import hermes_state"` — clean import, no syntax/type errors ## Why this solution : Why reuse get_conversation_root instead of writing root resolution from scratch: it already handles compaction, branching, and delegates during the upward walk, already has regression tests (test_conversation_root.py), and is already called by other production consumers. Duplicating that logic in the new function would create two sources of truth that could silently diverge if one were fixed and the other weren't. Reusing it means any future fix in get_conversation_root (e.g., a new lineage type) benefits get_delegation_tree_usage for free. Why BFS in Python instead of a WITH RECURSIVE CTE in SQL: the file already has both styles coexisting (get_compression_lineage uses a Python loop plus one query per iteration; record_gateway_session_peer uses a recursive CTE). I chose a Python loop because: (1) the delegation tree per conversation is small — dozens of sessions, not thousands, so the cost of N small queries is irrelevant; (2) BFS in Python is trivial to test with plain pytest (the 6 tests don't need elaborate SQL fixtures); (3) cycle protection (seen) is more readable as if sid in seen: continue than as a cutoff clause in a recursive SQLite CTE, which historically already caused an infinite-loop bug elsewhere in the file (mentioned in the get_conversation_root comment; the chain is limited to 100 hops for the same reason). Why with self._lock: around the entire while loop, rather than locking per query: the rest of SessionDB uses this pattern — one critical section per logical operation, not per individual SQL statement — to prevent another thread from inserting a new child (create_session) in the middle of the traversal and producing an inconsistent sum (half pre-insert, half post-insert). More granular locking would be more "efficient" in theory, but it would break the consistency guarantee that the rest of the file assumes. Why return session_ids in addition to the summed totals: for auditing. If a number looks wrong in the future, you can inspect exactly which sessions were included in the sum without reconstructing the query manually — that's how the original investigation in #92004 validated the 2.35x factor, comparing row by row. Why no call sites were touched: the function is purely additive. Deliberate decision to keep the PR small and reviewable — wiring it into /cost/dashboard requires deciding where and how to show the aggregated total (which can be confusing if mixed without context with the individual session total), which is a product decision, not just a bug fix. I preferred to leave that decision to whoever maintains the user-facing surface, with the utility already ready and tested. ## Infographic :

## Scope
- Add a repeatable full-data audit for the 20-topic technology taxonomy.
- Audit topic-parent track integrity, topic/event assignments, event-cluster aggregation, source counts, and strongest-evidence primary source selection.

- No HeatScore changes.
- No crawler collection or ranking changes.
- No Google Alerts subscription changes.
- No config/user_tracking.json changes.

The first audit found 232 cross-track topic assignments. After removing tracking-seed leakage and acronym substring false positives, the comparable count fell to 49 before parent-track calibration; event-cluster/source integrity checks were already clean.

| USB-C: TP1 → D−, TP2 → D+ | **TP1 = GND, TP2 = D−, TP3 = D+** (Pico datasheet). The old wiring shorts GND onto D−. `usb_c_wiring.png` demoted to illustration. |
| `PS2_DRIVER = usart` on RP2040 | `vendor` (PIO); `usart` is ATmega32u4-only and does not build |
| CLK = GP21, DATA = GP22 | **DATA = GP21, CLK = GP22** — the PIO driver requires clock = data + 1 |
| "GP21/GP22 = UART0" | removed; not a UART pair on RP2040 |
| `BACKLIGHT_DRIVER = timer` | `software` — the workaround QMK #24470 actually records |
| 8×13 matrix, "all 26 GPIO used" | closest documented ThinkPad keyboard is 17×9 = 26 lines; design adds **3 × 74HC165** sense chain (24 lines on 3 GPIO), 8 GPIO spare |
| No TrackPoint | first-class feature via the ClickPad's Synaptics pass-through; GP19/GP20 reserved for a standalone line |
| "$25–35 total" | **$90–150** all-in; donor parts were omitted |
| Adafruit #1436 = ZIF breakout | it is a solder-pad plate; BOM lists real ZIF breakouts |

author: ctrlspice
body:
Follows #382, which taught the server to read named params. This is the client learning to send them.

## What

- All 14 methods that have parameters now send them by name; the 3 with none send nothing, and the 2 variadic deletes stay arrays because their params *are* the id list
- `named` drops keys the caller never supplied — that is the whole mechanism
- `ns()` deleted, and timestamps decode through `UseNumber()`
- Carries #381's root-span label, which conflicted with main only in built assets

## Why

- Positional params have no notion of a hole, so sending the fifth argument meant sending the first four. `getMetric` carried a placeholder list, a trailing-trim loop and a `null` in slot 11; `getMetricAggregate` carried three placeholder comments and a `'0'` — all so `tzName` could be reached past slots that do not care
- The four search methods each carried a ternary that existed only to leave the query slot out. Named, an absent query is an absent key, so there is nothing left to decide
- Nanosecond timestamps exceed float64's exact range; `UseNumber` parses them as int64, which is what lets `ns()` go

## Two bugs this surfaced

Both found by doing the conversion, neither by a test:

- `deleteMetricStream` was registered as `streamIDs` but takes a bare id
- `params: {}` was refused for every method with nothing to name

## Tests now pin the request

The suite asserted only responses, so it passed on named, positional or nonsense — which is how both bugs above reached a running server. Each method is now deep-equalled against the exact object it sends.

Mutation-checked: reverting `searchTraces` to an array fails 2, renaming `streamID` fails 1, `clearTraces` sending `{}` fails 1, wrapping `deleteLogByID` fails 1. One survives correctly — deleting `named`'s undefined filter changes no wire bytes, since `JSON.stringify` omits undefined keys anyway.

## Verified against a running store

- Named and positional return byte-identical responses for all 14 methods, including a fourteen-parameter `getMetric` over real histogram data
- Driven live in the browser: the wire carries `searchTraces {startTime,endTime}`, `searchSpans {traceID}` and six more, with the absent `query` key visible

author: tutunannan
body:
## Summary

Issue #611 — ACP native round prose + thinking honest degrade. The ACP engine now groups `agent_message_chunk` prose per round (round boundary = the tool-call batch split) into per-round `LoopRound.text` slots, emitting `RoundText` live before each batch's call events; `agent_thought_chunk` streams fold into a per-round `ThinkingTrace { duration_ms, text }` whose `ThinkingCompleted` fires at the round boundary, and an agent that emits no thoughts renders no fold and raises no error. The schema verification the issue asked for ran against `agent-client-protocol-schema` 0.13.8 v1 (local cargo cache, its own serialization fixtures): the thought variant exists, the discriminator is `sessionUpdate` (not `type`), and a ContentChunk carries ONE content block (not an array) — the previous hand-modeled shape never parsed a real agent's `session/update` line, which was silently dropped; the wire is recalibrated and the schema fixture JSON is embedded byte-for-byte in the wire tests. The terminal text settles to the trailing prose stretch after the last batch, falling back to the full accumulation when the agent sent no trailing stretch (fallback semantics unchanged), and a prose-only trailing round drops from the trace so zero-call turns stay round-free.

## Changes

- **Wire schema calibration** (`wire.rs`): `SessionUpdate` discriminates on `sessionUpdate`; `AgentMessageChunk.content` narrows from a `Vec<ContentBlock>` to ONE block (the `ContentChunk` shape); new `AgentThoughtChunk` variant (optional `messageId` + one block) leaves the `serde(other)` fallback for everything else.
- **Round accumulator** (`engine.rs`): `Pump` trades the flat trace for `Vec<RoundAcc>` — frozen thinking block, live thought buffer + start instant, prose buffer, `saw_call` seal, landed calls; a thought/prose chunk arriving after a called round opens the next round and fires `Thinking { attempt }` so the live round pointer tracks batches past round 1.
- **Batch prelude** (`engine.rs`): the round's first tool call fires the frozen `ThinkingCompleted` then `RoundText` BEFORE its `ToolCallStarted` (the ADR-0103 live order the frontend's round grouping relies on).
- **Terminal + settle** (`engine.rs`): terminal text = the trailing call-less round's prose, falling back to the full accumulation when no trailing stretch exists; settle drops a prose-only trailing round and keeps it only when it holds a frozen thinking block.
- **Pending rows** (`engine.rs`): `PendingToolCall` carries the round it opened in; late completions and the turn-end drain land on that round, not whichever round is current.
- **Comment calibration** (`agent_loop.rs`): `LoopRound::flat` doc redirects — the ACP-native engine groups its own rounds; the claude/codex stream formats remain the flat paths.
- **Fixture** (`acp_fake_cli.rs`): `agent_thought` builder, `raw_session_update` (hand-built `sessionUpdate` lines independent of our own types), and three scenarios — `round_prose_thinking`, `real_wire_chunks`, `midturn_prose_no_terminal`.
- **Tests** (`acp_engine.rs`): four new tests — round grouping + slot contents + the full phase-order chain, honest degrade (no thoughts → no fold, terminal prose is not round prose), schema-shape parse end-to-end, fallback text without a trailing stretch.

## Files Changed

- `src-tauri/src/runtime/acp/engine.rs` -- modified (round accumulator, batch prelude, terminal/settle rules; flat trace retired)
- `src-tauri/src/runtime/acp/wire.rs` -- modified (sessionUpdate discriminator, one-block ContentChunk, AgentThoughtChunk variant, schema-shape test pins)
- `src-tauri/src/session/agent_loop.rs` -- modified (LoopRound::flat doc calibration)
- `src-tauri/tests/acp_engine.rs` -- modified (+4 tests)
- `src-tauri/tests/fixtures/acp_fake_cli.rs` -- modified (+agent_thought, +raw_session_update, +3 scenarios)

## Testing

- **Rust** (`cargo test`): lib suite green (1111 tests, including the new wire tests round-tripping the schema crate 0.13.8 fixture JSON byte-for-byte) plus the `acp_engine` (27 passed, 4 new), `acp_session_wiring`, `acp_probe`, `mcp_gateway_integration`, and `ipc_contract` integration targets. `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests` and `cargo fmt` clean.

## Related Issues

Closes #611.

Follow-up (out of scope):
- Real-CLI E2E stays manual (#342); the wire fix means gemini-cli / opencode / qwen drives are the first real consumers of the recalibrated parse path.
- claude-code direct and codex direct round grouping remain flat paths (their own slices); the built-in runtime's thinking data source is the posture follow-up.

author: nullpriority
body:
# Summary

Fail closed on family-level candidate-bundle upper bounds until a bounded affected-cohort probe establishes one executable grammar and lower bound. Restore lowerability as the admission gate for exact-ability and material-residual OR thresholds, preserve upper-bound hypotheses as visible classification pressure, and allow the generated selector to return no eligible foreground.

## Change class and authority

- Change class: deterministic selector correctness and architecture governance
- Governing rules or capabilities: no Magic gameplay changes; work-selection authority remains the generated rules scheduler and existing frontier/reusable reports.
- Oracle/rulings snapshot: unchanged pinned snapshot; rules SHA-256 `68dab840bfb200a4fca4a061793269c40d57f83364cb1091ea9094b5b8f04769`, Oracle SHA-256 `9d44ab29ff15a239d48f190ec59adb8046049d9a18e8010b793a96361749295d`, rulings SHA-256 `8e4f6b41785ce7ca1fd881372598e48410e2643e95aa893668a784827deeb3ea`.
- Supported profile affected: Commander review work selection only.

## Ownership and implementation

- Owner before: synthesized family bundles were treated as executable coherent measurements even when their static exclusions removed large parts of the measured closure.
- Owner after: candidate bundles carry a closed measurement status. `upper_bound_only` hypotheses remain visible but ineligible; missing-lowering atomic ability/residual volume also remains ineligible until already lowerable or represented by a bounded cohort.
- Duplicate or superseded paths removed: no duplicate selector or registry; the misleading selected token foreground is removed from the existing queue.
- `CommanderEngine` delta: 0.
- Direct authoritative-write delta: 0.
- Prohibited identity-dispatch delta: 0.
- Oracle-ID literal delta: 0.
- Compiler/CardProgram changes: none; compiler remains `oracle-ir-v110` and CardProgram remains V2.
- Card, residual, and capability-closure deltas: no support counts change. The token and exile bundle upper bounds remain reported, but eligible candidate count becomes zero because neither has an executable lower-bound cohort.

## Evidence

| Class | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused regression and affected module | PASS — seven exact scheduler tests cover upper-bound bundle blocking, already-lowerable residual OR admission, structural zero-card blocking, broad complete-card ranking, fail-closed policy mutation, no false foreground, and generated freshness. |
| Multiplayer/APNAP and interactions | N/A — gameplay and interaction execution are unchanged; the existing zero-uncovered baseline remains a higher-priority selector input. |
| Replay, byte/hash, and compatibility | N/A — no Game Record, replay, database, or protocol schema changes. |
| Privacy and capability isolation | N/A — no runtime or projection changes. |
| Transaction rollback and malformed input | PASS — unknown or missing measurement status, malformed bundle policy, and stale queue inputs fail closed before selection. |
| Headless browser and protocol | N/A — no browser or wire behavior changes. |
| Property and fuzz | N/A — deterministic closed policy tables have no randomized input surface. |
| Focused mutation | PASS — policy mutation tests reject duplicated contexts and invalid bundle shapes; upper-bound hypotheses cannot become eligible by crossing raw count thresholds. |
| Compiler/corpus and residuals | PASS — bounded probe joined frontier residual IDs back to exact compiler spans for 881 affected cards. It found 904 token residuals across 872 distinct texts; the 22 modal/table leaves accepted after structural stripping close zero complete cards because sibling modes remain residual. No corpus rewrite is required. |
| Architecture, ownership, and identity flow | PASS — default bundle construction is extracted to the existing rules-governance bundle module; architecture reports no new oversized module, write, runtime prose, identity dispatch, or engine growth. |
| Local quick gate | N/A — only the dry-run impact inventory and exact focused selector/architecture/documentation checks ran locally; broad generated/core regression remains CI work. |
| Required exact-head CI | PASS — [exact-head generated run 32546714213](https://github.com/NullPriority/quorune/actions/runs/32546714213) and [exact-head PR regression run 32546714212](https://github.com/NullPriority/quorune/actions/runs/32546714212) passed for `bf759e09`. |

## Generated artifacts

- Source inputs changed: yes — selector policy/schema, bundle measurement logic, tests, and documentation.
- Generators run: `scripts/finalize_generated.py --write` was offloaded to [source-head run 32545904011](https://github.com/NullPriority/quorune/actions/runs/32545904011); [final-head run 32546714213](https://github.com/NullPriority/quorune/actions/runs/32546714213) reused the compiler corpus, frontier, and content-identical owners before exact-source assembly.
- Outputs changed: rules queue, dependency-queue Markdown, architecture audit, compact dependencies, and generated architecture/compiler status documents were installed from the exact-source bundle and committed together.
- Freshness checks: exact-source receipt, `scripts/validate_repository.py`, scheduler freshness, architecture, documentation, protocol, replay-fixture, history, secret scan, Python compilation, and diff hygiene passed. Generated-output fingerprint: `2b229b0f3ea61e8b5004e69212d11c0bc8d9d52602f4b8a90702e9a33daa13e5`.

## Documentation and decisions

- Current documents changed: CI pipeline reference now distinguishes candidate-bundle hypotheses from bounded executable cohorts.
- ADR added or superseded: ADR 0081 supersedes only ADR 0080's family-level bundle eligibility assumption; immutable history receipts and auditable bundle metadata remain.
- Changelog effect: N/A — this is internal deterministic selector correctness.

## Limitations and rollback

- Exact remaining limitations: the repository does not yet emit generated bounded-cohort filter identities. The selector therefore returns no eligible candidate until another family is classified or a bounded cohort is added. Upper bounds remain useful classification pressure but are not implementation promises.
- Rollback plan: revert this PR and regenerate the rules-scheduler owner; no gameplay or persisted data migration is involved.
- Compatibility or migration risk: generated work-selection schema remains version 3; candidate bundle measurement status is a required closed nested field. Gameplay and protocol consumers are unaffected.

## Safety checklist

- [x] The change is one coherent subsystem-sized unit; unrelated cleanup is excluded.
- [x] Advertised actions and accepted commands use the same authoritative legality path, or this is N/A with a reason above.
- [x] No card-name, collector-number, set-code, or Oracle-ID behavior was added to the generic runtime.
- [x] No direct `GameState` write was added outside a declared owner.
- [x] Deterministic replay, protocol/schema versions, privacy projection, and rollback are preserved or explicitly versioned and certified.
- [x] Generated outputs were regenerated only by their owners and contain no hand-edited metrics.
- [x] No credential, capability, private hand, library order, checkpoint, live record, bulk archive, database, cache, or artwork was added.
- [x] Third-party content remains within `docs/LEGAL_CONTENT_BOUNDARY.md`.
- [x] Required checks were not weakened, bypassed, renamed, or made optional.
- [x] Every N/A above includes a concrete reason.

body:
## Summary

First slice of Phase 1 (local-first file conversion platform). Sets up the
monorepo and the full spec-driven backlog that will drive the remaining 5
PRs, plus the actual foundation code.

## What happened (backlog)

1. **Tooling**: gentle-ai SDD workflow installed and configured for this
   workspace (`sdd`, `skills`, `permissions`, `context7` components only —
   skipped theme/persona/logo components, not relevant here).
2. **Proposal** (`openspec/changes/phase-1-conversion/proposal.md`):
   local-first architecture — one conversion engine on WASM/pure-JS,
   identical code in browser and Node, no server-side file processing.
   Scope: image, PDF/document, audio, video, CLI, web app.
3. **Specs** (`.../specs/`): 5 capabilities (`core-image`, `core-document`,
   `core-media`, `cli`, `web-app`), RFC-2119 requirements with
   Given/When/Then scenarios covering happy paths, edge cases, and error
   states.
4. **Design** (`.../design.md`): resolves the office-document research
   spike — `mammoth` + `SheetJS` instead of a LibreOffice-WASM blob —
   plus single-threaded `ffmpeg.wasm` and a lazy-loading `formatRegistry`
   so the web bundle only downloads the codec it actually needs.
5. **Tasks** (`.../tasks.md`): 6 stacked-to-main PRs ordered by risk

author: figtracer
body: solsymdiff found a replay-confirmed mismatch where contracts using layout at still generated storage accesses and .slot values from slot zero. The persistent storage cursor now starts at the already-validated layout expression, while transient and struct-relative layouts remain zero-based. author: crumbtrail-dev
body:
SDK and installer half of the round-three persona hunt. The hosted half is [crumbtrail#307](https://github.com/CrumbtrailDev/crumbtrail/pull/307).

Every finding here ends the same way: capture that does not happen, or evidence the reader cannot reach, with nothing saying so.

## The two silent ones

**Global Privacy Control.** `respectGpc` defaults on, Brave and DuckDuckGo send GPC by default, and `canTransport()` gates on it — so nothing is ever handed to the transport, and the transport is the only thing in the SDK that warns. A correct install with a green wizard captured permanently nothing, silently, and no surface in either product named consent or GPC as a possible cause. It now warns once and names the opt-out. This had no test coverage at all; it has three now.

**The Express preload.** `chooseEnvFile` prefers an existing `.env.local` for any variable including the non-bundled `CRUMBTRAIL_KEY`, while the injected `process.loadEnvFile()` reads `.env` only. Any Express repo that already had a `.env.local` got a green "wrote CRUMBTRAIL_KEY", a green "Setup complete", and a backend posting with no auth header. The snippet now tries both candidates in the installer's own order.

## The rest

| Was | Now |
| --- | --- |
| README MCP config had no `env`, so the server read the local disk and said "no sessions" while the dashboard showed them | Hosted config first; local config passes credentials; an empty result names which store it read |
| "Now start your dev server" printed in the terminal the wizard was blocking, then spun 300s | Says which terminal, and that this one is watching |
| CRA / webpack / Vue CLI / Electron ended on the supported list and exit 1 | Gives the two-step manual route, since no recipe is not no capture |
| "Pass --yes and --project" fired when `--project` had just been passed | Names only what is missing |
| Key report led with an internal id visible in no reader-facing surface | Matchable tail leads; id labelled as internal |
| Node floor is 22.15, nothing said so, dev note claimed 20+ | Both state 22.15 |

## Verification

- `pnpm vitest run` across the workspace — **4250 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped**
- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `crumbtrail` and `crumbtrail-node`
- The generated preload snippet run against real `.env.local` / `.env` / neither / real-env-wins cases — the first was the broken one and now resolves
- The built CLI run against a Create React App fixture, confirming both the manual route and all three missing-flag messages

Two pre-existing assertions pinned old wording (the MCP empty result, the `signUp` shape in the sibling PR) and were updated; the MCP one gained assertions for the store it names.

## Docs and published packages

- **Docs** — `README.md` updated here (MCP config, Node floor, dev note). No `PRODUCT.md` change: these are defects in shipped capability, nothing gained or changed gating.
- **Published packages** — these are the published packages. Changes are source-level in `crumbtrail-core`, `crumbtrail-node` and the CLI; **no version bump in this PR**, so a release dispatch is needed before any of it reaches npm.

author: cao825
body:
## What this files

`W1-T1117` — a merge race whose own GitHub message says *"Review and try the merge again"* is classified `permanent`, and because a failed arm still disposes `acted: true`, the head-keyed dedup then strands it on a head the moving base never changes.

**W1-T1079 is not being reversed.** Before it, 172 `arm-error-ignored` rows carried no cause and every failure was retried forever. Recording the reason is what made these modes visible. The default must stay refusal.

## The defect is narrower than "binary"

`armFailureAction` is already three-valued — `direct-merge` / `transient` / `permanent`. Read at `origin/main`, its `transient` arm is an allowlist, and **every member is a transport or server fault**: `timed out`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `ECONNRESET`, `ECONNREFUSED`, `EAI_AGAIN`, `network`, `secondary rate limit`, `rate.limit`, `abuse detection`, `too many requests`, `5xx`, `GraphQL: Something went wrong`/`Server Error`.

Not one entry is semantic. A merge race is semantic, so it cannot match, and `return "permanent"` catches it.

## The finding that inverts the obvious reading

The brief asks whether the sha-keyed dedup already bounds a retry. **It does not bound it — it strands it.**

`arm-error-ignored` is documented in `sweep.ts` as *"the attempt was made and did not stick"*, so it disposes `acted: true`, and `priorActionsFromLedger`'s `mergeable` arm adds `${pr}@${head_sha}` to `armed`. **The race moves the base, not the head.** The key never changes, nothing re-earns the attempt, and "a race clears on the next pass by itself" is false for precisely the failure mode that most deserves a next pass.

This is the W1-T1110 deadlock shape one lane over: an attempt recorded as terminal against a key the triggering condition cannot move. Classifying the race correctly changes nothing while the row still disposes `acted: true` — which is why the shard scopes both halves.

## Q1 — the population, named rather than counted

| message | today | should be |
|---|---|---|
| `clean status` | `direct-merge` | correct |
| transport / `5xx` set | `transient` | correct |
| `not on any branch` | — | **fixed upstream** by W1-T1111, no longer occurs |
| `Base branch was modified` | `permanent` | retryable |
| `Pull Request is not mergeable` | `permanent` | **undecidable from the string** |

## Q1's rate is not measurable from this host, and the zero is structural

`arm_error_ignored` reads **zero** across the deduped union, with a per-form control proving all three forms were read (`automerge.armed`: 520 gz, 225 plain). But the classifier shipped **2026-08-21** (`5db454b5`, #2392) and this corpus's newest `automerge.armed` row is **2026-08-14** — it predates the step by a week. The zero is guaranteed by construction and says nothing about frequency. An implementer must re-derive the message set on the fleet host.

## Q2 — no counter, and the ceiling question dissolves

The retry is bounded by the **condition**, not a clock or a tally: one attempt per sweep pass, only while the race recurs, stopping when the base stops moving. What W1-T1079 cured was retrying a *permanent* failure forever. A ceiling derived from a frequency this host cannot measure would be a guessed constant — the bound-that-fires-on-a-healthy-condition defect.

The mechanism is the `acted: false` shape every other stand-down in that switch already uses.

## Q3 — no stable code exists on this path

`armAuto` runs `execFileSync("gh", ["pr", "merge", …])` with `stdio: "pipe"`, so **stderr prose is the only signal**. GitHub's GraphQL API does return `errors[].type`, but `gh pr merge` collapses it, and nothing in `src/` calls `gh api graphql` at all.

So the classifier must stay prose-keyed, and the honest response is to make that fragility **visible**: an unrecognised message reads `unknown` and takes the same non-retrying path `permanent` takes today. Behaviour unchanged, but a GitHub wording change surfaces as a rising `unknown` count rather than a silent misclassification. Replacing `gh pr merge` with a hand-rolled mutation to obtain a code is refused by name — far larger blast radius than the defect.

## Carried separately, unscoped

The daemon restarted **16 times on freshness** in one night, every summary reading `attempted: (none)` and `idle ticks: 1` — a fast merge cadence advancing main before a tick completes, so the daemon spends its time re-booting rather than dispatching. Different concern, different owner, named here only so it is not lost and can be minted.

## Acceptance
- a base-branch race is classified retryable rather than permanent | unit test: test/arm-failure-classification.test.ts
- a transport failure keeps its existing transient classification | unit test: test/arm-failure-classification.test.ts
- an unrecognised failure reads unknown and still does not retry | unit test: test/arm-failure-classification.test.ts
- a retryable arm failure leaves the head free for the next pass to re-attempt | unit test: test/arm-failure-classification.test.ts
- the clean-status completion still routes to a direct merge | unit test: test/arm-failure-classification.test.ts

author: hherb
body:
Closes #115. Closes #116. Closes #117.

Three measured JATS defects, all in how an exhibit's own content is routed to it, plus two more found while pinning them. Same family as #110/#111 and found the same way — on the way *out* of bmlib, porting fixes to the Swift `BioMedLit` parser this module descends from (hherb/bmlibrarian_lite#166, whose `doc/cross_platform/jats_parsing.md` carries the normative state machine). All of them produce a well-formed result that reads as correct, so none raised anything.

## The three filed defects

**#115 — a nested `<fig>` dropped its parent.** eLife wraps every figure supplement inside the figure it belongs to. `current_figure` was a single slot: the inner open overwrote the parent's builder, the inner close emitted the child and cleared the slot, and the parent's own `</fig>` found nothing to build. **19.6% of 225 surveyed articles nest a `<fig>`; PMC8754430 carries 12 and the parser returned 9** — exactly the three with supplements. `in_figure` was cleared by the inner close too, so the parent's remaining internals were read under the enclosing `<sec>`'s rules and reprinted as article prose.

Two halves, and **a test that only counts figures catches neither**:
- the open exhibits are a **stack**, with `in_figure`/`current_figure` *derived* from it rather than stored — a stored flag is what leaked the parent into prose, and it returns the moment someone adds an early return;
- the list entry is **reserved when the element opens and filled when it closes**, because an exhibit is built at its end tag but has to be *listed* at its start. Pop-and-append restores the parent and still lists every supplement ahead of it.

**#116 — a `<table-wrap-foot><fn><label>` overwrote the table's number.** A footnote carries its marker (`a`, `b`, `*`) as its own `<label>`, and every `<label>` was routed on the ambient flags, so the last marker won — PMC12661592's single table reported its label as `a`. **27 of 225 articles (12.0%)** carry one; `<fig>` has the identical hole. An empty label is not inert: the renderer substitutes `Table {i + 1}`, so the symptom is an *invented number*, not a blank.

The footnote depth is compared against the depth **that exhibit** opened at and **never against zero** — JATS lets a `<fig>` or `<table-wrap>` open *inside* a footnote, and the obvious "am I in a footnote?" test eats that exhibit's own label, which is #116 one level down.

**#117 — a figure with several `<graphic>` resolved to the thumbnail.** **58.0% of 959 surveyed figures** carry more than one and **52.9% end on a thumbnail**. Position cannot decide it: a thumbnail is deposited *last* (PLOS, Springer) while an `<alternatives>` archival master is deposited *first*, so first-wins merely trades the thumbnail for a TIFF no renderer displays. The deposits are **ranked** — `ARCHIVAL < THUMBNAIL < FULL` — and accepted only when **strictly** better, which is what makes the first win among equals. `thumb` is a lowercased substring of `content-type` **or** `specific-use`; **nothing is inferred from the file extension**, since every corpus thumbnail is a `.gif` only because PLOS and Springer both deposit that way.

Each attribute is tested in **both deposit orders**: with the thumbnail last, plain first-wins already resolves the image, so a test in that order passes with the attribute dropped from the predicate entirely.

## Two more found while pinning those, fixed here

- **`current_table` was the same single slot** — a `<table-wrap>` inside another's `<table-wrap-foot>` lost the outer table outright. #115 on the other exhibit; unmeasured, but structural.
- **An inner exhibit's label and caption went to the exhibit enclosing it.** Both asked whether a figure was open *anywhere above* before considering the table. Neither the issues nor the Swift reference had this — the test for #116's "compare against the exhibit's depth" rule is what exposed it. Both now route to the innermost open exhibit.

## Two filed rather than fixed

Both reproduce on this branch. **#123** — a nested `<caption>` truncates the enclosing caption *and* absorbs the inner element's legend; same shape as #115, but a depth counter is not enough, since the caption's *owner* is what the routing needs. **#124** — footnote prose is dropped entirely, so a rendered cell reads `12.3a` while the note it points at exists nowhere; needs a model decision first.

## Verification

- **41 new tests**; full suite **2455 passed, 63 skipped** (2414 on `main`). ruff 0.15.20 check + format and `uv run mypy` all clean.
- **Mutation testing: 28 of 29 killed.** The survivor is the `is not None` filter over the reserved slots, unreachable by construction (expat rejects an unbalanced document), documented as such at both properties in the form this module already uses for `nested_article_depth`. It found two real gaps first, both closed by adding the tests that earn them: `table-wrap-foot` as a `_FOOTNOTE_CONTAINERS` member, and two of the four archival mime-subtypes.
- PostgreSQL half not re-run: this touches no SQL.

## For reviewers

- **What moves for a caller**: `JATSArticle.figures` gains the figures that were being dropped, and `graphic_url` changes from a thumbnail to the full image for roughly half of all figures. No bmlib path carries `figures`/`tables` anywhere — `service.py` never reads them and `FullTextResult` has none — so a bmlib *sync* stores nothing different. A downstream calling `JATSParser` itself and persisting the result should re-parse.
- **`_FOOTNOTE_CONTAINERS` has two members and only one is measured.** `fn` is earned by #116's sample; `table-wrap-foot` is the container, earning its place by covering a `<fn-group>`'s own heading, with a test.
- **One thing is deliberately unpinned and says so**: a `<graphic>` marked both thumbnail and archival takes THUMBNAIL because that predicate is tested first. No corpus instance exists and neither ranking serves a form that does not render, so it is the reference implementation's order, recorded rather than asserted.
- HANDOVER.md was stale before this session on two counts and is corrected: PR #118 had merged, and the open-issue list said eight when there were eleven.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: gonos2k
body:
Reproduced before anything was changed: `cap_sink` and `partition` are
**bit-identical** between the `window=False` and `window=True` tables, because
the cap walked the whole stream and `partition` counted every sub-step in both.
The flag selected the span for four responses out of six.

So the "first-call" table was a hybrid of first-call residuals and whole-window
diagnostics, and **no statement about C or L in it was a first-call statement.**

## Three statements withdrawn

**"C moves its own cap invariant on the first call."** The published
`+2.435 -> -3.400` was the whole 300 s window. On the first call the ice cap
term runs `+3.540e-02 -> -1.988e-02` — about **seventy times smaller**.

**"The same N x C shape appears in the cap."** Not on either span. On the first
call the cap has **no N x C term at all**: C's conditional effect is
`-9.379e-01` at N=0 and `-9.379e-01` at N=1, identical, and every cap
`beta_NC` is exactly zero. Over the window there is one, and it is the *other*
shape:

```
R_ni         C at N=0  -9.085e-02    C at N=1   3.198e-17   <- C masked by N
cap_ice_rel  N at C=0   1.691e-04    N at C=1  -1.564e-02   <- N gated by C
```

Both are N x C interactions and they are different sentences. One `beta_NC`
cannot tell them apart, so conditional effects are now reported beside it.

**"`partition` is L-selective on the first call."** After one sub-step the two
decompositions agree completely.

| response | legacy | `lncmin` | beta_L |
|---|---|---|---|
| `partition_first` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `partition_endpoint` | 4 | 0 | -2.000 |
| `partition_path` | 45 | 0 | -2.250e+01 |

The published 45 was a **path count over twelve sub-steps**. L's effect is real
and it is a trajectory effect.

## What survives

`R_nr`'s first-call N-selectivity, with cross terms genuinely at roundoff
(1.99e-20 against a main effect of 1.843e-03 and a screening scale of 5.97e-08).

`R_ni`'s N x C **masking**, on both spans:

```
first call   beta_C = -5.865e-03   beta_NC = +5.865e-03
window       beta_C = -2.271e-02   beta_NC = +2.271e-02
```

Equal and opposite on each span, both resolved against a ~6e-08 screening scale.
Stated as a measured interaction of two operators, not as dynamical coupling.

## What the cap actually does, once destruction and creation are separated

`Sink.signed` says in its own docstring that it is a **signed defect, not a
sink**, and offers `destroyed`/`created` separately for exactly this reason.

Ice chain, whole window, kg m-2:

| arm | destroyed | created | signed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `legacy` | 2.435 | 0.000 | +2.435 |
| `conservative` | 0.000 | 3.380 | -3.400 |

**C removes the destruction completely and replaces it with creation of larger
magnitude.** `|signed|` goes 2.435 -> 3.400. Half of what restoring its own
invariant would require is met (`destroyed -> 0`); the other half moves 40 %
further away.

Scoped: this is the interface term as `g33_cap_interface` defines it, on one
fixture. `R_qi` is at roundoff in every arm on both spans, so it is **not**
column non-closure.

## Four gates the old table had no way to fail

- **Partition universe must match exactly.** Intersecting was fail-open: a split
  stream missing a column compares fewer states and reports *better* invariance.
- **Residual coverage must be complete.** An all-`None` span returned `0.0`,
  indistinguishable from a residual that vanished. `column()` refuses
  `mstep > 1`, so a `mstep ~ 10` factorial is now a refusal, not a silent zero.
- **Each arm's streams must declare the arm's own name** and agree on fixture,
  nsplit, mode, rho, width, levels — and differ in tile count.
- **Same atmosphere on the first call**: every arm's `_den` is identical,
  `beta = 0` exactly.

## Also

Numerator and denominator are separate responses: over the window
`beta_L(R_ni_num) = +1.808e+04` against `beta_L(R_ni_den) = -9.891e+05`, so the
ratio moves through both and the earlier attribution to the numerator alone does
not hold.

Responses carry units and nothing compares magnitudes across rows — the previous
version's "largest effect in the table" compared a dimensionless ratio with a
mass term. Each coefficient is screened against `sum|terms| * (U32 + gamma(n))`
from its own terms rather than a bare epsilon; integer counts are exact and
unscreened.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_013RJ8FFvEz8m4AsexoxMB8W

---

## Follow-up commit: the actual-transfer reader (§17.6), and what it found first

`--matched` puts the residuals on `g33_matched_closure`, which reads the `XFER`
records and reconstructs nothing ("mstep > 1 is admissible"). Doing it surfaced
a defect in the table this PR had just rewritten.

**`R_qi` closes by construction under the recovered reader.** `column()`
recovers transfers by *inverting the update*, so the budget it rebuilds cannot
fail to balance — the module header says the mass rows "return ~0 BY
CONSTRUCTION of their weight". Same first call, same fixture:

| arm | recovered `R_qi` | matched, actual transfers |
|---|---|---|
| `legacy` | -8.828e-17 | **-6.006e-01** |
| `conservative` | -6.822e-17 | **+2.306e-08** |

Legacy's ice mass column is short by **60.06 %** of its starting inventory —
exactly the cap interface term (`+6.006e-01`, same number, opposite sign by the
`signed = -mass_term` convention). The conservative arm closes it to 2.3e-08.

**So C does restore the ice mass budget on the first call**, and this withdraws
the "replaces destruction with creation of larger magnitude" reading added
earlier in this PR. That came from the interface term alone, and the response
meant to check it could not fail. *A response that cannot fail is not a
control.* The mass rows are now labelled reader-dependent, in the table and in
the CLI output.

**The `mstep > 1` factorial is still NO-GO, for a better reason.** The recovered
reader refuses (1 of 3 rows recoverable at `nsplit = 3`, where the old code
returned a ratio over the survivor). The matched reader is admissible at any
`mstep` and refuses too, on its *own* control — chain mass rows fail their
`gamma_n` screening threshold on every fixture available here: 4 of 6 at
`nsplit = 3` (worst 6.9e+05x), 2 of 6 at `nsplit = 24`, and 3 of 6 on the
factorial's own `boundary_mapping` fixture (1.4e+06x). The module's rule is that
the mass row is the control for the number row beside it, so neither is evidence
there. **What an `mstep > 1` factorial needs is a fixture whose mass accounting
closes, not a different reader.**

The first attempt applied `usable()` to the *number* row, which rejects the very
defect the experiment is about. The control is keyed by `(chain, column)` from
the `q` species, as the module's own report says.

body:
## Linear

[OCT-96](https://linear.app/ogard-labs/issue/OCT-96/move-project-memory-and-navigator-to-their-natural-homes) — Move Project memory and Navigator to their natural homes. Parent: OCT-87.

## What changed

Project memory now lives on every mode's Project Overview, where its Project ownership is explicit. Navigator stays one host-owned conversation and opens as an app-wide popover from the bottom-left profile and Settings control. Context, Project memory, and Navigator are gone from the dock launcher and tool strip.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Project Overview exposes Project memory active entries, audited history, add, supersede, retract, transfer, and archived read-only states.** Existing inspector UI is embedded in Overview (`ProjectMemorySection` + `ProjectMemoryInspector`). Evidence: `apps/web/src/projects/ProjectMemorySection.test.tsx`, `ProjectMemoryInspector.test.tsx`, `ProjectOverview.test.tsx`.
- **Project memory never shows data from a previous Project while another loads.** Each Overview owns its load; a Project switch drops the previous view before the next fetch settles. Evidence: `useProjectMemory.test.tsx`, `ProjectMemorySection.test.tsx`, `App.test.tsx` split-Overview cases.
- **Navigator opens from the bottom-left profile and Settings control without changing the active Project or thread.** Profile menu item opens `NavigatorPopover` instead of Settings. Evidence: `SidebarProfile.test.tsx`, `App.test.tsx` ("opens Navigator from the profile control…").
- **Navigator keeps one host-owned conversation across opens and uses its configured model.** Same `useNavigatorAssistant` controller; conversation survives close/reopen and reports the configured model. Evidence: `App.test.tsx`, `NavigatorPopover.test.tsx`, `NavigatorPanel.test.tsx`.
- **Navigator unconfigured, unavailable, and Settings deep-link states remain truthful.** Unchanged panel states, now shown in the popover. Evidence: `NavigatorPanel.test.tsx`, `NavigatorPopover.test.tsx`.
- **Context, Project memory, and Navigator are absent from the dock launcher and tool strip.** Removed from `RIGHT_UTILITY_DOCK_SURFACES` and the dock summary. Evidence: `rightUtilityDockModel.test.ts`, `App.test.tsx` dock launcher assertions.
- **Persisted selections of removed dock categories migrate to a safe closed or available state.** Retired ids still decode in `ContextSurfaceId`; the dock resolver returns `unknown-surface` / closed. Evidence: `rightUtilityDockModel.test.ts`, `packages/contracts/src/shell.ts`, `App.test.tsx` (`lastContextSurface: "project-memory"` / `"navigator"`).
- **Keyboard, focus, narrow overlay, permission-negative, and rendered QA pass.** Escape restores focus from the Navigator popover and the narrow dock; Overview memory stays on the Project when a thread pane is activated. Evidence: `NavigatorPopover.test.tsx`, `App.test.tsx` narrow dock and split-pane cases.

## Verification

- `cd apps/web && bun run test --` focused suites: Overview, memory inspector/section, Navigator panel/popover, dock model/surface, SidebarProfile, ShellSidebar, WindowChrome, `App.test.tsx` (55 passing).
- `cd apps/web && bun run typecheck`
- `bun run wiring:check`
- `bun run fmt` / `git diff --check`

## Residual risk

- Maintainer visual QA at narrow overlay and real-provider Navigator settings remains. Remote Project Overview still has no memory client, so remote snapshots do not show memory (same as before this change's mutation path).
- Live dock tools (OCT-98), first-run (OCT-97), and PR list (OCT-100) are out of scope.

Merge waits for Henrik. Do not merge without that instruction.

author: stormer78
body:
**Zero source changes.** Two `vta-sdk` minors were crossed and nothing here broke — which is worth stating, because the 0.22→0.23 and 0.24→0.25 moves each broke exactly one struct literal. Manifests and the lockfile, and that is all.

Two commits: the sdk line, then the `did-git-sign` floor that VGI had to publish before this repo could take it.

## What moves

| requirement | from | to |
|---|---|---|
| `vta-sdk` | 0.25 | **0.27** |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | 0.9 | **0.11** |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | 0.8 | **0.9** |
| `vta-service` (**dev**-dependency) | 0.17 | **0.19** |
| `affinidi-messaging-sdk` | 0.19.4 | **0.19.9** |
| `affinidi-messaging-delivery` | 0.1.12 | **0.1.14** |
| `affinidi-tdk` | 0.8 | 0.8.5 |
| `agent-names` | 0.1.2 | 0.1.3 |

The first four cannot move independently: `vta-sdk` 0.27 declares `trust-tasks-rs ^0.11`, `trust-tasks-capability-client` re-exports the same `TrustTask`, and `vta-service` 0.19 is the line built on `vta-sdk` 0.27. Any one held back is a second semver-incompatible copy of a type that crosses the sdk boundary.

`affinidi-tdk` 0.8.5 and `agent-names` 0.1.3 are floors **by construction** — both are `vta-sdk` 0.27's own requirements. The manifest now says so rather than implying the older versions are still viable.

## A third crate has to follow trust-tasks, not just `vta-service`

`affinidi-messaging-sdk` carries `trust-tasks-rs` types in its own public API — `acl_setup.rs` hands a `MediatorAcl` built from its own copy into `atm.trust_tasks().account_update`. A copy left on 0.9 is not untidy, it is `expected MediatorAcl, found a different MediatorAcl`.

So its floor goes to **0.19.9**, the release where affinidi-tdk-rs #717 moves the messaging crates to 0.11. This is easy to miss because it reads as an unrelated transport dependency — same shape as the `vta-service` trap #229 documented, where the crate that reintroduces the duplicate is never the one you set out to bump.

## Three floors that are live defect fixes

**`affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.19.8 — the listener flapping we chased for weeks.** tdk #716: `_refresh_authentication` discarded `force_refresh`, so the websocket transport's proactive refresh at 80% of token life rebuilt the socket *without* refreshing and re-armed at 80% of the time **remaining**. A geometric cascade of reconnects per token instead of one clean cycle — the symptom #231–#234 saw as two listeners flapping every ~15 minutes. The lockfile has carried it since #232; the **floor** did not, so a clean checkout could resolve straight back onto the storm.

**`affinidi-messaging-delivery` 0.1.14 — messages destroyed, not delayed.** tdk #710: the dispatcher acked every inbound message unconditionally, and an ack is a **delete at the mediator** — including when `subscribers.send` had just reported nobody listening. No subscriber is installed for a moment at startup and again on the way down. For this repo the contents of those windows are a membership credential or a join reply: exactly the class of loss #218's pickup-on-connect exists to prevent, being undone one layer below it.

**`vta-sdk` 0.27.0 — a silent degradation on our own call sites.** VTI #1033: #1000 folded Trust-Task payloads to lowerCamelCase per SPEC §4.10 but excluded `client/types.rs` on a stale path assumption, so the agent moved to `basePath` while the client went on demanding `base_path` — eleven required fields with no `default`, across `contexts` create/get/update/list and `keys` sign/rename/revoke/export-secret.

Both our `list_contexts()` call sites sit behind `let Ok(..)`/`match` (`state_handler/mod.rs:766`, `openvtc-core/src/context_probe.rs:137`), so against a post-#1000 agent this never surfaced as an error — the sub-context probe simply saw nothing. The fix is intake **aliases** rather than a rename, so 0.27 still decodes an older agent's snake_case: safe against a VTA on either side of the fold.

## Also in 0.26, not adopted

VTI #1012 adds `VtaClient::idempotent`, which holds one `idempotencyKey` across every attempt of an operation so a retried `create_key` is deduplicated at the VTA rather than taking effect twice. Our retry owner is still `vta_retry()`. Left alone here — but it is the seam that should replace it, and the manifest note records that so it is not rediscovered from scratch.

0.26 is also **not a viable floor**: it declares `trust-tasks-rs ^0.9`, so a checkout resolving back to it while this workspace is on 0.11 puts two `trust-tasks-rs` in the binary — the same trap 0.24 (`^0.6`) posed against 0.9 and 0.23.0 (`^0.4`) posed against 0.6.

## The other half: `did-git-sign` had to be released first

`did-git-sign` 0.4.5 requires `vta-sdk ^0.25`, so moving this workspace to 0.27 left the published signer dragging the old line back in through a single edge:

```
vta-sdk v0.25.1
└── did-git-sign v0.4.5
    └── openvtc v0.3.1
```

**Third cycle running** — the same position #229 described before VGI 0.4.5, and #216 before that. OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#32 published **0.4.6** on `vta-sdk` 0.27, and the second commit here takes it. `cargo update -p did-git-sign` states the result plainly:

```
Updating did-git-sign v0.4.5 -> v0.4.6
Removing trust-tasks-rs v0.9.0
Updating vgi-core v0.4.5 -> v0.4.6
Removing vta-sdk v0.25.1
```

### Why the requirement names 0.4.6 rather than staying on a caret

`"0.4.3"` already admitted 0.4.5 — that is exactly how the duplicate arrived while this line looked untouched. A caret permitting any release built on an older sdk lets a clean checkout resolve straight back onto the second copy, with nothing in the manifest to say it happened. The floor has to name the release that is actually on the current sdk line.

The comment also records why this particular duplicate never broke a build, because the reason is narrow and should not be read as safety: we use only `did_git_sign::{config, init}`, so no type crosses the boundary. One new import is all it would take — `vti-common` re-exports `vta_sdk::acl::{ActScope, ApproveScope, ContextDirection}` as its own public API, so the copies do carry types that cannot unify.

Note VGI still holds `trust-tasks-rs` 0.9 via `trql-client` → `verify-trust` (the trust registry has published nothing on 0.11 yet). That does **not** reach here: `did-git-sign` has no trql-client edge. Documented on both sides.

## Comments updated

Every block that moved now records **this** move rather than the last one, and older satisfied floors are dropped to git history rather than kept as a wall of constraints. New notes: why `affinidi-messaging-sdk` is a trust-tasks follower, why 0.26 is not a floor, and the standing cross-repo obligation on `did-git-sign` — written once, in that crate's floor note, with the root `vta-sdk` block pointing at it rather than describing it twice.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test --workspace` — pass
- `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features` — pass
- `cargo test -p openvtc-core --features arbitrary --lib` — 430 pass
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` — clean (a separate lint set from clippy, and its own CI gate)
- `cargo test --workspace -- --ignored` — pass, including `mockvta_bootstrap_e2e`, `join_lifecycle_e2e` and `relationship_e2e`. These are the only thing here that actually exercises **`vta-service` 0.19**; plain `cargo test --workspace` skips every one of them.
- `cargo outdated --root-deps-only` — *"All dependencies are up to date"*
- `cargo tree -d -e normal,build,dev` — lists **none** of `vta-sdk`, `vta-service`, `trust-tasks-rs`, `trust-tasks-capability-client`, `vti-common`, `affinidi-tdk`, `dtg-credentials`, `didwebvh-rs`, `agent-names`, `did-git-sign` or `vgi-core`
- `cargo tree -i vta-sdk` — a single **0.27.0** node, with all four consumers (`openvtc`, `openvtc-core`, `did-git-sign`, `vta-service`) on it

The full gate was re-run after the second com

## What changed

- Keep exact current FAA admission as the zero-provider primary path.
- For RegistrationNotFound only, inspect exactly one retained primary listing photo and accept only a different normalized N-number whose current FAA record and serial agree.
- Persist one bounded immutable correction artifact so crash/retry is provider-free and media-network-free.

author: andrelaf
body:
…foi classificado

A primeira versao tinha dois estados: ha tabela, ou nao ha. E "nao ha" cobria duas situacoes que pedem acoes opostas:

    contrato classificado, sem ambiguidade  ->  confirme o que o laudo afirma
    contrato sem laudo desta versao         ->  o check provavelmente reprovou

Nas duas saia "Nenhuma pendencia encontrada nos laudos commitados desta versao", que na segunda e quase o oposto da verdade: nao ha pendencia porque nao ha classificacao — o `check` parou antes, no nome do arquivo, no YAML ou no schema ODCS.

Agora sao tres saidas, e cada uma diz o que fazer.

--- "Sem laudo para a versao atual"

Nomeia os contratos e admite que nao sabe qual das duas causas e — porque este passo **nao roda o harness**, de proposito, e portanto nao tem o veredito. Manda ler o comentario do pull request, que e onde o motivo esta escrito com o sha256 do arquivo e a versao da regua.

E diz a frase que faltava:

    Aprovar nao conserta contrato invalido: o `check` e um status check
    proprio, e continua vermelho depois do rotulo.

Sem ela, quem ve o gate vermelho tende a aplicar o rotulo achando que destrava. Nao destrava, e o desenho e esse: os dois workflows sao independentes justamente para que aprovacao humana nao passe por cima de contrato quebrado.

--- "Nenhuma ambiguidade — e ainda assim precisa de decisao"

O gate nao bloqueia porque ha pendencia; bloqueia porque **alterar contrato de dados exige decisao humana registrada**. Duas regras diferentes, e a mensagem antiga misturava as duas: dizia "nenhuma pendencia" com o merge travado, e quem lia nao entendia o que estava sendo pedido.

O texto agora separa: nao se pede resolver ambiguidade, pede-se **confirmar o que o laudo afirma** — que campo e dado pessoal, sob qual base legal, sob qual versao do criterio. Quem responde pelo dado assina isso, e nao a esteira.

--- Verificacao

Rodei o passo inteiro, com `jq`, contra o repositorio de contratos real nos dois estados novos: com os dois contratos classificados (sai a segunda mensagem, com os dois nomeados) e com `version:` removido de um deles (sai a primeira para o quebrado **e** a segunda para o intacto, que e o comportamento certo num pull request com varios contratos).

-->

body:
## Summary

closes #134#

Implements a self-contained connection pool health probe with adaptive sizing in src/core/pool/health_probe.rs, following the project's existing pool architecture and coding conventions.

---

## What was changed

### New file: src/core/pool/health_probe.rs
Full implementation of \HealthProbeManager\ and supporting types:

- **\ConnectionProbeState\** — per-connection state: health status, consecutive failure counter, exponential-backoff probe interval, in-use flag, last-probe timestamp
- **\ConnectionHealth\** — \Healthy\ / \Degraded\ / \Failed\ based on probe outcome and P99 latency budget (100 ms)
- **\ProbeEvent\** — observable events: \ProbeSucceeded\, \ProbeFailed\, \ConnectionEvicted\, \PoolScaledOut\, \PoolScaledIn\
- **\HealthProbeManager\** — orchestrates probing, eviction, checkout/checkin, and adaptive sizing:
  - Exponential backoff: 500 ms → 1 s → 2 s → 4 s → 8 s → 16 s → 30 s cap
  - Eviction after 5 consecutive probe failures (\MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES\)
  - Scale-out at ≥ 75 % pool utilisation (+4 connections per step, max 128)
  - Scale-in at ≤ 25 % pool utilisation (−4 connections per step, min 1)
  - Pool bounds clamped: \POOL_SIZE_MIN = 1\, \POOL_SIZE_MAX = 128\

### src/core/pool/mod.rs
Registered the new \health_probe\ module.

### Cargo.toml
Added \soroban-sdk\ workspace dependency to \lumina_core\ (was declared in the workspace manifest but omitted from the package — the existing \poc\ module requires it).

### src/core/poc/tests.rs
Fixed pre-existing field-name drift: \l.sequence\ → \l.sequence_number\ (soroban-sdk 26 API change) — minimum required to unblock test compilation.

---

## Testing / validation performed

- 24 unit tests added inside \health_probe.rs\, covering:
  - Backoff curve: 500 ms → 1 s → 2 s → 4 s → 8 s → 16 s → 30 s cap
  - Eviction after max consecutive failures
  - Scale-out / scale-in / no-scaling at 75 % / 25 % / 50 % utilisation
  - Pool size clamped at min and max boundaries
  - Checkout/checkin flag tracking
  - \due_connections()\ scheduling
  - Probe result events (success, failure, unknown connection)
  - Initial size clamping to \[POOL_SIZE_MIN, POOL_SIZE_MAX]\

Run: \cargo +stable-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu test --package lumina_core --lib core::pool::health_probe\
Result: **24 passed, 0 failed**

---

## Risks / follow-up notes

- The two pre-existing test failures (\poc::test_concurrent_validator_submission\ — missing contract context; \ ackpressure_sender::test_suppress_zero_window_ack_after_threshold\ — logic bug in existing code) are unrelated to this PR and tracked under issue #136.
- \HealthProbeManager::evaluate_pool_size()\ adjusts the *target* size only; the caller is responsible for actually creating or destroying connections to match the target.

body:
Refs #894. **The literal reported case was already handled. Two worse things were not.**

## What it did today, established from the code first

`validateProjectDir` already gates every `--dir`-taking command on `existsSync('.macf/macf-agent.json')`, so an **absent** config was refused cleanly before `restart-self` ran. The issue's headline case was covered.

**But a PRESENT-but-corrupt config crashed.** `readAgentConfig` did `JSON.parse(readFileSync(...))` with no `try/catch`, so malformed JSON threw an uncaught `SyntaxError` out to the top-level handler — a generic `Unexpected token…` naming no path. Reachable from **~20 call sites** across the CLI, and hit **twice** in one `restart-self` run because it reads config a second time for the canonical-branch check.

Fixed at the root in `config.ts` rather than locally: returns `null` with a warning naming the path. A strict safety-net change — it never throws where it used to, and behaviour for valid or schema-invalid input is byte-identical.

## The ambient-env question — verified negative here, POSITIVE next door

I asked whether `#763`'s mechanism (a restart deriving identity from ambient `MACF_*` rather than the target) was reachable through `--dir`.

**In `restart-self`: no.** `workspaceDir: projectDir` is hardcoded, and identity comes only from `config?.*`; `MACF_WORKSPACE_DIR` populates a conflict *warning* and is never a value fallback. That was already correct from `#888`/`#893`. **A verified negative, established by reading the branch rather than assuming.**

**But three sibling commands have exactly the pre-`#888` shape:**

```
fleet-resume.ts:397  · fleet-reconcile.ts:269  · fleet-install-cron.ts:449
    process.env['MACF_WORKSPACE_DIR']?.trim() || projectDir
```

with no `dirExplicit` guard. `createVmDriverFromConfig` then binds the driver's project to whatever it is handed — so **an explicit `--dir <other-project>`, run from inside your own agent session, silently reconciles your OWN project instead.** Same class as `#1101` (a missing scope filter silently retargeting an operation).

**Not fixed here** — different command family, no `dirExplicit` plumbing exists there, and expanding scope would turn a focused fix into a much larger one. **Filed separately.**

## Decisive pair, with the zero-effect property asserted

```
✓ refuses (exit 1, NO stash/write/spawn/kill) on missing config, naming the target path
✓ refuses with DIFFERENT wording on unreadable — distinguishable from missing
✓ fires even in DRY-RUN — the refusal precedes the plan print entirely
✓ a valid config proceeds normally — the pair's second half
```

Each refusal test asserts `order` / `killed` / `spawned` are all empty — **not merely a non-zero exit**, per `assert-the-wrong-path.md`. For a command that kills live sessions, "it exited 1" is not evidence nothing happened. The unreadable case also asserts it does **not** match the missing-config wording, proving the two are genuinely distinguished.

## `--dir` audit across every command

Fixing `readAgentConfig` at the root closed the crash-on-corrupt-JSON cell for **essentially every row at once**. The per-command table (13 rows) is in the implementer's report; the ambient-fallback cell is live in exactly the three commands above.

## A correction the implementer flagged on itself

Early on, three `find`/`ls` calls returned empty and it concluded the citation-guard test "doesn't exist." That was the **disk-full condition breaking Bash's own output capture**, not a missing file. It re-ran once the box recovered — the test exists and passes 11/11.

Worth recording: **an empty result from a broken tool reads exactly like a negative finding.** That is the same shape as tonight's stale-checkout grep, where I concluded a shipped fix was absent because I asked my disk instead of GitHub.

## Test plan

- [x] **Verified by me** on a clean worktree off current `main`: `Test Files 3 passed (3)`, `Tests 100 passed (100)`; typecheck and canonical lint clean; citation guard passes.
- [x] Staged on `/dev/vdb` (49G free), not `/tmp`.

author: addieflips
body:
Documentation only — no code changes. Two instructions in `CLAUDE.md` sent me down blind alleys while shipping PR #4, so both are corrected rather than quietly worked around.

## §1 — the deploy command has not worked for a while

The file said the way to publish the website was `git push origin main`. That is rejected outright:

```
GH013: Repository rule violations found for refs/heads/main.
- 2 of 2 required status checks are expected.
```

The two required checks only run through a pull request, so a **direct push can never satisfy them** however green the suite is locally. Corrected to: branch → push branch → PR → both checks green → merge, with Netlify publishing from main once the merge lands. §0's "merge back to main and push" is corrected the same way.

## §9.14 / §9.15 — the browser suite is not parked

Both sections said there is no browser job in CI and that the Playwright specs are parked, run by hand only. Neither is true: `tests.yml` has run **"Browser tests (Playwright)"** alongside the fast suite for some time, and it is one of the two required checks on `main`.

The practical consequence is worth stating plainly, so it's now in the file: **a red browser run blocks every merge, including a money fix.** It doesn't gate the functions deploy (that workflow runs its own fast-suite job) and it doesn't gate Netlify directly — but nothing reaches `main` without it, and Netlify publishes from `main`.

## What I deliberately did not delete

§9.15's original argument — that a suite nobody acts on is worse than none — is kept intact and labelled as history rather than removed. It was sound when written, because the specs were permanently red; the premise changed when all eight went green. It is still the live guidance for what to do if that flips back: **delete the job**, which is exactly what the header comment in `tests.yml` instructs, rather than adding `continue-on-error` back — the option both sessions that argued about this agreed was worthless.

`npm test` — **3709 passed, 0 failed** (gate A 10, selector contract 18, money parity 32). No source files touched.
