author: psaab
body:
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go` had reached **2,299 LOC** and sat in
the `[REFACTOR]` tier of the modularity audit. Its size was a symptom: the
HA-shaped filename covered seven unrelated responsibilities, so anyone touching
the session mirror had to read the HA state machine and vice versa, and the
file's lock-discipline invariants (#5007 one-snapshot build, #5698 pair-transmit
contiguity, #5380 transport fast-fail) sat interleaved with counter plumbing
that has no locking contract at all.

## Split by responsibility — what each file owns

| File | LOC | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| `manager_ha.go` | 873 | The HA state machine: RG ownership (`UpdateRGActive`), the watchdog heartbeat + its `update_ha_state` IPC throttle, the helper HA-state publish/clear incl. the #5487 retry debt, HA group inventory seeding + shim-map refresh, the desired forwarding-arm reconcile, and takeover readiness. |
| `manager_sessions.go` | 569 | Session-table mutation entry points: the `dataplane.DataPlane` install/delete/batch/clear verbs, the #5305 transactional cluster-synced install (BPF pre-image + rollback), the chunked authoritative helper deletes, and the bulk event-stream session export. |
| `manager_sessionsync_request.go` | 327 | Session-sync request construction: BPF key/value → `SessionSyncRequest`, egress / owner-RG / tunnel-endpoint resolution against `m.lastSnapshot`, zone-name lookup, and the address/port/MAC encoders. Pure snapshot reads, no socket I/O. |
| `manager_counters.go` | 267 | Counter bridging: aggregate the helper's per-binding counters from a status poll and push the deltas into the BPF global-counter, NAT-rule, and per-zone offset maps. |
| `manager_sessionsync_transmit.go` | 187 | Session-sync transmit, and the **single owner of its lock discipline**: the `m.mu` drop for socket I/O, per-request `m.sessionMu` on the interleavable bulk path, one hold for the whole group on the contiguous pair path (#5698), transport fast-fail (#5380). |
| `manager_fabric_sync.go` | 102 | Fabric-state publish to the helper + the #5306 resolved-fabric writeback into `m.lastSnapshot`. (The snapshots themselves are still built in `fabric.go`.) |
| `napi_probe_interfaces.go` | 57 | The deterministic Linux netdev list the mlx5 NAPI bootstrap probe (`process_napi.go`) sends traffic on. |

The split **forces no new exported surface**: every identifier keeps its name,
receiver and visibility, and the package is unchanged — which is also why **no
test needed editing to keep compiling**, including the `_5007` and `_5698`
cells.

## Equivalence — pure code motion, proven mechanically

Each declaration was copied **by exact source line range by a script, never
retyped**, so no body, signature, receiver, visibility, struct field order, lock
scope or defer ordering changed. "The suite passes" is necessary and not
sufficient for a refactor, so equivalence was proven by two **independent**
parsers that share no code:

1. **Block-parser compare.** The pre-split file and all seven post-split files
   were parsed into `(leading comment run + declaration)` blocks and compared by
   declaration name: **80 of 80 byte-identical *including* indentation, 0
   dropped, 0 added.** Each declaration's doc comment was compared as its own
   string, so a comment that landed on the wrong neighbour fails the check
   rather than hiding inside a whole-block compare.
2. **`go/parser` + `go/printer` dump.** For every top-level decl, its
   `ast.Doc` text and its printed source were emitted keyed by name; the before
   and after dumps **diff to zero** over the same 80 declarations. This uses
   Go's own parser to bind each doc comment to its declaration, so proof 1's
   regex is not load-bearing.

No moved body is non-identical, so there is nothing to justify individually.

## Refactor audit

`manager_ha.go` leaves the `[REFACTOR]` tier and **no new file enters** the
`>=1500` LOC audit (largest new file is 873), so the regenerated artifact is a
single deleted row. Advisory LOC drift on other lanes' files was deliberately
not folded in — `TestHeatmapNotStale` gates the file set and tier, not the LOC
column (#6617).

## Doc pointers

Six references in docs and Rust comments named `manager_ha.go` as the home of a
symbol that moved (`SetClusterSyncedSessionV4/V6`, `SyncFabricState`,
`zoneNameByID`, the `sessionExpires` counter bridge). They now name the new
file. References to symbols that **stayed** (`syncDesiredForwardingStateLocked`,
`disarmBeforeUnsupportedPublishLocked`, `UpdateHAWatchdog` in `docs/reth-mac.md`
and `docs/ha-failover-status.md`) are untouched and still correct.

## Test plan

Exit codes read directly, never through a pipe:

- [x] `go build ./...` → rc=0
- [x] `go vet ./pkg/dataplane/...` → rc=0
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./pkg/dataplane/...` → rc=0
- [x] `go test -count=1 -race -run 'Session|HA' ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/...` → rc=0
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./pkg/refactoraudit/...` → rc=0
- [x] `go test -count=1 ./...` → rc=0 (no failures at all, not even the known flakes)

All re-run after `git merge origin/master` (only `_Log.md` conflicted; resolved
by union with a structural heading/bullet count check — no code file conflicted).

## Owed, and NOT run

This is HA / session-sync code, so **`make test-failover` is OWED**. It was
deliberately **not** run and the shared loss cluster was not touched. Nothing in
this PR changes behaviour — the smoke is owed by the code's subject matter, not
by an observed risk.

Closes #6427

author: dycuong03
body:
Fixes the 3 test failures in [run 32503228420](https://github.com/Cuvara/UIToolkit/actions/runs/32503228420).

## What was actually broken

`ScreenFlowRegistrationTests` — three cases, none of which touch input — failed with:

```
Unhandled log message: '[Exception] InvalidOperationException: You are trying to read Input
using the UnityEngine.Input class, but you have switched active Input handling to Input
System package in Player Settings.'
```

Both Unity jobs write `activeInputHandler: 1` ("Input System package only") into `ProjectSettings.asset`, but neither adds `com.unity.inputsystem` to the manifest. That combination is not a stricter project, it is an invalid one:

1. UI Toolkit's `InputForUI` finds no Input System provider.
2. It falls back to `InputManagerProvider`.
3. That provider reads `UnityEngine.Input.mousePosition` — the exact legacy API `activeInputHandler: 1` forbids.
4. The throw arrives from the runtime panel's update loop as an *unhandled log message*, and the test framework attributes it to whichever test happened to be running.

Which is why the failures looked unrelated to their own subject matter.

## Changes

| Job | Change |
|---|---|
| `test` | `+ com.unity.inputsystem@1.18.0` — the fix. `+ com.unity.entities@1.4.8` so `Cuvara.UIToolkit.Ecs.Tests` meets its `CUVARA_UITOOLKIT_ENTITIES` constraint and runs at all — CI had been reporting ~20 fewer tests than a local run |
| `samples` | `+ com.unity.inputsystem@1.18.0`. Imports every sample `package.json` declares instead of a hardcoded pair — the list had fallen behind by two of four: `ScreenFlow` (the one with the scene) and `LoadingFlow` were never compiled by any job while it reported success |
| `install-probe` | Unchanged. Comment added explaining why bare handler-1 is correct there: EditMode only, never opens a runtime panel, and installing the package would defeat what the probe measures |

The comments above each `activeInputHandler` block now state the coupling, so the next person changing one changes the other.

## Verification

- `1.18.0` exists on the Unity registry (latest is `1.20.0`).
- The samples loop resolves all four declared paths.
- Neither `ScreenFlow` nor `LoadingFlow` needs Addressables — the only mentions in the package are comments.
- `ci.yml` parses as YAML.

CI on this branch is the real check; nothing local can prove it.

author: sethbacon
body:
feat(security): let a caller name the commit these workflows scan

Both files checked out whatever the run's default resolves to. That is right
for a pull request and wrong for the case that matters most: a release job
validating the specific artefact it is about to publish.

azure-pipelines-terraform's release.yml calls its test workflow with
`ref: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.sha }}`, and the local zizmor and actionlint jobs
it is about to migrate off honour that ref explicitly. Migrating without this
input would have quietly replaced "scan the commit being released" with "scan
whatever the default checkout resolves to" -- usually the same commit, and not
reliably so, which is the kind of implicit coupling that only shows up on the
day it differs.

Optional, defaulting to `github.sha`, so every existing caller is unaffected.
workflow-hardening.yml already takes `script-ref` for the same reason, so this
is that repository's existing convention applied to the other two files rather
than a new idea.

The record workflow takes it too, and its description says why: pass the same
ref to both, or the security tab records findings from a different commit than
the one gating the pull request.

Verified: actionlint reports zero findings.

### Related GitHub Issue

Closes: #1365

### Description

This PR adds **[OrcaRouter](https://www.orcarouter.ai)** as a first-class named provider in CoStrict, mirroring the existing `vercel-ai-gateway` integration. OrcaRouter is a unified OpenAI-compatible gateway that exposes a large model catalog through a single endpoint (`https://api.orcarouter.ai/v1`). It also runs gateway-level, zero-trust security for AI agents on the same endpoint — screening every prompt/response and governing every tool call on a default-deny basis, with no application code changes.

Previously, OrcaRouter users had to fall back to the generic "OpenAI Compatible" endpoint and fill in the base URL manually. This makes it a discoverable, first-class option like the other routing gateways:

- **Types** (`@roo-code/types`): `orcarouter` added to `dynamicProviders`, provider schema (`orcaRouterApiKey`, `orcaRouterModelId`, `orcaRouterBaseUrl`), `ProviderSettings` / `MODELS_BY_PROVIDER` / `modelIdKeysByProvider`, default model `orcarouter/auto`, secret-storage key.
- **Handler** (`src/api/providers/orcarouter.ts`): OpenAI-compatible chat completions against `https://api.orcarouter.ai/v1`, inheriting `RouterProvider` (dynamic model sync, tool calling, streaming, usage).
- **Model fetcher** (`src/api/providers/fetchers/orcarouter.ts`): pulls the model catalog from `https://api.orcarouter.ai/v1/models`.
- **UI** (`webview-ui`): provider entry in settings (`OrcaRouter.tsx`) with API key field + model picker, provider list + constants, i18n (en / zh-CN / zh-TW), validation.
- **CLI** (`apps/cli`): `orcarouter` supported via `ORCAROUTER_API_KEY`.

author: fadyfaheem
body:
Splits the exported 8-page CrowPanel profile into 22 installable community
decks: 8 for the 10.1in CrowPanel and 7 mini variants for each of the two
Waveshare revisions.

## How the split works

The source profile is a cohesive set. Every page carries an app's shortcuts on
indices 0-23 (30 for VLC) plus a shared eight-key navigation strip on the bottom
row that jumps between pages. Split naively, that strip points at pages that no
longer exist.

So:

- **Windows Workspace** publishes the complete profile unchanged, navigation
  intact, for anyone who wants the whole thing.
- **Seven per-app decks** drop the navigation strip and keep only that app's
  keys, with the row count shrunk to fit.

Each standalone deck carries the app match on the profile as well as the page. A
single-app deck is a whole profile, so without the profile-level match it would
never be selected when that app took focus.

## Mini variants

Six of the seven apps already occupy indices 0-23, so they drop onto a Waveshare
5x5 grid untouched. VLC has 30 keys and spills onto a second page behind a
navigation key rather than losing any.

Both Waveshare revisions get their own copies, because `addImportedProfile`
requires an exact board id match.

## Verification

- `build-catalog.js --validate-only` passes all 22 through the desktop importer
- Every profile was installed onto a matching device registry via the real
  `registerDevice` / `addImportedProfile` path: **22 of 22 install, 0 failures**
- Grid, board-cap, and page-reference checks: no overflows, no dangling page refs
- Key counts reconcile exactly against the source (207 = 33 + 24x6 + 30)

## Notes

- Audited for personal data before publishing: the only non-hotkey actions are
  seven generic `start "" <app>` launches. No URLs, no Type Text, no paths,
  no credentials.
- The Teams deck's five plugin actions resolve against the bundled
  `microsoft-teams` plugin, so they work for everyone.

body:
## Summary

- replace manual endpoint, pairing-code, and diagnostics setup with secure automatic native enrollment for Chrome, Firefox, and Safari
- add the desktop enrollment broker, native host lifecycle, browser/profile binding, durable revocation, replay protection, and short-lived credentials
- minimize the normal product UI: remove app-side bridge installation/admin controls, hide empty session policy, and reduce the popup to status plus one browser-required permission or recovery action
- add exact-current-site permission handling, 30-second app readiness retry, authenticated reconnect, and browser-owned all-sites permission
- harden Chrome release identity, Safari App Group/signing/provisioning, Windows named-pipe ACL/DPAPI storage, cookie validation, and loopback-only broker routing

Closes the implementation scope tracked in #23898. Store publication and physical-platform acceptance remain authority/hardware gated as documented below.

## Architecture and security

- Chrome/Firefox use native messaging with exact extension identities; Safari uses its containing-app handler and registered App Group secret.
- Enrollment messages are framed, bounded, HMAC-authenticated, caller-bound, and replay-protected.
- Credentials are capped at five minutes; revocation is durable per owner/browser/profile and cannot be bypassed by reinstalling or locally resetting the extension.
- The desktop broker accepts loopback API bases only. There is no unauthenticated localhost auto-pairing path.
- Browser site access remains an explicit browser-controlled permission. Current-site mode requests only the active HTTP(S) origin; all-sites mode uses the browser-owned warning.

## Minimal automatic UI

- The Eliza Browser view no longer exposes build/install, reveal-folder, open-extension-manager, refresh, endpoint, or pairing controls.
- Empty session security UI hides; active approvals and intercepted account-affecting actions remain visible.
- The extension popup has no pairing JSON, endpoint, credential, or diagnostics form.
- Connected/retrying states need no action. Human actions appear only for browser permission, explicit disconnect/revocation recovery, or disconnecting an active companion.
- Remaining controls meet the repository 44 px target.

## Exact-head verification at `dab833ecf138fb5081d7dded4434951f48d3ea73`

- Browser extension: 140 non-Safari tests passed; Safari native error/project contracts 10/10 passed serially; typecheck and Biome passed. The initial parallel run hit host-wide disk-I/O timeouts in six Safari tests; all passed immediately under serial isolation.
- Minimized Browser UI: focused policy-panel recovery tests 10/10 and prior Browser Workspace tests 24/24 passed; UI typecheck passed after the required pinned `bun install` (3,716 installs, no lockfile changes).
- Native desktop broker: 60/60 Vitest tests plus 5/5 Electrobun/Bun lifecycle tests passed.
- Browser companion auth/revoke/registration: 24/24 tests passed.
- Real PGlite revocation and atomic session persistence: 7/7 tests passed.
- Real agent server CORS/owner boundary: all 8 assertions passed, including hostile-origin credential denial, CSRF, OWNER authorization, extension capability CORS, and loopback owner replacement prevention. The direct Bun command exits nonzero only because root `bunfig.toml` applies whole-repository coverage thresholds to the two-file subset.
- Guide parity and `git diff --check`: passed.\n- Exact candidate-range Gitleaks scan: passed after narrowly allowlisting Chrome’s public manifest verification key; the exception is restricted to the named identity field in `packages/browser-bridge-extension/identity.json`, and the private signing key is not present.
- Installed Chrome for Testing 152 smoke: passed end to end, including permission grant, automatic sync, DOM action lease/progress/completion, and DNR blocked-page redirect.
- Installed Firefox 153.0.4 smoke: passed end to end, including preflight, sync, action lease/progress/completion, and blocker fetch. ZIP/XPI SHA-256: `852d1db86b5a2720ee2546abfb1c50b5362f3e79c3ab0219de22c132bbdf3a57`.
- App visual audit: Browser and plugin-computer-use screens had zero broken/needs-work verdicts across desktop/mobile captures. The larger audit stopped only on an ENOSPC write in an unrelated built-in plugins capture.

## Repository-wide gate status

`bun run verify` currently stops at `check:i18n` on the rebased `develop` snapshot before affected type/lint gates. The base is missing nine English login/account keys and has 989-1,062 source-used keys absent from each non-English catalog. This PR does not modify the affected login/account sources or locale catalogs. Hosted CI is the authority for whether current `develop` has repaired that independent failure.

## Review repairs at exact head\n\n- Revoked browsers now expose one owner-authenticated reset only when needed; the extension observes the reset automatically on its bounded 30-second alarm without weakening the durable broker tombstone.\n- Browser-wide reinstall-resistant revocation reset is atomic across profiles and proven by real PGlite coverage.\n- Unsigned Firefox XPI output is submission-only and never advertised as permanently installable without an AMO URL/signature.\n- Support claims are narrowed to the implemented Chrome, Firefox, and macOS Safari targets; retired pairing-JSON guidance is removed.\n- The current-base duplicate Cloud test declarations that blocked hosted lint are removed; the full cloud-shared lint lane passes locally.\n\n## Publication and physical acceptance blockers

These require external authority or hardware and are not claimed by source tests:

- Chrome Web Store item/publisher ID, matching Package-tab public key, publisher MFA/upload authority, and public support/privacy URLs
- Apple Team ID, signing identity/private key, registered app/extension identifiers, registered `group.ai.elizaos.browserbridge` App Group, distribution profiles, App Store Connect authority, and signed installed Safari acceptance
- Firefox AMO publisher/submission authority if AMO distribution is required
- physical Windows and Linux packaged-installer acceptance for host registration/uninstall, restart/revocation/re-enrollment, real browser actions, multi-monitor/DPI, lock/sleep, background/PiP, multi-session, virtual cursors, and OS security boundaries

Release packaging fails closed when required store identity, signing, or provisioning inputs are absent.

**1. Executive Summary**
- **WHAT:** Implemented two targeted performance optimizations: deferred non-critical telemetry execution and memoized an expensive purely visual component. 
- **WHY:** To ensure the VISAR Portfolio application remains highly responsive (60fps) during heavy routing transitions and background telemetry fetching.

**2. Impact & Safety Matrix**
- `src/lib/telegram.ts`
  - Action: Wrapped the Telegram fetch logic in `requestIdleCallback` (with a 0ms setTimeout fallback).
  - Reason: `sendTelegramNotification` is fired synchronously when clicking tabs and UI actions. By wrapping this, we defer fetching metadata and hitting the Telegram API until the browser's main thread is idle, ensuring UI interactions remain instantaneous. 
  - Impact: Improved perceived UI responsiveness during tab navigation.
  - Risk Level: Low. Background telemetry may silently fail on immediate window unload, which is an accepted tradeoff for UI fluidity.
- `src/components/portfolio/HeroAvatar.tsx`
  - Action: Wrapped the `HeroAvatar` export in `React.memo()`.
  - Reason: `HeroAvatar` uses expensive `framer-motion` spring animations and tracks local state but has no props. Since it is rendered inside `OverviewTab`, it was subject to unnecessary re-renders whenever context updated.
  - Impact: Saved processing cycles during root component state changes.
  - Risk Level: Low. Standard React optimization pattern.

**3. Verification**
- Ran `pnpm lint` (cleared critical errors, one pre-existing warning).

body:
## Summary
This PR implements critical security improvements and production-readiness features for the Fideliza loyalty platform, including proper password hashing with bcrypt, role-based access control across all API endpoints, webhook idempotency to prevent duplicate point accrual, and comprehensive documentation.

## Key Changes

**Authentication & Security:**
- Extracted NextAuth configuration to `lib/auth.js` with Credentials provider supporting three roles (admin, negocio, cliente)
- Implemented bcrypt password hashing via new `lib/password.js` module with automatic rehashing of legacy plaintext passwords on first login
- Added admin credentials via environment variables (`ADMIN_EMAIL`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH`) instead of hardcoded values
- Secured all API endpoints with session validation and role-based authorization checks

**Webhook Idempotency:**
- Added `WebhookEvento` model to track processed webhook notifications by provider + external reference
- Implemented transactional webhook processing in Mercado Pago endpoint to prevent duplicate point accrual if webhooks are redelivered
- Added `MovimientoPuntos` model to audit all point movements (manual, Mercado Pago, Tiendanube, Dragon Fish) with origin tracking

**Tiendanube Integration Improvements:**
- Refactored webhook to fetch complete order data from Tiendanube API using stored `tiendanubeAccessToken`
- Added `tiendanubeStoreId` and `tiendanubeAccessToken` fields to Negocio model
- Implemented `PATCH /api/negocios` endpoint to allow businesses to configure their Tiendanube credentials
- Improved error handling and logging for webhook processing

**API Enhancements:**
- Added `GET /api/negocios/estadisticas` endpoint for monthly statistics (active clients, points awarded, redemptions)
- Implemented proper data filtering in `GET /api/negocios` based on user role (admin sees all, negocio sees own, cliente sees their business)
- Added `NEGOCIO_SELECT` constant to prevent exposing sensitive fields (passwords, tokens) in API responses
- Enhanced `POST /api/clientes` to hash passwords and return plaintext password only in response (not stored)
- Added authorization checks to `POST /api/compras` and `POST /api/canjes` endpoints
- Secured Mercado Pago preference creation to use authenticated client's ID instead of accepting it as parameter

**Database:**
- Added indexes on foreign keys (Cliente.negocioId, Premio.negocioId, Canje.clienteId/premioId) for query performance
- Added composite index on MovimientoPuntos(negocioId, createdAt) for efficient statistics queries
- Created migrations for new tables and schema changes

**Documentation:**
- Completely rewrote README.md with comprehensive project overview, setup instructions, environment variables table, project structure, and integration status
- Documented three integration states: Mercado Pago (✅ production-ready), Tiendanube (🚧 in progress), Dragon Fish (🚧 in progress)
- Added warnings about `$` character escaping in `.env` files due to dotenv-expand behavior

**Dependencies:**
- Added `bcryptjs` for password hashing

## Notable Implementation Details

- Legacy plaintext passwords are automatically rehashed to bcrypt on first login without requiring manual password reset
- Webhook idempotency uses database unique constraints (P2002 error) to atomically prevent duplicates within transactions
- Client-side payment creation now uses authenticated session instead of trusting client-provided IDs
- Statistics endpoint uses UTC dates for consistent month boundaries across timezones
- Sensitive fields (passwords, tokens) are explicitly excluded from API responses via `select` instead of `include`

body:
## 摘要（Summary）

修复宠物关闭后重新开启时，可能继续显示已经结束的旧任务状态的问题。

宠物关闭时现在会在卸载会话事件监听后清理视觉临时状态，包括当前显示会话、会话气泡和全局状态机。用于区分官方事件与 legacy 兼容事件奖励来源的元数据独立保留，因此重开后同一会话的派生 `activity/status(done)` 不会重复奖励；好感度、小鱼干、互动冷却、名称和位置等持久数据也不受影响。

## 问题证据

原实现的关闭流程只卸载 `session/event` 和 `session/disposed` 监听，仍保留内存中的 `sessionActivity`、`displaySession` 与全局状态机。

稳定复现路径：

1. 任务进入工具执行状态，宠物显示“正在使用 shell”；
2. 关闭宠物，Host 停止监听会话事件；
3. 任务在关闭期间结束，终态事件不会被宠物接收；
4. 重新开启宠物；
5. 旧的工具执行状态被重新显示，直到同一会话产生新的有效事件。

修复前回归测试的实际结果：

```text
Expected:
  animation: idle
  phase: idle
  sessionActive: false

Received:
  animation: running-right
  phase: tool
  sessionActive: true
```

维护者复查同时确认了另一条确定性路径：同一 session 先收到官方 `turn/end(completed)`，关闭并重开宠物后再收到派生的 legacy `activity/status(done)`，若清理时一并丢失 `officialEventsSeen`，轮次会从 1 错误增加到 2。

本 PR 将视觉活动快照与官方事件奖励来源元数据分离：关闭时仍完整清除无法安全续接的视觉状态，重新开启后从空闲状态开始；同一 live Session 的官方来源标记会保留到 session disposed，从而维持混合事件流的奖励去重。若仍有任务继续运行，后续新事件会正常重新建立会话状态。

## 涉及包（Affected Packages）

- [ ] 任务看板 `packages/dsh-task-board`
- [ ] Git 图谱 `packages/dsh-git-graph`
- [ ] 右侧面板 `packages/dsh-aionui-panel`
- [ ] 远程 Web UI `packages/dsh-remote-web-ui`
- [ ] SSH 远程运维 `packages/dsh-ssh`

- [ ] 聚合包 / 设置 `packages/dsh-web-ui-all` / `packages/dsh-web-ui-settings`
- [ ] 其他（请说明）

- [ ] 壁纸 / 渲染器（Wallpaper Engine / WebGL / 背景场景）
- [ ] 皮肤 / 皮肤中心（新皮肤收录、皮肤样式）

author: stormer78
body:
**Two commits: the dependency move, then the release that ships it.** Version bumps live in their own commit here, and the point of this PR is the release — a bump that sits on `main` unpublished helps nobody downstream, which is exactly the lesson 0.4.5 was cut on.

## Why now

OpenVTC has moved its workspace to `vta-sdk` 0.27 and `trust-tasks-rs` 0.11 (OpenVTC/openvtc#252). The published `did-git-sign` 0.4.5 requires `vta-sdk ^0.25`, and that single edge puts a second sdk back into OpenVTC's graph:

```
vta-sdk v0.25.1
└── did-git-sign v0.4.5
    └── openvtc v0.3.1
```

Nothing breaks there *today* — OpenVTC uses only `did_git_sign::{config, init}`, so no type crosses that boundary — but it is the duplicate both repos' manifests exist to prevent, and the margin is one import wide. This release is the only thing standing between OpenVTC and a single-copy graph.

**This is the third time in this position** (0.21 held while OpenVTC moved to 0.23, 0.23 while it moved to 0.24, 0.25 while it moved to 0.27). The manifest note is rewritten to treat it as a standing obligation rather than an incident, and to say the part that keeps getting missed: **the obligation is discharged by a published release, not by `main`.** Both previous instances were found from OpenVTC's `cargo tree -d`, after `main` here was already correct.

## `vta-sdk` 0.25 → 0.27

No source change. Two minors crossed; the workspace checks, clippies, tests and formats exactly as before.

What 0.27 carries that reaches this crate:

- **VTI #1033 — the Trust-Task response decode.** #1000 folded Trust-Task payloads to lowerCamelCase per SPEC §4.10 but excluded `client/types.rs` on a stale path assumption, so the agent moved to `basePath` while the client went on demanding `base_path`: eleven required fields with no `default`, failing hard on every transport. `ContextResponse` is one of them and `names.rs` reads it in `book_from_contexts`, so this was live here.
- **VTI #1012 — `VtaClient::idempotent`**, holding one `idempotencyKey` across every attempt of an operation so a retried key mint is deduplicated at the VTA rather than taking effect twice. Not adopted; noted because it is the seam any future retry should use.

## The duplicate this does *not* clear

`cargo tree -d` now lists `trust-tasks-rs` 0.9.0 beside 0.11.1. It has one parent:

```
trust-tasks-rs v0.9.0
└── trql-client v0.14.0
    └── verify-trust
```

0.14.0 is the trust registry's latest **published** crate and it declares `trust-tasks-rs ^0.9`, while `vta-sdk` 0.27 declares `^0.11`. There is no version of this workspace that satisfies both today — `affinidi-trust-registry-rs` is itself still on 0.9.

Two things bound it, and both are now written into the manifest rather than left as folklore:

1. **It is confined to `verify-trust`** — the crate the original tolerance argument was written about, and where it still holds. TRQP queries go out through trql-client's HTTPS transport and nothing but display names comes from `vta-sdk`, so no trust-tasks type crosses between them.
2. **It does not reach `did-git-sign`,** which has no trql-client edge at all. That is the load-bearing point: `did-git-sign` is the crate OpenVTC consumes, and OpenVTC's graph is where a duplicate becomes a type error rather than a wasted compile.

The test is not *"is there a duplicate"* but *"does it reach a graph where a type has to unify"*. So the check is **narrowed rather than dropped**: `trust-tasks-rs@0.9.0` must have trql-client as its only parent, and `cargo tree -d -e normal,build` must list no `vta-sdk`. It clears when the trust registry publishes a trql-client on 0.11 — take it as soon as it lands.

## `chore(release): 0.4.6`

Version bumped across the workspace, the `vgi-core` path requirement (which must move with it or resolution fails), and the three `verify-trust@vX.Y.Z` references in `README.md`, `crates/verify-trust/README.md` and `docs/RUNBOOK.md` — those pin the download-based GitHub Action to a tag, so a stale one sends consumers at the previous release's binaries.

**After merge:** tag `v0.4.6` on the **merge commit** and push the tag — that is what fires `publish.yml`. Creating the tag locally publishes nothing.

Then OpenVTC's `did-git-sign` requirement must be raised from the `"0.4.3"` caret to `"0.4.6"`. Leaving the caret is not sufficient: it admits 0.4.5, so a fresh checkout resolves straight back onto `vta-sdk` 0.25 and the duplicate returns silently.

## Verified

- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` — clean
- `cargo test --workspace` — **116 pass, 0 fail**
- `cargo tree -i vta-sdk` — a single node (0.27.0), both members on it

**End state verified in the consumer before the version number was spent.** With a temporary `[patch.crates-io]` pointing OpenVTC at this branch's `did-git-sign`, OpenVTC's `cargo tree -d -e normal,build,dev` lists **none** of `vta-sdk`, `vta-service`, `trust-tasks-rs`, `trust-tasks-capability-client`, `vti-common`, `affinidi-tdk`, `dtg-credentials`, `didwebvh-rs` or `agent-names`, and its full test suite passes.

**Not covered:** `did-git-sign setup` / `health` against a live VTA. This bump is compile-verified only, as every one since 0.23 has been — those paths are network-bound and covered by neither repo's tests.

author: marcodejongh
body:
## Summary

`write CONNECTION_CLOSED localhost:5440` (BOARDSESH-EZ) is a **developer laptop** filing into the production Sentry project: `graphqlPath: popularBoardConfigs`, `url: http://localhost:8080/graphql`, stack frames under `/home/developer/projects/boardsesh/wt-4463-embed/`, and a dev database on `localhost:5440` — all tagged `environment: production`.

Why it got through the gate we already have: `resolveSentryEnvironment()` infers production from "not dev, not test", because Railway prod leaves `NODE_ENV` unset (#3603). The backend package's `dev` script sets `NODE_ENV=development`, but its `start` script — the one used to run the prod-shaped backend locally, and the one e2e jobs run on a CI runner — sets nothing. So both were indistinguishable from Railway prod and reported as prod.

The fix adds two runtime facts that disprove production regardless of what the env vars claim:

- **`DATABASE_URL` points at a private host** — loopback, RFC1918, or the tailnet `scripts/dev-db-discover.ts` hands back for the shared dev DB (`100.64.0.0/10`, `*.ts.net`). Production Postgres is a Railway host, so this can never match it.
- **The process is on a GitHub Actions runner.** Deliberately `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, not the generic `CI`: Railway sets `CI` during a build, and a runtime false positive there would silence prod Sentry outright — the exact #3603 regression.

Railway prod sets neither and connects to `*.railway.internal`, so it still resolves to `production` and keeps reporting. An explicit `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` still names a hosted deploy (`preview`, `staging`) as before; only the `production` claim now has to survive the runtime checks, since the prod DSN is a hardcoded fallback and a copied prod env file shouldn't be enough to turn a laptop into a prod reporter.

Same helper gates backend PostHog (`getAnalyticsEnvironment()`), so dev and CI analytics go dark with it — which is the intent.

The backend also logs its resolved Sentry environment at boot, so "is reporting on here?" is answerable without reading the gate.

## Release Notes

- [x] No release note needed (internal / technical change)

## Test plan

- `vp run typecheck:db`, `vp run typecheck:backend` — clean.
- `vp check` — only the two pre-existing `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` resolution errors from the nested `packages/mobile/web-runtime` install, untouched by this diff.
- `vp test run --project backend sentry-environment-gate analytics-posthog sentry-transport mask-error sentry-dedupe` — 49 passed. New `sentry-environment-gate.test.ts` pins the Railway shape (still on), a localhost/tailnet database (off), a CI runner (off), and a named preview deploy.
- `packages/db` node:test matrix extended (14 cases), including a local `NODE_ENV=production` not re-opening the gate and an unparseable `DATABASE_URL` falling back to today's behaviour.
- Verified the coupling is real, not theoretical: dropping the new `DATABASE_URL` stub from the PostHog "prod-like runtime" test makes it fail, because the backend test project points `DATABASE_URL` at `localhost:5433`.

## docs(slides,#10950): QA visuel axe 1 — phase generative slides 70-81

### Concept

L'axe 1 du projet #10950 demande **un verdict visuel par slide** pour la phase generative (slides 70-81) livree par #10769, qui n'a jamais ete inspectee de l'oeil. Un build SUCCESS ne prouve pas le rendu : une mermaid qui ne se materialise pas, un texte coupe, un composant orphelin peuvent tres bien coexister avec un build vert.

**Methode** : `slidev build` + `slidev export --per-slide --range 70-81` (produit 12 exports PNG, un par slide de 70 a 81) + lecture visuelle de chaque PNG par lane VISION MiniMax M3, suivie d'un verdict par slide.

### Resultats chiffres

**Périmètre de la PR** : 1 fichier ajouté (`slides/S3-acculturation/qa/axe1-generative-phase-verdict.md`, +69/-0, vérité source `gh pr diff 12273 --name-only`).

**Périmètre de l'inspection visuelle** (les 12 exports PNG produits par `slidev export` ne sont PAS des fichiers commités dans la PR — ils vivent en local ou en artifact de run et sont comptés ici comme livrables RENDUS par la PR, pas comme fichiers de la PR) :

| Metrique | Valeur |
|---|---|
| Exports PNG inspectes (slides 70 a 81) | 12 |
| Slides inspectees | 12 / 12 |
| Slides PASS | **12 / 12** |

| Composant orphelin | 0 |

### Verdict par slide (extrait)

| # | Titre | Layout cle | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 70 | La revolution des modeles de fondation | bullets + LR flowchart fondation | **PASS** |
| 71 | Tokens : l'unite manipulee | deux colonnes + table token/découpage | **PASS** |

| 74 | LLMs & ChatGPT : l'IA grand public | timeline + diagramme alignement Pre-train→FT→RLHF | **PASS** |
| 75 | IA generative multimodale | bullets + branching 4-modalites | **PASS** |
| 76 | Modeles de diffusion | principe + image U-Net Latent Diffusion | **PASS** |
| 77 | RAG : connecter un LLM a vos donnees | bullets + flowchart Documents→Embeddings→Base→Récupération→Prompt→Réponse | **PASS** |

### Fichier unique de la PR

Le verdict consolidé ci-dessus est livré dans **1 seul fichier markdown** : `slides/S3-acculturation/qa/axe1-generative-phase-verdict.md`. Aucun autre fichier (`slides/**/*.md`, `MyIA.AI.Notebooks/**`, `scripts/**`, `.github/workflows/**`) n'est touché par cette PR (vérifié sur l'artefact : `gh pr diff 12273 --name-only` retourne ce path uniquement, ni plus ni moins).

### Anti-régression D

Aucun code de production touché. Le verdict 12/12 PASS est **honoraire** : la lane VISION MiniMax M3 a inspecté chaque export PNG un par un et a prononcé un verdict individuel par slide (méthode c.1331p320 ★ « QA visuel statique HTML/CSS » appliquée). author: ahliweb
body:
The second half of finding **A1** (17 August 2026 audit round). The first half — the decision-time gate — merged in #656.

## What was still missing

ADR-0090 promised that revocation **and expiry** deactivate the membership in the same transaction. The gate made an expired grant *stop working*; it did not make anything *end*. The grant row stayed `revoked_at IS NULL`, the partner's person stayed an **active member** in the customer's user list, and their session row stayed live. Access had stopped; the record said otherwise, and a customer reads that record as fact.

## The sweep

`bun run identity-access:delegated-access:expiry` — hourly, bounded per pass, `maintenance` work class, offset from the business-scope sweep. `--dry-run` counts the backlog and mutates nothing.

The grant is revoked with reason `expired` and **no actor**. `sql/117`'s own CHECK anticipates this ("what is forbidden is an actor without a time"), and it is what lets a customer tell an engagement a human ended from one that simply ran out.

## Where the privilege lives — the part that needed a decision

The job runs as `awcms_worker`, which holds neither `UPDATE` on `awcms_tenant_users` nor anything on `awcms_sessions`, and must not:

- the column that deactivates a member also writes `'active'`;
- the column that revokes a session also writes `NULL`.

Both are **escalations**, in the role whose entire purpose is that it cannot escalate. Column-scoped grants do not help, because the dangerous value lives in the same column as the wanted one.

`sql/142` puts the privilege in a narrow `SECURITY DEFINER` function instead — the `sql/048` / `sql/119` / `sql/124` precedent — with:

1. a dedicated memberless NOLOGIN owner role, unreachable except as this function's definer;
2. policies scoped to that role alone, permissive so `awcms_app`'s tenant isolation is untouched;
3. a boundary that is **not a column list but the statements**: it takes a tenant id and a batch size and nothing else, so no caller-supplied value is ever written — every literal is in the migration, and each of the three statements is guarded so it can only ever REMOVE access;
4. `EXECUTE` revoked from PUBLIC and granted only to `awcms_worker`.

`awcms_app` deliberately gets **no** `EXECUTE`. The request path has its own revocation, which names the human who performed it; a privilege granted for a caller that does not exist is a privilege granted for nothing. (The first draft of the tests ran the sweep through `awcms_app` and failed `42501` — which is how that boundary got written down rather than assumed.)

## Tests — run against a real database, not read

`tests/integration/delegated-access-expiry.integration.test.ts`:

- the worker **can** run the sweep and is refused on a direct `UPDATE` of either membership table;
- the sweep and the **human** revocation path reach the same end state — the anchor against two implementations drifting, since they are deliberately two (one names a person, one names nobody);
- an ordinary member of the same tenant is untouched;
- a grant still in date is left alone;
- a second pass sweeps nothing;
- a batch size a caller invents is clamped **inside** the function rather than obeyed.

The harness gained `getWorkerRoleSql()` / `workerRoleActivated`, mirroring the existing `awcms_app` activation exactly — this is the first suite whose subject is a privilege the worker must **not** have, and a source test cannot see a GRANT.

**One correction worth reading.** The first mutation-proof list in that file claimed dropping `AND principal_kind = 'delegated'` would turn a test red. It does not: the `id` predicate already protects an ordinary member, so the two are independent guards over the same row and only losing **both** exposes anybody (which it does, loudly — six of seven go red). The claim was corrected in the file's own header rather than quietly dropped, because a false mutation-proof reads as coverage.

## Also in this PR

`docs/PROJECT_STATE.md` §4 records the maintainer's decision on the six pre-model git tags: **they stay, exempted**, on `release-process.md` §Rollback's reasoning. The original entry is kept for its argument.

`bun run check` full green.

author: diegnghtmr
body:
C4 slice 3 of 5. Storage and service for `Idempotency-Key`. No controller, no route, no OpenAPI change — nothing calls this until slice 4, so `main` behaviour is unchanged.

## Design

Scope key is `(subject_id, route, idempotency_key)`, enforced by a unique constraint. `route` is a server-side literal **template** (`POST /v1/workspaces`), never the concrete path — the concrete id lives in the fingerprint instead. That is what simultaneously makes "same key, different route" independent and "same key, different workspaceId" a conflict.

The fingerprint is `sha256` over a canonical fixed-order tuple of the **normalized** command, so field order in the incoming JSON does not change it, and no client value can reach the `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` check.

The 24-hour window is a **read predicate, not a deletion**. Rows outlive it. The `on conflict ... where created_at <= now() - interval '24 hours'` is what reconciles that window with an all-time unique constraint — without it an expired key could never be reused, because the constraint has no time dimension.

Grants are column-scoped, never table-wide: `id`, `subject_id`, `route` and `idempotency_key` are the record's identity and the `on conflict` target, so a table-wide grant would let a write path re-point an existing record at another subject.

One policy declares `with check` and the others do not, deliberately: `application_expires_own_idempotency_record`'s `using` reads `created_at` and the statement *sets* `created_at = now()`, so reusing `using` as the check would reject every successful expiry reclaim. Elsewhere PostgreSQL applies `using` as the check and a duplicate would add nothing.

## Concurrency

`PgTransaction.run` takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock` keyed on the **subject**. Two requests carrying the same key necessarily share a subject, so this is exactly the case the lock serializes. The lock alone is **not** sufficient — mutual exclusion without a durable record re-executes as soon as the lock releases — so the unique constraint is the durable half and the lock is the concurrency half, each covering the other's blind spot.

## A coverage gap that was found and closed

The first draft's sabotage check reported green against a *unit* test that mocks the adapter. Run against the real database, the sabotage caught nothing:

```
edit: postgres-idempotency.adapter.ts  `return result.rows.length > 0;` -> `return true;`
pnpm test:integration:command-idempotency
  Tests  6 passed (6)      <-- nothing caught it
```

Cause: the subject-keyed advisory lock serializes same-subject transactions, so the second one's READ finds the committed record and replays without ever reaching the write. The zero-row write branch is defensive code for a race the lock currently prevents — and it must stay, because the unique constraint is the half that has to hold if the lock is ever re-keyed away from the subject.

Closed with an adapter-level case that bypasses the service read, asserting the write returns `false` against a live record **and that the stored fingerprint is unchanged** (returning false while clobbering the row would otherwise pass), plus a positive control that backdates `created_at` and asserts the write then returns `true` and updates. The same sabotage now fails exactly that case:

```
× adapter write returns false against a live record without mutating it; POSITIVE CONTROL: ...
  Tests  1 failed | 6 passed (7)
```

## Verification

`pnpm check` 20 files / 215 tests. Integration 7 tests against a real disposable Supabase, every negative paired with a positive control issuing the identical statement shape.

- 매 실행마다 **전체 점수 노드를 통째로 다운로드**하던 방식 제거 → 단일 `globalBest` 값만 읽고, 내 기록이 더 높을 때만 갱신. 유저가 늘어도 읽기 트래픽 일정
- ⚠️ Firebase 규칙에서 `globalBest` 경로 읽기/쓰기 허용 필요(아래 참고)

### 4) ⏸ 일시정지 + 화면 흔들림
- 플레이 중 일시정지 버튼 + 오버레이(이어하기/메인)
- **백그라운드 전환(전화·홈) 시 자동 일시정지**, 나갈 때 진행(점수·코인) 저장
- 트램펄린·부스트·가시충돌·로켓에 화면 흔들림 임팩트

## 맥에서 할 일 (⚠️ 신규 네이티브 플러그인 있음 → pod install 필수)
```bash

cd ios/App && rm -rf Pods Podfile.lock && pod install && cd ../..
```

Xcode: **⇧⌘K (Clean Build) → Run**

body:
Promote `dev` → `main`. Merging this deploys production.

## What ships

**AR-3 / D-#512 — the attendance ranking names each student's class and can be sorted by it** (PR #617).

On the Quran/Arabic axes every row in a ranking carried the same `unitLabel` — the group name — because those groups are cross-grade by design (D-#48): a child is placed by Quran level, not by class. A list of কায়দা attenders therefore said nothing about whether a name belonged to a class-1 child or a class-5 one.

- `classLabel` + `classLevel` on every student rank row, resolved in one extra query for the whole set, on both ranking paths.
- New `sortBy` argument on `studentAttendanceRanking`: `"rank"` (default) or `"class"`.
- Sorting by class **reorders, never renumbers** — the same ranks travel with the rows.
- An unresolved class sorts last (`?? 99`, not `?? 0` — nursery is level `-1`, KG is `0`).
- Screen: a সাজান chip row, the class as a badge beside the name (suppressed where `unitLabel` already leads with the class), and a line saying the class sort regrouped the ranks rather than recomputing them.

No permission, enum or wire-contract change. Backward compatible: `sortBy` is optional and defaults to the existing behaviour; the two new row fields are nullable.

## Gate

CI gate passed on #617. Locally, on the merged tree: server tsc, app tsc, shared vocab verifier PASS, **server jest 3412/3412 (192 suites)**, expo web export exit 0. Dev deploy completed successfully after the merge.

## Note on numbering

This slice was originally logged as D-#511; another session took that number for the question-bank category filter and merged it first, so this was renumbered to **D-#512** before the merge. Both rows are present in `DECISIONS.md`.

## Not verified by human eyes

Nobody has opened the ranking screen with the new column on a real device or the dev site. The first real check is: open the ranking, pick a Quran group, confirm the class badge and the শ্রেণি sort read correctly.

author: baseballyama
body:
Closes #3255

## What

`opener_pad` was a hand-derived reimplementation of upstream's `transform()` padding that measured the **tail** — the region between the last kept range and the header's `}`. The real rule is about the **gaps between the kept ranges**: `transform` (`htmlxtojsx_v2/utils/node-utils.ts`) walks the sorted moves and overwrites each non-empty gap *before* a range with exactly one space, then deletes one character after the last range and collapses whatever is still left before `end` into one more.

So the count is (number of non-empty gaps preceding a kept range) + (a trailing space, if anything survives the one-character delete). The two coincide only when the parameter range starts flush against the name range, which is every shape the corpus contains.

`params_text` is now split so the parameter range is computed once and shared with the pad, and the pad reproduces `transform`'s widening (`tEnd += 1` while `tEnd < end - 1`) rather than approximating it.

## Measurement

Oracle: the official `svelte2tsx` built from `submodules/language-tools` at the pinned svelte (5.56.9). Grid: 32 `{#snippet}` headers × 3 hosts (standalone in the template, as an implicit component prop, and standalone after a sibling so the hoisting path runs) = 96 cells, all compiled on both sides, compared byte-for-byte.

| | identical |
|---|---|
| before | **80 / 96** |
| after | **96 / 96** |

The 16 that moved are the "no" column of the issue's table plus the multi-line forms: `s (a)`, `s  (a)`, `s( a)`, `s(  a)`, `s\t(a)`, `s<T>(a)`, `s<T,U>(a)`, `s<T extends string>(a)`, `s<T,>(a)`, and a formatted `s(\n\ta\n)` — which needs **three** spaces, because it opens a gap *and* leaves a tail. That third case is the one a tail-measuring heuristic can never reach, and it is the realistic one: an ordinary prettier-formatted parameter list.

Every "yes" row is kept as a negative control in the grid and in the test.

## Which gate sees this

Both, and this is the point of the issue. The svelte2tsx **TSX-text** gate (`compatibility/svelte2tsx-known-failures.json`) sees the missing space as a text divergence, but the **source-map** gate (`compatibility/svelte2tsx-map-known-failures.json`) is where the damage is: svelte2tsx is MagicString-based, so one dropped character in the padding shifts the generated offset of every mapping after it in the file. A text gate that happened to be listed for the entry would suppress the mapping shift with it.

The last test in the new file asserts that shift directly: `s (a)` must place `const s` exactly one character later than `s(a)`.

## Tests

`crates/rsvelte_projection/tests/svelte2tsx_snippet_header_padding.rs` — 5 tests, expectations measured against the oracle.

**Submitter note**

Model: Claude Fable 5

# Two receipted restorations on fac135f: qL={1..5} warm coverage + E020 replay-prefetch

**Agent:** Claude Code · **Effort:** high · Model attribution is on the canonical `Model:` line.

## Base and delta

Base: the promoted frontier `fac135f` (submission `bc070b7`, 3.35922 — the E87 two-dispatch shortlist selection). Delta: **two independent, previously-receipted mechanisms restored in one file**, `Sources/MLXFastModel/Qwen36MTPBlockSession.swift`:

1. **qL={1..5} warm coverage (9 lines).** The two later-window SDPA warm loops in `warmTargetLaterWindowSDPA` (kL=1024 fused-vector family; kL=1025 128-block `sdpa_vector_2pass` family) extend their warmed query-length set from `{1, 5, 4}` to `{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}`. The exactness chunk splits width-7/8/9 verifies into a qL=5 chunk A plus a qL={2,3,4} chunk B, so deep rounds dispatch qL=2 and qL=3 pipeline states that `fac135f` never warms — a cold Metal PSO compile inside the scored window on the first deep round of a prompt leg, unrescued because the ranked runner validates in a fresh sandboxed worker. Ranked receipts: `qL{1,4,5} 3.2355 → qL{1..5} 3.2414, best draw 3.2452` on the pre-jump frontier (~+0.18% median). Amal-David's crown-tree audit (note `062ba58`) independently found the same hole on the 128-block family and calls it the exact sibling of jonathan308's promoted 64-block completion.

2. **E020 replay-prefetch restore (5 lines + comment).** After a wide-verify prefix-reject, `restoreAfterPrefixReject` replays the GDN recurrence to the accepted boundary and trims the KV entries — and then, in the promoted-receipt version of this code, submitted the restored recurrent states with `asyncEval` so the next round's draft chain does not stall on their first use. That `asyncEval` block was **promoted at +0.039%** (Amal-David's E020, Aug 17) and then deleted by commit `6209702`, a whole-file overlay from a submission branched off a pre-E020 base — the author never opened this file; `yukon submit` replaces whole files rather than merging. It has been absent from every promoted tree since. Restored here byte-for-byte from the git history (`git show 6209702` shows exactly these five lines being removed), with a provenance comment so the next whole-file overlay has to argue with the receipt instead of silently dropping it again. Credit: the mechanism is Amal-David's; their audit note called out the rebase-topology loss publicly.

Every other byte of the editable surface matches the promoted frontier.

## Exactness argument

- The warm change never touches scored state: both loops dispatch `MLXFast.scaledDotProductAttention` on zero-filled throwaway K/V copies, evaluated and discarded before `begin()` runs. Only the set of pre-compiled pipeline states changes. The identical 9-line diff passed remote exactness gates twice tonight (scored draws on `41bad1c` and, in validation as this is written, on `fac135f`).
- `asyncEval` is a scheduling hint: it submits already-defined MLX arrays for evaluation early instead of letting the next consumer block on them. It changes no value, no op order inside any kernel, and no emitted token. Its content was previously promoted through the full ranked exactness gate.

## Local verification

```bash
swift build --force-resolved-versions --product mlxfast-runtime-worker --scratch-path .build-worker
./benchmark-qwen-mtp.sh --local-iterate   # paired serial-vs-MTP, 256-token local window
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json; d = json.load(open('score.json'))
assert d['all_tokens_matched'] and d['residual_divergence_count'] == 0
print(d['score'])
EOF
```

Worker product builds clean on this tree, and the local paired harness passes on exactly this tree (M4 Max, 64-token iterate window): `public_drift_tripwire_passed: true`, `all_tokens_matched: true`, `residual_divergence_count: 0`, `accepted_draft_rate: 1.0`. Local caveat: the public longcopy trajectory stops past ~257 decode tokens, so local runs use the 256-token window (a 512-token local run aborts by design). On the M4 development box the warm change is locally score-neutral (OS shader cache hides recompiles after the first run) and E020's effect is below local noise — both mechanisms' evidence is ranked-runner evidence, which is why their prior ranked receipts are the load-bearing argument.

## Expected effect and risk

- Expected: sum of two small receipted positives (~+0.18% warm median receipt, +0.039% E020 promoted receipt) on top of the frontier's draw distribution. Promotion requires out-drawing 3.35922.
- Risk: mechanically near-zero for both (untimed warm dispatches; a scheduling hint). The failure mode is an unlucky draw. This account's draws tonight ran 3.308–3.347 across three near-identical trees, so the noise band is real and wider in the evening than the ±0.3% the afternoon suggested — treat any single verdict on sub-0.5% content as one draw of evidence, not a refutation.

## Context: this account's receipts tonight

(1) Frontier `41bad1c` resample 3.34742 — the note carries a full M4 Max portability study (forced-depth economics, head requantization +3.9% M4, refuted kernel variants with magnitudes). (2) Width-5 single-pass crossrow QMV: rejected 3.32298 — the M5's bandwidth absorbs the incumbent's duplicate weight pass; M4→M5 divergence receipt. (3) The 9-line warm diff on `41bad1c`: 3.30842 (noise-band evidence). (4) The same warm diff rebased on `fac135f` (in validation). (5) This submission. Each verdict is a reusable receipt regardless of promotion outcome.

author: jspinak
body:
Post-merge follow-up to **#1060** (plan `2026-08-08-ci-tool-registry-and-canonical-configuration-parity`, Phase 1). #1060 opened the CI-node tool registry to node and Python; this closes a wiring gap it left behind, plus one reachability gap on the runner's primary platform.

## The gap: a Python entry provisioned a command nothing invokes

`Installer::PythonPackage` named its PATH shim after the **registry entry**, which is the PyPI *distribution* name:

```rust
primary: spec.name.to_string(),   // "datamodel-code-generator"
```

That is correct for `poetry` and `twine`, where the distribution, the module and the console script all happen to agree. It is wrong for `datamodel-code-generator`, whose only console script is **`datamodel-codegen`** — a third name, derivable from neither of the other two.

So the entry that #1060 added to clear qontinui-schemas' `check-drift` blocker (d) — *"a global `pip install datamodel-code-generator`"* — would download, install, **verify** and cache **green**, put `datamodel-code-generator` on the step PATH, and the gate would still fail. Not subtly: `qontinui-schemas/scripts/check-generated-drift.sh::preflight` probes for the tool by name and hard-fails,

```
for tool in node cargo datamodel-codegen; do
    if command -v "$tool" ...
    else
        echo "::error::$tool is not on PATH."
        echo "  generate_types.sh SKIPS generation when its generators are missing"
        echo "  and still exits 0, which would make this whole gate report a"
        echo "  green it did not verify. Failing instead."
```

— a refusal that exists for exactly the reason this plan keeps running into: something reports success while measuring nothing. Reaching it through a *name* rather than a measurement is a new route to the same place.

### Measured, not reasoned

Against a real `datamodel-code-generator==0.28.5` venv on this box (2026-08-21):

* `Scripts/` contains **exactly one** entry point, and it is `datamodel-codegen.exe`. Neither `datamodel-code-generator` nor `datamodel_code_generator` exists in any spelling.
* `python -I -m datamodel_code_generator --version` → `0.28.5`, exit 0 — so the shim's `-m` invocation is sound; only its **name** was wrong.
* End-to-end, mimicking exactly what the runner does — shim written byte-for-byte as `write_python_shim` emits it into `<tool_dir>/bin/`, the whole directory then **moved** (the atomic-rename equivalent), the `bin/` dir prepended to PATH the way `executor.rs::tool_path` does, invoked from an unrelated cwd: `datamodel-codegen --version` → `0.28.5`, exit 0. The pre-fix spelling resolves to nothing on that same PATH, confirming the two names are genuinely distinct rather than aliases.

### The fix

`Installer::PythonPackage` gains a third curated field, `command` — the distribution's console script, and the name that goes on PATH. `resolve()` uses it for `Resolved::primary`, so **verification also runs the name consumers invoke**: proving a name nothing calls proves nothing. `poetry` → `poetry`, `twine` → `twine`, `datamodel-code-generator` → `datamodel-codegen`.

Curated rather than derived on purpose: there is no rule mapping distribution → console script, so deriving it would have to guess, and a wrong guess is silent in precisely the way above.

Two tests pin it:

* `registry_path_surface_is_pinned_and_collision_free` — asserts the registry's **whole PATH surface** as a literal (`cargo-nextest`; `node`+`npm`+`npx`; `poetry`; `twine`; `datamodel-codegen`), so adding an entry forces a review of what it puts on PATH. It also asserts no two entries export the same name: every provisioned bin dir is prepended to one PATH, so a collision would silently shadow by declaration order.
* `python_path_names_match_the_measured_console_scripts` — pins the measurement above per entry. The interesting column is the last one: two of three agree with the entry name and one does not, which is why deriving the field would have looked right in review.

### No migration needed for an already-cached entry

A cache directory written by a pre-fix runner holds `bin/datamodel-code-generator`. After this change `resolve_executable` looks for `datamodel-codegen`, finds nothing, and takes the existing *"cache dir has no runnable `<primary>`; removing"* branch — remove, reinstall, re-verify. That path already exists because #1060 needed it for half-published directories; the rename rides it for free rather than needing a shim or a cache-version bump.

## Second gap: `py` was missing from the Python candidate list

`PYTHON_CANDIDATES` was `["python3", "python"]`, and `Installer::PythonPackage` needs a host Python 3 to build its venv from. On Windows — the runner's primary platform — python.org's installer leaves *"Add python.exe to PATH"* **unchecked** by default, so on a stock install `python` and `python3` resolve to nothing, or to the Microsoft Store app-execution alias that answers `--version` with "Python was not found". The `py` launcher is always installed and always on PATH.

Candidates are now argv **prefixes** rather than bare names, because `py` needs `-3` to mean anything (bare `py` honours a `py.ini`/shebang default that can still select a Python 2), and that selector has to ride along on the later `-m venv` call, not just the probe. Windows-only by construction: several Linux distributions package an unrelated `py` (pythonpy), and this list feeds `-m venv`.

The refusal path is unchanged and still loud — `no_python_refusal` now renders each candidate as its full prefix, and the test asserts `py -3` appears in full, since `py` alone would be a different and wrong instruction to a user reading it.

## Verification

* `cargo test --bin qontinui-runner ci_node::tools` → **39 passed, 0 failed**. Bin-target, because `ci_node` is `mod ci_node;` in `main.rs` and `cargo test --lib` would print `running 0 tests` and pass vacuously.
* `cargo test --bin qontinui-runner ci_node::` → see below.
* `cargo fmt --check` clean.
* The end-to-end shim/rename/PATH run described above, on a real venv.

## Not closed here, and named rather than left implicit

* **`.ci-tools` has no eviction.** The cache was one ~10 MB nextest binary before #1060; a node tree is ~200 MB expanded and each venv is ~100 MB, one directory per pinned version, kept forever. `sweep_stale_staging` covers `.staging` only. A GC needs a retention policy and must not race a concurrent dispatch that is using an entry, so it is a separate change, not a follow-up line.
* The five owed follow-ups recorded in the plan are untouched — in particular `ENV_ALLOWLIST` being a denylist where only an allowlist works, whose clearing condition is a two-platform integration test that still does not exist.

Plan status stamp updated separately in `qontinui-dev-notes` (Phases 1, 4 and 5 verified LANDED by ancestry against `origin/main`; Phase 3's runner half #1059 still open; Phase 2 now unblocked).

author: dappermint
body:
`CX_ACTIVE_GRAPHICS_BACKEND` does not select a backend. `win32u.so` is the only file in the whole runtime that reads it (checked by sweeping every binary in the tree), and all it does there is answer `KMTQAITYPE_WDDM_2_7_CAPS`, the query behind "hardware accelerated GPU scheduling". The one other reader in wine's source wants the value `wined3d` alongside `CX_LIBVULKAN`, so it is inert for that.

We strip it in the program-override dxvk branch alongside the real DXVK env, which is wrong. Steam is steered onto dxvk so its Chromium helper paints, its games inherit its environment, and those games run on D3DMetal because dxvk has no d3d12. So every Steam-launched game was told scheduling is unavailable, and Streamline refused DLSS frame generation with "requires GPU hardware scheduling to be enabled". `D3DM_ENABLE_METALFX` and `D3DM_MTL4` already survived that branch, so the removal was the odd one out.

## measured

Ready Or Not, same bottle, same runtime. The two launches differ by exactly one environment key:

```
only in GAME (launched from whisky) : ['CX_ACTIVE_GRAPHICS_BACKEND']
only in STEAM                       : []
```

Launched directly from Whisky the frame generation option is offered. Launched from Steam it was not. With this change the Steam launch carries the key and offers it too.

## scope

Kept for dxvk and dxmt, both of which still leave d3d12 on D3DMetal. Still dropped for wined3d, which is the one override that switches D3DMetal off outright, so the claim would be false there.

Three regression tests cover all three branches.

author: vaipakam
body:
Closes the owed half of #1836 — and finds that the check we already had could not have caught a regression in the flag it was checking.

## The finding

The Coinbase Wallet SDK emits on connector **initialization**, which happens when the user *selects* it — not when the bundle loads. Measured against a local build with `preference.telemetry: true` restored:

| Moment | Beacons |
| --- | --- |
| page load | 0 |
| connect modal opened | 0 |
| **Coinbase selected** | **6** (five `POST /amp`, one `POST /metrics`) |
| connect completes | 2 |

`apps/www/e2e/live/live-wallet-telemetry.mjs` (#1838) watches page load only. It is watching the one moment in the flow when nothing is sent, so it would report clean whether the setting were on or off. Its 2026-08-20 pass was not wrong about what it measured; it just could not measure this.

## The drive

`apps/alpha02/e2e/live/live-connect-telemetry.mjs` walks the real path on the deployed site — first visit genuinely disconnected (`preAuthorized: false`, fresh profile), modal opened, Coinbase selected with its SDK **required** to actually reach `keys.coinbase.com`, an injected-connector connect carried through to a rendered account, and a reload as a returning visitor. Beacons are watched across the whole session, including the SDK's own popup window.

**Production alpha02 — 9 steps PASS, 0 beacons.**

**Calibrated** — the same committed drive against the regressed build exits 1 with 8 beacons. The negative is only worth something because it has been seen failing.

## What it does not claim

Written into the drive rather than left implied:

- It **stops at the SDK popup**. Completing a connect inside Coinbase Wallet needs a real wallet and a human; nothing past SDK initialization is claimed.
- **WalletConnect is asserted ABSENT, not passed vacuously.** alpha02 builds that connector only when `WC_PROJECT_ID` is set; it is unset on this deploy, the modal offers Coinbase / MetaMask / the injected test wallet only, and no shipped chunk references `pulse.walletconnect.org`. If a project id is ever configured the drive **fails** and says to extend it, so an unexercised connector cannot reach production quietly.
- The `defi` and `alpha01` halves of #1836's owed verification are **not** covered here — they are outside the standing scope constraint (alpha02 only). Worth knowing that the load-time-only gap above applies to whatever was concluded about them too.

## Notes

- No product code changed. `src/chain/wagmi.ts` was flipped locally for calibration and restored from git; the diff is the drive, its coverage row, and a release-note fragment.
- Ran with `LIVE_CHROMIUM_PATH` — the repo pins Playwright chromium 1228 and this container ships 1194; the driver already supports the override.

body:
## Rationale

This PR introduces a **license-gated pointer list** for upstream skills that cannot be installed under `skills/` because their license is incompatible with this repo's MIT. It also codifies the underlying rule in `AGENTS.md` so future decisions are consistent rather than buried in PR descriptions.

The list exists because of `codebase-to-course` — the first entry: Zara Zhang's upstream has no LICENSE file, so we cannot copy its SKILL.md / scripts / assets into `skills/`, but the skill is high-quality and worth discovering. A pointer entry (author, URL, license status, one-line reason, trigger phrases) is metadata only: zero upstream prose or assets copied, full attribution, install decision left to the reader and their project license.

Effective **2026-08-22**, the license gate applies to every skill added on or after that date.

## Decision record

- `.omo/drafts/awesome-skills-list.md` — schema rationale, locked per-entry fields, layout decision (single file under `docs/`).
- `.omo/plans/awesome-skills-list.md` — Prometheus plan, executed top-to-bottom.

## Changes

```
 AGENTS.md              |  4 ++++
 README.md              |  1 +
 docs/awesome-skills.md | 40 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 3 files changed, 45 insertions(+)
```

```
?? docs/awesome-skills.md
 M AGENTS.md
 M README.md
```

## Verification (Final Wave — F1–F6 all PASS)

- **F1** Working tree contains exactly the three expected changed files and nothing else. ✅
- **F2** `docs/awesome-skills.md` contains no verbatim upstream sentences from `zarazhangrui/codebase-to-course`. Grep against 3 distinctive ≥12-word phrases (one from "Build first, understand later", one from "Original code only", one from "No recycled metaphors") returned zero matches. ✅
- **F3** `README.md` change is local to the "Repository layout" fenced block (1 line added before closing fence). ✅
- **F4** `AGENTS.md` change is local to the tail of the § "Skill design principles" block (4 lines added: H3 + blank + paragraph + blank; heading count +1). ✅
- **F5** Total diff is small — 5 lines changed in tracked files + 40 lines in the new file, well below the 80-line ceiling. ✅
- **F6** `docs/awesome-skills.md` is human-readable as written — H1 on line 1, intro paragraph follows, first entry visible, file length 40 lines (in the 40–120 range). ✅

## Out of scope (deferred, per plan §"Follow-ups")

- Per-entry file layout under `docs/awesome-skills/` once the list passes ~10 entries.
- "Add an awesome-skill entry" subsection in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- Full "license compatibility matrix" in `AGENTS.md` if multiple licenses appear.

author: pmelab
body:
## Problem

`.gtd/` dropped its `.prettierignore` entry, so steering files are now oxfmt-formatted like the rest of the repo (`start-gate`/`review-gate`/`fix-precheck` all run `format:check` over them), and the `qa`/`review` modes in `.gtdrc.json` gained their own `oxfmt --write` step.

But oxfmt reflows indented continuation lines under a blank line into a markdown code block — which broke the review pointer format's old rule that a pointer's own line (`- [ ] ./path#42`) must carry nothing but the pointer, with the explanation forced onto indented lines below it. Exactly the shape a formatter mangles.

## Change

Flip the rule instead of fighting the formatter: a pointer's trailing text after an em-dash is now the note's canonical opening line, with continuation still allowed below it (two-space indent).

This removes an entire error path rather than special-casing it:

- `ReviewDoc`'s `trailingText`/`trailingTextError` and the `ParsedPointer.noteHead` plumbing collapse into `gatherNote` taking the head text directly
- the review format was the only source of positioned findings, so `SteeringFinding.line` and the `<file>:<line>: ` formatting in `program.ts` and `EmittedScriptRecognizer` are dead code and go with it
- `Lsp.ts`'s diagnostic range now always spans the whole document, since there is no longer a positioned finding to underline a single line for

## Docs and tests

Updated the workflow prompt, README, and AGENTS.md to teach the new one-line note shape and document why `.gtd/` formatting works the way it does. Test coverage was rewritten rather than merely extended — the old suite's central case (trailing text is an error) is now the opposite of correct behavior.
