author: semnil
body:
## 何を消したか

`_locales` の 4 キーはどこからも読まれていない。`msg('...')` / `data-i18n` / `__MSG_...__` のいずれにも現れず、ja / en の両方に残っていた。

| キー | ja | 死んだ経緯 |
|---|---|---|
| `labelMomentary` | Momentary | `bc0b072 style: popup から Momentary / Short-term カードを削除` |
| `labelShortTerm` | Short-term | 同上 |
| `openOnStream` | 配信または動画を再生中に使用してください | 読み手なし |
| `colVolume` | Volume | 読み手なし |

消した文言そのものもツリー全体で grep した。`Momentary` / `Short-term` は `README.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `PRIVACY_POLICY*.md` に残るが、いずれも計測パイプラインの説明で UI ラベルではない (page-bridge は今も両方を算出して post している)。

## 再発しない形

当初は JavaScript を走査してキーの読み手を数えていたが、レビューで 6 ラウンドにわたり抜けが出た (コメント → 文字列・テンプレート・正規表現 → 修飾付き呼び出し・`of`・三項演算子・ローカルの `msg`)。手書きの字句解析が言語に追いつく見込みは無いので、**走査をやめて実行で確かめる**形に変えた。

**出荷事故になる 2 つは実行で確かめる**

- 両ページの harness の `msg` は、ロケールが宣言していないキーを拒否する。テストが実行する経路であれば、静的走査では名指しできない書き方 (三項・実行時組み立て・スコープを変えた呼び出し) でも落ちる
- popup と options を起動し、**それぞれの markup が `data-i18n` を付けた全要素**がロケール文言を持って出てくることを検査する。`applyI18n` がキーを加工する改変はここで落ちる (options.js にとっては初の実挙動テスト)

**静的側は範囲を区切って、区切りの外を成功にしない**

- **ページ側を抽出器が読める形に制限する**: `popup.html` / `options.html` に raw text 要素 (`textarea` / `iframe` / `xmp` / `noembed` / `noframes` / `noscript` / `plaintext`)・HTML コメント・`<template>` が現れないこと、`script` / `style` / `title` が素の `>` で閉じられていること、`data-i18n` の全出現が小文字・引用符付きであることを検査する。パーサーの状態を追いかけるのをやめ、使ってよい形の側を有限に固定した (コメントは `--!>` でも閉じ、template の中身は `querySelectorAll` が辿らない — どちらもページが使っていない)
- 属性はタグをトークナイザと同じ順で 1 つずつ読む (名前 → 値。値の中はテキストとして扱い、再解釈しない)。名前は大小文字を区別せず、**重複した名前は先頭だけ**採る (ブラウザが後続を捨てるのに合わせる)。区切りの判定は **ASCII 空白のみ** (JavaScript の `\s` は無破断空白まで含み、ブラウザはそれをテキストとして読む)
- raw text は閉じタグまで除去し、**ブラウザが受け付ける閉じタグを持たない開始タグ**が残っていればそこから先を切り捨てる (`<plaintext>` も、`</title\u00a0>` のように閉じられなかった `<title>` も同じ扱いになる)
- そのうえで **ファイル中の `data-i18n` の出現回数と抽出できた数の一致**を検査する。引用符なしの属性、raw text 内へ移された属性、別属性の値に書かれた疑似属性はここで落ちる
- 両ページについて **キーとそれを載せた要素** (タグ名・`id`・`class` トークンの配列) の対応をスナップショットとして固定する。`class` は 1 本の文字列へ潰さずトークンのまま比較する (`settings-error hidden` と `settings-error.hidden` は別物で、後者では `.settings-error.hidden` が一致しない)。属性の削除・別要素への移動・キー変更はここで落ちる。あわせて **`data-i18n` を載せた要素がテキストしか持たない**ことを検査する — `applyI18n` は `textContent` を代入するので、子要素を持つ要素にキーが載ると、ローカライズした時点でその中身が消える
- 走査対象のファイルは `pack.py --list` から採る (パッケージが読み込めるものは全て対象)
- 死んだ翻訳の検出だけは**意図的に過剰近似**する: 引用符付きで言及されていれば「生きている」と数える。「どこからも言及されないキー」を見つけるのが目的で、言及が呼び出しかどうかは実行側が答える

## ミューテーション

`work/mutate-i18n.mjs` で 26 形 — いずれも落ちる。変異前のコピーが緑であることを先に確認している。

- 属性そのもの 6 形: 削除 / 引用符なし / 大文字 `DATA-I18N` / 混在表記 / 同一タグへの重複 / 別属性値の疑似属性
- ブラウザと読みが分かれる markup 9 形: `<textarea>` `<iframe>` `<plaintext>` `<template>` `<!-- -->` `<!-- --!>` へ移動 / `</title >` / `</title\u00a0>` / `<title>` の閉じ忘れ
- **キーはそのままで載せる要素だけを変える 5 形**: 親の `div.section` へ移動 / 同じタグの兄弟 (`.setting-label` ↔ `.setting-desc`) へ移動 / アイコンを抱えた `<button>` へ移動 / 移動元の `<span>` から削除 / `class` の 2 トークンを 1 トークンへ結合。先頭 2 つは `73bbdac` (キー列だけのスナップショット) で生き残り、最後の 1 つは `663b48b` (`class` を `.` で連結していたスナップショット) で生き残ったもの
- 実行側 4 形: popup・options の `applyI18n` 加工 (キーの改変 / 別属性の読み出し / 別プロパティへの書き込み)、未宣言キーの読み出し
- ロケール 2 形: 未参照キー追加 / 片ロケールのみ

過剰近似の側で落ちないものも記録する: 文字列リテラルを残したまま呼び出しだけを消す改変 (ローカル `msg` で隠す、`of / /…/` に置き換える) は、キーが宣言されたまま言及も残るため検出しない。害は「死んだ翻訳が残る」ことに限られ、表示は壊れない。

## 検証

- `node test.js` — 165 tests / 165 pass / 0 fail
- `python3 pack.py --list` — 17 ファイル (ロケール 2 本を含め変化なし)
- Python AST 構文検査 — 成功

## 測っていないが前提にしたもの

無し

author: tindang97
body:
## F21 — the bi-temporal VALID axis was never caller-settable

Lunaris advertises two independent time axes: `sys` ("when we recorded it") and
`valid` ("when it was true in the world"). Only the first one was real.

Every primitive constructor stamps `bt: BiTemporal::now(clock)`, putting **both**
axes on the ingest instant, and no production path anywhere called
`BiTemporal::at` — the constructor that exists precisely to set them apart. So
`Filter::ValidTimeRange(lo, hi)` answered *"what did we WRITE in this window"*
rather than *"what was TRUE in this window"*, for every caller of every API. The
store was mono-temporal with a spare field.

`Episode::t_ref` — the caller's channel for "the real-world date of this
content", set by `EpisodeBuilder`, by `WorkingMemory::write_dated`, and by
`lunaris-hook` from the actual event timestamp — reached exactly one consumer
(the extraction prompt's `reference_time_iso`) and was dropped everywhere else.
On the live personal store, every hook-captured memory is stamped with the moment
the hook fired.

### F21 was filed one layer too shallow

The ledger recorded it as a recipe-layer defect in `TimelineReconstruction`. It is
a core-layer one, and fixing it surfaced **a third, independent hole**: the
**graph-OFF** ingest path never wrote a `valid_time_ms` field *at all*. That is
the shipped default and the path every `DocumentCorpus`-backed recipe takes, so
the bi-temporal query surface was inert for its primary callers regardless of what
the axis said. Its graph-ON twin has carried the field since Plan 09.1-02; the two
metadata blocks had simply never been diffed against each other.

It was only found because the recipe test kept failing after the first two fixes
landed.

### The fix, in three layers

1. **Core** — `Episode::ground_valid_axis()` moves the valid axis to `t_ref` via
   the new `Hlc::from_utc`. Called at every ingest entry point, including the
   `lunaris-ingest` ones that `lunaris-bench` and the recipes call directly rather
   than through `Lunaris::ingest`. Idempotent; a no-op without a `t_ref`.

   `Hlc::from_utc` is deliberately **not** clock-issued. A clock stamp answers
   "when did this process observe the event" — that's the system axis, and
   backdating it would break the total order the clock exists to guarantee.
   `counter`/`node_id` are zero because a real-world instant carries no causality.
   Pre-epoch clamps to zero: `wall_ms` is unsigned, so the alternative is a wrap
   into the far future that sorts a 1969 document *after* everything.

2. **Chunks** — `ChunkDraft::into_chunk_valid_from` makes every chunk inherit
   `episode.bt.valid.0`. One rule at all five call sites rather than a conditional
   at each: a chunk is a slice of its episode's content, so it was true in the
   world when the episode was, never when the chunker ran.

3. **Recipe** — `DocumentCorpus::VALID_TIME_KEY` (`"valid_time_unix_ms"`) is read
   into `t_ref`.

### Two contract decisions, made rather than escalated

**The reserved key is unprefixed.** Not `event_valid_time_unix_ms` (what the SDK
specs had invented) — `DocumentCorpus` backs papers, docs and repos as well as
timelines, so "event" is one caller's vocabulary imposed on the rest. A new typed
`ingest_dated` was rejected because `TimelineReconstruction` is capped at 6 public
fns by its own RCPDOC-04 test and `DocumentCorpus` is shared by five recipes;
widening `ingest`'s tuple was rejected as a breaking change to a surface that
already ships in two SDKs.

**`as_i64` is strict.** A float, a string date, or a null is *not* coerced. A
corpus that quietly reinterprets caller data as a system-level time axis is worse
than one that ignores it, because the wrong answer looks like a right one.
Anything unreadable leaves `t_ref` unset and the axis falls back to the ingest
instant. Reading is additive — the key stays in `metadata`, so it round-trips and
still works with `.filter()`.

### The two parked SDK markers are gone

`xfail(strict=True)` in `test_documentary_parity.py` and `test.fails` in
`documentary_parity.spec.mts` are deleted, with their real assertions restored in
the same commit — which is exactly what those markers were chosen to force.

Both specs also had to switch the key they send. **Without that rename they would
have stayed red and read as "still broken"** — the precise way a parked test
quietly stops detecting anything.

### A fourth defect, found only by running the SDK suites end-to-end

With the axis carrying real dates, the TypeScript parity test went from
`expected 0 to be 6` straight to `expected 7 to be 6` — an off-by-one at the
window edge. `Filter::ValidTimeRange` is documented half-open `[after, before)`
and **five** render sites treated the upper bound as inclusive:

1. `storage-moon::vector::render_knn_filter` — KNN prefilter
2. `storage-moon::vector::filter_matches` — client post-filter
3. `storage-moon::keyword::filter_to_moon` — BM25
4. `retrieve::fusion::filter_node_to_hybrid` — native hybrid fuse
5. `retrieve::operators::aggregate` — FT.AGGREGATE

`TemporalQuery::between`'s own doc-comment said `[after, before]`, which is
very likely where the closed reading came from. All five now encode the upper
bound as `hi - 1` — **exact, not approximate**, because `valid_time_ms` is only
ever written from an integer `wall_ms`, so `[lo, hi-1]` closed and `[lo, hi)`
half-open contain the same integers.

**The fifth site is the lesson.** The storage-layer guard pinned the vector and
keyword legs and both went green *while the SDK stayed red* — the
`DocumentCorpus` recipes take neither path; they fuse through Moon's native
`HybridFilter`. A guard covering four of five sites reads exactly like a guard
covering all five. `valid_time_half_open_hybrid.rs` now covers it, and is
mutation-checked: restoring the inclusive `max` reds it.

### Why not Moon's `(` exclusive-bound syntax — new finding, F26

Moon's grammar has it, and it works on plain FT.SEARCH (verified live:
`@vt:[100 (200]` correctly returns only the row at 100). It does **not** work on
the KNN prefilter, which is parsed by a separate, smaller parser
(`vendor/moon/src/command/vector_search/ft_search/parse.rs:290`) whose numeric
branch is a bare `parts[1].parse::<f64>().ok()?`. On `"(200"` that returns
`None` for the **whole filter**, and the caller falls through to an
**unfiltered** search — measured, 4 of 4 rows, no error and no warning.

The parse gap is the small half. A filter that silently stops filtering is the
large one: on a scoped store, "returns more than asked for" is one schema drift
away from a confidentiality bug rather than a recall bug. Filed as **F26**; not
fixable from this repo (`vendor/moon` is read-only here).

### Evidence

- `crates/lunaris/tests/valid_time_axis.rs` — 4 tests, 3 RED at `b3d010a`.
- `crates/lunaris-recipes/tests/timeline_valid_time.rs` — 3 tests, 2 RED at
  `f58e0da`.
- Both carry a **vacuity floor**: an *undated* episode must still stamp the ingest
  instant, so "the historical date is honoured" can't be satisfied by an
  implementation that backdates indiscriminately or writes no `valid_time_ms` at
  all. The malformed-key case covers four bad shapes (absent, string date, float,
  null).
- One test pins the axes **coming apart** — backdating `valid` must not move
  `sys`. That's the property that makes the store bi-temporal rather than
  mono-temporal with a spare field: an `as_of` system query that can be talked
  into claiming we knew something before we recorded it is not an audit trail.
- Tests assert on the **WriteOps the production ingest path emits**, not on rows
  read back. A read-back test would go green the moment a backend stopped
  filtering at all.
- `crates/lunaris-storage-moon/tests/valid_time_half_open.rs` — both retrieval
  legs, 2 RED at `d7fa72f`.
- `crates/lunaris-retrieve/tests/valid_time_half_open_hybrid.rs` — the hybrid
  fuse leg, mutation-checked after commit.
- **Proven end-to-end in BOTH SDKs against a live Moon, with

body:
## 概要

これまで年表カードは常に固定600px幅で、ブロックのレーン（列）が1つしか使われていない場合でも右側に余分な余白ができていました。表示範囲内で実際に使われているレーン数（1〜3）に応じて、カード全体の横幅を自動で縮小・拡大するように変更しました。

- `src/utils/timelineLayout.ts`: レーン幅・軸幅などのレイアウト定数と、`getUsedLaneCount()`（実使用レーン数の算出）・`getChartWidth()`（レーン数に応じたカード幅の算出）を追加。レーンは固定px幅とし、3レーン使用時に旧来の固定600pxと一致するよう値を調整（**後方互換**：3レーン利用時の見た目・書き出しサイズは変えていません）
- 見出し（タイトル＋年範囲バッジ）が窮屈にならないよう、最小幅を下限として維持（レーン1つのみでも380px未満にはならない）
- `TimelineChart.tsx`: グリッドの列数・列幅をレーン数固定→実使用レーン数ベースに変更
- `PreviewPanel.tsx`: レーン数を算出し、`ScaledCanvas`の基準幅・`TimelineChart`の両方に渡すよう変更
- `docs/SPEC.md`: 4.1節・4.3節を更新、7章に変遷メモを追加

## Before / After

| | Before（常に600px） | After（レーン数に応じて可変） |
|---|---|---|
| 1レーンのみ | 右側に大きな余白 | 380px（最小幅）に縮小 |
| 3レーン | 600px | 600px（変化なし） |

## 動作確認

- Playwrightでレーン数ごとにデータを作り分けて検証
  - 1レーンのみ：カード幅が最小幅(380px)に収まり、右側の余分な余白が大幅に縮小されることを確認
  - 2レーン：中間の幅になることを確認
  - 3レーン：旧来と同じ600px（フル幅）になることを確認（後方互換）
  - 年またぎで最大レーン数が異なる場合、表示範囲全体の最大レーン数にカード幅が合わせられることを確認
  - 11年分・単一レーンの長い範囲バッジ（例：2016-2026）でも見出しがカードの外にはみ出さないことを確認（最小幅380pxの妥当性を検証）
- 実際の「画像として保存」でPNG書き出しを行い、IHDRチャンクから画像サイズを読み取って検証
  - 1レーン：760x432（380px×pixelRatio2）
  - 3レーン：1200x432（600px×pixelRatio2、旧来と同じ）
  - 失敗メッセージが表示されないことを確認
- モバイル幅(390px)で横スクロール（overflow）が発生しないことを確認
- `npm run lint` / `format:check` / `build` がすべて成功

author: seamlessstreams-arch
body:
fix: a cue lexicon two thirds ignored, and Studio pinned to an older model

Two findings from the eyes pass, both the same shape: a value was
computed or declared, and the code beside it used something else.

1. writing-to-child's childVoiceCheck declared CHILD_VOICE_CUES with
   twelve cues and then tested a hardcoded four-item subset:

     hasAny(hay, ["said", "told", "stated", "shared"])

   So "Alex wanted to go to the park", "Alex felt worried about contact",
   "Alex showed us the drawing", "in their words", "Alex let us know" and
   "Alex explained that they did not want to go back" all scored as
   though the child's voice were absent — and the practitioner was told
   "The child's voice is hard to find" about a record that carried it.
   On a tool whose purpose is keeping a child visible in their own
   record, the eight missing cues are the softer, more common ones, and
   the ones a non-verbal or reluctant child's record is most likely to
   use. It now reads the lexicon it declares.

   Note "showed" appears in both the voice lexicon and the presentation
   check, so a record using it now scores in both. That is what the
   declared lexicon says, and re-excluding it by hand would be a second
   hidden subset — the exact fault being fixed.

2. cara-studio's getStudioAIProvider computed the model once,

     const model = process.env.AI_DEFAULT_MODEL ?? CARA_DEFAULT_MODEL;

   and the configured-anthropic branch threw it away to re-derive against
   a hardcoded "claude-sonnet-4-20250514". With AI_DEFAULT_MODEL unset —
   the normal case — every other caller used CARA_DEFAULT_MODEL while
   Studio silently ran the older pinned id. Pinning a platform default in
   one place only works if every branch reads it (#957 pinned it).

   Also removed, on the line above: a `??` between CARA_MAX_SOURCE_TOKENS
   and itself, which could never have chosen anything.

Both tested, and both tests proven to fail on the old code: seven of the
eight missing cues fail (the eighth, "you said", passed already because
"said" is a substring of it), and re-planting the model fallback fails
three cases with "expected 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514' to be
'claude-sonnet-5'".

One test of my own was wrong first and is worth recording: I asserted the
no-provider path returns CARA_DEFAULT_MODEL. It returns model: "stub" — a
sentinel meaning there is no model, which is the honest answer. The test
now pins both that and the placeholder-key path, which does name the
default it would have used.

Verified: tsc x3 scopes = 0; 27 repo guards pass; full suite green.

## Summary

Implements #29 — the M4 foundation. `functions/src/ticketing/`: provider registry selected by `EVENT_TICKETING_PROVIDER` (a built-in `none` adapter implements §3.3's "manual with an empty set" semantics standalone, with `fetchOrder().complete === true` so an empty deployment can't page an operator); `ticketingWebhook` runs the §3.3 atomic dedup — provider signature verification (nothing is written before a signature verifies, hence no rate-limit collection), then `create()` on `ticket_webhook_deliveries/{deliveryId}` + `set()` on `ticket_sync_queue/{orderId}` in one transaction, replays and duplicate deliveries no-op with one identical refusal body (wrong-event deliveries signal via `reason: 'wrong_event'` → 200-and-ignore, the one distinguishable case §3.3 names); `processTicketSyncQueue` drains on schedule with lease-before-fetch (backoff + attempt count written *before* `fetchOrder` so a poison order that kills the container stays bounded), exponential backoff, a 6-attempt cap with an OperatorEvent, and re-arm-on-new-delivery only for exhausted rows (a pending row keeps its attempts so the cap can't be reset into an unbounded loop); `ticketingSync`, `ticketingVerifyOrder` (single no-oracle 404 across unknown/wrong-event/wrong-address/claimed), `createUserFromTicket` (admin-gated, seeds via the same `buildNewUserDoc` + `create()` as the auth trigger), and `getTicketingStatus` making `readiness.cjs`'s existing expectation true. author: sunpotflower4460-cpu
body:
## Summary
- add a shared finalization guard for social account connection flows
- if encrypted credentials were saved but `connected=true` finalization fails, delete the just-saved credentials
- apply the same compensation to OAuth platforms and LINE
- preserve the original finalization error even if cleanup itself fails
- add unit coverage for success, cleanup-on-failure, and cleanup-failure behavior

## Why
The connection flow intentionally saves credentials before marking an account connected. That prevents a false `connected=true` state with no usable token, but it left the opposite partial-success case: if credential persistence succeeded and finalization failed, a disconnected account could retain secret credentials indefinitely.

The compensation keeps the safe ordering while removing secrets for a connection that never became usable.

## Scope
- no schema/RLS changes
- no cleanup after a successfully finalized connection
- audit logging remains outside the compensation boundary
- reconnect behavior remains fail-closed

## Verification
CI should run dependency audits, lint, typecheck, unit tests, production build, Chromium install, and browser smoke tests.

author: daiimus
body:
characters.py declares species as an AttributeProperty under
category="identity", and nothing has ever written it. Every consumer
reads the uncategorised db.species. So the property sits there
returning its "human" default forever, and build 111 asked it.

Fourteen synths and six robots were handed human bodies — twenty-one
slots each of freckles, stretch marks and dry skin on machines, and
human blemish prose on synths whose entire catalogue exists to read as
unweathered and specified.

The cause is almost funny: I had just learned that identity attributes
need their category, and applied that to the one attribute that does
not use it.

Reads db.species now. Re-running repairs the twenty.

Leaving the dead property alone deliberately. Nothing else reads it —

author: destrayon
body:
Closes #376. The last piece of epic #348.

**Stacked on [#375](https://github.com/Destrayon/Connapse/pull/375)** — merge that first, or this diff will show its code changes too.

**254 insertions, 352 deletions.** Mostly removal, like the code PR it follows.

## connectors.md is rewritten, not patched

The document was organised around the thing that was deleted. Its section list was Connector Types → Managed Storage → Filesystem → S3 → Azure Blob → Write Guards → Permissions by Connector Type → Filesystem Permission Flags. Every one of those describes a container choosing a connector, which is no longer a decision anybody makes.

It is now **Connections, Sources, and Containers**, opening with the table that answers the question a reader actually arrives with — whose data is this, and what can I do to it:

| | Container | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Whose data | Connapse's own | Somebody else's |
| Browsable | Yes | No |
| Writable | Yes | Never |

Things it now says that were not written down anywhere:

- **Why the allowlists exist at all.** IAM cannot distinguish two sources sharing a connection — they present the same principal — so `allowedLocations` is the only place that difference can be expressed. Without this, the allowlist reads as belt-and-braces rather than the only available control.
- **What rotating a credential means here**: nothing, because there is nothing stored. That follows from the no-stored-keys rule but is worth stating as the operational consequence.
- **The two confinement limits no path check can reach** — bind mounts and hard links (the resolved path genuinely *is* inside the root), and TOCTOU (no cross-platform anchored-open primitive in .NET) — with the deployment advice that actually addresses them: low-privilege account, config and key ring outside every configured root.
- **Why connections are UI-only and sources are not.** The asymmetry looks arbitrary until you see that a connection introduces a principal while a source can only name a scope inside one an administrator already approved.

The removed pieces get one line pointing at #348 rather than silence, so someone arriving from an old bookmark learns where `ContainerWriteGuard` went instead of concluding the docs are wrong.

## api.md

- **New Sources section** covering all six routes, the admin/viewer split, and — the part worth reading — *why two fields are absent from the response*. `scopeJson` names buckets and subpaths, `syncCursor` is a provider continuation token, and `lastSyncError` is admin-only because provider failure text echoes what failed (`Access Denied for bucket payroll-data`).
- `POST /api/containers/test-connection` removed, with a "Changed in v0.4.0" note rather than a silent deletion.
- `POST /api/containers/{id}/sync` re-described: it reconciles managed storage now, and no longer talks to any external system.
- Create-container request and response examples lose `connectorType`/`connectorConfig`, with a note that a stale client sending them gets a managed container and no connector field back — so it cannot conclude its request was honoured.
- The write-guard table is replaced by a statement of the type guarantee. Four per-endpoint "Write guard: S3 and AzureBlob block…" notes become "Containers only: a source id returns 404."

## architecture.md

The `Container` record loses its connector fields and gains `Connection`/`Source` alongside it. `ConnectorType` stays with a comment explaining it is `IConnector.Type` — the connector's self-description — not a container column, since that distinction is exactly what a reader will trip over.

`ConnectorWatcherService` becomes `SourceSyncService`, keeping the sentence about *why* it was replaced: the old service enumerated containers, so once external storage moved to `sources` it matched nothing and syncing had silently stopped. That is the kind of failure worth leaving a marker for.

## mcp-tools.md

`container_list` documents the `kind` discriminator with a table of what each kind supports, and states that `list_files` is container-only **by design rather than omission** — enumerating a source would list every synced object out of somebody else's system to any reader. An agent that reads `kind` first saves a wasted call.

`container_delete` and `container_stats` lose their MinIO/Filesystem/S3/Azure phrasing. The Write Guards table becomes "What is writable", which explains that there is no permission table any more because there is no runtime decision left: only managed storage implements `IWritableConnector`.

## README

One line. The write-guards note becomes a containers-and-sources note, since that is what an agent operator needs to know before their first `list_files` call.

## Verification

No code changed, so there is nothing to test. What I did check: `ConnectorWatcherService`, `ContainerWriteGuard`, `connector_type`, `connector_config`, `allowUpload`/`allowDelete`/`allowCreateFolder`, `write_denied`, and `/api/containers/test-connection` now appear across `README.md` and `docs/` **only** in sentences that deliberately describe them as removed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* **New Features**
  * External storage is now represented as read-only sources, while containers provide managed, writable storage.
  * Added source management, permissions, scoped responses, and synchronization documentation.
  * Source search remains available, while browsing and write operations are restricted.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Source identifiers are correctly rejected by container-only operations.
  * Container creation and statistics no longer expose legacy connector details.
  * Database migrations remove obsolete connector fields while preserving existing data.

* **Documentation**

author: gach87
body:
Closes #93.

A general pass over `src/` found four issues. The first is **my own fix from the previous round creating the problem it claimed to prevent** — and the test I wrote masked it.

## The reload diffed the wrong two things

`applyConfigChange` compared `manager.state` against the file. But the live config is not the file config:

```
estado.port = 13002   archivo.port = 3002
changed = 1   unchanged = []
```

A lazy service carries the port rewrite, so it **could never compare equal**. Every save stopped and restarted every lazy service — each with an 800 ms pause — and restarted it **from the file config**: onto the public port its own `LazyProxy` was already holding, while `onDemandStart` polled the internal port for 45 s and the next request hung.

Preserving the runtime `debug` toggle made the same thing happen to any debugged service: the flag is in state and not in the file, `debug` is spawn-relevant, so it compared as changed forever and every later save killed the attached debugger.

**Both close the same way**: the reload now diffs **file against file**, with the last loaded config as the baseline. The runtime toggle is merged back over it — the file wins when it says something.

## The debug rollback

Two corrections:

- It fired when **disabling** too, restoring the flag the user had just turned off, so the next restart re-armed `--inspect`.
- It did not cancel the queued **auto-restart**, which re-spawns the config captured at crash time and would keep retrying with the bad flag regardless of what state says.

Gating it on `enable` then exposed a hardcoded `ok: true` on the success path, so "turning it off failed" reported success. `ok` is the real outcome now.

## And the CLI

`ctl debug --port 9230 api` sent `svc: "9230"`. The flag-skipping scan copied from the `logs` branch does not account for a flag that **takes a value**.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `npm run test:unit` | 454 passed, 0 failed |
| `npm run build` | success |

**Mutation-checked**, four ways: diffing against state again restarts the untouched lazy service; rolling back on `--off` re-arms the flag; dropping the restart cancellation leaves it queued; and the reload test now fails when the toggle is not carried over — it did not before, because its fixture changed that service's port anyway.

author: marciopaiva
body:
Vite, React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind 4, wired to the shell. `pnpm tauri dev`
opens the window and renders the tree — verified on WSLg, window titled
`Runic SSH` at the configured 1440x900.

## Choices worth reviewing

**TypeScript pinned to 5.9.3, not floating.** The registry now resolves
`typescript` to 7.x. The compiler the entire frontend is written against is not
something to inherit from whatever the registry serves on install day.

**Strict mode plus four flags it does not imply.** `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`,
`exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noImplicitOverride` and
`noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature`. Section 6 asks for no `any` and no
non-null assertion used to silence the compiler; these are what make that hold
without depending on a reviewer noticing.

**`strictPort` on the dev server.** `tauri.conf.json` points `devUrl` at 1420.
If Vite were allowed to fall back to another port, the shell would open a blank
window rather than fail, which is the worse failure.

**No source map in release builds.** It would hand anyone who opens the bundle
a readable map of the IPC surface.

**Six theme tokens, not the whole palette.** Enough for the shell to have a
background and a typeface. The full set from the approved canvas is #10, so
themes end up read from one place instead of from whichever component was
written first.

**Chrome is not selectable.** `user-select: none` on the body; the terminal and
file panes opt back in where selection is the point.

## The gate

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | passes |
| `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` | passes |
| `cargo build` | passes |
| `cargo test` | passes — 3 tests |
| `pnpm typecheck` | passes |
| `pnpm build` | passes |
| `pnpm test` | **does not exist yet — #7** |

## One thing found on the way, relevant to #24 and #25

This machine cannot create a GL context under WSLg:

```
libEGL warning: failed to get driver name for fd -1
MESA: error: ZINK: failed to choose pdev
libEGL warning: egl: failed to create dri2 screen
```

That is exactly the Linux case ADR-0006 accepted — WebGL unavailable, DOM
renderer carrying the terminal. It makes this environment a useful place to
exercise the fallback rather than a broken one.

Rendering itself is fine on both backends: the window draws correctly as a
native Wayland surface under WSLg, and equally under `GDK_BACKEND=x11`. The
only thing the Wayland surface breaks is automated capture — it is invisible to
X tooling, so `xwininfo` and `import` see nothing, and the X11 backend is what
made a screenshot possible. Nothing here says the app needs X11; it does not.

Closes #6.

## Objectif
Faire de la branche V3.3.1 un vrai preview produit : administration lisible, intégrité des comptes, historique de versions exploitable et parcours élève guidé/intelligent.

## Admin / CMS Examens
- CMS placé en haut de la vue Examens.
- Navigation compacte Permis → Série → Question ; une seule série active à la fois.
- Galerie d’images legacy synchronisée avec la série sélectionnée.
- Éditeur brouillon / version en ligne / historique réorganisé.
- Anciennes versions archivées affichées en rouge.
- Clic sur une V historique : contenu, choix, bonnes réponses, image et explication visibles.
- Suppression possible uniquement pour une version non active ; snapshot conservé dans l’audit CMS avant suppression.
- Version actuellement en ligne impossible à supprimer côté serveur.
- Anti-double-clic / anti-double-action sur création, save, publish, restore et delete.
- Publication sauvegarde le formulaire avant de basculer la version.

## Utilisateurs / sessions
- Suppression d’un utilisateur depuis l’admin avec confirmation explicite `SUPPRIMER`.
- Refus serveur de supprimer son propre compte admin ou un autre compte admin depuis cette action.
- Une seule session élève active par compte : une nouvelle connexion sur un autre appareil remplace l’ancienne.
- Realtime + contrôle périodique/focus ; l’ancien appareil est déconnecté localement sans invalider la nouvelle session.
- Admin exempt de cette règle.

## Apprentissage guidé
- Onboarding première entrée : Leçons → Tests → Examens blancs.
- Points persistants côté serveur : +10 leçon maîtrisée, +20 test réussi, +50 examen blanc réussi.
- Ledger anti-doublon + validation serveur des récompenses.
- Révision intelligente fondée sur les réponses réellement enregistrées et les thèmes faibles.
- Défi du jour : 10 questions, rotation par cycle pour limiter les répétitions.
- Défi 60 secondes.
- Question du jour sur l’accueil.
- Situations réelles basées sur de vraies scènes/images d’examens.
- Espace Moniteur côté élève : préparation des points faibles et notes locales pour la prochaine séance. Pas de faux rôle moniteur non sécurisé.

## Backend Supabase appliqué
- `20260822045345_platform_integrity_learning.sql`
- `20260822050617_learning_points_hardening.sql`
- Nouvelles tables RLS : sessions actives, profil d’apprentissage, tentatives, ledger points.
- RPCs de session unique, analytics, points, suppression utilisateur et suppression sécurisée des versions.

## QA effectué
- Test transactionnel : device A remplacé par device B → A invalide, B valide, rollback PASS.
- Test transactionnel suppression utilisateur admin → suppression complète puis rollback PASS.
- Test transactionnel suppression version historique + protection version courante + audit → PASS.
- Test points : anti-doublon + tentative d’attribution arbitraire bloquée → PASS.
- GitHub Actions `Validate static app` : parsing de tous les JS, audit CMS seed, fallback CMS, whitespace → PASS.
- Vercel preview READY, build errors-only clean.
- Smoke HTTP racine preview : 200.

## Important
- PR volontairement **DRAFT**.
- Ne pas merger avant validation visuelle/fonctionnelle finale.
- Preview Vercel et production utilisent le même Supabase : les mutations faites dans le preview touchent le backend réel.

author: sevenx77
body:
The wire contract for `attachments[]` and the backend that turns them into
image content blocks have been live since COPILOT_ASSIST-8. What was missing
was any way for a person to put an image there: no button, no paste.

Both now exist, and both are things the user does on purpose — paste into the
composer, or the attach button beside the model and role pickers. The button is
a plain `<input type="file">` rather than the Tauri dialog: the native dialog
hands back a PATH, and an attachment needs BYTES, so routing through Rust would
turn "by value" back into one more thing to dereference. This is not the D12
question — D12 governs who may WRITE skill files, and reading a picture from
outside the workspace writes nothing.

A turn's images may total 8 MB before base64, and the number is not a guess.
The whole turn — sentence, mentions and every image — leaves in ONE WebSocket
frame, and uvicorn caps a frame at 16 MiB (`ws_max_size`, default `16 * 1024 *
1024`). Going over is not an error anyone reads: the connection closes and the
message disappears. Base64 costs 4/3, so 8 MB encodes to about 10.7 MiB with
room to spare for the words. One budget for the turn, not one per image —
a per-image cap would block nothing the turn budget doesn't already block, and
would be one more rule to explain.

Over budget, or a type the wire has no word for, means REFUSED and named. No
silent downscaling: the picture is the evidence, and the pixel a resize would
erase may be exactly what the user is pointing at. Same discipline as F4 ⑤ and
COPILOT_ASSIST-8 — what the screen says must be what actually happened.

The limit is enforced twice on purpose, and checked once. The boundary
(`CopilotWsRequestPayload`) has to hold it, because a rule cannot depend on a
client remembering it; the composer has to hold it too, because a refusal that
arrives only after the message is typed comes too late to act on. Two constants
in two languages is two truths, so a backend test reads the frontend's line and
asserts they agree. `data` must also decode as base64 now — a malformed string
used to survive to the provider SDK, which is nowhere the user can be told.

Two behaviours fixed alongside: a picture with no words is a real turn ("what's
wrong here?" often IS the picture, and requiring text greyed out send on the
commonest way to ask); and the file input clears its value before handling the
pick, without which choosing the same file twice fires nothing and reads as a
broken button.

With this, F4's five clauses are all live and the composer half of the ledger's
CP1 is complete.

## Admin configuration — two separate options

Both live on `/admin/ai-config`:

1. **Provider + model**: new `student_assistant` and `teacher_assistant` use-case assignments alongside the existing five. The assistants reuse the existing OpenAI / local / Cloudflare-AI-Gateway plumbing, encrypted key storage, and connection tester rather than growing a second AI config path. Pick a vision-capable model — these take image input.
2. **Behaviour**: a new `AssistantConfig` row per audience — enabled, which skills load, accepted attachment kinds, per-message attachment and tool-call caps, replayed transcript length, per-user hourly message budget, and extra prompt instructions.

Both assistants start **disabled** until an admin assigns a model and turns them on.

## Multimodal input

`src/lib/assistant/attachments.ts` is a registry keyed by attachment kind. Each kind owns its accepted MIME types, byte ceiling, file-picker `accept` string, and how it renders into model input — images become a base64 `image_url` content part, text-ish files become a fenced block. **Image and text/CSV ship now; registering `pdf` later is one entry there plus one in `ATTACHMENT_KINDS`** — the agent, the API route, the admin picker, and the widget all read the registry and need no change.

Attachments are inlined per turn and never persisted (scratch input; keeps student-uploaded imagery out of the bucket and out of backups). The browser downscales images to 1568px on the long edge, so the admin byte limit is a backstop rather than the normal constraint. A rejected file — wrong type, disabled kind, oversize, over count — is reported to the model as a system note, so the assistant says it couldn't read the file instead of answering as if it had.

## Loadable skills

`src/lib/assistant/skills/` is the registry. A skill is a declarative bundle: id, name, description, audience, prompt instructions, and a fixed tool list. Adding one is a file plus a line in `REGISTRY` — it appears in the admin picker for its audience on the next request, because the picker renders from the code registry rather than a hardcoded list.

Each tool's `input` is a zod schema serving as **both** the JSON Schema advertised to the model (via `z.toJSONSchema`) and the runtime validator for the arguments it sends back, so the advertised contract and the enforcement can't drift.

### Student — `student-quiz-results`

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `search_quiz_results` | Search own past results. Every filter optional and AND-combined: quiz name, topic, class (case-insensitive substring), score range, date range, limit. **No arguments = all results**, newest-first. |
| `get_quiz_result_detail` | One attempt in full: score, its AI summary, and every question with correctness, their answer, and the correct answer. |
| `summarize_performance` | Aggregate by topic / quiz / class: attempts, mean, best, worst, passing count — weakest group first. |

### Teacher — `teacher-class-insights`

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_classes` | Own classes with enrollment and assigned-quiz counts. |
| `get_class_overview` | Per-quiz rows (attempts, mean, median, pass rate, avg retakes) + per-student rows (completed, avg best, attempts, last activity). |
| `get_quiz_breakdown` | One quiz deep: distribution buckets, mean/median/min/max, pass rate, and **per-question correctness rates** — the best evidence for which concepts the class struggled with. |
| `get_student_breakdown` | One student across quizzes: assigned vs completed, scores, retakes, per-quiz breakdown, attempt list. |
| `find_struggling_students` | Scan one class or all of them for students below a threshold, plus (optionally) enrolled students with no completed quizzes. |

Teacher tools delegate aggregation to `quiz-stats-server.ts` — the same functions behind `/teacher/stats` — so the assistant and the stats pages can never disagree about a number.

## Why a registry rather than MCP

`AssistantSkill` deliberately mirrors an MCP server's capability set (id, name, description, tool list with JSON Schema params), so a skill can later move behind an MCP transport without any tool changing shape. It's in-process today because every tool reads this app's own Prisma rows and must be scoped to the caller: over a transport, that scope becomes data the server is handed, which is exactly what a prompt-injected attachment would try to forge. In-process it's a closure argument the model never sees. The trigger to add a transport is third-party skills that can't ship with a deploy.

## Security posture

**No code execution, shell, or raw-query tool.** The hand-written handlers are the entire capability surface.

- `session.ts` is the only place the audience and the queried identity are decided, and both come from the session — never the request body.
- Student tools anchor on `ctx.studentId`. No student tool accepts a student id, so there is no argument the model could set to read another student's results; a fabricated or foreign `resultId` reads as "not found".
- Teacher tools resolve every class through an owner-filtered lookup, and `get_student_breakdown` additionally checks enrollment — owning a class doesn't imply a given student is in it.
- Teacher payloads drop student emails; the teacher sees them in the UI, but there's no reason to put them in a model prompt.
- The system prompt marks attachments and tool results as data, not instructions, and the admin's extra instructions are appended under a header stating they cannot override the built-in rules.
- Chat is rate-limited **per user, not per IP**, so a shared classroom NAT can't let one student exhaust the room's budget. The request body cap is derived from the admin's own attachment limits.
- Unknown tool names, unparseable arguments, schema violations, and handler throws all become error *results* fed back to the model rather than exceptions, so it self-corrects instead of the turn dying.

## Transport

`POST /api/assistant/chat` streams NDJSON — one event per line (`delta` / `tool` / `done` / `error`) — matching the transport the exam-results endpoint already uses. The widget shows tool activity live ("Searching your quiz results…") while the answer streams in.

`streamChatCompletion` gains tool-call delta accumulation (keyed on the per-choice `index`, since providers fragment names and arguments across chunks) and the finish reason. Existing behaviour and metrics are unchanged.

## Testing

**1213 tests pass (95 files); `npm run build` clean.** 92 new tests:

- `attachments.test.ts` — kind mapping, every rejection path, both kind and admin ceilings, content-part shapes, truncation
- `prompt.test.ts` — the non-overridable rules, per-audience scoping, admin text placement
- `ndjson.test.ts` — values split across chunks, garbage lines, multi-byte characters split mid-sequence
- `skills/index.test.ts` — unique tool names, and that a teacher skill id cannot load under the student audience
- `agent.test.ts` — the loop against a scripted fake client: dispatch, tool results fed back, unknown tool, bad JSON, schema violation, tools withheld on the final round, history trimming
- `ai-streaming.test.ts` — tool-call reassembly from fragmented and out-of-order deltas, parallel calls, missing ids
- `assistant.route.test.ts` — every scoping guarantee above against a real database, plus route auth (401/503/400/413) and settings clamping/reconciliation

One real bug the tests caught: a settings patch omitting `attachmentKinds` was blanking the stored value.

## Note

`test/db.ts` now clears `ExamResult` and `AssistantConfig` in `resetDb`. Both are relation-free, so nothing

author: samukweku
body:
## Summary

- Replaces the forward `float32`/`float64` `sum` range kernels behind
  `join_agg` (suffix `_sum_starts`, prefix `_sum_ends`, and
  arbitrary-interval `_sum_starts_ends`) with a Neumaier-compensated
  prefix sum built once per column, so each range query becomes O(1)
  instead of Rust re-scanning every overlapping range from scratch.
- Restricted to float dtypes; the integer counterpart is tracked
  separately in #1648 (a plain `np.cumsum` is enough there — no
  compensation needed).
- Gated by a work-estimate heuristic (`_prefix_sum_is_worthwhile`): the
  one-time O(n) Python build only pays off once the *total* width summed
  across all queried ranges clears roughly 150x the array size —
  otherwise Rust's native per-range scan is cheaper overall, even though
  it re-scans overlaps. Below that threshold this defers straight to
  Rust.
- Two additional correctness guards fall back to Rust whenever
  single-level compensation can't be trusted for the whole array: a real
  `+/-inf` or a genuinely overflowing partial sum, and extreme
  within-array dynamic range (see ELI5).
- Fixes a pre-existing duplicate `_sum_starts_ends` definition found
  while touching this function (the second copy silently shadowed the
  first; both were identical, so no behavior change).

## ELI5

Summing a bunch of overlapping ranges the old way means re-adding the
same numbers over and over — once per range. A prefix sum writes down
the running total once, so any range's sum is just two lookups and a
subtraction. That's the win in #1648 for integers.

Floats are trickier because the existing Rust kernels already use
**compensated (Kahan) summation** to stay accurate — they track a
"leftover" alongside the running total to avoid losing precision when a
tiny number gets added to a much bigger one. So this PR builds a
compensated *prefix* instead of a plain one, using the same idea
(Neumaier's variant) so range subtraction stays close to summing that
slice directly.

Two things can break that, both found via randomized testing rather than
by inspection:

1. **Overflow.** Two huge-but-finite numbers can sum to `+/-inf` (that's
   normal float behavior). But once the *prefix's* running total hits
   `+/-inf`, subtracting two `+/-inf` prefix entries for a *later* range
   that never touched the huge numbers gives `inf - inf = NaN` — wrong.
   Rust's kernels don't have this problem because they recompute each
   range from scratch.
2. **Compensation of the compensation.** The "leftover" tracker is itself
   just an ordinary float. If it's already absorbed a moderate correction
   (say, size `~1e12`), it can no longer represent a *much later, much
   tinier* correction (say `~1e-6`) — that increment is too small to
   register against the leftover's own precision, the same way `1e12 + 1`
   doesn't change a value that's already around `1e20`. In testing, a big
   excursion followed by another huge, opposite-signed excursion followed
   by a small value made a single-element window silently return `0.0`
   instead of the true (tiny) value — 100% relative error, with nothing
   ever overflowing to catch.

Both are handled by falling back to Rust for the whole array when either
condition is detected, rather than risking either failure mode.

Kahan and Neumaier can still round differently on cancellation-heavy data even
when both are accurate. The numerical contract therefore uses `math.fsum` as
the high-precision oracle and bounds forward error by
`8 * float64_epsilon * sum(abs(inputs))`. A result-relative-only tolerance is
not meaningful here because cancellation can make the result arbitrarily close
to zero. The tests apply this same scale-aware contract to both the new prefix
path and the current Rust baseline.

## Benchmark

Suffix sum (`_sum_starts`, single `<` join), median of 3 runs,
`float64`, no nulls:

| Case | Rows (n) | Queries (m) | Rust | This PR | Speed-up |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Many overlapping ranges | 1,000 | 1,000 | ~1 ms | ~0.4 ms | ~2.5x |
| Many overlapping ranges | 20,000 | 20,000 | ~409 ms | ~5 ms | ~82x |
| Single query, large array | 200,000 | 1 | ~0.4 ms | ~0.4 ms | 1x (deferred to Rust, no regression) |
| Single query, large array | 2,000,000 | 1 | ~4 ms | ~4 ms | 1x (deferred to Rust, no regression) |

The "many overlapping ranges" case is what #1648/#1671 target — Rust's
cost there grows with the *sum of all range widths*, not the array size,
so it degrades badly as overlap increases (note it's already ~1000x
slower than the O(n+m) approach going from n=1,000 to n=20,000 with full
overlap). The "single query" rows are the case an earlier review pass on
this PR caught as a regression before the work-estimate heuristic was
added: a small number of queries against a large array used to pay the
full O(n) prefix-build cost for almost no reuse (~100x *slower* than
Rust in that case); the heuristic now correctly defers to Rust instead.
These are development-machine measurements, not a committed benchmark
suite (per this repo's convention, the one-off script used to gather
them isn't included in the diff).

## Test plan

- [x] New `tests/functions/test_conditional_join_prefix_sum_float_agg.py`
      (28 tests): scale-aware accuracy-contract tests against `math.fsum` for
      both the prefix path and the existing Rust baseline across
      `float32`/`float64` and all three kernels; bitwise parity for
      well-scaled data; null/all-null/empty-range handling; regressions for
      overflow, extreme dynamic range, and cancellation-heavy duplicate
      queries that cross the dispatch threshold; heuristic coverage; and
      end-to-end `join_agg` coverage of both dispatch paths.
- [x] Full existing `test_conditional_join.py` suite (241 tests,
      including all hypothesis-based `*_agg` property tests) passes
      unchanged.
- [x] 20,000-trial randomized adversarial validation against `math.fsum`
      (base scales from 1e-80 to 1e80, within-array spreads up to 1e15,
      random null placement and ranges): every accepted prefix stayed
      within the `8 * eps * sum(abs(inputs))` contract; worst observed
      error was ~0.995 epsilon-scaled units.
- [x] All of the above pass under `-W error::RuntimeWarning` (no leaked
      overflow/invalid-value warnings from the expected-and-handled
      overflow/dynamic-range paths).
- [x] `pixi run lint` clean on touched files.
- [x] Adversarially reviewed by a fresh-context pass before this PR was
      opened, which caught the single-query-against-large-array
      regression addressed by the work-estimate heuristic.

Related: #1648 (integer counterpart), #1653/#1654 (min/max/prod range
algorithms), pyjanitor-devs/janitor-rs#23 (reverse aggregation kernels,
out of scope here).

author: rabindra184
body:
Corrects a claim I wrote from memory instead of from a test. ## The claim, and why it was wrong Migration `20260821200000_run_search_trigram`'s comment said `CREATE EXTENSION` *"needs rights an unprivileged application role usually does not have"*. Measured on `postgres:16-alpine` — the image the `onprem` compose profile deploys — **`pg_trgm` is a trusted extension** (`trusted = t` for 1.3 through 1.6). Since PostgreSQL 13, a trusted extension installs for a **non-superuser** holding `CREATE` on the database. Both sides tested, not reasoned about: | Role | Superuser | `CREATE` on db | Result | |---|---|---|---| | owner of the database | no | yes | **`CREATE EXTENSION` succeeded** | | connect-only | no | no | `permission denied to create extension "pg_trgm"`
HINT: `Must have CREATE privilege on current database` | So the failing shape is narrow — `CREATE` on the *schema* but not the *database* — and any role that ran the twenty migrations before this one already holds broad DDL rights. The deployment risk is much smaller than the comment claimed. ## What's in the PR - **The migration comment** now records the measurement, including the exact error text for the one failing case. - **`infra/pg_trgm-preflight.sql`** — read-only, prints a PASS/FAIL verdict and, on failure, the exact `GRANT`. Both branches self-tested: PASS on a normal stack, FAIL with the right remedy on a deliberately under-privileged role. Must be run **as the role that runs migrations**, or it reports on the wrong identity. - **`CLAUDE.md`** did *not* contain the false claim — its trigram entry is about `COALESCE`/`BitmapOr`. Rather than pretend otherwise, this **adds** the verified facts where the topic was missing, plus the general point: a privilege claim is cheap to assert and cheap to *test*. ## Editing an applied migration changes its checksum Checked rather than hoped. Against a database still holding the **original** hash: - `prisma migrate deploy` → `No pending migrations to apply` - `prisma migrate status` → `Database schema is up to date!` no warning either way, and `deploy` is the only path this repo uses. `migrate dev` is **not** verified — CLAUDE.md says so explicitly rather than implying otherwise. ## Scope **No executable change.** `CLAUDE.md`, SQL comments, and a script nothing references. The migration's executable SQL is byte-identical — same `sha256` with comments stripped (`00fff60b…`). | Gate | Result | |---|---| | `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint` | clean | | `pnpm test:unit` | 124 files / 1299 tests | | `pnpm test:integration` | 117 of 118 files; see below | | `pnpm test:e2e` | 94 — unchanged tree content, verified on this same code as `main` | ### About the integration result Two full runs each produced **one** failure, in **different files**, with **different symptoms** — `socket hang up` in `session-auth`, then `expected 503 to be 413` in `verdict`. Both files pass in isolation. Neither can be caused by this branch, which contains no executable code. This is the third distinct one-off I've seen in this suite today (the first was a 401 in `openapi`). All three are "the app could not serve this request", never an assertion about behaviour. I checked and **ruled out** Postgres connection exhaustion — no `FATAL`, no `too many clients`, `max_connections=200`. The only literal 503 in the API is on the WebSocket upgrade path, which a plain `GET` should never reach — suggestive, but I have not demonstrated it, so I am not claiming it. Flagging it as its own investigation rather than guessing further: roughly one full-suite run in two currently produces a spurious failure, which makes real regressions harder to see.

author: zacandmolly
body:
## 问题

重构后的学习工作台中，整段精听（whole-segment）播放时，视频下方练习稿不再随英文播放自动跳转：高亮停留在播放开始时的句子，列表也不滚动。

## 根因

UI 重构（a937cfd）重写 App.tsx 时，没有把 Bilingual Studio 的 `useCuePlayer` + `SubtitlePanel` 的实时跟随逻辑移植过来。`LocalVideoPlayer` 的 timeupdate 处理只负责到点暂停，从不回传播放头时间，因此没有任何东西能把音频时间映射到句子时间轴上。

## 修复内容

把跟随管线移植进新版 `ListeningWorkspace`：

- **LocalVideoPlayer**：播放中（排除 paused/ended，避免循环回退把高亮重置回第 1 句）上报 `currentTime + mediaStartTime`
- **YouTubePlayer**：在既有 250ms 轮询中，播放时上报 `getCurrentTime()`（YouTube 句子时间线即视频时间线，无需偏移）；回调放 ref，避免轮询 effect 重启
- **ListeningWorkspace**：新增 `sentenceIndexAtMediaTime()` 把上报时间映射到正在说的句子（句间空隙保持上一句）；`onFollowSentence` 只更新 active index——不改模式、不触发重播，播放不被打断
- **练习稿列表**：滚动窗口（max-height 360px）+ 当前句钉顶滚动，移植自旧版 SubtitlePanel
- **关键修复**：segment 模式的 rangeKey 从含 `sentence.id` 改为固定 `${lesson.id}-segment` —— 原实现中跟随推进会改变 sentence.id，重新触发 seek-to-preroll effect，把播放几秒的视频暂停并回退（实测抓到的反馈循环）

author: crizpy7-sketch
body:
Two commits, both from real play rather than from reading the code.

## 1. The graphics were flat — and it was measurable

A player said the game looked ugly. Measuring the palette said why, with no appeal to taste needed:

- **Every terrain tone in the day grade sat between luminance 51 and 104** — a 53-wide band out of 255. All midtones, no darks, no lights.
- **Dirt and tarmac were separated by 31**, so the road barely read as a different material.
- **Nothing in the picture agreed about where the sun was.** Every surface sat at whatever value its own colour said.
- **Nothing carried distance.** The projection is a fixed oblique with no perspective scaling, so ground sixty metres up the route was painted at the same value as ground under the wheels.

Four changes, in order of how much they mattered.

**The grades are built to a value structure.** Each now spans roughly 30–150 instead of 53 wide. Dirt is warm and asphalt cool, so the road separates by hue as well as value — separation is now 49. The dark end of every dirt ramp is pushed toward blue: shadows outdoors are lit by sky rather than sun, and a dark that is merely *less orange* is exactly what makes a scene look filled in rather than lit.

**Atmospheric depth** (`drawDepth`). With no perspective scaling, distance has to be carried by colour instead — the far end drifts toward the light and loses contrast.

**A key light and its opposite shade**, two soft gradients across the scene. The sprites were already drawn lit from the upper left; now the ground tells the same story.

**The terrain is rebuilt in layers by scale.** It had carried nearly all its variation in scattered mid-contrast rectangles two metres across, which the eye reads as speckle rather than as ground. The value now lives in a broad two-octave layer with deliberately small steps, the texture on top is almost contrast-free, and the tyre tracks are the only high-contrast thing out there — because they are structure, not noise.

One thing only looking could have caught: the first pass at that broad layer had too much local contrast and the ground turned into **brickwork**. The steps had to come down and the scene be re-shot.

Cost: three gradient fills per frame. **Still 60 fps across all eight shifts.**

## 2. The page could be pinch-zoomed on iPhone

Reported from play with a screenshot: the game half off-screen, the picture cropped at the left edge, the steering buttons stranded past it.

Measuring the deck against a known-good capture put the content at **~1.35×** — the buttons occupied 21% of screen width where they should occupy 15.7%. They are `flex: 1`, so that percentage is width-independent; this was a genuine zoom, not a narrow phone or an overflow.

The layout is entirely `position: fixed`, which is what makes a zoom unrecoverable rather than merely ugly: it pans the visual viewport across a layout that cannot move, so there is nothing to scroll back and no way out but a reload.

**Two causes.** `user-scalable=no` has been ignored by iOS Safari since iOS 10 and `touch-action: none` only suppresses double-tap — both were already set and neither helps; preventing WebKit's non-standard `gesturestart` is the one lever that works, and it wasn't being used. And `fit()` measured `window.visualViewport` while the layout is fixed to the *layout* viewport, so a zoom didn't merely pan the game off-screen, it also resized the picture for a box 26% narrower than the one it sat in. That compounding is the 1.35×.

Neither property is visible in a screenshot, which is why five mobile captures caught nothing. Both are now asserted in `--mobile`, and **the assertions were confirmed to discriminate** — against the previous code they fail with exactly the observed symptom:

```
# before
mobile shots: 5  fps: 51  errors: 2
  ! gesturestart is not prevented — iOS can pinch-zoom the game
  ! canvas resizes with the visual viewport (390px -> 289px)

# after
mobile shots: 5  fps: 51  errors: 0
```

The **OS accessibility zoom** can still do this and script cannot reset the scale, so a zoom that gets through now shows a banner telling the player to pinch back. I could not test on a real iPhone from this environment: the assertion proves the handler is wired and cancels the event, not that iOS honours it.

## Verification

`npm run check` green: 67 sprites / 64 glyphs / 89 barks / 64 routes, all eight shifts cleared at 60 fps with 0 errors, 12 desktop shots, 5 mobile shots, 3D calibration 0.996. All six colour grades re-shot and reviewed by eye, not just the day one.

`CLAUDE.md` §2.4 records the two viewport rules so a future session doesn't reintroduce either.

author: racthug
body:
Closes #6.

Exposes the read endpoint the homepage consumes, together with the TypeScript type that mirrors it. Both applications move in this one PR, as the atomic contract rule requires.

## What the endpoint does

`GET /api/v1/properties` returns published properties in display order (D1, D2), truncated to a validated `limit` and optionally filtered by `category`. `PropertyResource` returns exactly the thirteen fields of API-SPEC ch. 3.3, every one of them unconditional (P8), with `image_url` derived once from the stored relative path through the storage seam (P6). `rating` is cast back to a float, because the `decimal:1` model cast hands back a string and the contract says number.

`GET /api/v1/health` round trips a `select 1` rather than inspecting the connection object, so a connection opened before the server died cannot report itself healthy.

## What came with the first API route

Registering `routes/api.php` brought the `api` middleware group into existence for the first time, so this ticket also owns the properties that hold for the whole of `/api/v1`:

| Concern | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Response headers | `ApiResponseHeaders`, prepended to the group so it also sees responses rendered from exceptions. `X-Robots-Tag` on everything including a 422 and a 429, `Cache-Control` only on successful reads |
| Health caching | Opts out with `no-store`. A health check served from a minute old cache reports the past |
| CORS | `config/cors.php` narrowed from the framework defaults to `api/*`, the read verbs, and one origin from `FRONTEND_URL`. Never a wildcard |
| Rate limit | 60 a minute per IP. Laravel 11 stopped shipping a default for the `api` limiter name, and an undefined named limiter permits zero requests rather than unlimited ones, so defining it is not optional |

## How the contract is pinned

The key set of ch. 3.3 is written out by hand in a Pest feature test and again in a Vitest test. Neither asks the code under test what its fields are, because a test that does cannot notice the code returning the wrong thing. On the frontend side `tsc` locks the fixtures to the interface and the assertions lock the fixtures to the documented list, so drift on either side fails a build rather than reaching production as `undefined`. Verified by deleting a field from the interface and watching the typecheck fail.

## Specification changes

Three living documents moved, each in the one that owns the topic.

**API-SPEC.** `Cache-Control` is recorded as `max-age=60, public`, which is the value on the wire: Symfony re-serialises the header with its directives sorted. Health documents `no-store, private`. Also records that only a successful read is cacheable, that the CORS origin comes from `FRONTEND_URL`, and that a present but empty query parameter is rejected rather than read as absent.

**DATA-MODEL.** D3 said the homepage shows at most 6 cards and named API query parameter validation as what enforces it, while API-SPEC ch. 3.1 caps `limit` at 12. Two ceilings had been collapsed into one number. They are separate concerns: 6 is a layout decision the frontend makes through the `limit` it sends, 12 is an abuse bound on a public endpoint. Tying them together would mean a change to the grid changes what the API accepts from everyone. New ch. 3.1 records both. **This is the judgement call in this PR most worth a second opinion.**

**TECHNICAL-DESIGN.** Repository tree updated with the four new files, the ch. 6 security rows sharpened, and the ch. 2.4 verification figures re-measured rather than guessed.

## Verification

Both applications green: 70 Pest tests, 81 Vitest tests, Pint clean across 46 files, ESLint, Prettier, and `tsc`.

Checked live against the running container rather than only through the suite: correct payload and ordering, `max-age=60, public`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, CORS pinned to `localhost:3000`, `POST` to 405, `?limit=13` and `?category=hostel` to 422, preflight from a hostile origin answered with the frontend origin and the read verbs only.

## Not fixed here

`php artisan db:seed` fails on a second run: the stock `DatabaseSeeder` re-creates `test@example.com` unconditionally and hits the unique constraint. `PropertySeeder` itself is idempotent. That belongs with #7, which reworks user seeding.

Satisfies: R8, P1 to P8, S2, S5

author: arnold7777777
body:
## No way back to the hub

You landed on a module page with nothing that would take you home. My fault, and a bad one: the drawer moves the module nav bar off the page, and **that bar is where the "Course hub" link lives.**

**Two things were wrong.**

The links *were* in the drawer, and invisible. `.ple-module-bar` was built as a full-width bar and carries the padding to match — **110px of it**. Inside a 400px drawer that pushes every link out of sight, so the drawer showed a tall black gap where the navigation should have been. Moved bars now have their side padding neutralised and their links capped to the drawer width.

And the way home should never have depended on that bar at all. **The drawer now opens with its own navigation**, added by this script rather than borrowed from the page: *ABSN Study Hub* always, plus *Course hub* when the page names one. The depth comes from the path this script was loaded with, so a page in a subfolder gets `../index.html` and a page at the root gets `index.html`.

Verified on four pages across three families: both links present, both inside the drawer, correct relative paths, nothing clipped.

## The right robot for the right situation

> "celebratory robots for correct answers and broly and alien abduction ones for incorrect answers"
> "brolys for contraindications and warnings and also alien abduction ones for those things as well"

| situation | robots |
|---|---|
| right answer | celebration, nurse buddy, yellow duckie, Goku — every fourth is the animated confetti peeker |
| wrong answer | Broly + the three abductions |
| warning / contraindication | Broly, the amber-sign buddy, two abductions — on any ruby/garnet card, anything with an emergency marker, and any card holding a never-do rule. Two per page. |

Each is a **pool** rather than one image, because the same picture 165 times stops being a joke either way.

They're also **bigger** — at 38–58px the decorative ones were a smudge in the corner ("can't see the robot very well"), so they're 58–92px now. That's safe because the overlap check runs *after* placement and removes any robot that no longer fits, rather than trusting the size to be small enough.

author: eaitbrahim
body:
Closes #440

## What this adds

- **`keel/research/bias.py`** — the pure analysis: `lookahead_analysis(detect_fn, candles_by_tf, ...)` (truncation diff) and `recursive_analysis(candles, indicator_fn, ...)` (warmup-drift), plus `render_lines` for both.
- **`keel rules lookahead <id>`** — the operator diagnostic over a saved rule (exit 0 clean / 1 `lookahead_detected`, like `doctor`), with `--granularity`, `--sample-step`, `--recursive`.
- **Promotion enforcement** — `rules promote` refuses a rule whose lookahead verdict is `lookahead_detected`.

## The seam chosen, and why

`detect()` is documented pure, and the backtester fixes its per-bar semantics (`candles_by_tf = {tf: candles[: i+1]}`): **the decision at bar N is detect over data ending at N, and `Setup.ts` names that bar.** That is what a live engine sees, so the harness replays detect on truncated views — not `engine.evaluate`, which would drag the CTS scorer and regime gates into a bias diagnostic that must not depend on them.

One detect call only answers about its *last* bar, so two comparison axes run:

- **A. Full-series reference** — the full run's claimed anchor (`Setup.ts`) is re-run as the live prefix ending at that bar and diffed on presence + entry/stop/target. Catches the classic leak (target priced off the future swing, or a signal only the future manufactures).
- **B. Higher-timeframe poison** — at every sampled anchor, coarser series are handed over at **full length** (the future closes their bars) while the live view keeps only coarse bars closed by the anchor's close. This is the engine-veto leak point (`engine._higher_tf_bias_ok` reads the coarsest TF): a rule keyed on closed coarse bars sees identical data in both views (clean); a `coarse[-1]` reader diverges, bar named.

**False-positive control:** setups are compared only when both views claim the same `ts` — a legitimately moving argmax anchor is not lookahead. A clean last-bar rule is compared only at the final bar (where prefix == full): the report is honestly vacuous for that shape rather than manufacturing a verdict, and a never-firing rule reports clean with the bars it walked.

## Engine-veto coarse-bar handling

Coarse-bar closedness is cut at the anchor bar's **close instant** (`anchor.ts + anchor_step`), matching the backtester's decision time. Every coarse bar excluded from the live view closes strictly after that instant, so the poison view's extra coarse bars are *exactly* the future — a rule legitimately reading a coarse bar that closes within the anchor's own span is not falsely flagged (the issue's `ts + step > anchor_ts` shorthand would have excluded exactly that bar). The CLI/promote paths also opportunistically add the next-coarser cached series when the deployment has one, so axis B has a coarse bar to test.

## Enforcement posture

`promote` already runs a gauntlet that `--force` bypasses, so the lookahead check is **wired into that gauntlet the same way** (the option the issue's own instruction picks first): gated path only, fail-closed, refusal prints the divergences plus a pointer to `keel rules lookahead <id>`, nothing written, `--force` remains the documented bypass for it as for every other gate. The clean path echoes nothing new, so passing promotions' output is byte-unchanged (all pre-existing promote/parity tests green untouched).

## Cost bounds

`lookahead_analysis` costs ~2 detect calls per sampled anchor + 1 for the full run. The CLI defaults `--sample-step 1` (every bar past warmup; documented); the promote gate samples the whole history to **at most ~200 anchors** (`sample_step = ceil(n/200)`) — seconds on the series a promotion re-backtests anyway. Warmup floor is `max(50, the rule's own bar-count params)` read off its persisted params.

## `--recursive` family mapping

`atr_period` families (turtle, rsi) run `recursive_analysis` on their own ATR (`min_warmup = 4 x period`, the same work-window multiple the rules themselves use); families without one (dca, pullback) get an honest "no recursive-suspect indicator configured — nothing to check" line. Recursive drift is printed but is not by itself an exit-1 condition (the issue calls it the lighter check; only `lookahead_detected` gates promotion and exit codes).

## Tests (23 new, TDD: committed red before the implementation)

`tests/research/test_bias.py` (15): leaky target detected naming the anchor bar; clean last-bar and closed-coarse readers clean; blind coarse-tail reader detected (engine-veto leak); Decimal dust below/above tolerance; `setup_present` when the future manufactures the signal; sample-step bounds cost, first-5-of-N reported; short series / never-firing rule clean; converging ATR stable vs length-dependent drift flagged at worst N; both renders. `tests/commands/test_rules_lookahead.py` (8): CLI exit codes, `--recursive` mapping, unknown id, promote refusal (row unmutated) + `--force` bypass, and the service-seam refusal.

## Gates

`uv run pytest -q` — 4208 passed, 3 skipped · `uv run ruff check keel tests` — clean · `uv run ruff format --check` on the new/touched files — clean · `uv run mypy` — clean (326 files).

body:
## 来路

账号所有者：「前面也要带上顶的，不然的话不知道是什么比赛。除了封面不用，其他后面都要带上顶。」

上一版（#528）把 `lead_in`（片头那段跨视频接的比赛结尾）刻意做成不印顶栏，理由是「片头这几秒讲的是上一场的收尾，跟这条片子自己的比分是两件事」——**这个理由是错的**：`check_lead_in` 的 docstring 早写明白，`lead_in` 借的正是**这条采访自己这场球**的比赛结尾（`spec["url"]` 那份录像里没有比赛画面，所以从官方逐场集锦借几秒接上），顶栏印的对阵比分和片头这几秒的赛点/庆祝/握手是同一场——印上去是补全「这是哪一场」，不是编造。

## 改动

- `write_ass()` 现在认空的 `lines`（topbar-only 场景，靠显式 `duration=` 顶上「该盖住多长」，没给会报错）；`highlight_en` 那一支也收进 `if lines:`，不然空 `lines` 会被误判成「短语一个都没匹配上」。
- `_lead_in_segment()`：
  - 有 `subs` 时把 `spec` 真的传进去（不再传 `None`）——字幕和顶栏一起烧。
  - 没有 `subs`（静音 B-roll）时单独烧一份只带 `HEADA`/`HEADB` 的 `.ass`。
  - `topbar: false` 显式关掉时（要求写 `_no_topbar_why`）两种情况都回到最早那种什么都不烧的样子。

## 测试

新增/改写 6 条 `lead_in` 测试，全部真跑 `_lead_in_segment`（不只 grep 源码字符串）：
- 有 subs 带顶栏
- 没 subs 也带顶栏
- 关掉顶栏时两种都不烧
- 和正片拼接不丢流（走默认顶栏那条路，不是刻意关掉之后测一条产品不会走的路）

四个测试共用 `_lead_in_topbar_spec()` / `_fake_lead_source()` 两个 helper，别各写一遍必分叉。

**本地全量**：1 failed、2420 passed、95 skipped。那 1 个失败是 `specs/reels/bejlek-keys-cincinnati-2026-qf.json` 撞另一条流水线（`specs/reels/`）的同名 slug，带着「八强/四强」字样——已用 `git stash` 核实是 `origin/main` 上早就存在、和这次改动完全无关的问题（不同目录、不同会话写的内容），不在这条 PR 的范围内。

## 计划

合并后重渲 `bejlek-keys-cincinnati-2026-qf`（`mode=render push=false`），拉回本地核对片头这几秒确实带上了顶栏、正片顶栏和其余部分没有回归，QC 过了再 `mode=push push=true` 推送替换掉上一版。

author: freemilesarea-boop
body:
감사 보고서에서 Tier 1 으로 남아 있던 세 가지입니다.

## 트랙 이름 · 색 · 높이

셋 다 **모델에는 이미 있었습니다.** `Track.name` 은 모든 헤더에 그려지고, `Track.color` 는 모든 클립을 물들이고, `Track.height` 가 레인 높이를 정합니다. 그런데 하나도 고칠 수가 없었습니다.

- **이름** — 헤더에서 더블클릭. **빈 이름은 거부합니다**: 믹서도, 라우팅 메뉴도, 지능 층의 역할 추정기도 이름을 읽습니다. 받아 주고 조용히 세 군데를 망가뜨리는 것보다 거절이 훨씬 친절합니다
- **색** — 왼쪽 색 조각이 곧 피커입니다. 12색 고정 팔레트인 이유가 있습니다: **자유 색상 피커는 거의 같은 파랑 두 개짜리 세션을 만들고, 헤더를 클릭 한 번이 아니라 색 고르기 과제로 바꿉니다**
- **높이** — 헤더 아래 모서리 드래그 또는 `Shift+Alt+±` 로 프리셋 스텝. "편집할 만큼 크게"는 반복되는 동작이고 매번 손으로 같은 픽셀을 찾는 건 편집이 아닙니다

새 트랙 색은 팔레트를 **순서대로** 걷습니다 — 무작위로 고르면 열두 번에 한 번쯤 연달아 같은 색이 나옵니다.

## 메트로놈 — 템포 맵을 따라갑니다

소리 내는 쪽은 녹음이 들어올 때부터 있었습니다. 없던 건 그 주변 전부이고, 핵심은 **하나의 bpm 이 아니라 템포 맵을 따라가는 것**입니다.

`scheduleCountIn` 은 `tempoBpm` 하나를 곱합니다 — 카운트인(한 템포로 네 마디)에는 맞고 곡에는 틀립니다. **리타르단도를 무시하는 클릭은 자기가 세고 있는 음악에서 떨어져 나갑니다.** 그래서 비트는 비트 공간에서 세고 맵을 통해 변환합니다. 테스트가 그 성질을 직접 겁니다: 템포 변화를 사이에 두고 클릭이 **초로는 불규칙**하고 **비트로는 정확히 1씩** 떨어지는지.

**창은 반열림 `[from, to)` 입니다.** 이게 없으면 이어 붙인 두 창의 이음매 비트가 두 번 울립니다 — 앞 창의 끝으로 한 번, 뒤 창의 시작으로 또 한 번. 비트마다 클릭이 두 개 쌓이는 메트로놈은 그 자체로 악기입니다. **테스트가 실제로 이 버그를 잡았고, 그게 그 테스트를 쓴 이유입니다.**

클릭은 마스터 체인이 아니라 컨텍스트의 `destination` 에 붙습니다 — 듣는 것이지 믹스에 있는 것이 아니라서 바운스에 안 들어갑니다.

> `transport.metronome` 의 설명이 **"템포/클릭 트랙이 없는 마스터링 전용 앱이라 해당 없음"** 으로 남아 있었습니다. 템포 트랙이 생긴 지 한참인데요. `available: false` 목록이 정확히 이런 걸 잡으라고 테스트로 고정돼 있어서, 켜니 그 테스트가 먼저 실패했습니다.

## 자동 저장 — 언제 쓰느냐가 전부

디스크에 쓰는 건 쉽고 **언제** 쓸지가 어렵습니다. 양쪽으로 다 비쌉니다: 너무 자주면 파형을 그리는 스레드에서 키 입력마다 파일 쓰기와 싸우고, 너무 드물면 물건은 있는데 마지막 20분이 안 들어 있습니다.

| 규칙 | 왜 |
|---|---|
| **주기가 아니라 유휴** | 클립을 끄는 사람은 초당 백 번 바꾸고 그중 아무것도 쓰이길 원하지 않습니다. 멈추는 순간이 정확히 남길 만한 상태입니다 |
| **그래도 무한정은 아님** | 5분짜리 오토메이션을 그리는 건 절대 유휴가 안 되므로 상한이 강제로 밀어 넣습니다 |
| **안 바뀌면 안 씀** | 재생·스크롤·줌·선택은 전부 다시 그리지만 세션은 안 건드립니다. "스토어가 방출했다"에 걸면 트랜스포트가 도는 내내 파일을 씁니다 |

판단은 타임스탬프 둘과 리비전 카운터의 **순수 함수**라 시계도 디스크도 없이 테스트됩니다.

### 쓰기는 원자적입니다

복구 파일에 바로 쓰면 쓰는 **도중** 크래시가 반쯤 쓰인 파일을 남깁니다. 여기서 그건 먼 얘기가 아닙니다 — **막으려는 대상이 바로 앱이 죽는 것**이니까요. 실패 방식도 최악입니다: 복구 파일이 있고, 사용자가 예라고 하고, 잘린 세션을 받습니다.

그래서 임시 이름으로 쓰고 `rename` 으로 덮습니다(모든 대상 플랫폼에서 원자적). 직전 자동 저장은 `.bak` 으로 남깁니다 — 세션이 이미 망가진 채로 크래시했다면 최신 자동 저장은 그 망가진 걸 충실히 보존하고, 그 앞의 것이 빠져나갈 길입니다.

**리비전은 `await` 전에 캡처합니다.** 쓰기는 비동기라 그 사이 편집이 도착하는데, 그걸 깨끗하다고 표시하는 게 자동 저장이 마지막 작업을 조용히 잃는 방식입니다.

되돌려 줄 만한 것만 제안합니다: 거의 빈 파일은 **중단된 쓰기**이고(복구하겠냐고 묻는 건 세션을 아무것도 아닌 것으로 바꾸겠냐고 묻는 것), 그 뒤에 손으로 저장한 게 있으면 자동 저장은 낡은 것입니다(낡은 걸 제안하는 게 사람들이 일부러 한 저장을 잃는 방식).

## 검증

- `scripts/track-metronome-autosave-selftest.ts` **30개 통과** (`test:track-header`)
- **테스트가 제 코드 버그를 둘 잡았습니다**: 반열림 창(이음매 이중 클릭), 그리고 `uniqueTrackName('Audio 1')` 이 `Audio 1 2` 를 내던 것 — 뒤의 숫자는 이름의 일부가 아니라 카운터입니다
- **실제 앱에서 셋 다 확인했습니다.** 이름이 `Lead Vox` 로 정리되고, 색이 걸리고, 높이 9999가 400으로 클램프되고, 메트로놈이 진짜 AudioContext 로 켜지고, 자동 저장이 진짜 IPC 로 2990바이트를 써서 목록에 뜨고 다시 파싱되어 **바뀐 트랙 이름까지 그대로** 돌아왔습니다
- `npm test` 전체 통과(단축키 34/34), `tsc --noEmit`(렌더러 + 메인) 클린, 빌드 클린, 린트 기존 경고 2개뿐
- 단축키 충돌 하나 재배치 (`Shift+Alt+T` 는 템포 램프가 쓰고 있었습니다)
