body:
## Por qué existe este PR

La fundación (#1) fue integrada a `main`, mientras la ampliación de negocios (#2) fue fusionada sobre la rama de fundación durante el trabajo. Este PR recompone el **estado final limpio** directamente sobre `main`: un commit, cero historia duplicada.

## Qué integra

### Señalética por intención
`NECESIDAD → RUTA → PROMPT → ARTEFACTO → GATE → SIGUIENTE PROMPT`

7 entradas para visitantes que saben qué necesitan lograr pero no conocen todavía la jerga correcta: idea/PMF, marketing-growth, inteligencia comercial, producto-Agile, DevOps, MLOps y escala.

### Business Prompt Engineering
13 Prompt Maestros desde Lean Startup y Customer Discovery hasta GTM, Marketing Digital, CRM, Reporting, Pricing, Agile, DevOps, MLOps y Business Operating System.

Todos conservan el contrato:
`CONTEXTO → HIPÓTESIS → ARTEFACTO → EVIDENCIA → DECISIÓN → SIGUIENTE CICLO`

### Canon con procedencia
21 fuentes curadas como framework/documentación oficial, research, portal profesional, comunidad/curso y libros. La interfaz muestra el tipo de señal para no confundir popularidad con evidencia.

### Frontend
Mantiene el lenguaje visual del Atelier: oscuro/editorial, oro + verde, serif + sans, marcos finos, responsive y reduced motion. Añade rutas interactivas, filtros de negocio y exploración de fuentes.

### Git como fuente de verdad
El lector de Markdown obtiene el documento versionado desde GitHub. Vercel sigue siendo capa de publicación, no un segundo CMS.

## Vercel
La versión correspondiente ya fue desplegada y validada en producción en `prompt-maestros.vercel.app`; el alias y el endpoint `data/business_paths.json` respondieron correctamente.

## Gate
No fusionar este PR por automatismo: CI debe validar primero la fundación + los nuevos contratos en conjunto.

author: skrymer
body:
Closes #161.

Slice 7 could never merge on CI — it needed the Cloudflare dashboard, a real deploy, and a second person with a real address — so its acceptance criteria are observations against the live origin rather than tests. They have now been made.

`V9`→`V13` applied to production in one go, preceded by a clean `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` and a Litestream restore drill whose restored row counts matched production exactly (`entry 51 | weekly_review 1 | food 45 | weight 4`).

## What the live origin showed

- **The second User was provisioned just-in-time** from the Access policy alone — empty Foods catalog, no Entries, no history. Confirmed by them, on their own phone.
- **Both Users hold a Weight Measurement on the same date, both intact.** This is the evidence worth keeping. It is exactly the hole slice 4 closed — `WeightMeasurementRepository.save` used to resolve the date unscoped, so the second person weighing in on a day would silently overwrite the first's reading — and `idx_weight_measurement_user_day` on `(user_id, measured_on)` is what lets both rows exist. A production database is the only place that collision was ever going to be real.
- **Each Calorie Budget derives from one body.** Both Users' Maintenance, Budget and Protein Floor were re-derived by hand from their own profiles and trend weights, and match what the engine stored (Mifflin-St Jeor × 1.4; floor 2.0 g/kg). Before slice 4 one engine averaged both people's scale readings and logged intake into a single Maintenance — wrong for both.
- **Reminders reach one person's devices.** The two Push Subscriptions sit on different push services (FCM and Apple), the timezone is captured onto the enabling User's Profile alone, and `reminder_state` keeps a separate absent-today stamp and dedupe per User.

## Recorded as not done, rather than glossed

- **A live reminder send was not observed.** `ReminderPolicy` needs a review ≥7 days overdue *and* the User absent that day; with both Users active and freshly reviewed, every gate is correctly shut. Waiting a week is the only honest way to see one — the send-and-dedupe path stays covered by the `reminder-send` real-stack smoke.
- **AC5 (revoke) was not exercised**, by choice: it locks a real person out of a live account to prove a Cloudflare behaviour rather than a Tucker one. The two-step procedure, and why each step alone is insufficient, is already documented in `deploy/README.md`.

## Also in here

The deploy hold is **replaced by a note that it has lifted**, not deleted — the reasoning is why `V9`→`V13` had to land together.

And a fix to the restore drill, which could not have worked as written: the litestream image runs as a non-root user that cannot write to a root-owned bind mount, so the restore dies with `create temp database path: … permission denied`. It needs `--user 0:0`, and the numeric uid specifically — the image is distroless, so `--user root` fails differently (`unable to find user root`). Found by running the drill for real.

## Follow-up

[#241](https://github.com/skrymer/tucker/issues/241) — the birth-date field can't be typed on Android, found by the second User during this very setup. Not a blocker; filed separately.

author: harsh71019
body:
## Purpose

Add fast, explainable personal category recommendations without silently categorizing transactions, leaking narration, or replacing the full category hierarchy.

This PR is an implementation specification, not feature code. It is written as a direct handoff for an implementation model and follows the existing NestJS, Next.js App Router, generated-client, and shared-Zod boundaries.

## What the design now specifies

- One recommendation engine shared by imports and the interactive picker, with explicit versioned ranking policies.
- Deterministic ranking across explicit rules, exact personal history, token history, frequent categories, and recent categories.
- Exact confidence thresholds, support counts, tie-breakers, abstention behavior, deduplication, and five-item cap.
- Reuse of the current bounded history repository and ranking primitives instead of a parallel ML system.
- Shared Zod request, response, reason, source, and confidence schemas.
- A tenant-scoped `POST /api/v1/category-recommendations` endpoint using the generated web client.
- UTC timestamp validation and server-side conversion to the existing ranking context.
- Privacy controls covering application logs, Pino serializers, nginx, APM, errors, metrics, and staging observability.
- Identity-scoped cache keys, logout/session-switch clearing, debounce, cancellation, and out-of-order response protection.
- A reusable category-specific searchable hierarchy picker for quick add, create drawer, transaction drawer, and transaction detail page.
- Full-list availability at all times; recommendations never auto-select and saving remains explicit.
- Mobile, keyboard, screen-reader, reduced-motion, dark-mode, loading, empty, stale, and error states.
- Backend, frontend, contract, cache, race, privacy, accessibility, and performance test matrices.

## Product behavior

The picker opens with a compact Suggested section when confidence is useful. Each suggestion has a short explanation such as From your rule, Often used for this merchant, or Recently used. Search and the complete category hierarchy remain directly available.

The system abstains when evidence is weak. It does not train a cross-user model, create hidden categories, mutate transactions, or store recommendation decisions.

## Suggested implementation order

1. Shared contracts and exact ranking policy tests.
2. Recommendation service and tenant-scoped API route.
3. Generated client, identity-safe query keys, and race-safe hook.
4. Reusable searchable hierarchy picker.
5. Integrate all four transaction surfaces.

author: denzmilk
body:
Part of #813 — its artefact half closed in #861.

A link that does nothing is indistinguishable from a broken link, and the player has done nothing wrong: a
friend sent them today's word after they'd already played it. Your two sentences, verbatim:

> you've already played WOTD today!
> **You guessed the word EVOKED in 6 tries**

> you've already played WOTD today!
> **You didn't guess the word in time, it was EVOKED**

## ⚠️ Two things to check, both flagged rather than quietly decided

**1. One liberty taken.** Your second version reads *"you've already **playing** WOTD today"*. I used
"played" in both, from your own first line. If that was deliberate it's one character to put back.

**2. "Tries" and "guesses" are different numbers, by your own arithmetic.** *"5 guesses before getting the
word on the 6th try is a score of 5"* — so the score is the guesses and the tries are one more. It's the same
reading you confirmed for Guesstimator. Which means **one run reports two numbers**:

| | |
|---|---|
| the share artefact (#861) | "I found today's word in **5 guesses**" |
| this message | "You guessed the word EVOKED in **6 tries**" |

Both true, both yours, and consistent — but they're the same run, and a player could well see both. Say the
word and I'll make either one match the other.

The word is **recomputed, not stored** — `pickWotd` is a pure function of the date. Naming it costs nothing:
this only ever runs for somebody whose attempt at that word is already over.

## ⚠️ And the bug I nearly shipped inside this

The first cut built the popup inside `linkStart` and deferred it 60ms so it would land *after* the screen. It
produced **nothing at all** in the harness — which is the tell. Both callers do `if (!linkStart())
showScreen('home')`, and a popup built before that screen is torn down by it; `clearUiText` takes everything.
**An ordering that depends on a delay is not an ordering.**

`linkStart` raises a flag now; the callers show the message after the screen exists, and the flag is cleared
as it's read — so it's said once, not on every screen for the rest of the session. That last one is asserted,
because it's the failure mode a flag invites.

## Testing & sign-off

`npm test` green — both sentences asserted verbatim, the winning and losing halves, the tries arithmetic, and
the said-once rule. `npm run test:render` and `npm run test:layout` run by hand — both green.

### How to try it on `/preview/`

1. Solve (or lose) today's **WORD OF THE DAY**, then **SHARE** and copy the link.
2. Paste it back into the address bar. The game opens as normal and the message appears over home.
3. Dev panel → **Reset WOTD**, open the link again — it deals straight into the run, no message.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Stacked on #4 (exp-15 answer-forcing). Extends exp-15's two-pass forcing; the control arm (`ITS_SC_SPLIT_BUDGET=0`) reproduces exp-15's 0.4088 by construction.

## Changes
- **New default-OFF sub-flag `ITS_SC_SPLIT_BUDGET`** (only active when `ITS_SC_ANSWER_FORCE=1`). Re-tunes the NUMERIC arm of the two-pass answer forcing into a decoupled reasoning/answer (Br/Ba) split.
- **Numeric arm (split ON):** main-gen reasoning cap `Br 3600 → 3200`; forced answer-completion pass `Ba 48 → 500`. Sized so `prompt + draft + primer + Ba ≈ 4020 < 4096` (the hard window). Attacks the coupling tax: a box-absent numeric sample now gets a real finish-and-box pass instead of a 48-token blind guess (arXiv:2605.07686, +3.0pp MATH-500 at 4096).
- **MCQ/GPQA arm byte-untouched** (Br=3600, Ba=16, `CONTINUATION_PRIMER_MCQ`) → the all-empty forced-fallback rescue (0.200 → 0.462) is preserved by construction.

- **Telemetry (observability only, no behavioral effect):** extended the existing logging line with `br=%d ba=%d split_budget=%s` and added an `n_completed_by_extraction` count.

author: omerk1
body:
## Summary
- New `src/patterns/curves.py` (`fit_roundedness`) + `src/patterns/detectors/cup_and_handle.py`.
- Scoped to Cup & Handle + Inverse only, not Rounding — the progress tracker's own Phase 6 entry already deferred Rounding until after phases 1-5 are validated; resolved a pre-existing inconsistency in the plan (Phase 4's title also mentioned Rounding) in favor of the more detailed Phase 6 wording.
- New structural problem this phase introduces: unlike every prior pattern's fixed-size pivot window, the cup's own pivot sequence allows an unknown number of intermediate pivots forming the rounding. Resolved by decoupling pivots from geometry — the scan only anchors three fixed points (left rim, right rim, handle), while roundedness is checked against the raw close-price path between the rims via `curves.fit_roundedness`, not the pivots themselves.
- Cup & handle's flat trigger level means `target_price` needed no "value at formation end" approximation the way H&S/triangle's sloped/two-sided boundaries did — the design doc's literal §3.6 formula applies exactly.
- Checked (not assumed) that R² alone doesn't reliably separate a real cup from a sharp V — a plain symmetric V scores ~0.94 against a parabola, comfortably above the default 0.5 floor. Documented as a known limitation matching the design doc's own framing (R² is one of "two practical approaches," not a claimed-perfect discriminator), not a bug.
- `docs/features/chart_pattern_detection_design_notes.md` and `docs/done.md` updated with the full Phase 4 narrative.

- [x] 17 new unit tests: `tests/test_patterns_curves.py` (4, direct coverage of `fit_roundedness` including the direction-agnostic and constant-price edge cases), `tests/test_patterns_cup_and_handle.py` (13: happy path with hand-verified target/stop/neckline values, inverse mirror, every hard gate incl. the roundedness-rejection case, invalidation, failed-breakout, expired, pending).

body:
## What changed
Simplified `Owner.hasPetsNamed(Collection<String>)`, introduced in this pull request, to avoid re-scanning every pet for every requested name.

**Before:** for each requested name, loop over every pet calling `equalsIgnoreCase` until a match is found (O(pets * names)).

**After:** build a `HashSet<String>` of lower-cased pet names once, then check each requested (lower-cased) name against that set (O(pets + names)).

## Behavior preserved
- Same public signature and return semantics: returns `true` only if every supplied name matches some pet, case-insensitively.
- Same handling of an empty `names` collection (returns `true`).
- Same handling of duplicate names in the input.
- No new dependencies; only imports already present in the file (`Collection`, `HashSet`, `Set`) are used.

## Evidence
- Full clean build/test suite passes before and after the change with the same test count (76 tests, 0 failures).
- The pull request's own `OwnerTests.shouldCheckAllPetNamesWithoutRegardToCase` test, which exercises case-insensitivity, duplicate names, an empty collection, and a non-matching name, passes unchanged against the new implementation.
- JaCoCo shows full line and branch coverage of the rewritten method.

## Limitations
- No timed benchmark was produced since realistic pet counts per owner are small; the benefit is a proven reduction in asymptotic complexity rather than a measured wall-clock speedup.

author: jsonbored
body:
`call_subnet_surface` took a `method` argument spanning GET/HEAD **and** POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE. The Connectors Directory review criteria name that exact shape as an automatic rejection:

> A single tool that accepts both safe HTTP methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) and unsafe methods (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) is rejected. Do not ship a catch-all `api_request` tool with a `method` parameter. […] Documenting safe versus unsafe operations within one tool's description does not satisfy this requirement.

It is the better surface regardless of the listing. A read-only tool can run **without a per-call confirmation**; one that might write always prompts. Merged, every catalogue read paid the write tool's interruption.

## The split

| | verbs | annotation |
|---|---|---|
| `call_subnet_surface` (keeps its name) | GET, HEAD | `readOnlyHint: true` — truthfully, for the first time |
| `write_subnet_surface` (new) | POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE | `destructiveHint: true` |

One implementation behind both. The schema gate, credential handling and response bounding are untouched.

`path` and `method` are **required** on the write tool. There is no curated write: a write always names a declared operation, and making that structural stops an agent discovering it by being refused.

## Enforcement — and a correction to my own first reading

I assumed MCP dispatch does no argument validation, so a narrowed enum would be advertisement only. Half right, and the difference matters:

- dispatch **does** reject unknown argument *names* — so dropping `body`/`content_type` from the read tool's schema genuinely stops a body reaching the handler through it;
- it does **not** check enum values or required-ness — so a caller may still send `method: "DELETE"` to the read tool.

The handler therefore holds the verb boundary, and the refusal **names the sibling tool**: an agent that guessed wrong has a correct intent and a wrong address, and telling it only "no" turns a one-step correction into an abandoned task. A verb in *neither* set still gets the enum message, because "use write_subnet_surface" would be a lie for `TRACE`.

The verb sets are **derived** from `CALL_SURFACE_METHODS`, so a verb added there lands in exactly one tool and cannot appear in neither.

## Registration

Annotations, output schema, tool-exposure classification and the `validate:mcp` sweep exemption all follow the checklist.

The write half **cannot** be swept and should not be — succeeding would mean CI issuing real writes against third-party hosts on every run. Its response envelope is identical to the read tool's, which *is* swept, so the shape stays proven.

Open-world count moves 23 → 24. It is the one increment that adds **no new reach**: both halves call the same catalogued surfaces the merged tool already did. The count moved because one tool became two.

## Incidental

- Lowered `MAX_UNREFERENCED_EXPORTS` 731 → 730, which the gate asked for.
- Covered four refusal paths the extraction pulled into the diff that no fixture had ever reached: a catalogued surface with no url, a probe block with no method, a surface with no `surface_id` of its own, and a body with no operation to send it to.

## Verification

- **Patch coverage 100%** — 135/135 lines, 212/212 branches, by diff intersection
- Full suite green: 967 files, 22,243 tests
- All 70 `validate:*` scripts, `tsc` clean, prettier clean

Part of #11561.

Closes #11568

author: pengpeng
body:
## Background

Router's audio data plane is one route per capability, and the Market ships one
application per capability — an application declares only the thing it does.
`audioqwenalignerv3` declares align and not stt; `audiosoulxdialogv3` declares
tts_dialogue and not tts. The CLI covered a subset of that surface, and the
gaps were not visible from the help text:

- `categoryAlign` was `categorySTT`, so `call align` without `--model` resolved a
  transcription engine that has no align route and answered a bare 404.
- Six capabilities had no verb at all, including `audiosortformerdiarsv3`, which
  nothing in this tree could call.
- Nothing could submit work asynchronously, so an hour of audio depended on a
  request surviving an edge timeout or a laptop lid.
- A multipart upload was read into a buffer before any of it was sent, which is
  what the function's own comment set out to avoid.

## What changed

**Every capability has a verb.** Adds `clone`, `dialogue`, `listen` and
`diarize --stream`. The two streaming verbs open a WebSocket and send raw PCM;
the dialer carries the profile's credential by hand, because gorilla's `Dialer`
does not reuse the HTTP client's `Transport` and a handshake without it returns
a 401 that reads as a routing failure. `categoryAlign` now resolves align.

**Work can outlive the request.** Every audio verb takes `--async`, and
`call task get|result|cancel|list` reads what it hands back. Two details belong
to the engine rather than this tree, and the flag handling follows them:
`--async` is a form field on the multipart routes and a query parameter on the
JSON ones, and sending it in the wrong place is ignored rather than refused.

**A task can be followed by its id alone.** Router remembers which backend
answered each `--async` submission and routes a bare `/v1/audio/tasks/{id}` back
to it. The flag was already optional, but the help text, the flag usage and the
error message all said a model was required — the kind of wrong that keeps a
working call from being tried. `--model` is now described as covering what that
memory cannot: a gateway that restarted, work submitted through another one, or
an id old enough to have aged out. `task list` still requires it, because a
board has no id to be remembered by and each application runs its own queue.

**The upload is streamed.** The body is encoded into the request as it is read.
It is no longer replayable, so the upload relies on the same pre-flight token
rotation `files upload` uses.

**A task refusal says which of the four it is.** 409 is a task with no result
yet — still running, or ended without one — and points at `task get --wait`;
410 is a result the engine has since dropped, which means submitting the work
again rather than waiting for something that will not arrive.

## Verification

```
cd cli
go build ./...
go vet ./cmd/...
go test ./cmd/ctl/...
gofmt -l cmd/ctl/router
```

All clean on this branch, rebased onto current `main`. Help output was checked
for every new verb.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

body:
## Summary
- Adds `tests/test_examples_smoke.py`, which runs every `examples/*.py` script as a subprocess under `SWIFT_HEADLESS=1` and checks it doesn't raise within a short window.
- Most examples end in an intentionally endless `env.hold()`/`env.run()`/`while True` (interactive demos meant to keep a browser tab open), so there's no "finished successfully" exit to wait for — still running when the timeout hits counts as a pass, same as a clean voluntary exit. Only an early non-zero return code (an uncaught exception) fails the test.
- The example list is discovered via `glob` at collection time, not hardcoded, so it tracks `examples/` automatically as files are added, renamed, or removed.
- Examples that `import roboticstoolbox` are marked `rtb`, matching the existing convention (`tests/test_assembly_handle.py`) — excluded from the default run, opt in with `pytest -m rtb`.

## Note

Executable enumerator for frozen v0.4.2. Contract only: ```text Output(M) = 1 iff M ∈ R(P, D) ∩ F ``` `--s2c2-enumerate` prints `Enum_F` on stderr in `F_0` declaration order. Empty flags use ```text scheds = cpu-seq,gpu-async,npu-staged-dma maps = default,t5 devices = cpu,gpu,npu,cim ``` Requested labels are intersected with `F_0` (so `devices=cpu,gpu` is `D_test`). Unknown labels fail. Because the pass does not rewrite `P`, every emitted `M` has `HB_M = HB_source`. ## Not in this pass - ArgMin / Pareto selection - Search / Placement / Rewrite - Cost / HB / `π` changes - score lines (`total=`) Tests: `test/Analysis/realization-enumerate.mlir` (L1–L4). v0.4.0–v0.4.2 math stays frozen.

New Features: - Add the `--s2c2-enumerate` pass to list realizations in `R(P, D) ∩ F` on stderr. - Support deterministic enumeration of the default finite family and filtered scheduler, map, and device selections with validation of unknown labels. Enhancements: - Preserve the source program and existing HB, cost, and π semantics while enumerating realizations without selection, scoring, or rewriting. Build: - Include the realization enumeration implementation in the S2C2Cost library build. Documentation: - Document the realization enumeration listing pass, its contract, supported options, and v0.4.3 roadmap status. Tests: - Add coverage for default and filtered enumeration counts, declaration order, label presence, invalid output fields, and unchanged IR.

author: nickflach
body:
Closes #418.

## The bug

`replayMissedEventsOnStartup()` re-offers a deferred partner event (#103) by holding its cursor — but the hold leaked on every path that wasn't the single per-event guard. A deferred event on a full page, or in a type with no saved cursor, was skipped permanently: the exact recovery path `EventDeferredError` exists to protect.

## Why the first attempt wasn't enough

A first fix with site-local `deferred` guards went up, got an adversarial review, and the review earned its keep — it found:

1. **The pin was missing.** A type whose *first* event defers never persisted a per-type cursor, so next boot it seeded from the shared, mutable `lastEventUuid` that other types advance — #418 one level down.
2. **A sibling loop had the bug wholesale.** `POST /admin/obc/replay` recorded `lastUuid` per page with no hold and no event type — and it's the catch-up-a-new-handler path, where a deferral is *most* likely.
3. **`break` wedged the backlog.** Stopping pagination on deferral meant pages 2..N were never fetched; a cross-page dependency livelocked.
4. **The failure breaker reset every page**, so it could never trip.
5. A cursor-write error on the success path was miscounted as a handler failure.

## The fix: one owner

All cursor advances now go through a single `ReplayCursor` (`lib/replayCursor.ts`) that holds the invariant:

- a deferral **freezes the persisted position** and **pins the type** onto `eventCursors[type]`, so it never falls back to the legacy cursor;
- the **fetch position keeps moving**, so later pages are still tried;
- the **failure count lives in the cursor**, surviving page boundaries;
- persistence errors propagate to the outer handler, never the per-event failure count.

Both replay loops — startup and admin — drive the same object, so a new persist site can't be bolted on beside it and forget the hold.

## Verification

- `replayCursor.test.ts` — 7 behaviour tests (mocked writer) covering every scenario the review named: freeze-and-keep-fetching, the first-event pin, failure-behind-deferral, the cross-page breaker.
- `replayCursorPerType.test.ts` — updated to pin that neither loop holds a raw `recordEventCursor`; #67 coverage intact.
- `reactionDeferral.test.ts` 5/5 on a fresh DB.
- Pre-existing worktree tsc drift in `admin.ts` (commerce_orders columns, stale `@workspace/db` dist) is unrelated to this diff.

author: sehyun0518
body:
#27과 #30에서 내린 구조 결정이 커밋 메시지와 PR 본문에만 남았다. ADR로 옮긴다.

## 왜 필요한가

스킬 15개 중 **7개가 남의 저장소에서 복사해 온 것**이다. 문서 179개, 미러 두 벌까지
537개다. 그런데 벤더링 규칙이 어디에도 없어서 **세 번 어겼다.**

1. #24가 `markdownlint --fix`를 돌려 Vercel 파일 7개를 고쳤다. 지금도 main에 있다(#28).
2. #27에서 규칙 문서를 옮겨 적다 9개 중 5개를 건드렸다. 원본을 다시 받아 교체했다.
3. #27에서 "실행 코드 금지"를 근거로 에셋을 뺐는데 **그런 규칙이 없었다.** #30에서
   되돌렸다.

특히 3번은 기준을 한 번 뒤집은 것이라, 지금 상태로는 두 PR이 서로 다른 말을 하는
것처럼 보인다. ADR-0006이 "cursor 미러 하나 제거"로 남아 있는데 이번 건은 파급이 더
크다.

## ADR-0008 — 3자 스킬은 원본과 바이트 일치로 벤더링한다

결정 6개다.

| # | 결정 |
|---|---|
| 1 | 바이트 일치를 유지한다. 더하는 건 frontmatter·배너·`출처` 절뿐 |
| 2 | 고칠 것이 있으면 상류에서 고친다 |
| 3 | 서식 검사에서 제외한다 |
| 4 | `metadata.source`에 저장소·**브랜치**·경로를 적는다 |
| 5 | 실행 코드를 포함할 수 있다 |
| 6 | 가져오지 않은 것을 `출처` 절에 남긴다 |

**5번이 핵심 정정이다.** #27의 근거를 확인해 보니 ADR-0002는 하네스 자체의 실행 코드화
조건이지 스킬에 딸린 도구가 아니고, 스키마도 제약하지 않고, 생성기는 파일 종류를
가리지 않는다.

판단 기준을 **"실행 코드인가"에서 "그것 없이 문서가 성립하는가"로** 바꿨다. 그래서
`rspeedy-bundle-size`의 에셋은 가져오고(빼면 `SKILL.md`가 없는 파일을 가리킴)
`reactlynx-best-practices`의 스캐너는 안 가져온다(규칙 문서만으로 목적 달성).

2번에는 상류에 올릴 것과 안 올릴 것의 기준도 적었다. **명백한 사실 오류는 올리고
스타일 논쟁은 올리지 않는다.** [#142](`lynx-community/skills` PR 142)가
전자, 예제의 미선언 식별자 지적이 후자다.

4번의 브랜치가 중요하다. lynx-community/skills는 기본 브랜치가 `release`인데 `main`에는
같은 내용이 다른 경로에 있다. 적어두지 않으면 다음 동기화에서 다른 곳을 본다.

## ADR-0009 — 규칙 팩 선택은 실행 에이전트가 한다

`skillsOneOf`가 "실행 시 타깃 판별로 하나만 고른다"고 선언하는데 그 타깃을 읽을 곳이
없었다. 생성기는 전부 주입한다.

`target` 선언 필드를 두지 않기로 했다. 타깃은 이미 소비 저장소의 `package.json`에 있고,
프로파일에 다시 적으면 두 곳이 어긋난다. 모노레포는 저장소 단위 필드로 표현되지도
않는다.

대신 **각 `SKILL.md`의 상단 배너가 판별 근거를 소유한다.**

```text
react-best-practice       react + next / react-dom
react-native-skills       react-native / expo
reactlynx-best-practices  @lynx-js/react
vanilla-lynx              @lynx-js/rspeedy 있고 @lynx-js/react 없음
```

`skillsOneOf`(상호 배타)와 `skills`(항상 함께) 구분도 적었다. 레퍼런스 3종은 후자다.

## 두 ADR 모두 「현재 강제 범위」를 적었다

- **바이트 일치를 검사하는 도구가 없다.** 사람이 `md5`로 대조한다. 고쳐도 CI가 모른다.
- **검증기가 배너 존재를 검사하지 않는다.** #27에서 실제로 배너를 안 고치고 통과했고
  사람이 리뷰에서 잡았다.
- 벤더링 팩과 자체 제작 스킬을 구분하는 표식이 `metadata.author`뿐이고 검증기가 보지
  않는다.

기계 강제는 별건이라 이번 범위가 아니다. 무엇이 강제되지 않는지를 남기는 것이 목적이다.

## 리뷰 반영 2건

### 비교 범위가 정의되지 않았다 (`79446b8`)

"바이트 일치"라고만 쓰고 같은 파일에 frontmatter·배너·`출처` 절을 더하도록 허용했다.
그러면 `SKILL.md`는 **항상** 상류와 다르고, 정상 상태와 로컬 드리프트를 구분할 수 없다.
검증기를 만들어도 무엇과 무엇을 비교할지 정할 수 없다.

실제로 재보니 경계는 이미 깨끗했다. 문구가 그걸 표현하지 못했을 뿐이다.

```text
SKILL.md          일치 0 / 5
rules·refs·에셋   일치 64 / 64
```

파일을 세 종류로 나눴다.

| 종류 | 무엇 | 비교 범위 | 개수 |
|---|---|---|---:|
| A | `SKILL.md`가 아닌 모든 파일 | 파일 전체 | 64 |
| B | 상류 본문을 담은 `SKILL.md` | 마커 사이만 | 4 |
| C | 이 저장소가 새로 쓴 `SKILL.md` | 비교하지 않음 | 1 |

B는 상류 본문을 HTML 주석으로 감쌌다. 렌더링에 안 보이고 마크다운 의미도 안 바꾼다.

```markdown
<!-- vendored:begin -->
...상류 본문 그대로...
<!-- vendored:end -->
```

frontmatter는 따로 본다 — 상류 키는 값까지 같아야 하고, 더할 수 있는 키는 `license`와
`metadata` 둘뿐이다.

C는 `reactlynx-best-practices` 하나다. 상류 본문 8472B를 쓰지 않고 4057B로 다시 썼다.
그 사실을 ADR에 적고 **C를 최소화한다**는 원칙도 넣었다.

정규화 규칙도 고정했다. LF, 파일 끝 개행 하나, 마커 구간은 앞뒤 개행 하나씩만 벗김.
그 외 아무것도 하지 않는다.

### 주입과 선택을 뭉갰다 (`67c210f`)

ADR-0009에 "Lynx가 아닌 저장소에서는 에이전트가 고르지 않는다"고 썼는데, **계약이
보장하지 않는 것을 보장하는 것처럼** 읽힌다.

```jsonc
// profile.schema.json
"skills": { "description": "항상 함께 주입되는 스킬." }
```

```js
// generate.mjs — 조건 분기가 없다
target.skills.push(...(binding.skills ?? []), ...(binding.skillsOneOf ?? []))
```

웹 React 저장소에서도 Lynx 팩과 레퍼런스가 목록에 들어간다. **주입은 무조건이고 선택만
에이전트 판단이다.**

이 저장소가 계속 경계하는 것과 같은 실수다 — 프롬프트에 적는 것과 도구를 안 주는 것은
다르다.

결정 3을 다시 쓰고 스키마·생성기 근거를 넣었다. 조건부 주입을 안 넣는 이유도 적었다 —
조건을 쓰려면 타깃을 선언해야 하고 그건 결정 1이 거부한 것이다. 「대가」에 "목록이
저장소 종류와 무관하게 같다"를 추가했다.

## 확인

```text
21개 선언 파일 검증 통과
tests 15 / pass 15 / fail 0
Summary: 0 issues in 0 files
드리프트 없음
```

`README.md`의 결정 기록 표에 두 행을 추가했고 상대 링크를 전수 확인했다.

body:
## Summary

A bounded polish pass on `home/`, following the "v2.1" brief section by section — no rebuild, no new sections, every new visual replaces text rather than supplementing it.

- **Hero**: Canvas 2D particle typography -> a warm simplex-noise shader-mesh gradient plane (raw `three`, not React Three Fiber — see deviation note below), 18% opacity behind a scrim, frozen (not removed) under reduced motion, never mounted below 640px.
- **Section 01 (Problem)**: the text paragraph moves to `sr-only`; a side-by-side "Slop" vs "Anti-Slop" mock UI comparison carries the argument visually instead. The four real metric cards move below it as one row.
- **Section 02 (How it works)**: `RouterPanel` itself is untouched. Added a mock browser-chrome frame, a skill-group thumbnail, and a "narrowing the cost" token countdown — grounded entirely in `figures.*`/`skill.budget`, already-real numbers, never a new literal.
- **Section 03 (The Wall)**: `CheckerPanel` is untouched — **kept wired to the real `runRules()` engine**, not the brief's literal "hardcoded demo" instruction (confirmed with the user: faking the one thing on the page that demonstrates the pack's "verified rather than asserted" claim would be the exact defect this repo's own docs warn against). Added the shared browser-chrome frame, a 6-card CSS-only Mock UI Gallery (no React state per card), and the page's one signature scroll-driven moment — a `ScrollTrigger` pin where the default findings reveal in sequence.
- **Section 04 (Install)**: left as-is, per the brief's own read of it ("minimal is good") and this pass's "no net-new text" discipline.

## Deviation from the brief, verified against a real measurement

**Raw `three`, not React Three Fiber**, despite `skills/threejs-3d/SKILL.md`'s default ("write R3F, not raw Three.js"). An R3F build of this exact one-mesh scene gzipped to ~174KB — R3F's reconciler needs a generic catalog covering most of THREE's export surface to support arbitrary JSX tags, which defeats tree-shaking even for a single shader plane. That's more than 3x this pass's own ">50KB, find a lighter alternative" ceiling. A manual scene touching only the eight THREE classes it needs lands at ~118.5KB gz — still over 50KB (three's `WebGLRenderer` core carries an irreducible shader-compiler/program-cache cost no amount of tree-shaking removes short of hand-rolled raw WebGL, which is a materially larger, unauthorized rewrite outside this pass's scope). Reported here as a real, measured number rather than a guess — worth a follow-up call on whether ~118.5KB is acceptable given it's the page's only WebGL/shader background (`skills/animations/references/motion-budget.md` allows exactly one).

The pack's own `skills/threejs-3d/SKILL.md` constraint ids are followed by hand regardless of API: dpr capped at 2, geometry/material built once and disposed on unmount, OKLCH-sourced colour (never raw hex) in `THREE.Color`, delta-driven via `THREE.Clock` rather than a frame counter.

author: copilot
body:
`codeHighlighting: false` was not reliably excluding `ECodeBlock`/Shiki from Nitro builds under the `cloudflare-module` preset. The existing flag wiring only reached part of the server build pipeline, which left Cloudflare bundles pulling in Shiki artifacts.

- **What changed**
  - Extracted code-highlighting build flag setup into a dedicated helper.
  - Applied the flag to both Nitro config surfaces used during bundling:
    - `nitro.esbuild.options.define`
    - `nitro.replace`
  - Re-applied the same configuration inside the `nitro:config` hook so preset-specific resolved Nitro configs receive the flag as well.

- **Why this addresses the issue**
  - The module no longer depends on esbuild-only define propagation for dead-code elimination.
  - `cloudflare-module` now receives the same compile-time flag through Nitro’s broader replacement path, so `codeHighlighting: false` can exclude the Shiki-backed code path consistently.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Added a focused test for the build-config helper to verify:
    - the flag is written to both Nitro config locations
    - existing `define` / `replace` entries are preserved
    - existing esbuild targets are not overwritten

- **Example**
  ```ts
  export default defineNuxtConfig({
    nitro: {
      preset: 'cloudflare-module',
    },
    nuxtEmailRenderer: {
      codeHighlighting: false,
    },
  })
  ```

  With this change, that configuration propagates the `codeHighlighting` flag through Nitro’s resolved build config instead of only the initial esbuild define path.

author: tyz-works
body:
## 概要

`gh workflow run collect.yml -f promotion=njpw` を実行したところ、**自動マージ側のジョブが「PR を作る」で落ちた**。前回の実行で見つかった不具合の修正。

## 何が起きていたか

`--promotion njpw` を指定すると、自動マージ側のジョブは njpw を除外した結果「対象なし」となり、収集を実行せずに終わる（意図どおり）。ところがレポートが生成されないまま PR ステップに進み、こうなっていた。

```
##[error]File '.cache/report.md' does not exist.
```

さらに新日本のジョブは `needs: deterministic` で前段の失敗により **skip** され、**確認したかった LLM 抽出が一度も走らなかった**。

## 直し方

1. 収集したかどうかを `steps.collect.outputs.ran` に出し、していなければ「検証とビルド」と「PR を作る」を飛ばす
2. 新日本のジョブに `always()` を足す。順番のために `needs` は残すが、**片方の失敗でもう片方を止めない**（CLAUDE.md の「部分失敗を許容する」に合わせる）

## テスト方法

- ワークフローの YAML と各ステップの条件を確認
- 実際の確認はマージ後に `gh workflow run collect.yml -f promotion=njpw` を再実行して行う

前回の実行では Telegram 通知は成功していた（失敗時も飛ぶことは確認できた）。

author: oobles
body:
Closes #96.

Packaging, not release: `./gradlew publishToMavenLocal` now installs every module into `~/.m2` as
`io.ltr8:<module>:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`, with sources and javadoc jars, so a consuming build takes an ordinary
dependency instead of an included build.

```kotlin
repositories { mavenLocal(); mavenCentral() }
dependencies { implementation("io.ltr8:tson:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT") }
```

## Verified against a real consuming build, both ways

The jars carry real `module-info.class`es, so "does it work for a consumer" is two questions, and the
second was the open one:

- **class path** — resolve a schema, read a document, collect diagnostics: works.
- **module path** — the same consumer with its own `module-info` requiring `io.ltr8.tson` /
  `io.ltr8.tson.compiler` / `io.ltr8.tson.tree`, run with `mainModule` set, prints
  `module: demo.consumer / tson module: io.ltr8.tson / named=true`: works.

`tson-annotation` and `tson-regex` are `implementation` dependencies of the modules that use them, so they
reach a consumer's POM at runtime scope rather than compile. That is enough for both cases, and keeping
them off the compile classpath is the same call the module comments already make about what is public
surface.

## Deliberately no remote repository

Releasing needs signed artifacts, a POM with `scm`/`developers`, and a version that is not a snapshot —
and publishing under a name the project has not claimed is not something a build should start doing
quietly. The backlog item is rewritten to exactly that remainder rather than removed.

## Falling out of it

- **`./gradlew build` now runs javadoc for every module** (assemble builds the javadoc jars). The
  dangling-`{@link}` trap that used to pass locally and fail CI now fails locally, so CI's separate javadoc
  step is replaced by a `publishToMavenLocal` step — which exercises the publication itself, the one thing
  nothing else would catch.
- The README's exit-code bullet, stale since #90, now describes 70's two halves rather than only the bug one.

2035 tests green; `clean build publishToMavenLocal` clean; the CLI's `installDist` still works.

body:
### Motivation

- Add a new "Video reacciones" tab to visited user profiles that shows all the video reactions a visited user has shared, following the validated backend contract for `/api/users/<username>/activity/`.
- Ensure the tab fetches all pages of the mixed activity endpoint (not only page 1), shows items sorted newest→oldest, and keeps the UI behavior isolated to visited profiles without changing existing profile-feed behavior.

### Description

- Added a new client component `components/profile-feed/VisitedProfileVideoReactions.tsx` which iteratively follows the backend `next` links starting at `/users/<username>/activity/`, guards against loops with a `Set` of visited endpoints, collects only items where `activity_type === "video_reaction_created"` (and defensively checks `actor.username === username`), and finally sorts by timestamp descending before rendering.
- Integrated the new tab into `components/profile-feed/MyActivityColumn.tsx` (visited-profile branch only) and added the tab label and i18n keys; the tab appears between `Recomendaciones` and `Comentarios públicos` and is mobile-scroll-friendly in the single-row tab bar.
- UI/UX: the video reactions view uses a horizontal carousel with desktop arrow controls (disabled at ends) and native horizontal swipe/scroll on mobile; each card shows mini-poster (`movie.image` with placeholder), single localized title (via `resolveMovieTitles` using `useI18n` locale), formatted date (`formatProfileFeedRelativeDate`), and the vertical video (`payload.video_url`) preserving aspect ratio and playback constraints (`controlsList`, disable PIP/remote playback).
- Local state & invalidation: results are cached in the component state while the component remains mounted to avoid re-traversing pages on tab switch; the data is invalidated and reloaded when the visited `username` changes.

### Testing

- Ran `npm run lint` which completed with 0 errors and only preexisting `@next/next/no-img-element` warnings, so lint passed successfully.
- Type checking with `npx tsc --noEmit` passed with no errors.
- Ran the test suite with `npm test` and all tests passed (99 passed), including new regression tests added at `tests/visited-profile-video-reactions.test.mjs` that verify full-pagination traversal, loop protection, independent horizontal scrollers, and that the feature is isolated to visited profiles.
- `git diff --check` reported no problems; `npm run build` reached the Next.js build stage but the build failed in this environment due to network access needed to fetch Google Fonts (this is an environment limitation and not related to the feature logic).

author: robotphil
body:
## Summary

Adds `core/sdr/`: a direct ctypes binding to the RTL-SDR Blog `librtlsdr`,
a device-configuration value object, and a facade that opens, configures,
and reads raw IQ from an RTL-SDR. First of two PRs for Phase 2's Chunk D;
continuous streaming and the capture utility follow in the second.

## Related issues

None.

## Notes for reviewers

**No new dependency.** The device library decision was a hand-written
ctypes binding rather than pyrtlsdr or SoapySDR, and `ctypes` is stdlib.
This layer works in raw bytes, so numpy isn't needed either. The only
`pyproject.toml` change is widening the `integration` marker description
to cover the SDR as well as the rotator.

**Layering mirrors `core/rotor/` deliberately**, because the problem has
the same shape: `librtlsdr.py` is the thin wrapper (`SerialPort`'s role),
`device.py` the facade (`Rotor`'s role), `config.py` the value object.

**Opening an RTL-SDR Blog V4 through a library that cannot drive it is a
refusal, not a warning.** A V4 on a stock `librtlsdr` enumerates, opens,
and streams perfectly happily while tuning somewhere other than where it
was told — no error anywhere. The check is narrow: it fires only when the
EEPROM says Blog V4 *and* the loaded library exports `rtlsdr_set_dithering`,
which the Blog fork does not. It is one-directional and says so; absence of
that symbol doesn't prove the library is the Blog build.

**Two fields of `AppliedSettings` are echoed rather than read back** —
`manual_gain` and `agc_enabled` — because librtlsdr exposes no getter for
either. Documented in the class, since reading back is otherwise the whole
point of it. Everything else is what the hardware reported.

**Unit tests cannot verify the ctypes signatures**, because nothing in them
crosses a C boundary. That is what `tests/integration/test_sdr_hardware.py`
is for, and unlike the rotor integration suite it does configure the device
and read samples — tuning a receiver moves nothing and radiates nothing.
Verified against the real V4 before this PR was opened: 15 integration
tests, all passing, covering the ctypes signatures, the driver-directory
registration, and the gain-table fingerprint.

**`[sdr]` in station config is optional.** A station that only points an
antenna is a complete station, and every config file written before Phase 2
lacks the section. Gain, centre frequency, and sample rate are deliberately
absent from it: they change per satellite, so they belong to a profile.

## Checklist

- [x] PR title follows the `type: description` convention
- [x] Branch name uses one of the agreed prefixes (`feature/`, `fix/`, `docs/`, `refactor/`, `chore/`)
- [x] `uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format` pass
- [x] `uv run pytest` passes (or this PR is documentation-only)
- [x] New code in `core/` does not import from `ui/`
- [x] New behavior has unit tests in `tests/unit/`, or there's a note in "Notes for reviewers" explaining why not
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated under `[Unreleased]` if this is a user-visible change

author: sr2501
body:
Lands a day's governance findings that existed only in the coordinator's session state - which is what `docs/handoff.md` exists to prevent.

**Fifty-two findings became nine entries, five clauses, six backlog items and one handoff line.** Ten of the fifty-two were already in merged `main`; the lane checked rather than trusting the dump's own markers.

## The editorial call, which was the lane's and is better than mine

I asked for fewer entries. The lane found that entry count was never the problem: `risks.md` rows had become essays - R7 is a single 3,900-character table cell - in a file that renders as one unbroken wall. **Fifty-two entries nobody reads and nine essays nobody reads are the same artifact**, and that is the failure the register spends the most words on.

Hard length rule adopted: mechanism, consequence, remedy, at most one instance.

## What landed

- **risks.md R59-R63.** R59 is the spine - a check that examined an empty set and reported success, nine instances in one day across six sessions, **every one in the verification tool rather than the code**. Two limbs: the check observed nothing, and no check entered the code.
- **gates.md** - *prove a test reaches the code at all*, placed as the mutation bullets' missing precondition. Adapter gate gains raw-byte capture. Three new sections under *What gates cannot catch*, ending with **naming a defect class is not a mitigation** - which says plainly that it is the least reliable section in this repository, because it is the one part with no mechanism behind it.
- **Six backlog items** rather than prose, because a mechanism beats a rule.
- **Six `risks.md` rows repaired**: amendment prose had been sitting inside the Owner cell, so Mitigation rendered empty and Owner rendered as an essay. Verified: Owner cells of 800-4,800 characters before, none over 40 after.

## Verified independently before merge

- `git grep "app\.routes"` - **zero occurrences repo-wide**, so R59's repository-wide claim was narrowed to what it can support.
- Backlog: 128 headings, 128 unique slugs, 128 markers, 45/1/82. Slug set diffed against `origin/main`: **zero dropped, exactly six added.**
- Table structure: 63 rows, no row malformed by this change.

Gates: ruff format 165 files, ruff check clean, mypy 147 files, **pytest 1,339 passed**. Frontend gate stated not-applicable with its reason rather than left silent.

author: rancemxn
body:
## Summary

`Polyline` and `Polygon` were the two remaining fillable geometries whose stroke needs no
specification decision, so they close ahead of `Ellipse` and `RoundedRect`:

- Arc length is exact, because every segment is straight. The curved geometries wait on #528.
- The dash seam is the first declared point in declared order, so there is no #522-style
  ambiguity about where a closed subpath starts.
- Section 15.2 already fixes closure, the three join shapes with miter degrading to bevel at
  `miterLimit`, the three cap shapes, and zero-length segment handling.

This is also the machinery a `Path` stroke needs for its straight commands.

## Changes

- `crates/fcs-fcbc/src/writer.rs`: `Polyline` and `Polygon` join `Circle` in the arm that accepts
  a fill paint, a stroke, or both, and is rejected only when a node carries neither. `Rect`,
  `RoundedRect`, `Ellipse` and `Path` strokes stay rejected.
- `crates/fcs-render/src/semantic.rs`: `LocalShape::Polygon` gains `closed`, which only the
  stroke reads because fill uses the implicit closing segment either way. `stroke_polyline_contains`
  drops zero-length segments, accumulates exact arc length, tests each dash interval against each
  segment's rectangle, applies `cap` at every dash endpoint, and applies `join` at every vertex the
  stroke covers on both sides. `cap_contains` and `join_contains` are extracted so the join
  polygons reuse the existing `polygon_contains`.
- Two tests plus doc rebinding.

## Evidence

`polyline_stroke_joins_caps_and_closure_follow_section_15_2` uses a right-angle elbow whose outer
corner is exactly `(0.5, -0.5)` for a 1px stroke, which separates the three joins by construction:
bevel excludes `(0.45, -0.45)`, miter includes it, and round excludes it because it is `0.636` from
the vertex. A `miterLimit` of `1.4` degrades the miter back to that bevel, because a right angle has
`miterLength/halfWidth = sqrt(2)`. Round then includes `(0.2, -0.4)`, which bevel excludes, so no
two join shapes are conflated. The closed case asserts the implicit closing segment is stroked and
the open path's endpoints stop being endpoints, and the dashed case asserts coverage at exact arc
positions plus a square cap reaching past a dash end.

`canonical_polyline_and_polygon_strokes_reach_the_product_raster` asserts the Polygon covers
strictly more than the Polyline, which is the closing segment, and that a dash covers strictly
less. `canonical_rect_stroke_is_still_rejected` exists so adding two kinds cannot quietly widen
the writer to every fillable geometry.

Closes #529

author: robobun
body:
### Problem
- When a matcher registered with `expect.extend` carries a `toAsymmetricMatcher` property, a failing `toEqual` prints the custom asymmetric matcher as `"n": [object Object]toBeDivisibleBy [ 3, ]`.
- `ExpectCustomAsymmetricMatcher::custom_print` (`src/runtime/test_runner/expect.rs:2681`, removed here) looked up that property, then called the matcher itself in its place. The matcher returns `{ pass, message }`, which stringifies to `[object Object]`. It then returned `false`, so the caller at `src/runtime/test_runner/pretty_format.rs:2911` printed the default `<name> [args]` form as well.
- The Zig original (`ExpectCustomAsymmetricMatcher.customPrint`, #7319) had the same two defects. The hook has never produced correct output, and it has no types, no docs, and no Jest or Vitest counterpart.

### Fix
- Delete `custom_print` and its helper `maybe_clear`. The formatter prints the default form directly. The diff line becomes `"n": toBeDivisibleBy [ 3, ]`, with the `not ` and promise prefixes intact.
- Correct because a `toAsymmetricMatcher` property on the matcher function is ignored in Jest too: Jest and Vitest put the print form on the matcher instance, and `expect.extend` offers no user hook for it. The hook is dead native code with no user-visible behavior to keep. The repo guidance asks new user-reachable surface to ship complete (types, docs) or not at all, and a review of the first version of this PR found that enabling the hook as written would print `expect.not.x(3)` and `expect.x(3)` identically.
- This also removes a user JS re-entry from inside the formatter and an `.expect("unreachable")` around it.
- Verified: `test/js/bun/test/expect-extend-asymmetric-print.test.ts` (new file, one test, fails on stock bun 1.4.0). Also ran `expect.test.js`, `jest-extended.test.js`, `expect-extend-*.test.ts`, `pretty-format-overflow.test.ts`, `expect/huge-failure-message.test.ts`, and the three `test/regression/issue` files that use `expect.extend`.

### Background
- An asymmetric matcher is a value like `expect.any(Number)` that `toEqual` matches by a predicate. `expect.toBeDivisibleBy(3)` creates one for a custom matcher. Bun stores the matcher function and the captured args on a native `ExpectCustomAsymmetricMatcher` instance.
- When a diff or `this.utils.stringify` prints such an instance, `pretty_format.rs` writes the promise prefix, `not ` if negated, the matcher name, and the captured args array.
- Jest prints a custom asymmetric matcher as `[not.]name<args>` from a `toAsymmetricMatcher()` method that Jest itself generates on the instance. Bun's default form is `[not ]name [args]`. This PR does not change that form.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

- Repro on bun 1.4.0-canary.1 (4448a2e21) and on main at b30c6ff986:

  ```ts
  import { expect, test } from "bun:test";
  function toBeDivisibleBy(actual: unknown, divisor: number) {
    const pass = typeof actual === "number" && actual % divisor === 0;
    return { pass, message: () => `expected ${actual} to be divisible by ${divisor}` };
  }
  (toBeDivisibleBy as any).toAsymmetricMatcher = (divisor: number) => `DivisibleBy<${divisor}>`;
  expect.extend({ toBeDivisibleBy });
  test("x", () => { expect({ n: 7 }).toEqual({ n: (expect as any).toBeDivisibleBy(3) }); });
  ```

  Before: `-   "n": [object Object]toBeDivisibleBy [` / `-     3,` / `-   ],`. After: `-   "n": toBeDivisibleBy [` / `-     3,` / `-   ],`.
- The first version of this PR made the hook work (call `fn_value` instead of `matcher_fn`, return `true`). A self-review found that this enables an undocumented, untyped, Bun-only hook that nobody has asked for, and that the enabled form loses the `not` and promise flags, because `custom_print` never read them and the hook had no way to. Deleting the dead path is the smaller change and keeps no half-designed contract. If a maintainer wants a custom print form for `expect.extend` matchers, the complete version needs a `not`/promise decision, a `toAsymmetricMatcher?` member on `CustomMatcher` in `packages/bun-types/test.d.ts`, and a docs entry. That can be its own PR.
- `git show 90654143bb:src/bun.js/test/expect.zig` shows the Zig `customPrint` with the same call target (`matcher_fn.callWithThis`) and `return false`. The Zig instance-level `toAsymmetricMatcher` method was never exposed in `jest.classes.ts`, and the Rust port does not have it.
- `toAsymmetricMatcher` has zero hits in `docs/`, `packages/bun-types/`, and `src/js/`. No package in `test/node_modules` assigns the property to a matcher function.
- The test lives in its own Bun-only file, next to `expect-extend-asymmetric-match-throw.test.ts` and `expect-extend-matcher-utils-throw.test.ts`. `expect-extend.test.js` also runs under Jest and Vitest, where the default form differs, and its 10000-iteration GC test runs close to the 5 s limit on debug ASAN builds (#39359).
- Aligning Bun's default form with Jest's `[not.]name<args>` is a possible follow-up. It changes `.snap` files that hold custom property matchers, so it is out of scope here.
</details>

author: elanhasson
body:
`./scene` was missing. So were the other three.

```
$ ls apps/scene/scene apps/soundboard/soundboard apps/synth/synth apps/introtarget/introtarget
ls: cannot access 'apps/scene/scene': No such file or directory
ls: cannot access 'apps/soundboard/soundboard': No such file or directory
ls: cannot access 'apps/synth/synth': No such file or directory
ls: cannot access 'apps/introtarget/introtarget': No such file or directory
```

Beats **1.5**, **1.6** and **1.7** each host one of these, and 4.6–4.8 host `introtarget` three times over. Every one of them would have opened showing a red island instead of the app the beat exists to show — the failure mode `script.go` already describes as "has already caught two missing binaries", except that this time nothing caught it before a take.

## Why they were missing

They cannot be built by anything that runs today. Each guest is its own module, `go run ../scene` cannot cross that boundary, and the binaries are gitignored (`.gitignore:51,53,54,57`). The only mechanism was **prose**:

> **Before a run.** … 
> ```sh
> (cd ../intro       && go build -o intro .)
> (cd ../introtarget && go build -o introtarget .)
> (cd ../scene       && go build -o scene .)
> (cd ../soundboard  && go build -o soundboard .)
> (cd ../synth       && go build -o synth .)
> ```

A list of the deck's guests kept somewhere other than the deck, run by a human remembering to. It had rotted **in both directions**: four missing, and one entry — `intro` — that should not be there at all, because beat 3.2's `watchgo.sh` compiles that one itself on every change. Pre-building it is a second, staler copy of the exact thing that beat is about.

## `guests.sh` derives the set from the deck

A guest is a token in a `Cmd=` attribute of the form `./name` or `../dir/name` whose directory holds a `go.mod`:

```
$ sh guests.sh
  ..  introtarget
  ok  introtarget
  ..  scene
  ok  scene
  ..  soundboard
  ok  soundboard
  ..  synth
  ok  synth
```

Keying on `go.mod` rather than on the shape of the path is what excludes `./watchgo.sh` **without naming it** — a denylist there would be the thing this change deletes. `../intro/main.go` in the vim command is an argument rather than a binary and falls out for the same reason. Add a beat that hosts a new app and it is built unasked.

`NARRATION.md`'s block is now one line, and says why.

## Two derivations, required to agree

`guests_test.go` walks `NARRATION.md` again in Go and compares against what the script actually built — the same two-mechanism check `ci.yml`'s module discovery gets, and it *runs* the script rather than reading it, because a script that is read is one whose `sed` program is being reviewed instead of its answer.

Both halves mutated, not predicted:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| drop the `../dir/name` arm from `guests.sh` | `guests.sh builds [scene soundboard synth]; the deck runs [introtarget scene soundboard synth]` |
| re-add one `go build -o` line to `NARRATION.md` | `NARRATION.md:31 hand-writes a build command … That is a second guest list.` |

That second test earns its own name. Restoring the prose block would **not** fail the first one — it would sit beside `guests.sh` agreeing with it, until somebody adds a beat and updates one of the two. Now is the only cheap moment to catch that.

## What this does not do

It does not build the guests automatically when the deck starts. That would be a surprise during a take and would hide a compile error behind a spinner; the deck's existing behaviour — a red island naming the missing guest — is the better failure. What changed is that there is now a single command that makes it not happen, and a test that keeps that command correct.

## Verification

`go vet ./...` and the full `apps/introdeck` suite green. `gofmt` clean. `guests.sh` is `sh -n` clean and builds all four guests from a cold start.

author: esandu-meth-obadaarachchi
body:
Both COULD capabilities, built after the SHOULDs were finished and measured. 76 new tests, 404 total, `make verify-clone` green.

## M13 — per-person digests

Cross-source, uncapped, and **absent entirely for somebody with nothing approved** — enforced where digests are emitted, not by rendering an empty file. Both the document store and the `digests` table are asserted empty afterwards.

**Two people sharing a first name share a digest.** That was the instruction and it is defensible, but only because the cost is paid back in evidence rather than hidden:

- every line carries `owner_as_stated`, the string exactly as the transcript gave it
- the digest text says *"Grouped by first name, so this covers Priya Menon, Priya Sharma"*
- the interface badges the person and lists the aliases

`PERSON_IDENTITY=full_name` switches to the strict rule. Both are tested. A bare first name takes its full name from the meeting's participant list when exactly one participant matches, which is a metadata lookup rather than a guess; with two candidates it declines.

**Unowned work gets its own digest** headed "Assignee unspecified", where every line states the task and then says the assignee is unspecified. Dropping it hides real work, assigning it invents an owner.

## M12 — follow-up recap draft

**Rendered from the approved rows, not written by the model.** A model asked to summarise approved items produces sentences nobody approved: the reviewer approved a task description and a quote, and a paraphrase of five of those is new text that passed no gate. Costs no model call either.

Drafting is not gated — nothing leaves the machine and every line already passed the approval gate. **Sending is**, and `sent_by` is refused four ways:

| Depth | Mechanism | Refuses |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `followup/draft.py` | a blank name → 403 |
| 2 | `followup/draft.py` | `agent`, `system`, `scheduler`, `bot`, `service`, `llm`, `model` |
| 3 | `trg_followup_send_requires_person` | any UPDATE to `sent` with no `sent_by` |
| 4 | `trg_followup_agent_cannot_send` | any UPDATE to `sent` naming a service |

Five raw-SQLite tests drive the triggers with no application code in the path. The endpoint has no default for `sent_by` and a test asserts a request omitting it fails validation. One test is structural: **no file under `app/scheduler` mentions follow-ups at all**, because a scheduled job that sent a recap would pass every behavioural test and break the one rule M12 states.

## One real bug found on the way

**The test fixture redirected seven of the nine writable paths.** `notification_log_path` and `document_store_dir` were missing, so every test touching the notifier or the document store read and wrote the real files under `write_log/` and `data/documents/`. It surfaced only when a new test asserted no post had been made and saw 41 left by earlier manual runs — existing tests assert a post *exists*, which stays true whatever else is in the log. It also explains the generated files that kept appearing in `git status`.

## Documentation

- `docs/components/13-person-digests.md` and `14-followup-draft.md`
- `docs/architecture.md` — the send gate section, the data-flow diagram, recounted component lines with the counting command printed
- `docs/testing.md` — coverage table regenerated from `make test-inventory`, which had five files missing
- `decision_log.md` — Phase 10, 14 decisions, L31 to L34
- `README.md` — M12 and M13 marked Done with what each note actually claims

## Checks

- 404 tests pass, `make verify-clone` green from a clean clone
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` clean
- every relative link in every documentation file resolves

now prints the boundary on the card face.

**Live-proof strip (`live-proof.js`)** — audited, left unchanged. It already reads
the formal engine through `PDXReceiptCards.publicCardsFor()` filtered to the
`core` tier, already takes its verdicts from the shared engine rather than a seed,
already says "Built in this browser from roll-call votes this page loaded," and
already opens `#record=<pid>~<issue>`. It met every requirement of this task
before the task started, so touching it would have been churn.

## One figure, one source

The card's percentage and the profile's percentage were already the same call —
`PDXWordAction.read(pid).pct` behind `PDXProfileCard.brief()` — and the new tests
pin that rather than assume it. What was missing was the *story* around the
number. Lane detection and formal-story selection went into `profile-card.js`,
which already owns that one read, so the renderer still contains no reference to
`PDXWordAction` and hardcodes no verdict label. `brief()` gained a cheap
`lane` field (one `PDXExecRecord.eligible()` call); the more expensive
`formalStrip()` pick pass went into `read()`, which runs for the visible card
only. `read()` is still called exactly once per paint and `brief()` still stays
under its eight-call ceiling. Both hang off the existing derivation-epoch memo,
so a lazy roster merge or a vote warm invalidates the strip on the same boundary
that invalidates the number.

`brief()` also stopped computing vote coverage for executive-lane cards
(`var vc = (lane === 'exec') ? null : voteCoverage(pid);`). Today
`_pdxRecordMappedCounts('trump')` returns `null` anyway, so this changed nothing
in the current render — it is a fence that keeps a future data load from ever
printing "0 mapped votes on record" under a president.

## Before and after, against the profile

**Michael Guest (member lane), warm fixture — 18 roll calls across 6 issues.**

Before, the card showed `71% Direction match` and the coverage line, then
stopped. After, it shows the same 71%, the same coverage line, and beneath it
the profile's own standout block: 🏛 "What the record points to · 6 issues read ·
18 acts behind them", with chips for 🛡 Strong Border & Enforcement / "Supports"
/ "4 votes on file" and ✂️ Cut Federal Spending & Reduce Debt / "Mostly supports"
/ "4 votes on file". The profile's `PDXConsistency.recordStandout.html()` prints
the identical heading, the identical depth clause and the same two issues in the
same order; a test compares them directly rather than trusting the eye.

**Donald Trump (executive lane).**

Before, the card showed `71% Direction match`, a coverage line counting stances
and tracked pledges, and — while cold — the line "Pulling their voting record to
test what they have said." After, it shows the same 71%, the same coverage line,
and the profile's executive inventory: ✒️ "What the formal record holds · Of the
formal actions on file — 80 across 37 issues", then "8 laws signed · 4 vetoes ·
56 executive orders · 12 directives", then chips for 🛡 Strong Border &
Enforcement / "Acted on it" / "9 acts on file" and 🛢 Expand Domestic Energy
Production / "Acted on it" / "7 acts on file". These come from
`PDXConsistency.execRecordSummary.pick()`, the same source as the profile's
inventory, and are pinned against `execRecordSummary.html()` in test. An earlier
draft of the depth clause took the first two inventory entries and silently
dropped "56 executive orders" — the largest class — so the strip now renders the
volume clause and the full inventory exactly as the profile does.

The pending copy became "Reading their formal record to test what they have
said," which is true in both lanes.

## Loading, thin and empty

With a cold cache the card paints no percentage at all: `pct` is `null`, the
tested clause is empty, no `pdx-hs-sig-pct` element exists, and the face matches
no `\d\s*%` anywhere. A test asserts all four, so a regression that paints 0% or
a stale figure from an empty cache fails the suite rather than shipping. Below
the publishing floor (`MIN_TESTED_ITEMS = 3`, `MIN_TESTED_WEIGHT = 4`) the card
inherits the same `null` the profile shows, because it is the same value. The
formal strip is absent rather than invented when `recordStandout.pick()` or
`execRecordSummary.pick()` has nothing to say.

## Lane language

The member card carries no executive nouns. The executive card carries no
"mapped votes", no "Voted Yea", no "roll call", and `coverage.votes` is `null`
for it. Both are asserted against the actual painted HTML, not against the
source.

The public lane stays out of the headline percentage, and the hero receipt now
says so on its face: `Outside the score · statements & coverage` followed by
`Not in Direction Match`, printed between the verdict stamp and the byline.
`hero-receipt.js` runs deferred at index.html:4569 but `consistency.js` does not
load until line 20381, so `PDXConsistency.LANE_LABELS` is not available at draw
time; the two strings are mirrored as literals and the test extracts `OTS_LANE`,
`OTS_SUB` and `PUB_TAG` from the consistency.js source and compares them
byte-for-byte, so the mirror cannot drift.

## Link targets

Tapping the card body calls `showProfile(pid)` and then, on the established
~250 ms deferral, `window._pdxNavJump('pdxsec-standout')` — the profile's record
section, not the top of the page and not the ballot builder. If `showProfile` is
unavailable the card falls back to `#compare-hub` as before.

Tapping a formal chip stops propagation, pauses the rotation and sets
`#record=<pid>~<issue>` — the existing dossier hash, re-fired if it is already
current so the handler always runs. Every painted chip carries `data-pid` and
`data-iss`, which the test checks, and the test also confirms `pdxsec-standout`
is emitted by `consistency.js` and registered by `profile-spine.js`.

Keyboard Enter and Space route through the same `openProfile()` path as the
click.

## Payload and cache

`hero-showcase.js` is parser-blocking, so its cost is on the critical path. The
formal strip, the record landing and the issue door added about 1.4 KB gzipped,
most of it prose; seven comment blocks were trimmed to hold it down. The critical
path is now 1676 B of data plus 13797 B of renderer, 15473 B gzipped. The budget
assertions moved from 12.5 KB / 14 KB to 14 KB / 15.5 KB with the rationale
written into the test beside them. `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` went from `v64` to
`v65`.

## Suite

Green — 102 test files, exit 0. `scrip

author: obedkabakaba
body:
Les six espaces affichaient des analyses sans jamais permettre d'agir. Chaque menu concerné reçoit un bloc de gestion : liste filtrable, recherche, tri, pagination, export CSV, formulaire de création et de modification, soumission au circuit d'approbation.

## Le formulaire n'est pas écrit ici

Le serveur renvoie la description de ses champs — nom, type, obligatoire, bornes, valeurs acceptées — avec chaque liste. Redéclarer ces règles côté navigateur créerait deux copies de la même vérité, qui divergeraient à la première évolution : l'utilisateur verrait passer à l'écran ce que le serveur refuse.

Les messages d'erreur affichés sont ceux du serveur, champ par champ.

## Ce que l'écran ne fait jamais

Proposer une action que le serveur refusera. `peut_ecrire` vient de la réponse : un bouton « Créer » montré à quelqu'un qui recevra un 403 est un écran qui ment.

## Les analyses sont conservées

Les vues existantes répondent à « où en est-on ? » ; le bloc de gestion à « que fait-on ? ». Le bloc est monté dans `#zoneGestion`, jamais dans `#contenu` — les vues réécrivent ce dernier quand leur requête aboutit, et un bloc ajouté là serait effacé de façon intermittente. Le pire des défauts : celui qui ne se reproduit pas.

## Contrôles automatiques

Le site n'a ni build ni dépendances : rien à compiler, mais trois choses à vérifier.

**Syntaxe** — sans build, une parenthèse manquante ne se voit qu'à l'ouverture de la page, par l'utilisateur. Les 28 blocs de script sont analysés sans être exécutés.

**Palette** — contraste avec le fond, écart perceptuel entre séries adjacentes et entre toutes les paires, sur les deux thèmes, en CIE76 sur L\*a\*b\*.

Sa première version découpait le CSS sur `/(?=@media|:root)/` : un bloc `@media (…) { :root:not([data-theme="light"]) { … } }` se retrouvait coupé en deux, le morceau portant les couleurs perdait son contexte et était classé « clair ». Les deux thèmes rapportaient alors des valeurs identiques — le contrôle validait deux fois le même en annonçant qu'il en vérifiait deux.

Une fois corrigé, il a trouvé un vrai défaut : la série 4 (`#eda100`) n'avait que **2,17:1** sur fond blanc, sous le minimum WCAG de 3:1. Elle passe à `#d28300` — 3,01:1, et toujours à plus de 25 ΔE de ses voisines. Le seuil n'a pas été abaissé pour faire passer le contrôle.

**Secrets** — rien de sensible n'a sa place dans un dépôt servi publiquement.

## Vérifications

18 blocs branchés · parcours d'écriture exercé au navigateur sur trois espaces (champs décrits par le serveur, refus expliqué champ par champ, création, fiche, soumission) · 95 vues sans défaut · contraste et bascule de thème conformes dans les deux thèmes et aux deux largeurs.

⚠️ **Dépend du backend** : les blocs de gestion appellent `/api/ressources`, livré par la PR correspondante du dépôt backend. Fusionner celle-ci d'abord.

author: lordofbone
body:
### Motivation

- Ensure pull requests are validated against the current base branch and provide a lightweight required check so repository rules can require branches to be up to date before merging.
- Provide a fast, repository-wide Python syntax check that is cheap to run and easy to require as a status check.
- Cancel superseded runs to avoid wasting CI resources and limit permissions to least-privilege for safety.

### Description

- Add `.github/workflows/pull-request-checks.yml` which triggers on `pull_request` events.
- Configure `concurrency` with group `pr-checks-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}` and `cancel-in-progress: true` to supersede older runs for the same PR.
- Set `permissions.contents: read` and add a `python-syntax` job that uses `actions/checkout@v4` so the check runs against GitHub's synthetic PR merge commit and then runs `python3 -m compileall -q .` to compile all Python sources.

### Testing

- Ran `python3 -m compileall -q .` and it completed successfully.
- Parsed the workflow YAML with `ruby -e "require 'yaml'; YAML.load_file('.github/workflows/pull-request-checks.yml', aliases: true)"` which returned successfully.
- Ran `git diff --check` and `git status --short --branch` with no problems; `actionlint` was not installed so it was skipped, and an automated `gh pr create` attempt failed due to missing GitHub authentication in the environment.

author: ang-kl
body:
Operator: *"add the other languages for : privacy and legal"*.

## The reading, stated because it was ambiguous

The six languages were already in both strings and already merged in #1730, so the request could not mean that. Grep settled it — `privacy-html.js` opens with the comment *"Renders the i18n privacy.body string (**EN or FR**)"* and hardcoded its switcher:

```js
const altLang = lang === 'fr' ? 'en' : 'fr';
```

So **`/privacy?lang=ja` already served Japanese content** — `pickLang` and `tn` had handled that for versions — while the only link on the page said "Français", and six locales were unreachable from it. The strings had eight languages; the page offered two.

**And `/legal` had no URL at all.** One hosted route existed. The disclaimer, the liability limit and the takedown contact were reachable only as a chat command, so they could not be linked, cited in a reply to a takedown request, or opened outside Telegram.

## What shipped

- **Endonym switcher across all eight** — English, Français, Bahasa Indonesia, Русский, Deutsch, 中文, 日本語, Español. Same reason `language.btn.*` is left untranslated: a reader who cannot read the page they are on still has to be able to find their own language. Seven links per page, current locale excluded.
- **`<title>` and `<html lang>` localised per language *and* per page kind** — a Japanese legal page is `法的事項 — Soleat`, not `Privacy — Soleat`.
- **Markdown links now render as anchors.** `renderPrivacyHtml` converted `*bold*` only, so `legal.body` would have shown the literal `[linkedin.com/in/angadrian](https://…)` — the takedown contact route unusable on the very page it exists for. Found by rendering the page, not by reading the function.
- **`GET /legal`**, mirroring `/privacy`: `pickLang` → `tn('legal.body', lang)` → same renderer, same 5-minute cache.

## Verification

- `node --check` on `index.js` and `privacy-html.js` — clean.
- **All 16 pages rendered** (2 kinds × 8 locales): each begins `<!doctype html>`, ends `</html>`, carries the right `<html lang>`, and contains **no raw `](https://` markdown**.
- Switcher asserted per locale to equal `SUPPORTED` **minus the current one** — not merely non-empty.
- Unknown locale degrades to English chrome rather than throwing.
- `npx vitest run` — **174 files / 4,229 tests** (4,224 before; five added here).

## Please look at this before merging

**`/legal` is a new public URL.** It is one route rendering a string that is already public in the chat, but it is outward-facing, so it is flagged here rather than merged quietly.

Two further things named rather than left implied:

- The legal and privacy translations are **one reader's rendering — not a lawyer, and not a native review**, unchanged from #1730.
- `renderPrivacyHtml` still does not HTML-escape the body. It never did, and the sources are operator-authored rather than user input, so this change does not alter the exposure — but it should be a known property, not an assumption.

## Also records `[AMD-5]`

#1730 merged as squash **5aef0d3a** at 13:21:38 SGT. Verified on `main` by content (D-123): `privacy.body` and `legal.body` each return a **distinct** string for all eight locales — not the English fallback — and `[AMD-4]` is present. Gates re-run against the merged tree: live 1,835/1,836 safe, TMA 739 keys / 0 gaps / 0 failures, vitest 174 / 4,224.

On the retry you asked for, I also under-reported: the title and body update **had** landed; only the draft flag was still blocked by the rate limit, and you clicked it.

Still open and unchanged: register mixes du/Sie and tú/usted; the zh/ja example search terms in `cuisine.chat.webhookOnly`; `scripts/i18n-audit-jobs/` is stale; the three orphaned audit files remain (G2).

Anchor **13:25 SGT** per D-203 = `max(NEA 13:20, newest commit 13:21, system clock 13:25)`.

author: samson910022
body:
## Summary

Fixes a user-visible cold-start bug: **every cold start of the manager app showed a false "LSPosed module not enabled" dialog; closing and reopening showed the correct state.**

### Root cause (investigated by parallel agents, verified against bytecode)

`ActivityMain.onCreate` evaluated `App.mService != null` synchronously, but the LSPosed `XposedService` binder is delivered **asynchronously** via an inbound provider IPC (`SendBinder` → `XposedServiceHelper` → `App.onServiceBind`). On every new process the activity was created before the binder round-trip completed, so the one-shot check produced a false negative, showed the non-cancelable dialog, and skipped all UI setup. Nothing re-evaluated after bind — only reopening the app (warm process, binder already delivered) rendered correctly.

### Changes

1. **`App`** — thread-safe one-shot service-bound listener registry (`addOnServiceBoundListener` / `removeOnServiceBoundListener`): lock-guarded registration vs bind race (bind arrives on a Binder thread), listeners drained after token convergence so re-rendering consumers read aligned prefs, per-listener exception isolation with logging.
2. **`ActivityMain`** — replaces the immediate blocking verdict with a 3-second grace window (`awaitServiceBindThenResolve`): on bind, full UI initialization runs once; only if no bind event arrives within the window does the original non-cancelable "module not enabled" dialog appear. Single-resolution flag + main-thread serialization prevent double-init/dialog races; `onDestroy` cancels pending callbacks and deregisters its listener.
3. **`DiagnosticsActivity`** — registers the same listener when unbound at creation and re-renders on bind instead of freezing a stale "Module active: No" banner.

### Tests (closes three PR-review coverage gaps from the previous PR)

| Gap | Status |
|---|---|
| DiagnosticsProvider delegation ⚠️ Partial | ✅ arg-level integration tests verifying `call()` → `applyDiagnostics()` wiring with the new six-argument signature (context/method/extras/`callingUid`/`callingPackages` resolved via mocked `PackageManager`/`myUid`), success-flag propagation both ways via `mockConstruction(Bundle)` (android.jar Bundle is a stub under JVM tests), plus end-to-end remote-UID authorize/reject through the real store. Store singleton swap uses `sun.misc.Unsafe` reflection because JDK 17 forbids `Field.set` on static-final Kotlin object fields. |
| PixelifyModule.onModuleLoaded token provisioning ❌ Missing | ✅ via the public `attachFramework(XposedInterface)` seam: fresh UUID-v4 provisioning into remote prefs (asserts `commit()`, never `apply()`), keep-if-present, blank-string regeneration, swallowed framework failure, singleton publication. |
| App.onCreate/onServiceBind token lifecycle ❌ Missing | ✅ spy-intercepted self-calls: pre-bind `getOrCreateToken` into the local file store (UUID v4, commit-not-apply) and post-bind `convergeBroadcastToken` truth table (remote-wins divergence fix, local-mirror-to-empty-remote, both-agree no-op, swallowed failure with log-engagement proof). |

All new suites restore global state (`App.mService`, listener registry, `PixelifyModule.instance`, `DiagnosticsStore.INSTANCE`, static mocks) in teardown; final audit confirmed no vacuous assertions and no cross-suite pollution.

## Validation

- [x] I ran the relevant unit tests (`test`: 264/264 green, incl. 30 new tests across `AppTest`, `PixelifyModuleTest`, extended `DiagnosticsProviderTest`)
- [x] I ran `lintDebug` and `lintRelease` when Android sources or resources changed
- [x] I built the affected debug/release variants (`assembleDebug assembleRelease bundleRelease` green)
- [x] I updated user-facing documentation and translations where applicable (no doc claims invalidated; CHANGELOG is maintainer-owned at release time per CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I preserved package/Xposed identity consistency and upstream attribution (manifest/scope.list/version surfaces untouched)
- [x] I did not add credentials, signing material, generated artifacts, private logs, or local paths

Full release gate: `./scripts/with-android-env.sh ./gradlew --no-daemon --no-configuration-cache test lintDebug lintRelease assembleDebug assembleRelease bundleRelease` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
