author: runndownn
body:
## Purpose

Reassess the 2026-07-30 security report against the current repository, follow each control through supported composition instead of checking only for class/file presence, fix confirmed root causes, and align current security/architecture/status documentation with the resulting trust boundaries.

This PR is intentionally **draft**. GitHub Actions are disabled for this repository, so workflow YAML is not treated as execution evidence and no unobserved test, scan, image build, Caddy parse, browser run, Redis/PostgreSQL integration run, or private runtime check is represented as passing.

## Historical finding revalidation

The original twelve findings are retained as historical evidence in `docs/security/SECURITY_ASSESSMENT.md`. The current source-level result is `docs/security/SECURITY_REASSESSMENT_2026-08-22.md`.

In summary:

- JWT `jti`/revocation: implemented with bounded signed claims and shared Redis revocation in assurance environments; ordinary Bearer tokens remain replayable until expiry/revocation unless the deployment adds sender constraint.
- Distributed rate limiting: hardened to use shared Redis authority, trusted-proxy-only forwarding, hashed exact enforcement identity, no unauthenticated project-bucket selection, and fail-closed production behavior.
- CSRF: reclassified for the current explicit Bearer-header auth model; bound HMAC/double-submit protection remains for any future ambient cookie/session mutation path.
- Client error leakage: unexpected public errors are fixed/bounded; diagnostic redaction remains server-side.
- Historical Fernet key: active-tree secret removed/ignored; production rejects the development Fernet manager. Any value ever committed remains considered compromised.
- COOP/CORP/COEP, CORS, content-type validation, idempotency validation, and HSTS preload header: implemented in supported composition, with browser/domain runtime evidence still required where applicable.
- API audit: authentication and authorization decisions now persist to the hash-linked database ledger at the security boundary; required authorization-audit failure blocks protected work.
- Dependency scanning: repository tooling/manual lane and workflow/Dependabot definitions exist, but automated results are unavailable while Actions are disabled.

## New defects found and fixed during reassessment

### Shared request-admission state

- Trust `X-Forwarded-For` only when the direct peer is in private `WE3_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`.
- Keep exact normalized address for one-way enforcement identity while using only anonymized labels in logs.
- Prevent unauthenticated `X-WE3-Project-ID` from selecting a fresh pre-authentication bucket.
- Use collision-resistant Redis sliding-window members.
- Fail closed in staging/production when the distributed rate authority cannot decide.
- Give token-revocation endpoints a dedicated lower admission bound.

### OIDC / revocation

- Compose one application-lifetime authenticator instead of isolated per-request revocation state.
- Require bounded `jti`, `sub`, `exp`, and `iat` claims and restricted signing algorithms.
- Preserve revocation for the complete remaining signed token lifetime plus permitted skew.
- Normalize Redis security-authority errors so backend details do not become client errors.
- Keep the security claim precise: revocation is not cryptographic Bearer sender-binding.

### Authorization and audit

- Preserve exact workload role namespaces (`workload:*`) instead of stripping role prefixes.
- Give `system_admin` no implicit API superuser bypass; future administrative actions require explicit matrix grants.
- Route core validation/execution/read APIs through the same authorization matrix as extended APIs.
- Add request-scoped durable authorization allow/deny auditing before an allow returns.
- Distinguish compatibility best-effort audit logging from explicitly required fail-closed audit persistence.
- Add explicit `start` and `regrade` grants for intended evaluation-engineer/project-admin roles.
- Remove dossier-generation fallback from privileged `create:dossier` to generic export permission.

### Idempotency / operation safety

- Bind key + project + request-intent hash atomically in Redis for assurance environments.
- Reject same-key/different-intent reuse.
- Establish start-operation idempotency before creating process-local operation state, preventing ghost operations on backend failure/races.
- Preserve the explicit residual: synchronous operation state is process-local; durable long-running execution belongs to the PostgreSQL scheduler.

### Public ingress / deployment

- Require immutable operator-supplied image references and external mounted secret authority.
- Align production image dependencies with required Redis-backed security state.
- Keep only Caddy on published host ports.
- Overwrite forwarded client identity at the Caddy boundary.
- Block `/metrics`, `/ready`, `/openapi.json`, `/docs*`, and `/redoc*` on the public API site.
- Disable FastAPI interactive schema/docs endpoints in staging/production.
- Remove the public Prometheus Caddy route entirely; Prometheus remains internal on the observability network.
- Keep API/Caddy COOP, CORP, COEP, CSP, HSTS, frame/MIME/referrer/permissions/cache controls aligned.

## Regression contracts

Added/updated focused tests cover:

- trusted/untrusted proxy resolution and hashed rate keys;
- fail-closed distributed rate authority;
- Redis exception normalization;
- bounded token identifiers and revocation lifetime;
- exact CORS/preflight and `If-Match` behavior;
- malformed idempotency metadata before route side effects;
- exact workload-role identity and no implicit `system_admin` authority;
- authorization audit allow/deny and failure behavior;
- explicit experiment `start`/`regrade` grants;
- dossier authority without generic-export fallback;
- start idempotency replay without duplicate operation creation;
- concurrent audit-chain behavior;
- immutable images, mounted secrets, internal networks, no public Prometheus route, public diagnostic denial, and Caddy forwarding identity.

The manual security lane now includes the API authorization contract suite.

## Documentation alignment

Updated current documentation includes:

- `docs/security/SECURITY_REASSESSMENT_2026-08-22.md`
- `SECURITY.md`
- `docs/security/PRIVATE_RUNTIME_ASSURANCE.md`
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `docs/STATUS.md`
- `docs/README.md`
- `CHANGELOG.md`
- `.env.example`

GitHub Actions are disabled, so no current CI result exists for this branch through the repository workflow system. The repository-owned manual contract is:

```bash
make install-security
make lint
make security-check
make test
make coverage
```

These commands are requirements, not claimed results in this PR. Production approval additionally requires the private runtime-assurance sequence for exact image digests, Caddy/Compose, OIDC lifecycle/revocation, trusted proxy CIDRs, Redis failure behavior, PostgreSQL audit behavior, browser/CORS/header compatibility, TLS, egress, direct-port/Prometheus denial, and the exact release's recovery controls.

body:
## Claim

Repair the two remaining live integration drifts from #11695 without widening merge gates or changing product behavior:

1. regenerate and semantically validate the non-Rust inventory;
2. make the checkout-pin contract survive future pin bumps and catch incomplete sweeps across the established action-pin authority.

The other documented failures were already repaired upstream and are not reimplemented here.

## Authority boundary

The checkout invariant scans executable YAML under `.github/workflows` and `.github/actions`, matching the repository's action-pin provenance authority. It parses YAML `uses` values, ignores comments/prose, requires at least one checkout use, requires every reference to be a full 40-hex SHA, and requires all executable checkout uses to share one SHA. The provenance ledger remains the authority for the verified action version; this test does not perform network resolution.

## Verification

At final head `183ca5e684ca9725ba033a59e9c11e229b1fae7d`:

- `cargo test -p xtask --locked --test agent_capability_gate_workflow_policy`: 5 passed, including the symlink-loop regression;
- `cargo fmt -p xtask -- --check`: clean;
- targeted Clippy for the policy test: clean;
- diff and worktree hygiene: clean;
- executable scan: 132 checkout uses share the provenance-ledger SHA; four additional checkout-looking occurrences are comments and are intentionally excluded.

The candidate also retains the inventory regeneration and focused proof from the parent head. Hosted checks are being re-evaluated for this final SHA.

## Scope and limitations

- No production source behavior, dependency, inventory authority, or merge-gate policy is changed.
- The invariant proves immutable full-SHA shape and uniformity, not that an arbitrary 40-hex value resolves on the network; remote commit existence is a separate hardening concern.
- The full xtask suite contains unrelated current-main/control-plane failures already owned elsewhere; they are not silently absorbed here.

## Review map

- `docs/policy/NON_RUST_INVENTORY.md`: regenerated non-Rust inventory.
- `xtask/tests/agent_capability_gate_workflow_policy.rs`: structured checkout scan and fail-closed controls.
- `.github/actions/setup-perl-lsp/action.yml`: remaining action-pin straggler repaired in the parent candidate.

Fixes #11695

author: jjang-ai
body:
## Measured, not reasoned about

Two 70 KB entries under a 300 KB cap, then one 430 KB store:
`currentEntryCount` went **2 → 0**.

## Why

The store path writes the payload, indexes it, then runs the quota pass, which
evicts oldest-first until the total is back under the cap. For a single entry
`E` larger than the cap `C` with `others` already resident:

    excess = others + E - C

Evicting every other entry accumulates only `others`, and `others < excess`
exactly when `E > C` — so the loop kept going and evicted `E` too. Worst of
both outcomes: the oversized file written to the SSD and immediately deleted,
**and** every previously cached boundary deleted with it.

## Fix

Decide on the **measured** file size, not an estimate from `nbytes` — the
serializer may quantize or compress, so an estimate could drop a store that
would in fact have fit. Costs one write that was going to happen anyway, and
leaves the cache intact.

This is not a cap on what a caller may do: the request has already produced its
output, and an entry the existing quota pass would delete microseconds later is
not being taken away from anyone.

## Reachability — stated plainly, because it matters

**This hole is NOT on the shipping path.** `CacheCoordinator` passes
`enforceQuota: !usesCombinedQuota`, and `usesCombinedQuota =
config.enableDiskCache` — so whenever the disk cache is on, the combined pass
owns the quota, and that path already refuses an oversized newest boundary
while keeping the prior fitting prefix
(`combinedQuotaRejectsOversizedNewestBoundaryButPreservesPriorFittingPrefix`).

What this closes is the public `store(tokens:arrays:mediaSalt:)` surface, which
enforces `DiskCache`'s own quota and had no such protection. Real, measured,
and worth closing — but **defense in depth, not a live user-facing bug**. I am
not going to describe it as more than it is.

## Tests

`swift test --filter "uota|DiskCache|iskCache"` → **60/60 in 3 suites**,
including the inverted characterization
`aSingleOversizedEntryDoesNotWipeTheRestOfTheCache`, which asserted the wipe
before the fix and asserts the survivors after it.

Note this repo's `pull_request.yml` is gated on
`github.repository == 'ml-explore/mlx-swift'`, so every job reports *skipping*
on this fork — the local run above is the only gate there is.

author: tms-minhtang1
body:
Moving CI to `merge_group` left pull requests with no checks at all, and the queue merged one without running anything. Two facts, found by testing rather than reading:

- GitHub makes the merge queue wait only on checks the ruleset marks **required**. With no required check, the queue merged an entry immediately — zero `merge_group` runs.
- With a required check, `enqueuePullRequest` refuses the pull request outright: `Pull request Required status check "checks" is expected.` The check has to have passed **on the pull request** before it can be queued.

Together: the check runs on `pull_request`, or it never runs. A queue can only re-verify what already passed; it cannot be the only place a check runs. The merge-queue rule has been removed from the ruleset, which is back to the four rules it had before.

The waste that motivated the move is handled where it belongs:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
```

Three commits pushed in a row spend one run instead of three. Runs on `main` are never cancelled — each records a commit that landed. `workflow_dispatch` stays, for a branch with no open pull request.

The context-cost comment and the `pull-requests: write` it needs come back with the trigger.

**Verified locally**:

```
check.sh        80 passed · no duplication · clean on 3 vendor(s)
scanner         high:0  Final Score: 85
listing gate    True
```

This pull request produces its own CI run — the merge ref carries the restored trigger — so it proves the fix rather than asserting it.

`hol-plugin-scanner.yml` is untouched. It fails at startup because its vendor action is not a Marketplace verified creator and is not on the repository allowlist, and that is fine: the awesome-ai-plugins gate reads the file for the `uses:` and the trigger, never the run, and the catalog scores this repository from its own runner. Nothing downstream needs it to execute.

author: clutch-tim3
body:
Three commits: things reported against real packs, `SBD_COMPLIANCE.md`, a
production 503, and `Comprehensive_Tender_Document_Training_Guide.pdf`.

**1503 tests pass.** All three deployed and verified live: health all-true,
`claude-sonnet-5` resolving against the real API, memory at 2Gi, and
`/api/autofill/providers/status` returning 401 instead of the 500 it had been
returning on every request.

| commit | |
|---|---|
| `cf7b13f` | Ask when unsure, catch what disqualifies a bid, stop drawing on the form |
| `157cdba` | Stop holding every page of a pack in memory |
| `6f4d6bc` | "N/A" beats a blank, and the pack's own forms beat the current template |

## The red marks came off the form

> "i dont like the exclamation marks that it puts on fields it cant answer it
> ends up staying on the hard copy so no red exclamation marks remove that
> feature."

The SBD 4 page shows why: nine `[ ! ]` stamped down the Identity Number column
of a table that is **correctly empty** — no director is employed by the state,
so there is nothing to declare. Printed and handed to an organ of state, that
is a statutory form that looks defaced.

Removed from the PDF and .docx paths. Every refusal is still recorded, still
listed in the review, still blocks an export where it did. Verified on the
145-page pack: **269 refusals recorded, 0 marks on the page.**

## Being unsure is now a reason to ask

> "the address line was not filled i keep telling you the agent needs to ask me
> if its not certain, postal address or physical address"

Two things were blocking that question:

- `missing_profile_fields` only built questions from `"Nothing on file"`
  refusals. A bare `ADDRESS` is not that — both values are held; only the
  choice is missing.
- `_outstanding_rows` filters `advisory = 0`, and `ambiguous_label` is
  advisory, so the row never reached the builder anyway.

One flag was answering two questions: *must a person tick this before export?*
(no) and *is this worth asking about?* (yes). Now separated.

Questions carry a `kind` — `supply` (no value held) or `which_one` (value held,
question unknown). New tool `autofill_resolve_label` records the answer;
`update_company_profile` was wrong for it because nothing is missing from the
profile. It goes to `learned_labels`, so the question is asked **once ever**.

## Four reasons fields were left blank

On MBD 3.1, four blanks with every value already on file. Three now fill:

| blank | why it was empty |
|---|---|
| `Name of Bidder............` | the word fused to its dot leader, so the label arrived as `"Name of"` |
| `in my capacity as ______` | the SBD signature block runs its question *through* the blank; lower-case start was discarded as prose |
| `______(company name)` | the underscores are 0.72pt rectangles, not characters — nothing saw them |
| `I (full name) ______` | still blank — a personal name |

The dictionary now outranks the capitalisation heuristic, but on an **exact**
alias only. A test caught the first version letting `"representative of
(tenderer)"` through — the fuzzy matcher scores it 95 against `contact_person`
on the strength of one word.

## Claude is asked what a label means

One batched call per pack, on Sonnet 5, quoted as untrusted content because
tender labels are third-party text. It returns a **meaning, never a value**, and
any field it names goes through `is_blocked` and `SAFE_FILL_FIELDS` unchanged —
the module imports neither, and a test parses its AST to prove it. Answers are
cached, so a label costs one call in its lifetime.

On the 145-page pack: **129 "I could not tell what this field is asking for"
became 2.**

## SBD_COMPLIANCE.md

**P0-2** — The preference system is **read off the form**, not derived from
tender value against the R50m threshold. That threshold is what an organ of
state *should* pick, not what this tender *says*, and a Level 1 bidder claims
20 points under 80/20 and 10 under 90/10. The Johannesburg Water pack states
both (the buyer never deleted one), so it asks. Every pack also carries SBD
6.1's boilerplate explaining both systems, so keyword matching would have been
confidently wrong on all three.

The goals table could not be filled "from the four `owned_51pc_*` columns" as
the brief asks, because **every tender writes its own goals** — this pack wants
Historically Disadvantaged Individuals, Local Production, Locality. A row is
claimed only where a stored flag is strictly **narrower** than the goal, making
the implication airtight: 51% black-women-owned *is* 51% women-owned.

`owned_51pc_black` → HDI is **refused**. HDI is a defined term that black
ownership overlaps without being, and claiming three points on that reasoning
is a misrepresentation to an organ of state. A `False` flag asks rather than
declining — 51% white-women-owned is still women-owned.

**P0-3** — Closing dates extracted from all three real packs. With no closing
date found, nothing is compared: falling back to today would silently clear a
certificate that expired before the tender closed.

**P0-1** — The same fact written two ways across forms, a named
disqualification cause. Formatting differences are not conflicts, or the real
ones drown.

**P0-4** — A pre-export summary leading with what would disqualify the bid. On
this pack: 42 signature lines with their pages, in reading order. Counted from
the refusal **record** rather than `[ ! ]` marks, since those are gone — and the
record was always the real source. It reports and never refuses;
`export_reviewed` stays the only thing that blocks an export.

---

# `157cdba` · The production 503

> "im getting a server refused error frequently when i submit certain tender
> packs"

Every 503 in the Cloud Run log is `/api/autofill-packs/<id>/submit`, each paired
within seconds by `Memory limit of 1024 MiB exceeded with 1101 MiB used`. Cloud
Run killed the container mid-request, so the browser got a 503 with nothing to
explain it. The 19–28s latencies are Starlette background tasks: `process_pack`
runs before the ASGI call returns, so the whole fill happens inside the request.

pdfplumber caches every object it derives for a page and holds it for the life
of the PDF. Extraction never needs a page again once its blanks are collected.
On the real 145-page pack:

| | peak | retained |
|---|---|---|
| before | **573 MB** | 195 MB |
| after `flush_cache` | **64 MB** | — |

Same 353 blanks. **One of the two hogs was mine** — the goals-table scan added
in `cf7b13f` walked every page calling `find_tables()` and cost 198 MB. Memory
also raised 1024 → 2048 MiB, as headroom on top of the fix, not instead of it.

**Second bug found in the same logs:** `/api/autofill/providers/status` had been
returning **500 on every request** — `type "blob" does not exist`. Postgres has
no BLOB, and `provider_tokens.token_ciphertext BLOB NOT NULL` runs on every call
to that endpoint. `agent/db.py` translated `?`, `AUTOINCREMENT` and `DATETIME`
but not `BLOB`. Now `BYTEA`.

Neither bug was catchable by the suite as it stood: every extraction fixture is
one or two pages where the cache costs nothing, and the whole suite runs on
SQLite, which accepts `BLOB` happily.

---

# `6f4d6bc` · The training guide

## Golden rule 1 — complete every field, use "N/A"

CairoAI left them blank and `is_sentinel` read `"N/A"` as *absent*. The profile
cannot tell these apart, since both are an empty column:

| | correct answer |
|---|---|
| "we are not VAT registered" | **N/A** |
| "nobody has told CairoAI the VAT number" | **N/A would be a false statement** |

So nothing is inferred from absence. New tool `autofill_mark_not_applicable`,
called only after the user answers.

**A test stopped this widening the blocklist.** `director_names_and_id_numbers`
was declarable — a sole proprietor has no directors. But `"Name of State
institution"` maps to it, and that cell is in SBD 4's *sworn* declaration.
`is_blocked` catches that label only with document context, which `pdf_filler`
does not pass. It would have w

author: avpavlo8
body:
## Итог расследования

Восемь релизов подряд не доезжают до прода. Последний успешный деплой — `d7dd6cc` от 21 августа, 10:15; `ficusin.ru` до сих пор отдаёт именно его.

Лог деплоя не меняется:

```
Container started
Waiting for container healthcheck to pass
Health status: starting
<ровно 180 секунд>
Deploy failed
```

Три проверки, каждая исключает свою причину:

1. В логах того же контейнера — `bootstrap health endpoint started`, затем `api ready`. Приложение поднялось, порт слушает, миграции прошли.
2. В консоли контейнера на этой же платформе: `uid=65532`, `curl 127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/health` → `200`. Loopback живой, права те же. Значит не сеть.
3. PR #200 заменил пробу на чтение `/proc/net/tcp` — проверка, которая физически не может упасть, пока процесс слушает порт. Деплой откатился так же, на той же 180-й секунде.

Остаётся один вывод: Timeweb не читает результат docker healthcheck пересозданного контейнера («Recreating container with discovered ports»). Пока `HEALTHCHECK` в образе есть, ни один релиз не доедет до прода — что бы в нём ни было написано.

## Что меняется

`HEALTHCHECK` убран из образа. Job `image` в CI больше не ждёт `docker inspect ... Health`, а опрашивает `/api/v1/health` снаружи контейнера и требует `{"status":"ok"}` — то есть завершённые миграции и полностью собранный роутер, а не просто живой процесс. Проверка стала строже прежней: раньше засчитывался любой ответ 200, включая `{"status":"starting"}`.

Готовность после этого проверяется трижды и всегда снаружи, как её видит покупатель: Timeweb опрашивает `/api/v1/health` (путь задан в настройках приложения), CI поднимает production-образ, `Production smoke` бьётся в живой сайт после мержа.

## Побочное

Пока деплой откатывался, неудачные старты успевали применить миграции 055–058 к боевой базе, а под трафиком остался бинарник `d7dd6cc`. Отсюда `list category attributes failed` в логах и 503 на `GET /api/v1/admin/categories/{id}/attributes` прямо сейчас. Успешный деплой это закрывает.

Отдельно стоит написать в поддержку Timeweb: гейт по healthcheck у них не работает, и это стоило магазину суток простоя релизов.

author: worker-ants
body:
## 무엇을 고쳤나

`sanitize-error-message.spec.ts` 의 `caps recursion depth` 테스트는 `not.toThrow()` 하나였다. 두 가지로 vacuous 했다:

- **상한 값을 판별하지 못한다.** 10 을 1 로 바꿔도 GREEN 이다.
- **스택 회귀로서도 크기가 작다.** 25겹은 상한이 아예 없어도 안 터진다.

프런트 스캐너(`masked-markers.test.ts`)는 `nest(10)→true` / `nest(11)→false` 로 그 자리를 정확히 고정하는데, **마커를 놓는 쪽**이 고정돼 있지 않으면 두 상한이 어긋나도 아무도 모른다 — 스캐너 상한이 더 작으면 그 차이만큼 가드가 조용히 뚫린다.

## 델타 실측 — "위험 낮음" 은 틀렸다

트래커의 유예 근거는 *"실질 위험 낮음: `codebase/packages/**` 변경이 양쪽 워크플로에 relevant 라 프런트 경계 테스트가 같은 PR 에서 돈다"* 였다. **반증됐다.**

프런트가 무는 것은 **SoT 상수 값**의 변경뿐이다:

| 뮤테이션 | backend | frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_MASK_DEPTH` 10 → 9 (SoT 상수) | GREEN (심볼 참조라 따라옴 — 정상) | **RED** |
| `depth >= N` → `depth >= N - 1` (비교식만) | ? | 볼 수 없음 |

상수는 그대로 두고 **마스커의 비교식만** 어긋나는 방향은 프런트가 원리적으로 못 본다. 실측: **변경 전 spec + 효과적 캡 9 뮤턴트로 backend 전체 430 스위트 / 8,896 테스트가 전부 GREEN.** 위험이 낮았던 게 아니라 **아무도 안 보고 있었다.**

> 교훈: *"다른 가드가 덮는다"* 는 유예 근거는 **그 가드가 무는 변경의 방향**까지 세어야 성립한다. 값 하나만 보는 가드는 그 값을 쓰는 **식**의 변형을 못 본다.

## 추가한 경계 8종

전부 `MAX_REDACT_DEPTH` 를 import 해서 쓴다 — 리터럴 `10` 을 박지 않았으므로 SoT 가 움직이면 테스트가 따라온다.

| 단언 | 무엇을 가르나 |
| --- | --- |
| 상한 깊이 서브트리 → `'***'` | 상한이 커지면 RED |
| 상한 −1 서브트리 보존 | 상한이 작아지면 RED |
| 상한 깊이 **문자열 잎**은 그대로 | 값 검사 ↔ 깊이 검사 **순서** 뒤집으면 RED |
| 그 자리의 비밀 문자열은 가려짐 | fail-closed 방향 |
| 배열 / 객체↔배열 혼합 | 두 재귀 분기의 보폭 동일 |
| JSON 문자열 잎 | 세 번째 재귀 진입점(`depth + 1`) |
| 5000겹 no-throw + 산출물 형태 | 상한 제거 시 `RangeError` (25 → 5000 으로 유계화) |

`VALUE_MASK_MARKER`(`'***'`)를 기대값으로 적어, 이 경로가 `DEPTH_MASK_MARKER` 를 쓰지 **않는다**는 사실도 캐너리로 고정했다. `MAX_SANITIZE_DEPTH`(WS, `>`)·`stripExternalOnlyFields(maxDepth)`(`>`)는 별개 불변식이라 손대지 않았다.

## 뮤테이션 실측 — 생존 0/9

커밋 후 `cp` 백업으로 원복하며 9종을 걸었다(`git checkout`/`reset --hard` 미사용).

| 뮤턴트 | 결과 |
| --- | --- |
| M1 상한 −1 (효과적 캡 9) | RED (6건) |
| M2 상한 +1 (효과적 캡 11) | RED (5건) |
| M3 `>=` → `>` (off-by-one, fail-open) | RED (5건) |
| M4 **값 검사 ↔ 깊이 검사 순서 뒤집기** | RED (3건) |
| M5 상한 자체 제거 | RED (5건) — 5000겹이 `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` 로 죽는 것까지 확인 |
| M6/M7 배열 분기 보폭 0 / 2 | RED (각 2건) |
| M8 객체 분기 보폭 0 | RED (4건) |
| M9 JSON 재진입 보폭 0 | RED (1건) |

원복 후 소스가 원본과 **바이트 동일**함을 단언으로 확인했고 76/76 GREEN 재확인했다.

## plan 위생

`/ai-review` 체크박스만 미완이던 두 plan 을 정정하고 `plan/complete/` 로 옮겼다. 판정은 에이전트 서술이 아니라 **머지 커밋의 `review/code/**` 산출물**로 했다:

- `masked-marker-shared-package.md` — PR #1190, `/ai-review` **9라운드** (세션 9개가 `3f8543eae` 에 있다)
- `mirror-guard-single-copy.md` — PR #1191, `/ai-review` **2라운드** (`14_02_49`·`14_26_47` 가 `7b0e65aa8` 에 있다)

둘 다 `status: complete` + Gate C `spec_impact` 선언 확인, 상대링크 정정. `plan-frontmatter.test.ts` 153건 통과.

> `git mv` 가 인덱스에 **HEAD 판 내용**으로 rename 을 올려 편집이 빠지는 함정을 한 번 밟았다(`0 insertions`). `git show HEAD:<path>` 로 잡아 amend 했다.

## 검증

- TEST WORKFLOW 4단계 전부 PASS — lint / unit(backend **8,903** = 8,896 **+7**, frontend 6,101, web-chat 451, packages) / build / e2e(backend supertest **276** + playwright **51**)
- 타입체크 ratchet: 199건 / 38파일 — baseline 일치
- `/consistency-check --impl-prep` (`15_35_56`) — BLOCK:YES 였으나 CRITICAL 이 **diff 없는 상태에서 브랜치명으로부터 추정한 예방적 판정**이고 요구 조치가 전부 "착수 전 확인" 이라, 8개 항목을 실제로 수행하고 SUMMARY 하단에 처분표를 남겼다

### 리뷰 처분

author: abiggerhammer
haribo
body:
## Summary

- `file.replace` built a sed expression out of its own arguments, so the value was not written, it was interpreted. `&` means "the whole matched line" in a replacement and `|` was the delimiter: `file.replace(path, "URL", "https://a&b")` landed as `URL=https://aURL=oldb`, and a value holding `|` failed the run outright. The corrupted line never satisfies the `grep -qxF` observe, so apply re-ran and re-corrupted the file on **every** run.
- The apply now pipes both arguments through `awk` / `ENVIRON`: nothing the caller passes is parsed as syntax. It is staged the way `file.write` is (`cp -p` then `mv -f`), so the destination is never half-rewritten and keeps its mode and owner. One pass replaces the first matching line and drops the duplicates `s|^K=.*|…|` used to leave behind.
- The key is literal now too. The observe was already literal (`grep -qxF`) while the apply treated it as a regex, so a key holding `.` rewrote neighbouring lines.

Not fixed here, and stated in a comment on the def: a `=` in the key or a newline in either argument still gets through. Refusing them belongs in `check`, which can only compare with `==` — the only available spelling was a shell round trip to the target to validate a string the control host already holds, which contradicts ADR-0034 §5 and defeats the unit fakes. Tracked as #492.

## Test plan

- [x] `internal/std/file_test.go` — `TestFileReplace_SurvivesSedMetacharacters`, 6 cases against a **real shell** (`&`, `|`, `/`, `\1`, a `.` in the key, and the append branch). 4 of them were red before the fix; a fake executor would have passed against the broken version.
- [x] `internal/std/file_test.go` — `TestFileReplace_Contract`: creates an absent file, keeps one line instead of sed's duplicates, preserves mode `600`, leaves no staging residue, refuses an empty key.
- [x] `test/e2e/plans/coverage.shellf` — a value carrying `&`, `|` and `/`. Against the container: run 1 `ok.set`, run 2 `ok.already`, so the exact line is on the machine.
- [x] `SHELLF_E2E=1 bash test/e2e/run.sh` — full harness PASS.
- [x] `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go build ./...`.

`internal/std/std_test.go` changes two literals: `TestDeployDefs_TruthyAndValue` identifies the apply by the text of its shell (`applyMatch: "sed"` / `"printf"`), and this apply uses neither. What the test asserts is unchanged.

Closes #487

## Summary

Fixes #1608 — `test_retrieval_multi_session_evidence` (sparse-pinned by R3 #1605) failed in CI with `turn_recall@5 = 0.0`.

### Root cause
`mini_msr_002`'s evidence turns rank at 0-indexed positions 4 and 8 under sparse-only TF-IDF. The k=5 assertion (`>= 0.5`) was marginal — the second turn was never even asserted (only "≥0.5 of two" = one turn). Under CI load any ranking shift drops the k=5 boundary turn → 0.0.

author: gjcourt
body:
## What

Replaces **#33** (`modernc.org/sqlite` → v1.57.0) and **#35** (`github.com/go-chi/chi/v5` → v5.3.2). Both Renovate PRs are red on **Module tidy**.

| Module | From | To | Bump |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `github.com/go-chi/chi/v5` | `v5.3.1` | `v5.3.2` | patch |
| `modernc.org/sqlite` | `v1.56.0` | `v1.57.0` | minor |

## Why a replacement PR and not a fix pushed to Renovate's branch

Renovate writes the *new* `go.sum` hashes but never prunes the superseded ones, so `go mod tidy -diff` still reports a delta and the Module tidy job exits 1. From the failing run on #33:

```
-modernc.org/sqlite v1.56.0 h1:/D8e2RfFqoy/Zc6PuC76U28zFwmI/sYx1Kjm4yEn9e0=
-modernc.org/sqlite v1.56.0/go.mod h1:yCJ2cmAaIkHQ25oXWrF8H4O1lIfPYPR26yCEDj2P3pQ=
 modernc.org/sqlite v1.57.0 h1:qNQP6xnx5M0ISNtlnxoOX0+cD5bJ0/gr9aMmndFczzg=
```

Pushing a tidy commit onto `renovate/*` doesn't stick — Renovate rebuilds the branch and overwrites it. So this lands as a separate branch.

## Why the two are combined

They share `go.sum`. Landing them separately would just leave the second PR conflicting on that file for no benefit.

## Verification

- `go mod tidy` re-run after the bump is a **no-op** — `go.mod` and `go.sum` byte-identical, so the Module tidy job will be clean.
- `go.sum` delta is 4 insertions / 4 deletions — new hashes in, stale hashes pruned.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .`, and the full `go test ./...` suite all pass locally.

## After merge

Close #33 and #35. Renovate will not reopen them once `main` carries the target versions.

author: aadi-joshi
body:
The report has repeatedly said the hydrodynamic coefficients were engineering estimates requiring CFD. The vehicle now has a real shape, so they can be derived from it and checked. This was the largest remaining hand-wave in the project.

## Method

Bare hull friction from the ITTC 1957 correlation line with a form factor for a body of revolution; appendage build up over the ducts, pylons and fins exactly as modelled; added mass from Lamb's coefficients for the prolate spheroid of the same slenderness plus the water entrained by the ducts.

## The coefficient holds

| Contribution | N per (m/s)^2 | Share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bare hull, friction and form | 1.3 | 3 % |
| Four horizontal thruster ducts | 21.2 | 55 % |
| Four vertical thruster ducts | 14.7 | 38 % |
| Pylons and fins | 1.7 | 4 % |
| **Total from geometry** | **38.9** | |
| Value used in simulation | 32 | ratio 1.21 |

Within 21 percent of a number that was previously an assertion. Added mass brackets it the same way: 6.1 kg axial vs 12 assumed, 25.9 kg lateral vs 42. The simulation is the more sluggish in both axes, which is the harder control problem and so the safer direction to have erred.

## The design finding

The bare Myring hull is **3 percent** of axial drag. The eight thruster ducts are **93 percent**.

Refining the hull form on this vehicle would buy almost nothing: its drag is set by the hover authority bolted to it, not by its shape. If it ever needs to go faster or further, the thrusters are what to fair or retract. That conclusion is not available without the CAD.

## Honest consequence

The station keeping envelope was re-checked at the higher drag, since the entire case for this vehicle rests on it. It falls from 2.93 to **2.69 m/s** against a 2.4 m/s site current, so the margin is **1.12, not the 1.22 the simulation implies**. The design still holds, on a thinner margin than previously stated, and a further drag increase of a quarter would put it out of envelope at this site. The report says so.

The limitations section is updated accordingly: both sides of the comparison are closed form, CFD and tow tank remain required, and the appendage drag coefficients are flagged as the least certain input.

## Status

18 pages, 162 generated macros, CAD verification 9/9, no em dashes.

The failing `Analyze (go)` job was caused by CodeQL autobuild invoking an older Go toolchain (`1.26.x`) while the repo now requires `go >= 1.27.0`. This PR makes Go analysis deterministic by replacing autobuild dependency with an explicit build path aligned to `go.mod`.

- **Workflow addition: dedicated CodeQL pipeline**
  - Added `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` with an `Analyze (go)` job for `push`/`pull_request` on `main`.
  - Sets required CodeQL permissions (`security-events: write`, `contents: read`, `actions: read`).

- **Toolchain alignment with repository requirements**
  - Uses `actions/setup-go` with `go-version-file: go.mod` so analysis always uses the module-declared Go version.

- **Manual build mode for CodeQL**
  - Initializes CodeQL with `build-mode: manual`.
  - Runs explicit `go build ./...` before `github/codeql-action/analyze`, avoiding autobuild’s toolchain mismatch path.

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-go@v7
  with:
    go-version-file: go.mod

- uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
  with:
    languages: go
    build-mode: manual

- run: go build ./...
- uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4
```

ESS-971（PR #375）只修了 `RealtimeMediaSession.receiveDone` 的**同步**分支：
`markDone` 当场返回 `.barrierReleased/.zeroAudio` 时，按 `isSegmentBoundary` 跳过
`downlink.endSession()`。

但 `audio.segment_done` 先到、`0…final_sequence` 尚缺帧时：

```
audio.delta(seq 0)            → buffered
audio.segment_done(final=2)   → markDone → .waiting(missing: [1, 2])
audio.delta(seq 1) / (seq 2)  → receiveDownlink 尾部 checkBarrierRelease() 释放
                                ↑ 这条路径无条件 endSession()
audio.delta(seq 3…)  ← 第二段  → .sessionEnded，整段再次消失
```

`isSegmentBoundary` 只是 `receiveDone` 的入参，没有跨 `.waiting` 状态持久化，
异步释放时已经拿不到了。

- `Shared/RealtimeMediaSession.swift:290-294`（修改前）：异步释放后无条件 `endSession()`
- `Shared/RealtimeMediaSession.swift:308-332`（修改前）：`isSegmentBoundary` 只在同步分支用

## 修法

**边界类型跟着屏障一起等，不靠调用方在释放时重传。**

- `RealtimeDownlinkPlayback.markDone(…, isSegmentBoundary:)` 只在进入 `.waiting`
  时记住该标志（同步分支不需要跨调用记忆，也就不留残留）；
- 异步释放路径用一次性的 `consumePendingDoneIsSegmentBoundary()` 取回，
  据此决定是否 `endSession()` —— 同步 / 异步两条路同口径；
- 该状态与 `pendingFinalSequence` 在**同一处**被清（`resetBufferState` /
  `openGeneration`），所以不会残留成「终态 `audio.done` 忘记关 session」。

选这个位置而不是把标志存在 coordinator：coordinator 里要手工覆盖
`beginTurn / bargeIn / openGeneration / finishTurn` 四条重置路径，漏一条就是
「终态不关 session」的反向事故；存在 buffer 里，既有的重置路径全部免费覆盖。

## 回归覆盖（四类边界）

`Tests/Ess1002AsyncSegmentBarrierTests.swift`（7 条）+
`WatchTests` 里的 watchOS 运行时用例：

| 类型 | 用例 |
|---|---|
| 异步释放 · 段落 | `testAsyncSegmentBarrierKeepsSessionOpen`（本单核心失败面） |
| 异步释放 · 终态 | `testAsyncTerminalBarrierStillEndsSession` |
| 段落后接终态 | `testTerminalAfterAsyncSegmentStillEndsSession`（防标志残留） |
| 释放幂等 | `testAsyncSegmentBarrierReleasesExactlyOnce`（ESS-442 B1 口径） |
| zero-audio · 段落 | `testZeroAudioSegmentBoundaryKeepsSessionOpen` |
| zero-audio · 终态 | `testZeroAudioTerminalStillEndsSession` |
| buffer 层直测 | `testBufferRemembersBoundaryOnlyWhileWaiting` |
| 同步释放 | `Ess971SegmentBoundaryTests` 3 条（既有，全绿未改） |

**新用例确实覆盖到失败面**：把 `Shared/RealtimeMediaSession.swift` 的异步分支
临时改回无条件 `endSession()` 后，`testAsyncSegmentBarrierKeepsSessionOpen` 失败：

```
XCTAssertEqual failed: ("[DropReason.sessionEnded, DropReason.sessionEnded]") is not equal to ("[]")
Executed 7 tests, with 2 failures
```

## 验证（R-02.5 关卡一）

```
swift test                                  → Executed 713 tests, with 0 failures
xcodebuild test -scheme "WristAgent Watch App" \
  -destination 'platform=watchOS Simulator,name=Apple Watch Series 11 (46mm)'
                                            → Executed 357 tests, 3 skipped, 0 failures
xcodebuild -scheme WristAgent -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' build
                                            → ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **
AudioRealtimeGateway: npm test              → tests 163 / pass 163 / fail 0
MacRemoteFrontendBridge projection mock-tests → 12/12
git diff --check                            → 干净
```

**模拟器 WatchLog 运行时证据（R-02.1）**，来自
`testEss1002_AsyncSegmentBarrierKeepsNextSegmentPlayable`：

```
[realtime] downlink_segment_barrier | segment_index=0 final_sequence=2 response_id=r-1002
[realtime] done_barrier_waiting     | response_id=r-1002 missing_seq=[1, 2]
[realtime] done_barrier_released    | response_id=r-1002 final_seq=2
Test Case '…testEss1002_AsyncSegmentBarrierKeepsNextSegmentPlayable' passed
```

无 `downlink_drop reason=sessionEnded`，第二段 `seq 3/4` 进入播放队列。

未新增 `Shared/` `Watch/` `iOS/` 文件（只改既有两个 + 新增测试），无需重跑 `xcodegen`。

## 仍需真机验（R-02.5 关卡二）

合入后在含本修复的包上复测同一 `request_id` 两段都出声，贴 Gateway + Watch 运行时
日志，ESS-1002 才能置 `done`。

Closes ESS-1002

author: louistrue
body:
A reviewer pointed out that my sharding was unstable. They were right, and it invalidates a piece of evidence I used elsewhere.

## The problem

I sharded with `awk 'NR % n == s'` over the sorted file list, so a file's shard depends on its **index**. Adding or removing any test file shifts every file after it.

Measured on the real tree, not assumed:

```
adding ONE test file, index-based:   534 of 534 files reassigned
adding ONE test file, hash-based:      0 of 534 files reassigned
```

## Two things that breaks

**A flaky file wanders.** "Shard 2 is the slow one" or "the flake lives in shard 1" decays with every test added.

**Cross-PR comparison is invalid**, and this is the one that caught me. While chasing the `useSandbox.runSupersession` flake I argued that **#3038's shard 1 passing on the same base** showed #3027's shard-1 failure was unrelated. Different PRs have different file counts, therefore different shard composition — so those were not the same set of files, and the argument does not carry.

The conclusion still stands on the rest of the evidence: neither diff can reach that test, it passes locally 3 of 3, and five PRs hit it under `--test-concurrency=4` while none has since. But I put an invalid argument in the pile and presented it as proof, and it should not have been there.

## The fix

Shard membership becomes a hash of the file path, so it is a property of the file and nothing else.

Partition verified exact rather than assumed:

```
124 + 147 + 127 + 136 = 534 files
534 distinct paths across the four shards
no env set -> still selects all 534, so a local `pnpm test` is unchanged
```

The workflow comment records why, including the 534-of-534 measurement, so the next person does not reintroduce `NR % n` as the obvious way to shard.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Tests**
  * Test sharding now uses deterministic file-based assignment, keeping test files consistently in the same shard between runs.
  * Added documentation explaining shard membership and how it differs from index-based distribution.

author: kodjotouglo
body:
The `configure-totp` required action, built exactly where `configure-webauthn`
lives: after the flow admits, before the login completes, under an identity
the flow has finished proving. When both are owed, the key first.

- **Start leg**: a fresh 20-byte secret, shown once as the `otpauth://` URI
  an app scans and as base32 for the one that cannot; RFC 6238 defaults
  (SHA-1, 6 digits, 30 s). Remembered in the login's notes under
  `totp-register`, never in the execution column.
- **Finish leg**: the code the app derives proves the app holds the secret.
  Only then is the credential kept, **with that step spent**, so the code
  that enrolled the app cannot log in a second time. The instruction is
  struck last.
- A wrong code: login refused, instruction standing, nothing kept.
- The page shows the secret and takes the code under its own field
  (`totp_register`), so the flow's own TOTP step and the enrolment never
  read each other's answer.

## Verification

97 protocol tests (one new, wide: challenge shape, wrong code, right code,
credential kept and instruction struck). A mutation that never keeps the
credential fails it. Services suites, clippy and fmt clean.

body:
(#2702)

## What kind of change does this PR introduce?
Bug fix

## What is the current behavior?
Fixes #2702.
On `POST /auth/v1/recover`, attempting password recovery for an existing user on an invalid or reserved email domain (such as `@example.com`) returns `HTTP 400 email_address_invalid`, whereas a missing user returns `HTTP 200 OK`. This response discrepancy creates an account enumeration vector.
[Please link any relevant issues here.](https://github.com/supabase/auth/issues/2702)

## What is the new behavior?

Intercepts `ErrorCodeEmailAddressInvalid` inside the `Recover` handler and responds with `HTTP 200 OK`, matching the missing user response and eliminating the account enumeration leak.

Added unit test `TestRecover_EmailAddressInvalidNoLeak` in `internal/api/recover_test.go` to ensure both existing and missing users on invalid domains return `HTTP 200 OK`.

## Additional context

Verified locally against PostgreSQL test suite.

author: com6056
body:
## Description

Test-only coverage for the fsops call-site refactors in this branch. Three things that the refactors made correct but that nothing asserted:

- **Rollback under cancellation.** Both link modes and the season-pack apply path wrap their rollback in `context.WithoutCancel`, because the fsops methods early-return on `ctx.Err()` and a run cancelled inside `AddTorrent` would otherwise leave a partial link tree on disk forever. New tests cancel the run from inside `AddTorrent` and assert the base dir is empty afterwards; each fake records how many entries existed at add time so the assertion cannot pass vacuously. Removing the `WithoutCancel` at either link-mode site or in `rollbackSeasonPackTree` fails them.
- **Fail-closed backend resolution.** The local-match path resolves a filesystem backend at three points (`getSourceFileIDs`, the candidate lookup, and the source re-resolve before the shared-extent probe). A backend outage discards all hardlink evidence, so each site records `verificationErr` rather than returning "not linked", otherwise a strict-mode delete dialog reads a transient outage as "no cross-seeds found" and lets you delete the source. One test per site, plus one through `FindLocalMatches(..., strict=true)` to show the recorded error actually reaches the caller. The re-resolve test also pins the call ordering (exactly three lookups) via a counting store.
- **`resolveLocalTorrentFile`'s backslash and drive-prefix rejection.** Table test over POSIX and Windows escaping shapes, including a `C:/evil.mkv` row since that is the one Windows shape the backslash clause does not already catch. The interesting cases are the ones that carry no traversal at all, `AC\DC - Back In Black.mkv` and `dir/AC\DC.mkv`, because backslash is a legal filename byte on Linux, and rewriting it into a nested path makes a file that exists read as missing. Deleting that clause fails five cases: the two legal Linux names plus the Windows traversal, rooted and UNC shapes, which on Linux are single path elements the traversal guards never see.

It also fixes an existing test: `TestInjector_Inject_RollsBackLinkTreeOnAddFailure` never reached `AddTorrent`. The request was a partial match without `DownloadMissingFiles`, so `Inject` bailed at the partial-match check (`inject.go:250-252`) and `failingTorrentAdder.AddTorrent` was never called, meaning the test was exercising the "download missing files disabled" path, not the add failure it is named for. It now sets `DownloadMissingFiles: true` and asserts the adder was called, and a cancellation variant sits beside it.

Scope caveat: `rollbackSeasonPackTree`'s own `WithoutCancel` was already pinned by `TestRollbackSeasonPackTree_RunsUnderCancelledContext`, so the season-pack test's increment is the apply call site reaching rollback with the threaded `planBuild.backend` under a cancelled ctx, since `ApplySeasonPackWebhook` gets that backend from `assembleSeasonPack`. The `context.WithoutCancel` fallback resolve at `seasonpack.go:435` is only reachable when `planBuild.backend` is nil, which this test does not reach; a comment in the test says so.

No production code changed. Targets #1915's branch directly so it lands with the refactor.

## How has this been tested?

- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/services/crossseed/ ./internal/services/dirscan/`, green.
- Every new test was mutation-verified: the guard it protects was removed, the test was confirmed to fail, and the guard restored. That covers the three `context.WithoutCancel` rollback sites, the three `verificationErr` assignments, the backslash clause, and (for the existing-test fix) the `DownloadMissingFiles` flag that makes the add actually happen.
- `go vet` and `GOOS=windows go vet` on both packages; the new traversal table carries POSIX and Windows cases.
- `make fmt gofix-changed` plus golangci-lint v2.13.0 via `go run` with `--new-from-merge-base=develop` (the Go half of `make precommit`, run directly because the binary on my PATH predates the repo's Go target) reports nothing in these files. No frontend files touched.

## Checklist

- [x] My PR title follows the Conventional Commits format
- [x] I have read CONTRIBUTING.md
- [x] I ran `make precommit`'s Go half (fmt, gofix, golangci-lint) and the tests pass locally
- [ ] If this changes the database schema, I have added migrations for both SQLite and PostgreSQL

## AI disclosure

Written with Claude Code. The tests were drafted and iterated by the model, then each one was mutation-verified against the guard it claims to protect before being committed; what to assert, the scope caveat on the season-pack fallback branch, and the existing-test fix were reviewed by hand.

author: hansvilla21
body:
Recupera la skill que se perdió anoche — **por el modo de fallo que ella misma documenta**, que ahora es su mejor ejemplo.

## Qué pasó

El founder lanzó **4 sesiones en paralelo**, cada una auditando un proyecto distinto (el CRM, FreshAdFlow, Content OS, un sitio de PYME), todas con la misma instrucción: capturar lo aprendido como skills y actualizar el índice.

Cada sesión hizo bien su trabajo. El resultado combinado chocó:

- **Tres PRs reclamaron el "Tier 24".** Ninguna podía saberlo: cuando cada una leyó el índice, el último tier era el 23.
- **Los cuatro editaban la misma región del mismo archivo.**
- **El conteo declarado quedó mal en todos**, porque cada uno calculó "lo que había + lo mío" y lo que había cambió debajo.

Ninguna sesión se equivocó. **El defecto es del índice, que asume un solo escritor.**

## Y entonces la skill se perdió, exactamente así

Su primer commit se pushó a la rama del PR #13 **un minuto después de que ese PR se mergeara**. La rama quedó verde, el PR decía `MERGED`, y el archivo **nunca llegó a `main`**.

Se detectó corriendo el paso 3 de la propia skill: verificar los archivos contra el disco después del merge. De ahí sale el agregado nuevo — **un push exitoso a una rama no es un cambio entregado**:

```bash
git merge-base --is-ancestor <tu-commit> origin/main && echo "llegó" || echo "NO llegó"
```

Es el pariente directo de `verificar-base-del-pr-antes-de-mergear`: el PR reporta un estado que no responde la pregunta que importa.

## Las tres reglas de la skill

1. **El número se reclama en el PR, no en el archivo.** Gana quien abrió el PR primero; el que llega después toma el siguiente y pone la fecha de su sesión adentro para que el orden cronológico siga siendo legible.
2. **El conteo se deriva**, con `ls | wc -l` después de cada merge. Nunca "lo que había más lo mío".
3. **El índice se verifica contra el disco**, no se lee. Ese chequeo además atrapa un defecto que nada más detecta: un nombre partido en dos líneas por el ancho de columna deja de resolver por grep.

Y al resolver el conflicto: en un índice acumulativo la resolución correcta es `ours + theirs` con el contador recalculado. **Elegir un lado borra el trabajo del otro** — y como el archivo sigue siendo válido, nadie se entera.

## Verificación

- Conteo derivado del disco: **119**. Los tres lugares que lo declaran (`CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, índice temático) coinciden.
- **119/119** skills resuelven por grep contra los dos índices.
- Tier 29 porque `main` ya llegó al 28 — verificado contra `main`, no de memoria.
- El índice de `main` se auditó antes de tocar nada: estaba sano en 118/118 tras los cuatro merges.

body:
## Summary
- Bug 32: `CsvParser.parseDate`/`maskAccountNumber` threw NPE on a null cell instead of returning null, unlike every sibling parsing helper in the file.
- Bug 38: `RecurringService`'s reset-then-recompute pass only considers `active` (EXPENSE/non-transfer/non-duplicate) transactions, so a transaction whose type changed away from EXPENSE kept a stale `recurring = true` badge forever. Now explicitly resets anything that left `active` but still carries the flag.
- Bug 49: `CurrentUser` injected a `UserRepository` that's never used (leftover from switching `id()` from a DB lookup to a JWT-principal parse). Removed.
- Bug 51: `EnumParsing.parse` is now case-insensitive and trims whitespace, so acceptance of a value like `" active"` no longer depends on whether the specific caller happened to normalize it first.
- Bug 56: a `MerchantAlias` row can outlive its target merchant (`discard()` doesn't touch aliases). The dangling alias previously caused a brand-new duplicate merchant on every single resolve() call, forever, since the no-op `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` silently swallowed the re-link attempt. Now repoints the existing alias at a fresh merchant, mirroring `MerchantService.merge`'s existing pattern.
- Bug 58: one `String.format` in `InsightsService` was missing the `Locale.ENGLISH` every other call in the file passes (no behavioral impact -- `%s`-only format string -- but restores the file's own stated convention).
- Bug 39 (Flyway `V58` missing from the sequence): investigated, not a functional bug -- Flyway doesn't require contiguous version numbers, and backfilling migration history is against this repo's convention. No fix made.

Second of several thematic batches covering "Live Low" findings in `docs/quality/bug-reports/BUG_REVIEW_REPORT.md`.

author: dylan-conway
body:
### What does this PR do?

`test/no-validate-exceptions.txt` lists files that run without `BUN_JSC_validateExceptionChecks` on the ASAN lane because something on their path leaves a JS exception unchecked. Running those files under the validator on a debug build gives the exact site; this fixes the ones that are in Bun's code and removes the corresponding entries, plus seven entries that already pass clean on main.

Fixes:
- **napi**: `Napi::defineProperty` / `napi_create_function` now check after each `NapiClass::create()` (its `finishCreation` declares a ThrowScope) — this was the "every `.node` load trips it" case. `napi_define_properties` uses the `NAPI_PREAMBLE` scope like every other entry point instead of a `ThrowScope` that simulates a throw into addon code. The NapiClass constructor and `process.dlopen` check `env->throwPendingException()` through their scope instead of `if (…) return {}`.
- **vm.compileFunction / new vm.Script**: check after `isArray()` (a Proxy can throw) before building `ERR_INVALID_ARG_INSTANCE`.
- **node:module**: check after `jsSubstring` in `new Module(id)`; `RELEASE_AND_RETURN` the rope in `Module.wrap`; check after `isArray()` in `_resolveFilename({ paths })`.
- **URLPattern**: `RELEASE_AND_RETURN` around the scoped dictionary conversion in `convertURLPatternInputToJS` (tripped on every `exec()` with a dictionary input).
- **JSBundlerPlugin `onBeforeParse`**: check after `toWTFString` and the dlopen-handle `get()`.

Re-enabled: `module-resolve-filename-paths`, `urlpattern`, `isArray-proxy-crash`, `native-plugin`, `ctrl-c` (fixed here); `import-meta`, `resolve`, `websocket`, `web-crypto.test`, `wpt-webcrypto.generateKey`, and the two node-parallel webcrypto scripts (already clean).

Still excluded, with reasons unchanged: the static-property `PropertyCallback` builders (`BunObject.test`, `node-module-module`, …), two JSC-internal sites (`LiteralParser`, `Completion.cpp`), third-party napi addons, `napi.test.ts`/`require-cache` (not verified locally).

### How did you verify your code works?

Ran each re-enabled file under `BUN_JSC_validateExceptionChecks=1 BUN_JSC_dumpSimulatedThrows=1` on a debug build: no validator output, tests pass (`ctrl-c`'s vite cases time out on a debug build with or without the validator).

author: agusgonzaleznic
body:
Three findings in `scripts/new-post.mjs`, the markdown/HTML → Storyblok importer. Its pure helpers move to `scripts/lib/post-import.mjs` so they can be tested at all — `new-post.mjs` does its work at import time, so a test that imported it would perform a live Storyblok round trip.

## Re-importing a post destroyed fields the importer does not own

The update path PUT the freshly built content object, and a PUT replaces content **wholesale**. That lost data two ways on the most ordinary operation there is — fixing a typo and re-importing:

| field | how it was lost |
|---|---|
| `cover_image` | not a field the importer builds, so absent from the PUT → Storyblok dropped it |
| `seo_title`, `seo_description`, `original_url`, `canonical_override` | built with `\|\| ""`, so a source file that simply doesn't mention them overwrote real CMS-edited values with empty strings |

Losing `canonical_override` is the worst of those: it's what gates a syndicated post to its source locale, so clearing it silently re-enables five locale variants whose canonical points at another domain.

`mergeStoryContent()` now merges over the stored content — a non-empty imported value wins, an empty one defers to what's already there, and any key the importer doesn't manage survives untouched. Empty frontmatter means "not specified", never "clear it"; clearing is done in Storyblok. The re-import log names whatever it preserved.

The GET that reads the stored publish date is now unconditional, since the merge needs the same response.

## Named entities were published literally

Only the XML-mandatory five plus `nbsp` were decoded, so an imported article kept `’` and `—` as literal text. The table now covers the punctuation, symbols and arrows a CMS or word-processor export actually emits — and stops there on purpose: an unrecognised entity is left verbatim so it looks obviously wrong rather than being silently mangled.

**Frontmatter prose goes through the same decoding, which it did not before.** That mattered more than the body — the excerpt is what PostCard renders, what the RSS `<description>` carries, what the meta description says, and what's sent to DeepL for five locales. Verified with `--dry-run`:

```
before:  excerpt: "Checking that it’s decoded — properly."
after:   excerpt: "Checking that it’s decoded — properly."
```

URLs are deliberately **not** decoded: they're raw values in frontmatter, not HTML, so an `&` in a query string is part of the URL.

Also fixed: ` ` decoded to a plain U+0020, so `10 km` became breakable and the typography quietly changed. It's U+00A0 now, and every invisible character in the table is written as an escape — a literal one in source is the class that already cost this repo a NUL byte in `deepl.mjs` and a BOM in this very file.

## One malformed entity killed the whole import

`Number.isFinite(cp)` was the only guard before `String.fromCodePoint(cp)`, and `isFinite(1e9)` is true while `fromCodePoint(1e9)` throws. Reproduced end to end on the `.html` path — the Medium-export path this importer exists for, and the one that skips markdown-it, so it's where raw entities actually reach this code:

```
without the guard:  RangeError: Invalid code point 1114112     exit 1
with it:            "�" survives verbatim, 😀 decodes  exit 0
```

Markdown input never reached the crash, because markdown-it decodes entities first and turns an invalid code point into U+FFFD. So the guard is specifically about HTML imports, and range + integrality are what `fromCodePoint` actually requires.

## Tests

New `scripts/lib/post-import.test.mjs` — 14 tests, 54 in `scripts/lib` now. Each fix checked by reverting it:

| reverted | result |
|---|---|
| entity table → the original 6 | **3 fail** |
| guard → `isFinite` only | **1 fail**, and the `.html` import crashes with RangeError |
| merge → wholesale replace | **4 fail** |

The `nbsp` assertion compares **code points**, not string literals — a no-break space and a plain space are indistinguishable in source, and comparing them produced the useless `'x y' !== 'x y'`.

## Verification

```
lint 0 · typecheck 0 (125 files) · i18n:check 0 · 46 + 56 + 54 tests 0
build 0 — 84 pages, sitemap covers all, no broken internal links across 85
no NUL bytes, no BOM, no literal invisible characters in any changed file
```

The importer's module graph resolves (it reaches its usage error, not `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`) and both probe imports ran `--dry-run` without contacting the CMS.

author: chakki-the-potato
body:
## What

`changes.json` gains `after` — the sha256 of every file in `modified` and `created`, as the run left it. Rollback compares against that when deciding whether a path was edited after the migration.

## Why

The first real end-to-end rollback found the defect. `core/rollback.md` said to compare each modified file against its copy in `backup/`. The backup is the state from *before* the run, so a migrated file always differs from it — every path came back "changed since the run", and the check that exists to protect the user's later edits could never distinguish them from the migration's own writes.

## Verification

Full end-to-end at 0.6.0, on a seeded temporary target, never a real tool home:

- `seed-target.sh claude <tmp>` → migrate codex → claude → `verify-migration.sh` **70/70**
- pre-check against `after`: all six written paths UNCHANGED, and the run is the newest
- rollback → 2 restored, 4 files removed, 5 directories removed innermost-first, 9 ledger entries dropped, run record kept
- `verify-rollback.sh` → **13/13**, target byte-identical to a fresh seed

All twelve directions still pass. Existing manifests were backfilled from current on-disk content — accurate, since nothing has edited those targets since the runs that wrote them.

author: nvy-bot
body:
## 修改内容

- `pr-validation.yml` 的聚合门 `validate-and-test`：`if: always()` → `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`
- 同处补上为什么不能是 always() 的实测注释（#143 现场）+ 为什么这不开新口子

### 背景：#143 的红是「被取代的旧轮」留下的

`concurrency: cancel-in-progress` 取消同一 PR 的旧轮时，四个分 job 全部 `cancelled`，
而聚合门的 `always()` 让它**照跑不误** —— 它按 fail-closed 规则（`cancelled` 与
`failure` 同等判红）exit 1，于是在 head SHA 上留下一条 `validate-and-test = failure`
的 check run，**永不消失**。

#143（release mobile 0.13.0）的现场：

| | |
|---|---|
| `gh pr checks 143` | 13 项全 pass（它只取同名最新一条） |
| head SHA 上的 `validate-and-test` | `failure` @05:18:39（run 32554003375，被取代的旧轮）+ `success` @05:20:30（run 32554003374，真正跑完的那轮） |
| 分支保护 | 取同名**最新**一条 = success → **CI 并不挡它** |
| `reviewDecision` | `REVIEW_REQUIRED` → BLOCKED 的真正原因是待人工 approve |

所以代价不是「挡住合并」，是**把「红 = 该看一眼」训练成噪声** —— 一个每天两次
（release-please 更新两个 Release PR）稳定产出假红的门，很快就没人看了。

### 为什么是 `!cancelled()`，为什么它不开新口子

`!cancelled()` 与 `always()` 都会绕开默认的 `success()` 前置，**上游红时一样照跑照判红**；
唯一区别是**整轮被取消时不跑**（skipped，不留红）—— 正好只切掉这个假红面。

原注释担心的「skipped 的 required check 在 GitHub 眼里不是失败」在这里不成立：

1. **并发取代**（占几乎全部）：取代它的新一轮会在同一 SHA 上产出自己的 `validate-and-test`，
   新一条才是分支保护采信的那条；新一轮跑完前该 context 是 pending，PR 照样卡住。
2. **人工取消整轮**：`gate-checks` / `lint-typecheck` / `server-test` / `mobile-checks`
   四个分 job **各自也是 ruleset `main-protection` 的 required context**（已核对线上
   ruleset 20598653），整轮被取消时它们是 `cancelled`，GitHub 不当通过 → PR 照样卡住。
   兜底不依赖本聚合门。

`name: validate-and-test` 未动，ruleset 不需要改。

### 🚨 部署与存活前置确认 (Deployment & Smoke Gates)

- [x] **物理验证通过**：我确认本地已运行 `pnpm exec nx affected -t lint typecheck test build runtime-smoke --base=origin/main` 并拿到 exit code 0。
      ⚠️ 证据等级说明：本轮 nx 报 **`No tasks were run`** —— 改动只碰 `.github/workflows/**`，
      它不是任何 nx project 的 input，所以 exit 0 是**真的但空的**，不代表任何覆盖。
      本 PR 的真实验证在下面 Test plan。
- [x] **禁止过度 Mock**：如修改了 Guard / Interceptor / Filter / Pipe / Repository,我确认相关 spec 已使用 `Test.createTestingModule` 装 DI 容器,而非 `new Class()` 隔离实例化。（本 PR 不含任何 TS 改动，不适用）
- [x] **状态机闭环**：本特性的 `state_branches`(spec.md frontmatter)均已在 integration test 中 100% `it()` 覆盖。（本 PR 无 spec / 无 state_branches，不适用）

## Test plan

- `actionlint .github/workflows/pr-validation.yml` → OK（与 CI 的 `Actionlint (workflow YAML)` 同一把尺）
- **本 PR 自身这一轮就是活体验证**：改的就是跑它的那个 workflow。期望 `validate-and-test`
  正常出 `success`（证明 `!cancelled()` 在正常路径上与 `always()` 等价，没把门跳过去）
- 回归判据（合并后）：下一次 release-please 更新 Release PR 触发并发取代时，被取代的旧轮
  应留下 `validate-and-test = skipped` 而**不是** `failure`
- 反向判据（不必专门造）：任一分 job 真红时，聚合门仍应 exit 1 —— `!cancelled()` 不改这条路径

## 关联 Issue / PR

- 现场：#143（`chore(main): release mobile 0.13.0`，红的那条 check run 属于 run 32554003375）

## Summary
User reported the "Apply as a Founding Expert" form looked blank on desktop — boxes/button rendered but no text was visible, though typing/tapping still worked.

Documentation seule — aucun changement de code.

## Le brief était périmé

Il datait du 19 et **douze PR ont été mergées depuis**. Il annonçait 33 tests et
présentait la direction visuelle comme la dernière grande affaire. Il en annonce
désormais **119**, et la dernière grande affaire est le Mode jeu passé **d'un
verbe à sept**.

Ce que le nouveau brief met en avant pour qui reprend :

- l'état réel (`main` = `0911ac4`, 119 tests, déploiement vérifié) ;
- les sept verbes et ce qui est validé par toi *versus* ce qui ne l'est pas
  encore (les trois pilotes de paramètre, 39-41, ne sont pas essayés) ;
- **le tableau symptôme → cause réelle** de la session : cinq symptômes, cinq
  causes qui n'étaient pas là où on regardait, et aucune qui n'était un réglage
  de difficulté ;
- **les pièges qui ont coûté le plus cher** : un module pur et testé branché sur
  une valeur morte, un test qui tirait au sort et a fait sauter un déploiement,
  « vert sur la PR ≠ vert sur `main` », `npm run check` **après** avoir écrit les
  tests.

## L'architecture EP est consignée — pas appliquée

Ta réflexion sur la refonte du Mode jeu (EP, modules, presets, histoire,
marketing) est écrite dans une section **⏳ EN ATTENTE D'ARBITRAGE**, avec en
tête un avertissement explicite : *rien n'est arbitré, ne pas coder dessus*.

Elle contient le diagnostic (`PlayerProgress.level` est un seul entier qui porte

qui tue le jeu, la première tranche livrable, et **les quatre questions à
trancher avec mes réponses recommandées**.

Je l'ai consignée malgré l'absence d'arbitrage pour une seule raison : elle ne
doit pas être reperdue entre deux sessions. Le brief la désigne comme **le sujet
en cours**, et la section est titrée pour qu'on ne puisse pas la confondre avec

too, so every position where the spinner was visible at all was a position
where it covered the first row's top band. The code said so itself: the
comment on `pulledTransform` declined to assert the strong invariant on the
grounds that it was false, and asserted the flush line instead. That was the
honest ceiling while the rows stood still.

**Second defect.** `.directory-row-join:hover { background: var(--border) }`
was ungated. A touch browser synthesizes `:hover` on the element under the
finger and LATCHES it, so putting a finger down to scroll the list — or to
drive the pull above — painted the row it landed on and left it painted after
the lift.

## The design, and why this shape

Everything the finger drags — the parked slot AND the rows — now lives in one
`.directory-pull-track`, moved by ONE transform. Inside the track the slot
occupies `[-slotHeight, 0]` and the rows start at `0`, so translating by `dy`
lands the slot's bottom edge and the first row's top edge both on `dy`:

    slot bottom ≡ first row top, at EVERY dy

**That is an identity, not a bound.** The obvious alternative — translate the
rows, keep capping the slot — satisfies the invariant too, but by arithmetic
across two independently painted elements that a later edit to either one can
get wrong. One rigid body under one transform has no second number to keep in
step, so the invariant stops being something the tests check and becomes
something the markup cannot violate.

## The cap is REMOVED, and naming that was part of the ask

`min(dy, 100%)` existed for exactly one reason: keeping the spinner off rows
that stood still. With the rows carried there is no collision left to bound,
so the question stops being geometry and becomes feel.

Removed rather than retuned because **any cap makes the list stop following
the finger past it** — the reported defect in smaller print, arriving at the
moment the gesture is most committed. Damping past the commit point is the
alternative worth having, and it needs a constant measured on a device;
`PULL_COMMIT_PX`'s own comment already records that nothing about this gesture
was verified on a phone. An unbounded linear follow is the honest floor to
calibrate FROM, and damping is additive afterwards. The other coherent look —
the slot settling at the top edge while the gap grows beneath it — is named in
DESIGN_NOTES so it can be asked for after the feel is judged on a phone.

Two things fall out for free: the pane writes no transform to the slot at all,
so the parked `translateY(-100%)` stays in the stylesheet and the #1438 trap
(an inline transform replacing the declaration wholesale) is *gone* rather
than guarded; and the opacity ramp keeps its own axis, untouched.

The `a2dacafa` guarantee now spans two elements, which raises its stakes: a
commit-path cleanup that clears one and forgets the other strands the whole
channel list down the pane rather than just a spinner. Both are cleared, both
asserted.

## A mutant found a hole in the oracle

Mutating the paint to write the travel onto the SLOT instead of the track —
which is precisely the pre-point-3 defect, not an invented mutation — left "a
release that COMMITS wipes the paint too" GREEN: the track is trivially
unpainted under that mutant and the ramp is still cleared, so both assertions
passed while a stale transform sat on the slot. **A cleanup test that only
reads the elements the CURRENT code paints cannot see paint that went to the
wrong element.** Third assertion added; the pull group goes 4 red → 5 under
the mutant, and the 5th is that one. Recorded in DESIGN_NOTES as a pattern.

## The webkit arm was re-aimed, not dropped

It used to ask whether WebKit resolved `translateY(min(<px>, 100%))`; that
declaration no longer exists in production. The surviving engine question is
sharper: the invariant is an identity only if the engine composes the track's
px translate with the slot's own PERCENTAGE offset, which resolves against the
slot's box and not the track's. An engine getting that wrong puts the spinner
back on the first row with every chromium gate green — the empty-green class.
The division stands: chromium owns the PANE half (the declaration comes from a
real finger), webkit owns the ENGINE half (`new Touch(...)` is an
`Illegal constructor` there, so no gesture is synthesizable on that project).

## Measured corrections to the issue text

* The stylesheet applies the `@media (hover: hover)` cure **THREE** times, not
  eight — `.scroll-to-bottom-btn`, `.members-pane li .member-name`,
  `.next-active-btn`, brace-matched over the three gate blocks. The new one is
  the fourth. The gate's why-comment names them by SELECTOR rather than line
  number, so the citation cannot rot.
* `:active` was NOT smuggled in. A pressed affordance on touch is a separate
  decision.

## Why the hover guard is source-level

Not a shortcut: the behaviour needs a browser reporting `(hover: none)`, and
Playwright cannot emulate one. `page.emulateMedia()` accepts `colorScheme`,
`contrast`, `forcedColors`, `media` and `reducedMotion` — there is no `hover`
key (verified against the installed `playwright-core` types), so no project in
this repo can put the query into its false branch on purpose, and jsdom
applies no stylesheet at all. What is deterministic is what the cascade is
ASKED to do. The test COUNTS every declaration of the selector rather than
checking one exists, so a second ungated copy added later reds it; a control
ahead of it pins that the fill still exists, because "gate it" and "delete it"
are different changes.

## Gates run locally

* `bun run check` — 4/4 stages, including lock drift (so the tree is
  attributable), biome, tsc src and tsc e2e
* `bun run build`
* vitest — **5826 passed / 299 files**
* `scripts/design-notes-gate.sh origin/main` — 1 new entry heading, separator
  and marker present

## 🔴 NOT established, on purpose rather than by omission

* **The e2e arms have never been run.** They compile, and that is the whole of
  what can be said until they get a lane. Until then point 3 is proven as a
  CONTRACT in jsdom, not as geometry in a browser: the three geometric
  assertions (rows carried 400px, overlap 0, slot-height control at three root
  font sizes) are derived, not measured.
* **The FEEL, and with it the whole iOS question** — whether the follow is
  smooth, whether an uncapped travel is the right sensation, and above all
  whether iOS elects our gesture rather than its own overscroll. The binder
  claims LATE, on a touchmove, and a real device may have committed to a pan
  before that claim lands. Playwright's WebKit is not the reporter's phone.
* The hover fix is proven at the level of the cascade, not of behaviour, for
  the reason given above.

author: yochlin
body:
## Summary
As part of the **Server-Base Architecture Plan** (`docs/architecture/server-refactor-plan.md`), this PR extracts risk management and stop-loss evaluation logic from `internal/bot` into a clean, transport-neutral `service.RiskService` in `internal/service`.

## Scope & Changes
- **`internal/service/risk.go`**:
  - `RiskStore`, `RiskHistoryReader`, `RiskQuoteReader` interfaces for clean decoupling and testing.
  - `ComputeStopSuggestion`: Candidate stop levels (Low10, Low20, ATR14) with fallback to quote.
  - `SetStop`: Position validation, price validation against latest close, DB update, and risk distance calculation.
  - `AddBuyAlert` / `RemoveBuyAlert` / `RemoveBuyAlertByPrice` / `GetBuyAlerts`: Buy alert management and direction inference.
  - `EvaluateStopLoss`: Two-tier stop-loss checks (custom stop price vs. global percentage fallback) with deduplicated alerting.
  - `EvaluateTrailingStop`: Drawdown from peak close evaluation with fixed percentage and ATR-based distance.
  - `EvaluateTargetAlerts`: 2R take-profit target reached check.
  - `EvaluateMA5BreakAlerts`: 10% profit + MA5 trend-defense break check.
  - `EvaluateBuyAlerts`: Checks and automatically removes triggered buy alerts.
- **`internal/service/risk_test.go`**:
  - Unit test coverage for all risk operations and edge cases with mocks.
- **`internal/bot`**:
  - Wired `RiskService` into `Bot` via `b.risks()`.
  - Refactored `handlers.go` (`/stop`, `/buyalert`, `ExecuteSetStop`, `ExecuteAddBuyAlert`) to delegate to `RiskService`.
  - Simplified `jobs.go` (`checkStopLossAlerts`, `checkTrailingStopAlerts`, `checkTargetAlerts`, `checkMA5BreakAlerts`, `checkBuyAlerts`) to delegate to `RiskService`.
- **`docs/architecture/backend.md`**:
  - Updated backend architecture documentation to reflect `RiskService`.

## Verification
- `go test ./...` -> ALL PASS
- `go test -race ./...` -> ALL PASS (0 data races)
- `go vet ./...` -> ALL PASS

author: nickschmidt94
body:
## Why

Recommendation-heavy planning and delivery workflows often stop for repeated approval rounds even when a supported next choice is already clear.

## What users get

`ns-finish-line` selects evidence-backed recommendations and keeps moving toward the requested destination:

- decision work ends with resolved artifacts or ready implementation tickets;
- delivery work ends with one verified open pull request; and
- end-to-end work can carry the same goal through both phases.

## How to use it

Invoke `$ns-finish-line` when you want the agent to take the recommended path and continue without ordinary approval pauses.

## Boundaries

Autonomous choices are recorded as agent-selected recommendations rather than attributed to the user. The skill stops before merge or deployment and reports a hard blocker when no safe supported choice remains.

<details>
<summary>Maintainer checks</summary>

- Public repository validator: 11 skills validated.
- Installed and packaged NS Finish Line folders match.
- Five representative behavior cases cover decision completion, companion-free fallback, planning-only scope, PR delivery, and irreversible-decision blockers.
- The personal `ship-skill-pr` helper remains local and is excluded from the public package.

</details>

author: paulocpjunior
body:
Décima terceira leva — a **varredura inversa**: campo que a **tela grava** e que **nenhum gerador lê**.

## 🔴 O achado

```js
'A',  // perfil EFD: sempre A
```

O `perfilEFD` está no modal Dados Fiscais desde sempre. A pessoa escolhia, salvava… e o 0000 ignorava.

Por que importa: o **perfil de enquadramento (A/B/C) é atribuído pelo fisco estadual** e decide **quais registros o arquivo deve ter**. Declarar A num contribuinte de perfil B faz o arquivo prometer um detalhamento que o PVA vai cobrar — é a mesma família da recusa *"O registro não deve ser informado para esse PERFIL"* que a AFFITTARE levou ontem no EFD-Contribuições.

E tem a agravante que as outras não têm: **trabalho perdido**. O colaborador preenchia e nada acontecia — a família do "botão que não faz nada".

## ✂️ A correção

- `IND_PERFIL` passa a vir do cadastro;
- valor fora de A/B/C é **recusado com o motivo**, nunca descartado calado (lição do #382);
- perfil **diferente de A sai DITO** no aviso da geração, porque ele muda o que o PVA exige;
- perfil ausente continua **A e sem alarme** — é o enquadramento comum, e alarme sem ação é o que ensina a ignorar alarme.

## 📌 O que a varredura inversa também mostrou

Dos 40 campos da whitelist de `dadosFiscais`, só **dois** não são lidos por ninguém: o `perfilEFD` (corrigido aqui) e o `inscEstSubstTrib` — este último **não entrou no PR**: não achei campo do leiaute que ele alimente, e cadastrar um uso por dedução seria inventar. Fica nomeado aqui: ou é cadastro de referência para a equipe, ou tem um destino que só o Paulo sabe.

## Testes

3 novos: perfil B do cadastro sai B; ausente continua A sem alarme; inválido é recusado com o motivo.

`lint ✓ · 345 suítes / 5.093 testes ✓ · build ✓`

author: abhishekpauly
body:
Release prep for sprint 8. No source changes — version, changelog and branch
status only.

## What this does

- Bumps `pyproject.toml` and `__version__` to **0.20.0**.
- Promotes `[Unreleased]` to `## [0.20.0] — The people come out of the capture (G5-G7)`,
  with the `### Changed` and `### Tests` blocks the other releases carry.
- Refreshes `SPRINT_STATUS.md` for the post-merge state.

Verified `scripts/changelog_section.py 0.20.0` extracts the section cleanly, so
the GitHub Release notes and the changelog cannot disagree.

## 0.19.0 was never tagged, and cannot be

Worth reading before approving, because it is permanent.

`0.19.0` (sprint 1, `G1`-`G4`) merged in #70 but was never tagged — the latest
tag is `v0.18.1`. Backfilling it is not possible:

- At the sprint 1 merge `9668803`, `pyproject.toml` and `__version__` both said
  **0.18.1**, and `G1`-`G4` were still under `[Unreleased]`.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor eb233e4 9668803` → **false**. The commit that
  bumped to `0.19.0` and wrote the `## [0.19.0]` heading was not in #70.
- It reached `main` only via **#72**, because sprint 8 was cut from
  `sprint/1-governance` rather than from `main` and carried it along.

So no commit on `main` has a tree declaring `0.19.0` without also containing
`G5`-`G7`. Tagging `v0.19.0` at `9668803` would be refused by `release.yml`,
which re-checks that the tag and `pyproject.toml` agree. Tagging it at `main`
would pass that check but publish sprint 8's code under sprint 1's notes — and
`RELEASING.md` is explicit that a tag is never moved and never deleted.

`v0.20.0` therefore contains `G1`-`G7`. The changelog says so at the top of the
`0.20.0` section, and the `[0.19.0]` section stands as the record of the first
half.

This is a direct consequence of the branching deviation recorded in
`SPRINT_STATUS.md`, and it is why `BRANCHING.md` says to cut a sprint from
`main` after its predecessor merges.

## After this merges

```bash
git switch main && git pull
git tag -a v0.20.0 -m "0.20.0 — The people come out of the capture (G5-G7)"
git push origin v0.20.0
```

## Not done here

`SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `0.1.0`. Everything sprint 8 added is additive fields,
which `RELEASING.md` says does not move it.

`QA.2` — a real run against a real authenticated portal — is still outstanding.
It is the reason this sprint jumped the queue, and no fixture can validate
redaction recall against real customer data.
