body:
## Summary

Three clauses of the challenge brief were previously *represented* rather than implemented: federated model sharing (`federated_service.py` existed but no endpoint called it), ML forecasting (`ml_engine.py` was never invoked — the UI charted Open-Meteo's own forecast), and authority alerting (recommendations were rendered as text and never dispatched; feedback lived in a list that died on restart). Citizen "local sensor readings" had no intake at all. This wires all four to live code paths, adds SQLite persistence, and removes the USGS seismic feed and dead `gemini_service.py`.

**Federated** — three state nodes (Delhi NCR, Karnataka, Punjab agro) each fit a local Ridge model on their own CAMS/ERA5 observations plus local citizen readings; `POST /api/federated/sync` does sample-weighted FedAvg over node parameters only:

```python
# only these leave a node — raw observations never do
ModelUpdate(node_id, coefficients, intercept, n_samples, local_mae)
global_coef = Σ(w_i · coef_i) / Σ w_i      # w_i = n_samples_i
```
Offline nodes are excluded instead of contributing placeholders; rounds persist to `federated_rounds`. Live round: 3 nodes, 1,780 local samples, global MAE 5.29 µg/m³.

**Forecasting** — city payloads and `/api/forecast` now come from the RandomForest engine (`prev_pm25`, rolling mean, hour, temp, humidity, wind), trained on 30d × 5 cities of real observations, retrained at most hourly. `/api/model/status` exposes `training_data_source` / `training_samples` / `holdout_mae_ugm3` / `is_observation_trained`, so the synthetic fallback can never be mistaken for an observation-trained model (current: 3,710 samples, holdout MAE 6.08).

**Citizen sensors** — `POST /api/citizen/sensor` validates and persists a reading, scores it on CPCB NAQI, and diffs it against official telemetry; `GET` returns readings in a radius/time window. They become a fusion evidence channel and local training data.

**Alerting** — `dispatch_alert` actually delivers over webhook and/or SMTP, gated by confidence/PM2.5 thresholds and a per-region cooldown, and every outcome is persisted and named rather than silently swallowed: `SENT` / `PARTIAL` / `FAILED` / `NOT_TRIGGERED` / `SUPPRESSED_COOLDOWN` / `NO_CHANNEL_CONFIGURED`. Verified end-to-end against a local receiver (`webhook: SENT — HTTP 200`, with the rendered notice body). Authority routes now require `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN`; the console's hardcoded `'admin' || 'cpcb2026'` client-side gate is replaced by a real `GET /api/authority/session` check.

**Fusion** — reweighted over six channels (ground, image, citizen sensors, NO2, fire, meteorology) with confidence normalized over *available* evidence, and downwind zones now derived from the reciprocal wind bearing instead of fixed strings. NASA FIRMS VIIRS active fires are added as stubble/biomass evidence and report `Not configured` without `NASA_FIRMS_MAP_KEY` rather than inventing detections.

Backend tests added under `backend/tests/` (9 passing; live-data ones marked `network`). One bug they caught: `/api/authority/feedback` read `stored["created_at"]` where the store returns `recorded_at` — a guaranteed 500 on every feedback submission.

Not exercised here: SMTP delivery (no relay configured) and FIRMS (no map key), both of which fall back to their explicit unconfigured states.

author: paddione
body:
Drei gemessene Änderungen am Loadout `qwen38-220k` (`scripts/llm/loadouts.json`). Der Slug bleibt unverändert — er wird von `AGENTS.md`, `.opencode/*`, drei BATS-Dateien und `scripts/migrations/2026-08-22-llm-proxy-qwen38-backend.sql` referenziert.

## 1. `--cache-ram 0` → `12288`, `--ctx-checkpoints 0` entfernt

`qwen35` ist laut `llm_arch_is_hybrid()` eine Hybrid-Architektur (SSM-/Linear-Attention neben Full-Attention). Deren Zustand lässt sich nicht teilweise zurückrollen; ohne Kontext-Checkpoint fällt llama.cpp auf `forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data (likely due to SWA or hybrid/recurrent memory)` zurück. `--cache-ram 0` schaltete zusätzlich `--cache-idle-slots` ab (Startwarnung stand im Journal) — also genau den Mechanismus, der den Slot eines pausierten Agenten in den Host-RAM rettet.

Folge im Factory-Betrieb: jeder Wechsel zwischen zwei Agenten hat den vollen Prompt neu prefillt. Drei rotierende Agenten kosten jetzt 2,5 s statt 137 s.

## 2. `ctx 220000` → `114688`

Bei 220000 blieben 636 MiB VRAM frei, und die Konfiguration kippte schon bei kleinen Änderungen: `-ub 1024` allein drückte den Prefill von 1200 auf 264 t/s (identische Flags bei 131072: 1462 t/s).

## 3. `specType ngram-mod` → `draft-mtp,ngram-mod`

Der MTP-Head liegt im GGUF (`qwen35.nextn_predict_layers: 1`, Tensoren `blk.64.nextn.*`). Kontrollmessung bei identischem `-c 98304`, nur der spec-type unterschiedlich:

| Prompt | ngram-mod | draft-mtp |
|---|---|---|
| Prosa, 400 Token Ausgabe | 54,9 t/s | 66,3 t/s |
| Code-Generierung, 400 Token | 53,9 t/s | 66,6 t/s |
| 34k Kontext + 400 Token | 45,5 t/s | 58,7 t/s |

MTP kostet ~1235 MiB VRAM. Bei `-c 163840` startet der Server noch, stirbt aber beim ersten Request mit `CUDA error … cuMemSetAccess` in `ggml-cuda.cu:648`; `-ctkd q4_0 -ctvd q4_0` hilft nicht. Größtes stabiles Fenster: 114688. Die Kombination mit `ngram-mod` kostet kein zusätzliches VRAM.

## Verifikation

Live auf `:8094` nach Neustart durch den llm-proxy:

```
-c 114688  --spec-type draft-mtp,ngram-mod  --cache-ram 12288
Prefill 1333–1355 t/s über vier verschiedene kalte 34k-Prompts
Decode  62–70 t/s
Rotation dreier gecachter Agenten 2,5–3 s
15078 MiB VRAM belegt (1225 MiB frei)
```

`tests/spec/local-llm-proxy/`: 130/132. Die zwei Fehler (`ui-config-seed` segfaultet, `T012970` Allowlist) sind per `git stash` als vorbestehend nachgewiesen.

## Mitgezogen

`.opencode/agent-models.jsonc` trug `"context": 220000` — ohne Anpassung hätten Clients Prompts jenseits des Fensters geschickt und wären an `--no-context-shift` gescheitert. `AGENTS.md`, `agents.yaml` und `agents-map.md` folgen redaktionell.

Beide Messreihen samt Reproduktionsbefehl stehen dauerhaft in den Loadout-Notes.

## Issue

Closes #473

## Objectif

Réparer le flux de désignation d’un administrateur entreprise dans la Console DTSC, aussi bien lors de la création d’une entreprise cliente que lors de sa modification, sans affaiblir le contrat d’audit ni le workflow d’acceptation explicite.

## Impact livraison

High

## Changements

- suppression des boutons rapides `Admin: <nom>` ;
- combobox contrôlée pour l’administrateur initial dans le formulaire de création ;
- combobox contrôlée unique pour désigner/changer l’administrateur dans le formulaire d’édition ;
- apparition conditionnelle d’un champ de motif obligatoire après sélection ;
- validation Zod dédiée `adminUserId + adminReason` à la création ;
- maintien du contrat `grant_admin + reason` à l’édition ;
- persistance du motif dans `OrganizationAdminGrant.reason` et l’audit ;
- refus des invitations qui écraseraient silencieusement un admin actif, propriétaire actif ou une invitation pending ;
- affichage séparé des administrateurs actifs et invitations `INVITED` ;
- erreurs API structurées par `reasonCode` + champ métier, sans diagnostic Zod/Prisma brut côté client ;
- séparation de la mise à jour générale et de l’invitation admin pour éviter les toasts succès/erreur contradictoires ;
- messages spécifiques FR/EN ;
- renforcement responsive/mobile sur la surface touchée ;
- QA ciblée #473 intégrée à la regression gate canonique ;
- documentation/changelog du hotfix.

## Hors scope

- refonte globale de toutes les chaînes historiques de la Console ;
- modification du modèle Prisma ;
- changement du workflow d’acceptation des invitations ;
- déploiement Preview Vercel.

## Dette de contribution

- Dette créée : Aucune
- Dette maintenue : Aucune connue dans le périmètre
- Dette remboursée : désalignement motif UI/backend, création sans motif, boutons rapides non auditables, pending invisible, erreurs génériques et succès partiels trompeurs
- Dette reportée : Aucune

## Base de données / Prisma

- migration : aucune nouvelle migration dans le hotfix
- backfill : aucun
- compatibilité : modèles existants `OrganizationMember` / `OrganizationAdminGrant` conservés ; états `INVITED/PENDING → ACTIVE` inchangés
- rollback : revert applicatif/documentaire de cette PR, sans restauration de données

## Sécurité / RBAC / multi-tenant

- session DTSC interne, capability Console, same-origin et rate-limit conservés ;
- utilisateur cible revalidé `ACTIVE` côté serveur ;
- aucune autorisation fondée sur l’UI ;
- aucune extension d’accès inter-tenant ;
- motif d’attribution conservé dans l’audit protégé ;
- aucune nouvelle invitation ne remplace silencieusement un accès admin/propriétaire actif ou une invitation déjà pending.

## Variables d’environnement / secrets

Aucun.

## Validation automatique

- [x] diff check
- [x] Prisma generate
- [x] migrations sur base propre
- [x] type-check
- [x] lint
- [x] regression QA
- [x] QA ciblée #473 via la regression gate
- [x] build

CI_PROVEN : Quality gates #4076, head exact `93fe732f54d027ea0b7d89e68c72a3202b73434d`, conclusion `success`.

Le run précédent #4075 a détecté deux erreurs TypeScript dans `OrganizationEditDialog` ; elles ont été corrigées avant #4076. Aucune réussite n’est attribuée à #4075.

## Politique Vercel

Les commits de branche/PR restent sur GitHub et ne doivent pas déclencher de déploiement Vercel. Seul le commit fusionné sur `main` part vers Vercel Production. `OWNER_E2E` reste une preuve distincte et ne dépend pas d'un Preview Vercel.

## Validation UI / i18n / accessibilité

- [x] mobile — OWNER_E2E validé par le propriétaire
- [x] parcours de création — OWNER_E2E validé
- [x] parcours de modification — OWNER_E2E validé
- [x] invitation administrateur en attente visible — OWNER_E2E validé
- [x] motif obligatoire après sélection — OWNER_E2E validé
- [x] absence des boutons rapides Admin — OWNER_E2E validé

Les contrats statiques FR/EN, responsive et accessibilité sont couverts par la CI ; l’acceptation fonctionnelle du hotfix a été validée par le propriétaire sur le head exact de la PR.

## Validation fonctionnelle

- [x] création entreprise + admin initial + motif
- [x] modification entreprise + changement/désignation admin + motif
- [x] état invitation en attente
- [x] permissions — CI_PROVEN par Quality gates #4076 / regression QA
- [x] tenant isolation — CI_PROVEN par Quality gates #4076 / regression QA

## E2E

- [ ] non requis
- [x] requis et exécuté
- [ ] requis mais restant à valider

OWNER_E2E validé le 22 août 2026 par le propriétaire sur le head exact `93fe732f54d027ea0b7d89e68c72a3202b73434d`.

Scénarios validés :
1. création entreprise + admin initial + motif → invitation en attente ;
2. entreprise existante + changement/désignation admin + motif → invitation en attente ;
3. parcours d’invitation/admin conforme au hotfix.

## Matrice de preuves

| Contrôle | Statut | Preuve |
|---|---|---|
| diff check | CI_PROVEN | Quality #4076 · `Diff checks` success |
| Prisma generate | CI_PROVEN | Quality #4076 + Migration #4076 · génération success |
| migrations | CI_PROVEN | Migration #4076 · migrations from scratch success ; aucune nouvelle migration du hotfix |
| type-check | CI_PROVEN | Quality #4076 · `Type check` success |
| QA ciblée #473 | CI_PROVEN | `scripts/qa-hotfix-473-enterprise-admin-invitation.mjs` intégré à `Regression QA`, success dans Quality #4076 |
| responsive / standard experience | CI_PROVEN | Regression QA success dans Quality #4076 |
| regression QA | CI_PROVEN | Quality #4076 · `Regression QA` success |
| lint | CI_PROVEN | Quality #4076 · `Lint` success |
| build | CI_PROVEN | Quality #4076 · `Build` success |
| E2E requis | OWNER_E2E | Validé le 22 août 2026 sur `93fe732f54d027ea0b7d89e68c72a3202b73434d` |

## Risques

Les risques techniques sont couverts par la validation serveur et Quality gates #4076. Le parcours fonctionnel du hotfix a été validé en OWNER_E2E avant fusion.

## Rollback

Revert de la PR #474. Aucune migration ni backfill ; les invitations déjà créées restent des données métier valides et ne sont pas supprimées automatiquement par le rollback.

## Documentation

- `docs/CHANGELOG_ENTERPRISE_ADMIN_INVITATION_HOTFIX_473.md`
- Issue #473 enrichie avec création + modification et scénarios OWNER_E2E.

## Release note

La Console DTSC guide désormais la désignation d’un administrateur entreprise avec une sélection unique et un motif obligatoire, lors de la création comme lors d’un changement ultérieur. Les invitations en attente sont visibles et l’accès ne devient actif qu’après acceptation explicite.

## Preuves

- CI_PROVEN : Quality gates #4076 success sur `93fe732f54d027ea0b7d89e68c72a3202b73434d`.
- OWNER_E2E : validé le 22 août 2026 sur le même head exact.
- Production : déclenchée uniquement après fusion sur `main`, conformément à la politique sans Preview.

## Gouvernance de contribution

- [x] J'ai lu et respecté `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [x] Je n'ai introduit aucune dette silencieuse ; toute dette reportée possède une Issue.
- [x] Je n'ai déclaré aucun test, build, E2E ou déploiement réussi sans preuve réelle.

author: ronaldtse
body:
## Summary

Closes the DTD residual limits AND fixes the conformance runner's first-run find: a segfault present in released v1.1.0 (issue #478).

- **%pe; in decl bodies**: internal PEs splice into ELEMENT/ATTLIST/NOTATION declarations before parsing (content models, ATTLIST lists — the real-world pattern). ENTITY decls excluded (literal % legal in values). Nested refs depth-capped.
- **External PEs**: `leptris_dtd_set_pe_loader` — app-owned I/O for `<!ENTITY % pe SYSTEM>`; consulted when content is parsed into the DTD (contract in dtd.h); skipped leniently without a loader.
- **W3C conformance runner** (`test_dtd_w3c`): optional corpus via `LEPTRIS_XMLCONF_DIR` (not vendored — license/scale), scans all group masters, runs valid+invalid cases FORK-ISOLATED (crash = failed case). First-run floors recorded: valid 93.8%, invalid 26.6% (leniency by design). Ratchet only up.
- **Issue #478 fix**: UTF-16+entity documents corrupted sibling edges — `dp_wire_child`'s three edge writes were raw int32 casts that can collide with the overflow sentinel; decoding then reads an unwritten overflow-table entry and returns a wild pointer. All writes now route through `leptris_compact_int32_encode`; `last_child_stack` cleared on close-tag (placed after the decrement — the pre-decrement index at max depth wrote past the array, caught by ASAN).

## Test plan

- [x] 49/49 dtd specs (4 new); full suite 622/622.
- [x] ASAN clean across all suites; zero leaks over 3× parse+validate+free of the crasher document.
- [x] Crasher walks clean 10/10 (was 30/30 segfault); verified present at the v1.1.0 tag before the fix.
- [x] PerfRegression ratio gates pass unchanged (encode routing is free).

author: lior-nis
body:
## Summary

Second slice of Stage 5 ("seam factories") — spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-system-simplification-design.md` §5 item 1; plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-stage-5b-broker-factory.md`.

**This is the slice that sits on the paper/live safety boundary** — paper is simulated, live moves real money. Five hand-rolled helpers each re-read settings, re-checked credentials, and re-wired URLs to build one of four Alpaca broker classes. Now one registry owns that, and each helper is a one-line delegate.

- **`cd16841`** — `algua/execution/broker_factory.py`: name→spec registry over four venues. **Two entry points**, because the missing-credential policy differs by *caller*, not by venue: `build_broker` raises, `maybe_broker` returns `None`. **No default in the lookup.**
- **`6b17615`** — autouse snapshot/restore fixture isolating **four** name→factory registries. Restore, not delete: the previous manual `del _REGISTRY["dummy"]` pattern leaked when a test errored first, and could not revert an *overwrite*.
- **`bba16fa`** — the five helpers reduced to delegates, **with zero test edits**.
- **`69b56c6`** — the registry layer's default forward-certificate verifier routed through the factory.
- **`b46638d`** — review-round fixes (below).

## The design decision, and the measurement behind it

The spec says to *replace* the private helpers. This slice keeps their names as delegates instead — on evidence, not preference: **all 115 test pins target them by name**, so the rewrite cost **zero test edits**. Deleting the names would have forced ~115 pin edits across ten suites, and each fake would then have to dispatch on broker kind, since one factory serves paper, live, live-readonly and drain inside the same test module.

It isn't a dual path: there is exactly one construction implementation and five single-line adapters, so drift is structurally impossible. And the idiom pre-existed — `cli/live_cmd.py:148` was already a one-line delegate with a justifying comment. Each delegate still carries what the factory cannot encode: the concrete return type, the policy expressed as a *type signature*, and per-caller rationale ("resume-all stays lenient"; the drain broker's FAIL-CLOSED reasoning and its deliberate absence of a `LiveAuthorization`).

## Safety

The paper/live separation is enforced independently of construction — **four** separators, the strongest being each concrete class's own `_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, which rejects a crossed `base_url` at construction. The two holes a registry could open are closed: the lookup has **no default** (verified by emptying the registry and confirming both entry points fail closed for every kind), and test registrations can no longer leak.

The final review proved the refactor **byte-identical** to the pre-refactor code — seven entry points × two credential states, comparing class, `base_url`, authorization binding, exception type and message, signature, annotation, and docstring.

## Review found two Important issues; both fixed in `b46638d`

1. **A go-live guard was silently disarmed.** `test_forward_certificate.py`'s credential-refusal test patched `settings_mod.get_settings` — which worked while `transitions.py` imported it lazily in-closure. Routing through the factory moved that binding to module import, making the patch a no-op; the test was green only because the ambient shell had no credentials. With credentials set it **failed**. Now uses `monkeypatch.delenv` and passes both ways. (Same failure class as the `.env` hermeticity bug fixed in #582.)
2. **The refactor was a net loss of static safety, and the docstring claimed the opposite.** `build_broker` returned `Any` and `warn_return_any` is off, so a delegate declared `-> AlpacaPaperBroker` could return a live-readonly broker with mypy silent. Restored with `Literal`-keyed `@overload`s — which also make the `LiveAuthorization` positional **statically required** for the live venue. Verified by mutation: mypy now reports `got "AlpacaLiveReadOnlyBroker", expected "AlpacaPaperBroker"`.

Plus: a narrowed `MissingBrokerCredentials(ValueError)` so a crossed-URL `ValidationError` is no longer misreported as "needs credentials" (it was misreporting **on the safety boundary**), and three plan-text corrections.

## Disclosure

Commit `bba16fa` is missing the `Co-Authored-By` trailer the plan requires; the other four have it. Fixing it needs a three-commit history rewrite, which isn't worth the risk for a convention miss — flagging rather than papering over it.

## Follow-ups worth filing (out of scope here)

- `cli/live_cmd.py:96` `_live_account_equity` is a sixth hand-rolled live-credential site that hits `/v2/account` with raw headers, bypassing the broker classes' `_ALLOWED_HOSTS` and relying on the settings validator alone.
- The three §5 registries are inconsistent: brokers are enum-keyed (closed), providers and trackers string-keyed (open). The enum is the right trade at this boundary, but it should be a recorded decision.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest -q` — **3473 passed** (3454 → 3473; +19 tests, none deleted)
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` / `uv run mypy algua` (242 files) / `uv run lint-imports` (23 kept, 0 broken)
- [x] Zero test edits in the delegate task — verified by `git show --name-only`
- [x] 4 task reviews + final whole-branch review + fix-round re-review, all APPROVE

author: sanskar-soni-9
body:
## What kind of change does this PR introduce?

Feature

## What is the current behavior?

Closes #346

Foreign table column types aren't validated against what `Cell` can actually represent, so an unsupported type fails late and indirectly:

- **On read**, the `Cell`'s Datum is written into the output slot with no type check, so an incompatible type like `point` yields garbage or crashes rather than erroring.
- **On write**, an unrecognized `rowid_column` OID makes `Cell::from_polymorphic_datum` return `None`, so `DELETE`/`UPDATE` silently no-op.

Either way the user finds out far from the `CREATE FOREIGN TABLE` statement that caused it.

## What is the new behavior?

A `check_supported_column_types` event trigger fires on `ddl_command_end` and rejects the offending statement immediately:

```
ERROR:  foreign table "my_table" has columns with unsupported data types: "loc" (type point)
HINT:   supported column types are: boolean, "char", smallint, integer, bigint, real,
        double precision, numeric, text, character varying, ... arrays of these, and
        domains over any of these
```

- **Scoped to this extension.** The check resolves the table's FDW handler and confirms via `pg_depend` that it belongs to the `wrappers` extension, so `postgres_fdw`, `file_fdw` and friends are untouched — verified against a live `file_fdw` table with an unsupported column.
- **Domains resolve to their base type**, so `CREATE DOMAIN my_text AS text` is accepted. All offending columns are reported in a single error rather than one at a time.
- **`varchar`/`bpchar` are now genuinely supported.** `from_polymorphic_datum` previously matched only `text`, so a `varchar` `rowid_column` silently failed to parse. This PR adds the missing match arms — a latent bug fix riding along with the validation. Happy to split it into its own PR if you'd rather review it separately.

## Additional context

**On the approach.** I weighed an event trigger against `object_access_hook` / `ProcessUtility_hook` and went with the event trigger: it's the documented, version-stable interface for DDL interception, whereas those hooks are internal API with no cross-version guarantee and would require the extension to own global hook chaining. Flagging this explicitly since it's the main design decision in the PR — happy to rework it if you'd prefer a hook-based approach.

**Known limits.**

1. Validation is against the union of what `Cell` supports, not per-FDW. A type `Cell` handles but a particular FDW doesn't will still fail at query time; per-FDW type declarations would be a natural follow-up.
2. The trigger is registered for the `ALTER TABLE` tag as well as `ALTER FOREIGN TABLE`, because Postgres tags `ALTER TABLE <foreign_table> ADD COLUMN` as the former. It therefore fires on every `ALTER TABLE` and filters via the `pg_depend` lookup above — one indexed catalog query on a path that isn't hot.

**Implementation notes.** Registration reuses the build-time versioned-library-name pattern already used for `s3vec`, guarded with `EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object` so `ALTER EXTENSION wrappers UPDATE` stays idempotent. New `#[pg_test]` coverage uses a small self-contained test FDW rather than a feature-gated one, so it runs under CI's default `native_fdws` invocation and not just locally. No new dependencies and no changes to the ForeignDataWrapper trait; the only change to existing runtime behavior is the varchar/bpchar fix noted above.

body: The repository is mixed-license. This change makes that boundary explicit so `gallery/` is not read as MIT. ## Rule - **Ranger-authored code outside `gallery/`:** MIT unless a file or subdirectory says otherwise. - **Ranger-authored code under `gallery/`:** AGPL-3.0-or-later unless a file or subdirectory says otherwise. - **Third-party files:** keep the license their authors gave them. A path does not re-license vendor code. The compiler stays a tool. It does not impose a license on programs compiled with Ranger. The license of generated output follows the source: - proprietary `.rgr` → proprietary output - AGPL gallery source → AGPL output (`.js`, `.cpp`, `.wasm`, executable included) Runtime helpers the compiler writes into the output (`Lang.rgr` / `lib/` polyfills) are MIT. Using EVG or another gallery module is using that framework; the AGPL then applies. ## Files | File | Role | | --- | --- | | `LICENSE` | Mixed-license overview (not a single license text) | | `LICENSE-MIT` | Full MIT text | | `LICENSE-AGPL-3.0` | Full GNU AGPLv3 text | | `gallery/LICENSE` | Gallery notice so a copied `gallery/` tree still names AGPL | | `LICENSING.md` | Path rule, generated-output rule, commercial-license *may*, MIT→AGPL dependency direction, third-party exceptions, copyright/relicensing note | | Ranger `.rgr` sources | `SPDX-License-Identifier` so a copied file keeps its license | Root `LICENSE` is an overview on purpose. A GitHub license badge that said only “MIT” would be wrong once `gallery/` is AGPL. `package.json` stays `"license": "MIT"` because the published `ranger-compiler` package is the compiler only. author: delef
body:
Closes #24.

> **Stacked on #23.** This branch forks from `fix/replayed-tool-call-in-user-message`, so the first two commits here are that PR's — the base has to be a branch in this repo, and the parent lives in the fork. Review the last four commits; I will rebase once #23 lands.

The `claude` route sent no `cache_control` at all, so every agentic step reprocessed `tools`, `system` and the whole history at full weight — on a subscription that burns the compute window far faster than the CLI this route presents as. Two prefix-stability fixes land first, because a breakpoint over an unstable prefix is a cache write nobody reads.

### `fix(claude): order tools by name for a stable cache prefix`

`tools` renders at position 0 of the cached prefix, so any reordering invalidates everything behind it. Registration order belongs to the caller and plugin load order can differ between processes, so the wire order is fixed by name. Anthropic selects a tool by name; the array order carries nothing.

### `fix(claude): keep a mid-conversation system message in place`

`toAnthropicMessages` skipped every system-role message and `toAnthropicSystem` appended them all to the `system` array, so one produced at turn 20 landed ahead of the whole history and changed the prefix in front of every cached turn. Only the system messages preceding the conversation are hoisted now; a later one rides in `messages` at its own position, wrapped in `<system-reminder>` — the same shape Claude Code itself uses, and model-independent, unlike the typed `{"role": "system"}` form (Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 / Fable 5 only, 400 elsewhere).

### `feat(claude): cache the prompt prefix and the conversation tail`

Four breakpoints, the API maximum:

- **One on the last `system` block.** `tools` renders ahead of `system`, so one marker caches both. Keeping it separate from the message marks is what bounds the damage of an effort or thinking change: those invalidate the messages tier only, and this entry survives.
- **Three rolling marks across the history**, on the last content block and every 15 blocks backwards. A breakpoint looks back at most 20 content blocks for an entry an earlier request wrote; one agentic turn can append a dozen `tool_use`/`tool_result` blocks, so a lone tail marker silently falls out of range. Three marks at stride 15 keep consecutive write points inside the window and tolerate a turn appending ~45 blocks.

The history is append-only, so the block one request marks last is byte-identical in the next — that entry is what the next request reads.

Default 5-minute TTL only, and no new `anthropic-beta` flag. `ttl: "1h"` is deliberately out of scope: sources disagree on whether `extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11` is still required, and a rejected beta flag would fail every request on this route. Reads refresh the 5-minute entry, so a working loop keeps it alive; only an idle gap longer than 5 minutes costs one re-write.

### `test(claude): cover the cache breakpoints on the assembled body`

`claudeRequestBody` is extracted the way `codexRequestBody` already is, so the wire shape the adapter ships — breakpoint count and placement above all — is asserted without a network round trip.

## Verification

`pnpm test`: 128 tests, 122 pass, 0 fail, 6 skipped (the skips predate this branch). Mutating the two placement lines kills 9 of the new tests.

Live check against the subscription endpoint, ~9.4k-token prefix on Haiku 4.5 — whose 4096-token minimum cacheable prefix is the strictest of any current model, so a hit there holds everywhere:

```
request 1 (cold): input=3  cache_write=9411  cache_read=0
request 2 (warm): input=3  cache_write=14    cache_read=9411
```

The second request read 9411 tokens from cache and wrote 14 — only the new turn. Before this branch both fields were zero and `input_tokens` was ~9400 on every request.

author: mostvalue
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

The CUTLASS FP8 MoE kernels use `448 / amax` to quantize FC1 output.
For a very small nonzero block, this division can overflow FP32. The
quantized values then become non-finite, and FC2 can return NaN.

This change first computes the dequantization scale, `amax / 448`. It clamps
that value to the smallest normal FP32 value, then takes the reciprocal. This
keeps both scales finite. A block whose maximum is zero still uses scale 1.

The same helper is used in the four block-quantization kernels that had the
same division pattern.

The regression test uses fixed inputs. They produce a tiny but nonzero FC1
output that makes the old division overflow. The test checks that the result
is finite, nonzero, and close to a direct FP32 reference.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Fixes #2595

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

Validation:

- NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, SM90
- CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130
- Unpatched run: FlashInfer commit `76704c45003cabaa832d59896080f91dca23f74b`
- Patched source rebased onto FlashInfer commit `8cd56793b032bf8469da6d3b3487a26304e98765`
- The changed kernel file is the same in both upstream commits.
- Before the fix: the failing probe returned 512 NaN values out of 512 values.
- Before the fix: the fixed-input test returned zero; its FP32 reference was `1.0486e-34`.
- After the fix: all 11 scale probes returned finite values.
- Regression test: `1 passed, 3 warnings in 86.68s`.
- Full `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.

All tests run for this change passed. The full hardware matrix will run in CI.

## Reviewer Notes

This bug is separate from #3650. That PR handles NaNs from padded grouped-GEMM
rows. This PR prevents an FP32 overflow while quantizing a valid FC1 output
block.

TensorRT-LLM still has the same `448 / amax` pattern in its copy of this
kernel. I can send the same fix upstream after this change is reviewed.

## Summary

- keep the Linux Wayland native mpv plane transparent in Flutter
- retain the existing black background for texture-based playback
- add a focused regression test for both composition paths

## Root cause

The Linux native plane is stacked below Flutter's compositor and only becomes visible where Flutter paints transparency. `NativeVideoSurface` wrapped the active native-plane reporter in its default opaque black `ColoredBox`, so mpv could render successfully while the player stayed black.

## Verification

- focused regression test against base `8073ada`: native-plane assertion fails while the texture assertion passes
- focused regression test against this candidate: 2 passed
- `dart format --output=show --set-exit-if-changed lib/playback/native_video_surface.dart test/playback/native_video_surface_test.dart`: passed, 0 changed
- `flutter analyze lib test`: no issues found
- `flutter test --concurrency=1`: 1017 passed, 7 skipped
- `./android/gradlew -p android :app:testDebugUnitTest`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL with the tracked CI Firebase stub created temporarily and removed
- `flutter build linux --release`: passed with Flutter 3.44.8
- Linux bundle contract and `ldd`: required files present, no `not found`
- `git diff --check`: passed

## Manual acceptance

A real Linux Wayland playback session was not available in the build environment. Manual Wayland playback acceptance remains required before release promotion.

Closes #242

## Manual Wayland remediation

The first candidate at `6b452d5` passed CI and static review but failed real CachyOS GNOME Wayland acceptance: audio played while the video remained black. Remediation round 1/1 is now included at `40ba49d`.

The remediation preserves the existing native-plane Flutter transparency fix and additionally attaches/registers the transparent `FlView` before showing and realizing the GTK toplevel, matching Flutter's Linux initialization order. A focused Linux source-contract test freezes this ordering.

The PR remains Draft until `40ba49d` passes manual playback on CachyOS GNOME Wayland. Shutdown-only `FlutterEngineRemoveView` and messenger warnings are out of scope.

author: librevlad
body:
Часть #1131 — доводка по адверсарному аудиту.

## Что было

- Подпись шага гасла возвратом только у двух действий — «Создать событие» и «Добавить в контакты»: экран держал жёсткий список id. «Сохранить контакт» уводит в то же приложение контактов, а его подпись «Открыл карточку контакта: …» висела над объектом вечно — и погасить её человеку было нечем (HIGH из аудита). Та же судьба у «Открыть на карте», «Поделиться», «Открыть ссылку», «Позвонить», «Сообщение», «Написать письмо», «Открыть», «Открыть номер в приложении», выбранного приложения и «Открыть другим приложением» — класса, который карточка называет прямо.
- «Нет календаря» звучало по `resolveActivity` — вопросу, который Android 11+ фильтрует по видимости пакетов. Объявление INSERT/event лежало в `data/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` и доезжало в app-манифест слиянием, но сам вопрос был лишним: `startActivity` видит календарь без объявления и отказывает до того, как что-то откроется. Тест этого не ловил — он проверял `resolveActivity` тем же шадоу-списком, которым и отвечал.

## Что стало

- Признак «шаг отдаёт человека системе» принадлежит действию — `CapabilityMeta.handsOff`. Им отмечены все действия, которые кончаются чужим экраном: календарь, карточка контакта (обе двери), карта, диалог «Поделиться» (обе), набор номера, сообщение, письмо, ссылка, открытие файла, приложение у номера, выбранное приложение, «Открыть другим приложением». Экран спрашивает действие, а не держит список id — так же, как уже спрашивает `localOnly`, `network`, `revealsInside`.
- Возврат в Point гасит подпись у каждого из них молча (решение владельца 20.08.2026, вариант A). «Открыть другим приложением» идёт тем же швом: после запуска выбранного приложения подпись «Открываю в …» гаснет возвратом.
- «Нет календаря» звучит от отказа системы в запуске — до чужого экрана, без вопроса списку приложений. Ставшее ненужным объявление INSERT/event в манифесте `data` убрано: его больше никто не спрашивает.

## Как проверено

- `FlowViewModelTest` — путь человека: поделился → нажал действие → подпись шага → вернулся в Point → подпись погасла, объект на месте. Для каждого настоящего действия класса (`SaveContactCapability`, `VCardCapability`, `MapCapability`, `CallCapability`, `SmsCapability`, `EmailCapability`, `OpenUrlCapability`, `OpenCapability`, `ShareCapability`, `ShareAllCapability`, `PhoneAppsCapability`, `AppCapability`) и для выбранного приложения через `onPickApp`. На старом коде падают: «подпись шага save-contact висит после возврата», «expected null, but was: Открываю в Viewer».
- `AndroidCalendarInserterTest` (Robolectric): «без календаря слово звучит до чужого экрана» — система отказывает в запуске, ничего не открылось; «календарь, невидимый списку приложений, всё равно получает событие» — список о календаре не знает, запуск доходит вместе с найденным днём (#1035). На старом коде второй падает: «На этом устройстве нет календаря».
- Сторож `CementedWordingDoesNotGrowTest` зелёный: новые проверки идут через значения и константы.
- Гейт `./gradlew test assembleDebug` — зелёный.

## Находки аудита

1. HIGH — save-contact и жёсткий список id: закрыта в корне, признак у действия.
2. MEDIUM — `resolveActivity` и видимость пакетов: закрыта в корне, чувствительного вызова больше нет; объявление было в `data`-манифесте (доезжало слиянием), стало ненужным и убрано.
3. MEDIUM — тест календаря: переписан, проверяет путь и падает на старом коде.

Closes #1131

author: sevenx77
body:
Reading a finished run's `run_metadata.json` after two resumes: `auto_commit`
false on an ordinary run that archives, `input_summary` reading "resumed"
instead of what the run was given, `started_at` the last resume's clock rather
than the run's.

One defect. The endpoint built a whole new `RunMetadata` out of the adapter's
answer, so every field that answer did not mention fell back to its default. It
had been noticed once and patched field by field — `_preserve_resume_artifact_identity`
carried three of them across by hand — a list that has to grow with the model
and did not, so `auto_commit` became the fourth casualty the moment it moved
onto the metadata.

A resumed segment knows three things: how it ended, what it spent, and where it
stopped (`ResumeReport`). It does not know when the run started, what the run
was given, or whether the run archives — those belong to the run. So the report
is applied ONTO the run's own record instead of replacing it, and the adapter
stops sending `started_at` and a literal `input_summary: "resumed"` along with
it. `paused_at` is the one field a report clears: no new stopping point means
this segment went past the old one, and a record still naming it says a finished
run is waiting somewhere.

Two more that fell out of the same seam: the runtime-state snapshot also
overwrote the run's `input_summary` with "resumed", and the endpoint answered
with the metadata handed IN rather than the one sealing produced — so a resumed
run that auto-committed reported no `git_status`.

author: n-ichimura
body:
From the code-quality metrics survey (2026-08-22), recommendation 2 — design-doc-first, before any code moves.

`TesseraqlRuntime.start` is **2,344 lines**, the largest method in the tree by a factor of six. The review session just paid its size as a tax four times (a reassignment that broke eleven lambda captures, a declaration hoisted above the `try` purely to survive it, the seams record learning lazy ports).

The design records what is true today, measured: the 45-phase sequence, the three giant inline blocks (~825 lines with no home), the long-range couplings that make naive extraction fail, the catch block's load-bearing release order, the ordering constraints any split must preserve, and the seams that already exist (`StudioProviders`+`RuntimeSeams`, `HttpEdgeBeans` — the templates this reuses).

**Decisions**: extract by the existing patterns, only where a block has no name — no boot framework, no DI, no bean reordering; what a phase hands back, the catch must still see (records the method destructures). Target ~600 lines, explicitly not a gate.

**Four slices**: ① `IamAdminProviders` (~360 lines, verbatim), ② `OpsAccountProviders` (~375-line chain, `StudioProviders`-style groups), ③ `JobRunners` + dashboard assembly, ④ the construct-and-bind prefix as three builders that close their own partial work — which also retires the pre-`try` boot leak — with an explicit abort clause: if the method is already readable after ①–③, stopping is an allowed outcome.

Registered in both internal-doc lists (nav `EXCLUDED` ↔ `ErrorIndex.INTERNAL_DOCS`); sync guards green.

author: prodigystudios
body:
## Vad

Attestens dagtabell visade klockslag och arbetad tid men **aldrig rastavdraget**, så raden gick inte att kontrollräkna: 08:00–18:00 med 9 timmar ser fel ut tills man ser den timmes rast som drogs av. `breakMinutes` fanns redan hela vägen fram på `DayRow` (rättningsformuläret behöver den) — den renderades bara aldrig.

Dessutom: nya tidrapporteringens standardrast **30 → 60 min**.

| Yta | Före | Nu |
|---|---|---|
| Attest → fäll ut person | Datum · Klockslag · Arbetat · Frånvaro · Orsak/jobb · Anteckning | + **Rast** mellan Klockslag och Arbetat, plus månadssumma |
| `/tid` → Ny tidrad | rast 30 min förifyllt | **60 min** |
| Arbetsordern → Tid (installatörens vy) | 60 min | 60 min (oförändrat, men nu samma konstant) |

Gamla Blikk-flödet (`TimeReportModal` på `/tidrapport`, `/mina-jobb`, startsidan) är **orört**.

## Granskningsfynd

Andra commiten är åtgärdade fynd ur granskningen av grenen. Fem rör kolumnen själv:

- **Visa bara rast som faktiskt drogs av.** `workedMinutes` drar av rasten först när det finns två klockslag att räkna emellan — saknas de faller den tillbaka på `minutes_worked`, och radens lagrade rast har aldrig påverkat något. De gamla kontorsraderna är precis sådana, och att visa deras rast hade fått en korrekt rad att se överrapporterad ut med en timme. Regeln är `breakWasDeducted`, delad av cellen och månadssumman.
- Månadssumman ligger i `summarizePerson`, inte som en tredje reduce i klientkomponenten — där kan den testas.
- Foten i timmar, kolumnen i minuter. Fältet matas in i minuter, men månadsraden läses vågrätt mot Arbetat: brutto − rast = arbetat.
- Dagraden läser frånvaro ur `kind`, inte ur `absenceMinutes > 0`.
- Defaulten är `DEFAULT_BREAK_MINUTES` i domänlagret, inte en literal per formulär.

Två är **befintliga hål i `/tid`** som defaultbytet gör dubbelt så dyra — båda har varit spärrade i rättningsmodalen sedan den skrevs:

- Rastfältet tolkades med `Number(x) || 0`, så `0,5` blev en rast på **noll** minuter: en timme extra betald tid, utan felmeddelande och utan spår i ändringsloggen.
- Ingen spärr mot identiska klockslag. `grossMinutes` läser `end <= start` som midnattspassage → 1440 min, och serverns guard är `> 1440`, alltså exklusiv. Ett dubbeltryck skrev **ett dygn** på den egna månaden.

De två sista ligger utanför den ursprungliga beställningen — säg till om de hellre ska brytas ut.

## SQL

Ingen.

## Verifierat

`npm run type-check` ✓ · `npm run lint` ✓ · `npm test` 1760/1760 ✓ (9 nya) · `npm run build` ✓

## Task and requirements

- Task: trap-risk strategy heuristic repair
- Requirement IDs: FR-T3, PLANQ-008, ADR-006
- Task file: `docs/PRD_thief_strategy.md`, `docs/PLAN_thief_strategy.md`, `docs/decisions/ADR-006-strategy-heuristic-priorities.md`
- Related Issue: —

## Outcome

**Comment / architectural finding:** `Board.boxed_in(dest, barriers)` can never be `True` after a legal move from a reachable non-terminal state — the vacated origin is always an unblocked neighbour of `dest` (a barrier can't land on an occupied cell; that's rule-46 capture, not rule-47). The existing `w_trap` materiality test only exercised the term by faking an impossible state (origin set as a barrier), so `w_trap` was structurally dead against any real `ThiefBrain` decision.

Repaired the derived strategy heuristic, not the game rule: `Board.boxed_in` is untouched and stays the rule-47 terminal predicate. Added `scoring.trap_risk(mobility) = mobility <= 1`, a pure strategy-level "conservative dead-end/one-exit risk" signal, and wired it into `select_thief_action` in place of `boxed_in`. `w_trap` still dominates the score as before, now against a predicate that actually fires on reachable states.

author: sornbuen15
body:
Closes DG-266.

## Two guesses, one root cause

Nothing told the Discord daemon which project it was for — while **every MCP
server in this repository takes `--project` and refuses to guess.** The daemon
was the exception, and it guessed twice.

**1. `discord_router` carried a literal.**

```python
DEFAULT_TARGET_PROJECT = "drunken-team"
```

Fallen back to in seven places. That is the fallback checkout this project is
under standing instruction not to touch, so a command sent with no explicit
target acted on the wrong repository — silently, and by default.

**2. `discord_listener` was worse.**

```python
project_id = list(projects.keys())[0]
```

The first key in a JSON file. This machine's registry holds four projects, so
which one the daemon served depended on **insertion order**, and nothing anywhere
reported the choice it made.

**3. The exemption made the literal unfalsifiable.**

```python
if name != DEFAULT_TARGET_PROJECT and not ProjectRegistry().get_project(name):
```

The one name nobody had verified was the only one that skipped verification — and
it stayed trusted even after that project was deregistered.

## The fix

`default_project_id()` replaces all three, using the precedence this project
already settled:

| | |
|---|---|
| **environment variable** (`DRUNKEN_PROJECT`) | explicit and named — how a container passes a different project in |
| **registry, when it holds exactly one** | "the only one" is a fact, not a guess |
| anything else | `None` |

**`None` is a real answer, and the callers handle it.** mypy found every place it
reaches, which turned out to be most of the change. A project-scoped command with
no project **refuses before spawning the subprocess** and names the fix —
`/project <name>` or `DRUNKEN_PROJECT` — because *"unknown project"* only tells
the reader to give up, the rule `core/errors.py` already states for tool results.

The daemon starts either way and says on stderr which project it serves, or that
it has none.

## Tests

Four added, including the case the old code got wrong:

- an explicit variable wins
- one registered project is a fact, not a guess
- **several projects and no variable is no answer** — where the old code returned
  whichever was written to the registry first
- a command with no project refuses *before* the subprocess and names the fix

The three `_run_jira_bridge` tests now state their project rather than inheriting
a literal. That statement is the new contract, which is why they state it instead
of mocking it away.

## Verification

```
747 passed, 1 skipped, 2 deselected     (743 before, +4 new)
coverage            84%
ruff / ruff format / mypy --strict      clean
check_doc_drift     132 documents, nothing retired
```

Branched from `develop`, not stacked. No overlap with #4 or #5.

author: sym01
body:
Stacked on #47 — merge that first and GitHub will retarget this to `main`.

## Badges and switcher

Four badges under the H1, each verified to return a real SVG: **CI**, **Security** (the self-scan workflow), **Go Report Card**, **MIT**. Plus `**English** · [简体中文](docs/README.zh-CN.md)`.

Four badges I deliberately did *not* add, since each would be worse than none:

- **Quality Gate** — triggered by `workflow_run` gated on `workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'`, so it never runs on `main` and the badge renders "no status".
- **pkg.go.dev** — everything but `pkg/ir/v1` and `cmd/godzilla` is under `internal/`; the badge would link to a near-empty API page.
- **Coverage** — there is no `-cover` step anywhere in `.github/`, `Makefile` or `scripts/`.
- **Release/version** — zero git tags. Worth adding in the same commit that tags the first release.

## `docs/README.zh-CN.md`

A full mirror — 13 headings in each file, same order, both mermaid diagrams, all 29 table rows.

The part that silently breaks is link rewriting, so it was done explicitly rather than copied: repo files gain `../`, `docs/` siblings drop the prefix, and the three internal anchors point at the *translated* headings (`#受支持的语言与检测能力` etc.). Verified with a GitHub-compatible slugifier — every relative link resolves and every anchor matches a real heading, in both files.

Code blocks, CLI flags, paths, rule IDs, CWE numbers and mermaid node IDs are left untranslated; terms of art carry the English in parentheses on first use, since `docs/` stays English-only.

`CLAUDE.md` gains a convention (modelled on the existing proto→generated-bindings rule) so the two never drift.

## Drift fixed

- `go.mod` declares **`go 1.26.5`**, not 1.26 — 1.26.0–1.26.4 fails under `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, which the project's own Dockerfile pins.
- `GODZILLA_LLM_MODEL`'s default is `claude-haiku-4-5` only for Anthropic; under `GODZILLA_LLM_PROVIDER=openai` it is `gpt-4o-mini` (`internal/llm/openai.go:39`).
- Neither documented install command stamps a version — `go build` and `go install …@latest` both yield `version = dev`; only `make build` and the Docker image stamp one. Now said out loud.

## Vulnerability reporting

`CONTRIBUTING.md` told people to report vulnerabilities **in Godzilla itself by opening a public issue**. For a SAST tool that is the wrong instruction. It now points at GitHub private vulnerability reporting and states that a missed or false detection is an ordinary — and welcome — public issue.

⚠️ **Needs a one-time repo setting**: Settings → Code security → enable *Private vulnerability reporting*. The link is inert until then.

## PR template

`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` — one "what and why" line plus a checklist of exactly the gates CI already enforces, so the two cannot disagree. No screenshot sections, no breaking-change matrices.

## Not included

No SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, issue templates or CHANGELOG (out of scope by decision). The Docker `latest`/`full` examples stay as-is per your call to tag a release — until a `v*` tag fires `release.yml`, only `edge`/`edge-full` are actually pullable.

## Verification

Every relative link resolves and every anchor matches a real heading in both files; all four badge URLs return `200 image/svg+xml`; heading count, order, mermaid blocks and table rows match between the two; `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` and `gofmt` all clean.

author: rouges78
body:
Follows #105, which measured that RPG Maker composes the whole frame in memory and presents it with a single `StretchBlt`. That blit is the best place to take the image.

`GS_HOOK_FRAME_DUMP=<prefix>` now saves the first frames as `.bmp` from inside the hook, reading the source DC's bitmap directly with `GetDIBits`.

- **The present is recognised by `WindowFromDC(destination)`, not by size.** 320×240 belongs to this game; "the destination is a window" holds for any engine that presents with a blit.
- **The blit hooks are shared with the existing diagnostic** and installed once — two `MH_CreateHook` on one address is a bug, not a convenience.

**Proving the pixels don't come from the screen took two attempts.** Covering the window failed twice: the game takes the foreground back, and the script reported `il gioco NON e coperto, il test non prova niente` rather than passing off a test that hadn't reproduced its own condition.

Moving the window off-screen settled it:

```text
schermo virtuale: 2293x960 da (0,0)
finestra a (2343,100)-(3003,620)  interseca lo schermo: False
[gs-hook/FRAME] #0 320x240 -> ...fuori-0.bmp (ok)
[gs-hook/FRAME] #1 320x240 -> ...fuori-1.bmp (ok)
[gs-hook/FRAME] #2 320x240 -> ...fuori-2.bmp (ok)
```

Not one pixel of that window was on the monitor, and the three captured frames hold the **complete, correct** title screen. No screen capture can produce that.

| | screen capture | at the present |
|---|---|---|
| window covered | grabs the coverer's pixels | irrelevant |
| window off-screen | impossible | **measured: works** |
| overlays, notifications, cursor | land in the frame | don't exist yet |
| resolution | window size, scaled | native 320×240 |
| synchronisation | whatever was there | exactly one frame |

**What it deliberately does not do:** hand frames to the application. It writes a bounded number of files and stops. That bridge needs both sides built together — this repository has collected half-finished IPC before, and that is why the in-game chain stalled for so long. The tap is demonstrated here; the transport is a separate, deliberate step.

Both architectures build clean.

author: vyctorbrzezowski
body:
Part of #125222 (footnotes; math deferred — see scope note below)

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI transcripts currently leave Markdown footnote syntax as raw source text: `[^label]` references and `[^label]: text` definitions render literally, so citation-heavy replies are harder to scan, references are not navigable, and definitions read as broken prose at the end of a message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Footnotes are pure Markdown, so this change renders them with a local markdown-it plugin on the existing Markdown-It 14 stack — no new runtime dependency:

- ordered endnotes section per message with a hairline separator
- superscript references jump to their note; each reference carries its own labeled backlink (`common.back`) returning to the exact anchor
- note ids are namespaced per transcript message via a new `documentId` render option (stable FNV-1a hash), so identical notes in adjacent messages never collide or cross-link
- undefined labels keep their readable source text; duplicate labels merge into the first note; note bodies render as Markdown inside the existing sanitizer boundary (allowlist gains only `section` tags and `id` attributes; same-document fragment anchors keep native navigation instead of being forced to `target="_blank"`)

Scope note: math rendering is intentionally not part of this draft. Faithful TeX rendering requires a KaTeX-family dependency (`@mdit/plugin-katex` 0.22.0 pulling `katex@0.16.x`, ~4 MB unpacked including fonts, plus `@mdit/plugin-tex`/`helper`). Until that dependency decision lands, `$…$` input keeps rendering as readable source text.

## User Impact

Users can follow superscript footnote references to an ordered endnotes list and return through a backlink that targets the exact reference clicked. Identical footnotes in consecutive messages stay independent. Invalid or undefined footnote syntax remains readable source text instead of dead anchors. Dollar amounts and other `$` text are untouched.

## Evidence

Boundary tests added at the existing sanitized-Markdown seam (footnote navigation, per-message namespacing, repeated references, undefined labels staying literal, plain-text passthrough):

- `pnpm test ui/src/components/markdown.test.ts` — pass (116 tests)
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat` — pass (213 tests)
- `pnpm test ui/src/components ui/src/pages/custodian` — pass
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint, stylelint, oxfmt — clean
- `pnpm ui:build` — within budgets (startup JS +52 B gzip vs 512 B tolerance)

Before (current `main`: raw footnote source):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/362eaf08-b471-43fc-9c4c-e9fae2e15764

After (this branch: navigable endnotes with backlinks):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4eed2ac5-7853-42a1-945e-552d11036829

Captured from the mocked Control UI chat surface (Vite + mocked Gateway) against exact `origin/main` sources and this branch's sources; both frames inspected before attaching.

body:
## Summary

Adds Disaster Recovery Pilot Light to family 20 (release-deployment), the ninth entry authored for this family, taking it to 90 percent. This pattern replicates a workload's data tier continuously to a second region while keeping the compute tier switched off, cutting steady-state cost against a full duplicate environment while still recovering in the tens of minutes rather than the hours a pure backup-and-restore strategy needs.

Both citations come from AWS's own official documentation, the Disaster Recovery Workloads whitepaper and the Well-Architected Framework's Reliability Pillar (REL13-BP02), each at roughly 95 percent confidence and needing no dedicated verification pass. A third reference line cites the Well-Architected page a second time for a distinct passage, the ordered spectrum-free list of DR strategies by cost, complexity, RTO, and RPO, satisfying the structural minimum without inventing a new, unverified source.

All 18 dimensions present. name and lineage, problem and context, forces, applicability and non-applicability, structure, ASCII diagram, dynamics, implementation variants, known production uses, consequences, failure modes, trade-off matrix, related and incompatible patterns, refactoring path in and out, testing and verification, observability signals, security and privacy implications, code examples in Swift, Kotlin, and Python.

Related entries listed are Warm Standby (queued as the tenth and final family-20 entry) and Blue-Green Deployment.

Every generated code block was inspected directly before running the compile gate. No defects found.

This branch was rebased onto main after PR #358 (the coverage-gap queue update) merged mid-flight. The rebase conflicted in three generated files, resolved by taking main's content then fully regenerating from the merged tree, so the final numbers reflect both changes together rather than either one alone.

## Verification

Full six-pass gate run against the rebased tree, after PR #358 merged.

- `check-structure.py`. 796/796 entries pass. Two issues were caught and fixed during drafting, the frontmatter was missing `slug` and `verified` keys, and the non-applicability section heading did not match the required substring.
- `check-family-names.py`. 23 family folders match README
- `check-prose.py`. 830/830 files pass, zero banned terms. One AI-slop word, spectrum, was caught and reworded in two places before the write completed
- `markdownlint-cli2@0.23.2`. zero issues
- `validate-refs.py --strict`. 4133 distinct citations, all resolve
- `check-code.py --strict --only disaster-recovery-pilot-light`. 2/2 compiled, 0 failed (Kotlin excluded from the compile count per the existing repo-wide checker set)
- `check-duplicates.py` (advisory). one new advisory flag, the newly-queued Intercepting Filter shares a keyword with the published Chain of Responsibility. Genuinely distinct patterns (J2EE Core Patterns versus GoF), noted for when Intercepting Filter is authored, not a real collision

Three-pass review performed before merge. Structure pass, all 18 dimensions present and correctly ordered. Citations-and-prose pass, both AWS sources were high-confidence on first fetch, no dedicated verification agent was needed, and the two structural issues plus the one banned word were fixed before the final gate run. Gates pass, all six required gates plus the advisory duplicate check green against the rebased, freshly-regenerated tree, all Swift, Kotlin, and Python code compiled on the first attempt.

README family-20 row synced from 8/2/10 to 9/1/10. The three generator scripts were re-run in the standard order after the rebase and confirm published equals 796, target equals 882, stale equals 0, correctly combining this entry with PR #358's queue additions.

body:
## 概要

Closes #93

issue #45・#79でポイが破れるとゲームオーバーになり操作不能になるが、リスタートする手段が無く、ページ再読み込みするしかなかった問題への対応。

## 設計

- ゲームオーバー表示内に「リトライ」ボタンを追加。押下で以下をリセットする
  - `useGoldfishSchool`の新規`resetGoldfish`（金魚を初期配置へ再生成）
  - `useElapsedTimer`の新規`reset`（経過時間を0・未計測状態へ）
  - `setIsTorn(false)`
- ランキング（issue #89、過去の記録）はリセットしない

## 実装中に見つけた別バグの修正

リトライ後の2回目以降の掬うジェスチャーがPoi側で検知されなくなる実バグを発見し、合わせて修正しました。

`usePoiMotion.ts`のscoopCount更新が「effectローカル変数を0から数え直して`setScoopCount(ローカル変数)`」する実装だったため、`isTorn`の変化でこのeffectが再購読される（issue #79の既存仕様）たびにローカルカウンタが0からリセットされる一方、React state自体は前回の値を保持したままでした。リトライ前にちょうど1回だけ掬っていた場合、リトライ後の最初の掬うジェスチャーでローカルカウンタが1になり、直前のReact stateの値（1）と偶然一致してReactが更新を素通りし（`Object.is`比較で同値のためスキップ）、Poi側の`useEffect`が`scoopCount`の変化を検知できず`onScoop`が呼ばれなくなっていました。`setScoopCount(prev => prev + 1)`という関数形の更新式に変更し、常に直前のReact state値を正しく引き継いで増分するようにして解消しました。

## 影響範囲

author: llbartekll
body:
## Problem

`mnemonic_validate` accepts all 10 BIP-39 languages, but every parse path hardcoded `Language::English`:

- `mnemonic_to_seed` (key-wallet-ffi)
- `wallet_create_from_mnemonic` / `wallet_create_from_mnemonic_with_options` (key-wallet-ffi)
- the four `*_derive_*_from_mnemonic` exports in `account_derivation.rs` (key-wallet-ffi)
- `WalletManager::create_wallet_from_mnemonic` / `create_wallet_from_mnemonic_return_serialized_bytes` (key-wallet-manager) — which also feed the three `wallet_manager_add_wallet_from_mnemonic*` FFI exports and the `dash-spv` binary
- `impl FromStr for Mnemonic` (key-wallet)

A valid French/Spanish/… phrase validated and then failed seed derivation and wallet creation. This shipped in Dash Wallet iOS 9.0.0 and broke wallet recovery, Add Wallet, and the upgrade-time key migration for every non-English mnemonic — including wallets the old DashSync-era app itself generated on non-English-locale devices. (`rs-platform-wallet` carries its own `parse_mnemonic_any_language` workaround for the same gap; with this fix upstream it can eventually drop it.)

## Fix

- New `Mnemonic::from_phrase_in_any_language(phrase)` in key-wallet: a deterministic per-language walk in `Language::ALL` order (English first) — the same semantics `mnemonic_validate` already had. Deliberately **not** bip39's autodetecting `Mnemonic::parse`, whose `language_of` fails with `AmbiguousLanguages` when every word is shared across wordlists. First-match is deterministic, and since BIP-39 seeds are PBKDF2 over the phrase text itself, a hypothetical cross-language full-phrase collision could only affect language *reporting*, never the derived seed.
- `Language::ALL` (the previously private `ALL_LANGUAGES` const, now a public associated const) and a `Mnemonic::language()` accessor; the four `account_derivation` exports detect the language and pass it to the derivation helpers.
- All the call sites above switched to the new parse. `mnemonic_validate` now shares the same parse call, so validate ⇔ parse is one code path and cannot diverge again. The bincode `Decode`/`BorrowDecode` impls use the same walk (they previously used bip39 autodetect under a comment claiming "default to English").
- FFI signatures unchanged — no new extern fns. Doc comments updated (the "Uses the English wordlist" claims) and `key-wallet-ffi/FFI_API.md` regenerated.

## Behavior notes

- Strictly widening: English is tried first, so English phrases parse byte-identically to before.
- Error code unchanged (`InvalidMnemonic`). The no-match message is now uniformly `Invalid mnemonic: does not match any supported language` (byte-identical to what `mnemonic_validate` already produced). One visible difference: an *English phrase with a typo* previously got bip39's specific diagnostic ("unknown word", "bad word count") from the parse paths; it now gets the generic no-match message. Callers that string-match error messages would be affected; error codes are not.

## Testing

All new non-English tests **fail without the fix** — e.g. the symmetry test dies at `ChineseSimplified: to_seed must accept a validated phrase`, and the French reference-vector test at `French phrase must derive a seed` (verified by stashing the source changes and running the new tests against the unfixed code).

- **key-wallet**: 10-language `from_phrase_in_any_language` round trip (detected language, phrase, and seed all match the language-tagged parse); NFC-typed French input derives the same seed as the NFKD form; invalid/empty/bad-checksum rejection with the pinned message; English-first ordering contract; `language()` accessor across all 10 languages; `FromStr` on a French phrase; bincode round trip of a French mnemonic.
- **key-wallet-ffi**: `mnemonic_validate` ⇒ `mnemonic_to_seed` ⇒ `wallet_create_from_mnemonic` symmetry across all 10 languages; a French reference vector whose expected 64-byte seed was computed independently of this codebase (python `hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha512', NFKD(phrase), b"mnemonic", 2048)`); French+Spanish wallet creation; BLS/EdDSA provider keys derived `*_from_mnemonic` match `*_from_seed` for a French phrase; the secp helpers now get past the parse (standard-account refusal is `InvalidInput`, no longer `InvalidMnemonic`). All new FFI tests free every returned pointer (ASAN job).
- **key-wallet-manager**: French wallet creation; French serialized-bytes round trip through `import_wallet_from_bytes` (exercises the bincode decode path end-to-end).
- Suites: `cargo test -p key-wallet -p key-wallet-ffi -p key-wallet-manager --all-features` green (669 / 244 / all-suites); `cargo clippy` on the three crates `--all-features --all-targets` clean; `cargo fmt --all` clean; `contrib/verify_ffi.py` clean after the committed `FFI_API.md` regen (`dash-spv-ffi/FFI_API.md` untouched); `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc` clean; `cargo check --workspace --all-features` on 1.95 and `cargo +1.89 check` (MSRV) on the three crates clean.

author: helloprogh
body:
## What changed

Corrects the OpenCode web API prefix and aligns model parsing/UI with the concrete backend responses.

### OpenCode web API prefix

All session/model web APIs now use `/dataagent/web/opencode`:

- `POST /dataagent/web/opencode/api/session`
- `GET /dataagent/web/opencode/api/model`
- `GET /dataagent/web/opencode/api/model/default`
- `POST /dataagent/web/opencode/api/session/{sessionId}/model`

The Adapter and Vite dev proxy forward this prefix to upstream `/api/...` endpoints.

### Model response parsing

The model catalog supports the actual response where `data` is the model array. The default-model endpoint uses the same envelope with a single model object in `data`.

Only selection/display fields are normalized (`id`, `name`, `enabled`, `capabilities`, optional provider identity). Provider credentials such as `settings.apiKey` are neither retained nor rendered.

The switch API still requires `{ providerID, id }`. If the catalog does not include an explicit provider id, the frontend falls back to `local`, matching the supplied local-model response example.

### Composer UI

- model selector is visually positioned immediately left of the native CopilotKit Send/Stop button
- the previous dedicated model row no longer consumes vertical space
- composer uses the Soft Technical Dark surface, lighter border/focus treatment, improved textarea/placeholder contrast, and refined Send button styling
- model dropdown is compact and can show `TOOLS` / `VISION` capability badges
- CopilotKit continues to own send/stop behavior; no custom stop integration is introduced

### Conversation identity

Existing contract remains unchanged: `ConversationRecord.id === AG-UI threadId === OpenCode sessionId`.

## Validation status

Frontend typecheck/build and Adapter test/build are being re-run against this branch. Keep this PR Draft until verification completes.

body:
### Changed
- **All three deployment lists now open a rollout the same way: as a page of its own.** The release manager's list had that page, and 0.35.0 replaced it with a row that expanded in place — which turned out to be the worse of the two: the detail carries a day schedule, a target queue and a timeline, and inside a table cell each of those became a scroll pane nested in a scroll pane. The page is back, and the deployer's panel and the client's portal — which had always expanded their rows — now do the same. One interaction for „open this rollout", so somebody who works in two of these views does not carry two mental models. Every page has the same chrome: „← Back to the list", and the row it came from as a heading (applications and versions, then project · environment · date) — a page opened out of a list has to say which row it is. Escape closes it in all three, switching views in the rail closes it, and the scroll offsets of the day plan and the queue survive the re-render that every edit inside the page causes.
- With the list off screen while a deployment is open, **the package is named again on the action bar** — id, name and a copy button, for every role rather than only the ones that may edit it. Nothing repeats it there now, which is what made it redundant while the row was visible. The client's page carries the same line, since the id heads the fixed-issue list they read.

author: vinneyto
body:
## Summary

Turn the repository into an installable Python project so the Metal renderer can be consumed directly from another repository.

- add `pyproject.toml` with setuptools + `src/` layout
- expose the public API as:
  ```python
  from course_3dgs import GaussianData, MetalRenderer
  ```
- move the renderer to `src/course_3dgs/metal_renderer/`
- move all `.metal` kernels into the installed package
- load kernels through `importlib.resources` instead of paths relative to the repository checkout
- include `kernels/*.metal` as setuptools package data
- move covariance/quaternion helpers needed by `GaussianData.from_checkpoint()` into the package so the installed renderer does not depend on root-level `util.py`
- replace `requirements.txt` with runtime + optional dependencies in `pyproject.toml`
  - runtime: `torch`, `numpy`
  - `notebooks` extra: matplotlib, Pillow, torchmetrics, anywidget
  - `tilelang` extra: TileLang
- update `3dgs_metal.ipynb` and the Metal primitive smoke script to use the packaged implementation
- update tests to validate the public package import and that all five Metal source files are accessible as package resources
- ignore standard Python build artifacts

## Usage from another repository

With uv:

```bash
uv add "course-3dgs @ git+https://github.com/vinneyto/course_3dgs.git"
```

For reproducible builds, pin a tag or commit:

```bash
uv add "course-3dgs @ git+https://github.com/vinneyto/course_3dgs.git@<commit-or-tag>"
```

Then:

```python
from course_3dgs import GaussianData, MetalRenderer
```

For working on this repository itself, notebook dependencies can be installed with:

```bash
uv sync --extra notebooks
```

and TileLang additionally with:

```bash
uv sync --extra tilelang
```

## Validation

- branch is based on the current `main` after the class-based SH renderer merge
- GitHub recognizes the renderer and all five Metal kernels as moves into `src/course_3dgs/...`, rather than duplicated implementations
- tests now target the installed public API and package resources
- `3dgs_metal.ipynb` imports the same `course_3dgs` API an external consumer will use

End-to-end Metal execution still requires running on Apple Silicon/MPS.

author: uraitakahito
body:
pnpm 移行の Stage 1 + 2 です。

## Stage 1 と 2 を分けられませんでした

計画では別々の PR にする想定でしたが、**lockfile を替えた瞬間に `npm ci` が「package-lock.json が無い」で落ちる**ため、CI の変更と同じ PR でなければ緑になりません。計画のこの部分は誤りでした。

## `pnpm-workspace.yaml`

`packages:` は宣言していません（docs-site を入れるのは別の段）。このファイルが要るのは 2 つの理由です。

**`allowBuilds`** — pnpm 11 は依存の lifecycle script を既定で実行しません。`node_modules` を走査した実測で、該当は 2 つだけでした。

| パッケージ | 判断 | 理由 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@bufbuild/buf` | `true` | postinstall がプラットフォーム別の buf バイナリを取ってくる。止めると `buf generate` がまるごと落ちる |
| `protobufjs` | `false` | postinstall は警告を出すだけで機能に関与しない |

browserhive が許可している `esbuild` / `unrs-resolver` は **waggle の `node_modules` に入っていない**ので写経していません。`enablePrePostScripts` も足していません（waggle の script に `pre*`/`post*` は 1 つも無い）。

**`overrides`** — pnpm 11 は `package.json` の `overrides` を読みません。移設のついでに点検しました。

| override | 扱い |
| --- | --- |
| `js-yaml: ^4.3.0` | **削除**。依存グラフに 1 箇所も無く、何もしていなかった |
| `brace-expansion: ^5.0.8` | **`^5.0.9` に修正**。勧告の修正版は `>=5.0.9` で、旧指定は脆弱な版そのものを許していた |
| `axios: ^1.18.1` | そのまま移設 |

## ⚠ 依存の版が 56 個動きます

lockfile を作り直すと、**宣言した範囲の中で** 56 パッケージが新しい版に解決されます。`pnpm import` を試しましたが同じでした（範囲内で再解決するため、npm の固定は引き継げません）。`rm package-lock.json && npm install` でも起きることで、**pnpm 固有ではありません**。

そのうち 1 つが振る舞いに影響します:

- **`ts-proto` 2.12.0 → 2.12.1** — `decode()` に再帰深度の上限（100）が入りました。深く入れ子にした protobuf でスタックを食い潰す代わりに例外を投げます。生成物を作り直さないと `proto:check` が永久に赤になるので、**別コミット**にしてあります。

計画では「版上げは移行に混ぜない」としていましたが、lockfile を作り直す以上避けられませんでした。混ざったことが差分から見えるようコミットを分けています。

## 検証

| 検査 | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm install` で "Ignored build scripts" の警告 | 出ない（allowBuilds が効いている） |
| `node_modules/.bin/buf --version` | `1.72.0`（バイナリが実在する） |
| `pnpm run check` | green |
| `pnpm run proto:check` | green |
| `pnpm run proto:check-deps` | green（2 パッケージ） |
| `pnpm run site:build` | green（17 ページ） |
| `pnpm audit` | 0 件 |

## Problem

The root Dockerfile's CMD was written in exec form (CMD ["sh", "-c", "..."]), and while it referenced ${PORT:-8000}, the public service domain still failed to route traffic because the backend wasn't reliably binding to Railway's dynamically assigned $PORT at container start.

## Summary / Description

This patch addresses an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the incident-response WebSocket command handler by implementing defense-in-depth authorization controls. The fix restricts command execution to administrators only through dual-layer security checks: WebSocket security configuration rules and application-level message handler validation. Changes were made to WebsocketSecurityConfiguration.java to enforce authorization at the transport layer, UTMIncidentCommandWebsocket.java to add runtime permission validation, and a new UnauthorizedCommandExecutionException.java exception class was introduced for proper error handling. These modifications ensure that only authenticated users with administrator privileges can execute incident-response commands via WebSocket.

author: jakub-trzebiatowski
body:
The tail of #45 that never landed — that PR was merged while this commit was still on the branch, so trunk got the half where the store is registered and the controller is still discovered.

### What changes

```kotlin
fun main(args: Array<String>) {
  val store = PostgresCounterStore.build(readDatabaseUrl())
  CounterLambdaRuntime(CounterController(store)).run(*args)
}
```

The store stops being a bean entirely — it's a constructor argument now — and the only thing handed to the context is the controller. `grep` for DI annotations in the main sources returns exactly one line, the `@Controller`, which is only there because that's where the routes are read from; the instance they reach is ours.

### Why it's safe

I originally claimed supplying the controller would collide with the definition generated from its annotation, and built the store-only version on that assumption. That was wrong, and testing it settled it: give the hand-built controller a *different* store than the registered one and see which the routes hit — they hit ours.

It also turns out no `CounterStore` bean is needed at all, which makes the test self-proving: it registers a controller and nothing else, so a discovered controller could not have been constructed for want of a store. A passing round-trip can only be reaching the instance built in the test.

### Verified

`ktfmtCheck`, `detekt`, `build` green on top of current trunk, and the generated `native-image` command still ends with `software.medusa.counter.handler.CounterLambdaRuntimeKt` — the plugin substitution from #45 stays fixed.

Merging runs the deploy, and the gate from #47 now actually invokes the function, so this is the first change to the boot path that a green pipeline genuinely covers.
