author: etrobert
body:
Replaces the `github/copilot.vim` plugin with Neovim 0.12's native `vim.lsp.inline_completion`, driven by the nixpkgs-packaged `copilot-language-server`.

**Supersedes #870.** That PR did the same migration plus a clamp in the `<Tab>` keymap; the clamp was measured to destroy mismatching keystrokes (data loss), so it is deliberately not carried over here. This PR is #870 minus the keymap change — `pkgs/neovim-wrapped/plugins/remap/src/lua/remap/init.lua` is untouched, and its existing bare `vim.lsp.inline_completion.get()` binding (dead code until now) simply becomes live.

## Why: determinism

`copilot.vim` does not use its vendored language server when `npx` is available — it shells out to `npx` at runtime and pulls `@github/copilot-language-server` from the npm registry into `~/.npm/_npx`, on a caret range that silently floats (currently 1.534.0). It falls back to the vendored copy (1.408.0) only when `npx` is absent. The deleted plugin put `nodejs_26`, hence `npx`, on the wrapper's PATH, so today's editor has an unpinned, uncached, network-dependent dependency inside a Nix-managed closure.

The native route uses `pkgs.copilot-language-server`: hash-pinned, in the binary cache, offline-capable. That is the whole argument.

**Cost, stated plainly: the server version goes backwards, 1.534.0 → 1.530.0.** nixpkgs lags npm, and future bumps now arrive on nixpkgs' schedule. This PR buys reproducibility, not freshness — on freshness it is a small regression.

## What changed

- Delete `pkgs/neovim-wrapped/plugins/copilot/` and its entry in `pkgs/neovim-wrapped/default.nix`.
- Add `copilot-language-server` to `lspconfig`'s `extraPackages`; uncomment `"copilot"` in the `vim.lsp.enable` list.
- Uncomment `vim.lsp.inline_completion.enable()` in `set`.
- Swap the unfree allowance `"copilot.vim"` → `"copilot-language-server"`.

## This ships neovim#36529 unmitigated, on purpose

[neovim/neovim#36529](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/36529) was closed `not_planned`. In `runtime/lua/vim/lsp/inline_completion.lua`, `Completor:automatic_request()` shows immediately but defers the re-request by ~200 ms. `Completor:show()` trims the ghost text to the cursor unconditionally, while `Completor:accept()` applies the item against a _static_ range (`vim.range.lsp(...)`, which does not track the edit your keystroke just made). Inside that debounce window the two disagree, giving two failure modes:

1. **Matching input — stranded character.** A suggestion is showing; you type its next character and hit `<Tab>` before the re-request lands. The replacement range ends _before_ the character you typed, so it survives beside the inserted text: buffer ends up `func add(a int, b int) int {f`.
2. **Mismatching input — incoherent ghost text.** You type a character the suggestion does not start with. `show()` trims the ghost to the cursor regardless, so the buffer reads `x` while the ghost reads `unc add(…)` — a suggestion that no longer corresponds to anything.

**Neither is worked around here, and that is the point of this PR**, not an oversight. The intent is to live with the raw behaviour daily and judge how bad it actually is in practice before committing to any mitigation. A separate branch carries a Neovim runtime patch that fixes both.

## Verification

**Build:** `nix build .#neovim-wrapped --no-link --print-out-paths` → `/nix/store/hbwfr35qhlym9bfh6w6za1j9kd08mq11-neovim-0.12.4`

**Closure delta** (`nix path-info -S --human-readable`): 4,776,061,080 → 4,820,683,296 bytes, **+44.6 MB**; 4.4 GiB → 4.5 GiB. (`copilot-language-server`'s own closure is much larger, but nearly all of it is already shared with the editor's.) In exchange, `~/.npm/_npx` leaves the editor's real dependency set.

**Runtime, headless, on a real file in a git repo:**

```
copilot client attached: true
  client: copilot id=1
  supports textDocument/inlineCompletion: true
  cmd: copilot-language-server --stdio
inline_completion.is_enabled(buf): true
maparg <Tab> i desc: Get the current inline completion
maparg <Tab> i expr: 1
maparg <Tab> i callback type: function
maparg string mentions copilot#Accept: false
exists('*copilot#Accept'): 0
--- :messages ---
[]
```

`:checkhealth vim.deprecated` → `✅ OK No deprecated functions detected`.

**Auth:** picked up from the existing `~/.config/github-copilot/auth.db` with no sign-in prompt — the server's `checkStatus` returns `{ status = "OK", user = "etrobert" }`, and a live `textDocument/inlineCompletion` request returns a real suggestion (`insertText = "func add(a int, b int) int {"`).

**Checks:** `nix flake check --no-build` passes. `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.{statix,deadnix,stylua}` all pass — worth stating separately, because `nix flake check --no-build` does _not_ run those. `nix fmt -- --fail-on-change` reports 0 changed across all three touched `.nix` files.

**On screenshots:** there is a real user-visible behavioural change — ghost text now renders through Neovim's `ComplHint`/`ComplHintMore` rather than copilot.vim's `CopilotSuggestion` — but it only appears in response to a live model response and is not a static UI surface, so it is not meaningfully screenshottable. The transcript above is the substitute.

## How to road-test

```
nix run ".#neovim-wrapped" -- <some-file-in-a-git-repo>
```

Worth exercising specifically: typing into a suggestion that is already showing and hitting `<Tab>` immediately (both matching and mismatching characters), multi-line suggestions, accepting at end-of-line vs mid-line, and `<Tab>` falling through to a literal tab when nothing is showing.

author: tayfunates10
body:
## 1. Amaç ve kapsam

Tenant owner/admin kullanıcılarının Widget Branding Profile taslaklarını güvenli bir web arayüzünden oluşturup düzenlemesini ve kaydedilmiş bir revision'ı seçili widget deployment'a **ayrı ve explicit publish işlemiyle** yayınlamasını sağlar.

## 2. Güvenlik mimarisi

### Memory-only bearer session

- `/auth/login` ile alınan opaque bearer token yalnız React component memory state'inde tutulur.
- `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB veya browser cookie persistence yoktur.
- Token DOM'a, URL'ye, log'a veya kullanıcı hata mesajına yazılmaz.
- Parola her login denemesinden sonra temizlenir.
- Logout token ve tenant/profile/publish state'ini temizler.

### Same-origin allowlisted management proxy

Browser doğrudan cross-origin API çağrısı yapmaz. `/api/management/[...path]` Next.js route handler yalnız şu upstream işlemlerini allowlist eder:

- `POST /auth/login`
- `GET /organizations`
- `GET /organizations/{org}/widget-branding-profiles`
- `POST /organizations/{org}/widget-branding-profiles`
- `PUT /organizations/{org}/widget-branding-profiles/{profile}`
- `POST /organizations/{org}/widget-deployments/{deployment}/presentation`

Proxy generic API tunnel değildir: UUID pattern'leri zorunlu, query string reddedilir, body 16 KiB ile sınırlı, login Authorization header kabul etmez, authenticated route'lar bounded Bearer header gerektirir.

Upstream API base HTTPS olmak zorundadır; yalnız loopback development için HTTP istisnası vardır. Browser cookie/Origin/Referer veya arbitrary request header forward edilmez; upstream response header'ları da körlemesine iletilmez.

## 3. Draft / publish ayrımı

Profile create/update yalnız taslak kaydeder ve **hiçbir zaman publish endpoint'ini çağırmaz**.

Publish için aynı anda:

1. owner/admin organizasyonu,
2. persisted profile,
3. kaydedilmemiş değişiklik olmaması,
4. geçerli deployment UUID,
5. explicit confirmation checkbox,
6. ayrı publish form submit

gerekir.

Her draft değişikliği publish confirmation'ı temizler. Save sonrası kullanıcıya canlı widget'ın henüz değişmediği açıkça bildirilir.

## 4. UI kapsamı

- Yönetim login formu
- Owner/admin organizasyon seçimi
- Branding profile listesi
- Yeni profile oluşturma
- Existing profile revision düzenleme
- Theme / locale / density / title / font / radius / light-dark-error color ayarları
- Dirty-state koruması
- Explicit live publish bölümü
- Responsive layout ve semantic label/status/alert kullanımı

## 5. Değişen ana dosyalar

- `apps/web/app/widget-branding/page.tsx`
- `apps/web/components/widget-branding-manager.tsx`
- `apps/web/lib/widget-branding-management-api.ts`
- `apps/web/app/api/management/[...path]/route.ts`
- `apps/web/scripts/test-widget-branding-management.mjs`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `docs/adr/0028-widget-branding-management-ui.md`

## 6. CI / test contract

Yeni `management:test` gate'i şunları fail-closed doğrular:

- browser persistent token storage olmaması
- same-origin `/api/management` kullanımı
- direct arbitrary cross-origin browser management request olmaması
- exact proxy route allowlist
- upstream HTTPS / local-loopback transport sınırı
- Bearer forwarding sınırı
- query/body/header kısıtları
- save handler içinde publish çağrısı bulunmaması
- dirty + explicit confirmation publish guard'ları

Buna ek olarak mevcut Repository Contract, API Ruff/format/mypy/PostgreSQL pytest, Web Biome, TypeScript 7, Widget SDK v1.0-v1.2 contract'ları ve Next build aynen zorunludur.

**Tüm zorunlu CI yeşil olmadan merge yapılmayacak.**

## 7. Mevzuat / hesaplama etkisi

Yok. Finansal formüller, Türkiye mevzuat verileri, ruleset'ler, calculation snapshot'ları ve vergi/SGK/KDV otoritesi server-side kalır ve bu UI kapsamına taşınmaz.

## 8. Bilinen kapsam sınırı

Deployment discovery/list API henüz yoktur; bu PR bu yüzden publish sırasında tenant deployment UUID'sinin explicit girilmesini ister. UUID girişi client-side format kontrolünden ve server-side tenant authorization'dan geçer.

## 9. Sonraki PR

PR #29 merge sonrası önerilen sonraki kapsam: **PR #30 — tenant-scoped widget deployment discovery/list API + management UI selector**. Manual UUID girişini kaldıracak ama explicit publish ceremony ve tenant authority korunacak.

author: jacobinaural
body:
## Problema

En el wizard **Reportes Maquina Fiscal** (menú *Detalle de Ventas → Reportes Maquina Fiscal*, módulo `l10n_ve_account_mf`), al seleccionar un rango de fechas (p. ej. *01/08 a 01/08*) y pulsar **Reporte Z**, aparece la alerta de que se emitirá el Reporte Z del **día fiscal en curso (hoy)** y lo que imprime es el de hoy, no el del rango seleccionado.

## Causa raíz

Dos capas:

1. **Regresión respecto a V17.** En V17 (`l10n_ve_iot_mf`) la reimpresión era una herramienta completa (formulario `iot.device`): selector **Tipo** (fecha/número) × **Documento** (Facturas, NC, No fiscales, Reporte X, **Reporte Z**, Todos), que enviaba `Rf/Rc/Rt/Rx/`**`Rz`**`/Ra` (fecha) o `RF/RC/RT/RX/`**`RZ`**`/R@` (número). El wizard WebSerial de V19 colapsó todo en 4 botones y **eliminó ese selector**; solo dejó `Rf` (facturas por fecha). Se perdió la reimpresión del Reporte Z por rango, que es la función que el cliente usaba para "sacar el Z de una fecha pasada".

2. **UX confusa.** Por protocolo TFHKA (Manual V8.5.0, Tabla 59), `I0X`/`I0Z` son **siempre del día fiscal en curso** y no aceptan fecha (los botones X/Z ni leen el rango). El layout ponía las fechas encima de todos los botones sin agrupar, induciendo a creer que el rango aplicaba también al Reporte Z.

## Fix

Todo en `l10n_ve_account_mf` (no se toca el driver `l10n_ve_mf_base`; ya soporta `sendCommand`):

- **Wizard reorganizado en 3 secciones** claramente separadas: *Reportes del día fiscal en curso* (X/Z, con aviso de que no usan el rango), *Reporte de memoria fiscal por rango de fechas* y *Reimpresión de documentos (memoria de auditoría)*. El rango de fechas es compartido por las dos últimas.
- **Restaurada la reimpresión por rango con selector de documento** (Facturas / Notas de Crédito / No fiscales / Reporte X / **Reporte Z** / Todos), por **fecha** (`Rf/Rc/Rt/Rx/Rz/Ra`, 7 díg. `0`+DDMMYY) o por **número** (`RF/RC/RT/RX/RZ/R@`, 7 díg.) — Manual TFHKA V8.5.0, Tablas 39 y 40.
- **Reporte de memoria fiscal por fecha** con variante **Resumen (`I2S`) / Detallado (`I2A`) / Mensual (`I2M`)** (Tabla 61).
- **Etiquetas aclaradas** ("día en curso") y **diálogo del Reporte Z reforzado**: avisa que cierra hoy, que no usa el rango y remite a "Reimpresión de documentos" (documento "Reporte Z") para fechas pasadas.
- **Spec del módulo actualizado** (`module-specs/openspec/specs/l10n_ve_account_mf/spec.md`).

## Verificación

- Sintaxis validada: Python (`compile`), XML (well-formed), JS (`node --check`).
- **Pendiente de prueba en navegador** (Chrome/Edge, Web Serial, impresora conectada), tras `-u l10n_ve_account_mf`:
  - Reimpresión por fecha con documento **Reporte Z** en un rango pasado → envía `Rz0<DDMMYY>0<DDMMYY>` y reimprime los Z de esas fechas.
  - Resto de documentos (facturas, NC, X, todos) y modo por número (`RZ`, `RF`, ...).
  - Reporte de memoria fiscal con las tres variantes (`I2S/I2A/I2M`).
  - Reporte X/Z siguen operando sobre el día en curso, con el diálogo aclaratorio.

## Alcance

- Solo `l10n_ve_account_mf` (wizard Python + assets JS/XML + spec). **No** se modifica `l10n_ve_mf_base` (driver intacto) ni la lógica de facturación/cierre.
- Campos nuevos únicamente en el `TransientModel` del wizard (no persistentes). Sin migración.
- Restaura paridad funcional con V17 (`l10n_ve_iot_mf`) perdida en la migración al flujo WebSerial.

References: https://binaural.odoo.com/odoo/action-341/78328

author: dijkstra-kromatic[bot]
body:
<!-- hestia:host-ac-evaluated:none -->

Closes #1036

## What this does

The coverage-audit worksheet asked a human to mark each candidate relevant-or-not, and emitted a `coverage_miss_rate`. Neither was honest: push records store a query **hash** and never the query text (athenaeum#711's deliberate no-content-in-the-ledger invariant), so relevance is not recoverable from a push record — and with 82% of pushed items sharing a single tier/scope pairing, the resulting figure was a policy-set bracket `[0.0000, 0.8763]` rather than a measurement of retrieval behaviour.

This implements the **operator ruling of 2026-08-22, option (c)**: keep the ledger hash-only and change the audit's design instead. No privacy trade is made and no ledger-level sensitivity machinery is invented. The original AC1/AC2/AC3 (a stored relevance representation and the schema change that would carry it) are withdrawn, not relocated — nothing of the sort is built here.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Proof |
|---|---|
| No per-candidate relevant/not-relevant marking column; no `coverage_miss_rate` presented as a measurement | `build_coverage_worksheet` no longer builds `reviewer_verdict` — `tests/test_push_metrics.py::TestCoverageWorksheet::test_no_marking_column_and_structural_fields_populated` |
| Reports instead the structural facts derivable hash-only, with any bounds explicitly labelled policy-set and both endpoints named | `structural_summary` carries `tier_scope_concentration` (candidate-pool size + concentration), `window_mate_filter` (before/after counts, `removed_fraction`, range — how much athenaeum#986's filter actually removes) and `policy_set_miss_rate_bounds` with `lower_bound`/`lower_bound_label` and `upper_bound`/`upper_bound_label`. Same test, plus `test_policy_set_bounds_reproducible_from_worksheet_fields` |
| Worksheet opens with a plain-language statement of what it cannot establish and why | `push_metrics.LIMITATION_STATEMENT`, surfaced as `worksheet["limitation"]`, naming athenaeum#711's hash-at-record-time design — asserted in `test_no_marking_column_and_structural_fields_populated` |
| Ledger schema **unchanged**; a test asserts no raw query text reaches the ledger on the default path | `PushRecord` / `PushedItem` / `to_dict()` untouched. `TestRecordPush::test_no_raw_query_text_reaches_the_ledger_file_on_default_path` writes via `record_push`, reads the actual `_push_records.jsonl` back off disk, and asserts the raw query substrings are absent and only the hash present |
| Fixture tests over a synthetic ledger; a degenerate tier/scope distribution reported as such, not silently averaged | `test_no_marking_column_and_structural_fields_populated`, `test_degenerate_tier_scope_distribution_is_flagged`, `test_non_degenerate_distribution_is_not_flagged` |
| Optional config key for storing query text | **Skipped — see below** |

## The optional config key: skipped, and why

The issue marks it "optional, skip if not cheap," instructs that no ledger-level sensitivity routing be built for it, and says to state the reason if skipped. It is not cheap: even default-off and opt-in, it reaches the ledger writer, needs new config plumbing in `config.py`, and needs documentation explicitly reversing athenaeum#711's stated invariant for that install. That is not a small self-contained change, and building it well would require exactly the sensitivity machinery the ruling exists to avoid needing. Skipped deliberately; the reason is also recorded in the `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

## Verification

- `pytest`: `40 failed, 6542 passed, 122 skipped, 41 deselected, 1 xfailed, 4 warnings in 71.16s`. The 40 failures are **identical to the measured `develop` baseline** (sorted `FAILED` set diffs empty) — all environment-bound, none new, none fixed.
- `ruff check src/ tests/` → All checks passed.
- `mypy` → Success: no issues found in 143 source files.
- Ran on Python 3.13.15, matching CI's pinned version.

Version 0.19.24; `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `### Changed`. No live `~/knowledge` store or operator ledger was touched — fixtures only.

## Noted, deliberately not changed

`docs/memory-model-measurements.md`'s two historical dated snapshots still carry the old `coverage_miss_rate: n/a — awaits operator review` text. That section is an append-only record and the module docstring is explicit that a run never rewrites an earlier snapshot; rewriting past entries would misrepresent what actually ran at the time. Future `athenaeum push-metrics baseline` runs pick up the corrected note automatically.

Out of scope and untouched: recording any coverage figure (that is #998, which this unblocks), the tier/scope distribution of pushes, precision-side instrumentation, and any ledger-level PII routing.

author: k3np
body:
Third defect from the v0.16.0 unlock E2E, and the one that made the verb non-functional in practice.

The probe hit the lock and printed it:

```
| Error: Error acquiring the state lock
| Lock Info:
|   ID:        2c655069-36ee-1bd8-0847-d0467ebe8307
```

`lock-info` answered *no state lock reported in this output*. On a runner OpenTofu colours diagnostics, so those lines actually read `ESC[31m|ESC[0m ESC[0mLock Info:` — and every pattern in the parser anchors at the start of the line, which is where the escape sequence sits. The prefix strip handled `|` and nothing else.

**It failed safe.** The cell reported the lock state as *undetermined* and went red rather than claiming "no lock held" — the three-state distinction doing its job, and the reason this was diagnosable from the annotation alone.

Why nothing caught it earlier:

- `apply-comment` strips ANSI in `load_cells` before this parser runs, so stage 1 was unaffected.
- The fixtures were captured through a colour-stripping `sed` as they were taken, so "verbatim capture" was verbatim *after* a filter. The new fixture (`lock_error_s3_ansi.txt`) is the real probe output of this E2E run with all 70 escape bytes intact; with the strip removed it reproduces the production failure, and the two colour-free captures stay green.

CI-shape suite: 1197 passed.

author: seungjae3908-source
body:
## P0
Fixes `PRODUCTION_BROWSER_SMOKE_PROTECTED_ENV_HARNESS_RACE` from Central Hub #62.

Production Browser Smoke could be dispatched from exact current `main`, then wait behind the protected `production` environment. If `main` advanced during that wait, the live job re-fetched mutable `main` and failed before browser QA because the fetched SHA no longer matched dispatch-time `GITHUB_SHA`.

## Bounded fix
- add a dispatch-only, non-Production `resolve-harness` job
- before the protected environment wait, require dispatch ref=`main`, checkout exact event SHA, and prove it still equals current main
- export that immutable dispatch-time harness SHA as a job output
- after approval, fetch only that pinned harness commit and require exact resolution
- preserve exact deployed Production SHA checkout + `/api/health` identity gate
- preserve QA credential gate, fail-closed mutation policy, zero retries, and whitelisted harness overlay only
- strengthen the static safety-contract verifier so post-approval code cannot re-resolve mutable `main`

## Scope
Exactly 2 files:
- `.github/workflows/production-browser-smoke.yml`
- `api-server/scripts/verify-production-browser-smoke-contract.mjs`

## Safety
Draft only. No Production deploy, no Production browser dispatch, no server/DB/Secret mutation, no private provider/trading access, no order/cancel/amend/transfer/withdrawal authority, no test weakening or timeout/retry increase.

Base main at lease: `eb24b5eac8dd28812c7c02a9c16ab1b798507e8a`.
Hub lease comment: `5381092103`.

author: jeremyandrews
body:
Follow-up to #113, from testing on device.

## The bug

`\.healthAsk` was injected onto the NavigationStack's **root content** rather than onto the stack. A view pushed by a `NavigationLink` is presented *by* the stack, not rendered as a child of the root, so the action never reached it.

Every askable view below the dashboard root was **wired and inert** — the nutrient rows on Macros & calories, the meals and foods in the Food journal, the workout cards, the Sources rows, the charts. The dashboard root worked, which is exactly why it looked like patchy coverage rather than a single wiring fault.

Moved onto the `NavigationStack` on both platforms, which covers the root and every destination alike.

## The genuinely missing coverage

- **The metric drill-down sheet, row by row.** Tap Calories → the "What fed this" list → long-press a food. Each contributing food now carries its own ask with its contribution, its share and the ranking it sits in, which is what makes "why is this so caloric" and "what's a lighter swap" answerable about *one food* rather than about the day.
- **The Not-estimated rows**, with their own starters ("roughly how much would this have?", "what would I log to make it measurable?") — an unmeasured food raises a different question from a measured one, and unknown-is-not-zero *is* the question.
- **The "What fed this" header**, for the metric as a whole.
- **Rebuilt-day (neutral) rows** on Macros & calories — the one row type on the tab with no ask at all.
- **The two cross-link nav rows** between a nutrient's trend and its sources.

75 ask sites, up from 63.

## Not breaking what long-press already did

`.contextMenu` **takes over** press-and-hold text selection, so attaching an ask to a row carrying `.textSelection(.enabled)` would have quietly cost a Copy that used to be there.

New `.askable(_:copyText:)` variant puts a **Copy** in the menu beside the ask, used exactly where selection existed: the drill-down's food and Not-estimated rows, and the trend chart's verdict sentence. `DrilldownShare.contributionLine` is extracted so a row's Copy and the sheet's ShareLink export produce the identical line rather than two spellings of it.

The sheet's prose paragraphs, its value line and the on-device insight are deliberately **not** askable and keep their plain text selection. The ShareLink in the sheet toolbar is untouched.

## Verification

JesseKit (`swift build` + `--build-tests`), iOS app, Mac app — all clean, warnings-as-errors. Suites still need CI to actually run (Xcode's iOS SDK 26.2 vs a 26.3-only simulator runtime here).

body:
## Create Soroban SDK Quick Reference Guide

  **Closes:** #9

  ### Summary

  This PR implements a comprehensive **Soroban SDK Quick Reference Guide** that serves as the central learning resource for PLEarn contributors. The guide
  consolidates essential SDK patterns, verified code examples, and troubleshooting guidance all in one place—eliminating the need for contributors to
  consult external documentation.

  ### Motivation

  Issue #9 identified the need for a quick reference guide covering common Soroban SDK patterns used throughout PLEarn challenges. New contributors were
  struggling to understand:
  - How storage patterns work (instance vs persistent)
  - When and how to use `require_auth()`
  - Testing patterns and setup
  - Common error scenarios and solutions
  - Best practices for contracts

  This guide provides all that information with verified examples from actual challenges.

  ### Changes Implemented

  #### 1. **New File: `docs/SOROBAN_SDK_QUICK_REFERENCE.md`** (689 lines)

  A comprehensive reference guide covering 8 major sections:

  **Core SDK Patterns:**
  - **Storage Patterns**
    - Instance storage (set-once, rarely-changing data like admin addresses)
    - Persistent storage (frequently-changing data like balances)
    - Advanced storage with Maps and Vectors
    - Code examples from `01-hello-token` and `02-token-transfer`

  - **Address & Authentication**
    - Understanding `Address` type and its role
    - `require_auth()` verification pattern
    - Generating test addresses with `Address::generate(&env)`
    - Authorization in both production and test environments

  - **Contract Invocation & Cross-Contract Calls**
    - Registering contracts locally for testing
    - Creating clients with `ContractClient::new()`
    - Calling contract functions through clients
    - Test setup patterns

  - **Event Emission**
    - Event structure with `#[contracttype]`
    - Emitting events with `env.events().publish()`
    - Topic organization
    - Use cases for off-chain observers

  - **Environment Utilities**
    - Ledger information (`env.ledger()`)
    - Storage management
    - Current contract address
    - Time-based logic with ledger sequence

  - **Error Handling & Validation**
    - Panic patterns for error conditions
    - Common validation scenarios (balance checks, authorization, uniqueness)
    - Error message best practices
    - 7 documented common error patterns:
      1. "already initialized"
      2. "insufficient balance"
      3. "already voted" (duplicate prevention)
      4. "proposal not found"
      5. Borrow checker issues
      6. Authorization failures
      7. WASM compilation errors

  - **Testing Patterns**
    - Setup function pattern for test initialization
    - Using `env.mock_all_auths()` for authorization
    - Testing panics with `#[should_panic]`
    - Best practices for test organization
    - Coverage recommendations

  - **Troubleshooting Guide** (7 Common Errors)
    1. Compilation errors with imports and macros
    2. "Storage key not found" panics → use `.unwrap_or(default)`
    3. Authorization failures → verification and testing
    4. Borrow checker errors with Address type
    5. Vec/Map from different Env instances
    6. Test passes locally but fails in CI
    7. WASM compilation failures

  **Additional Features:**
  - All code examples **verified against actual challenges**
  - Quick reference table for common operations
  - Links to challenge implementations for each pattern
  - Links to official Soroban documentation
  - Organized by use-case categories for easy navigation

  #### 2. **Updated: `README.md`**

  - **Added to "Useful Resources"** section:
    - Positioned quick reference guide as "START HERE" resource
    - Clearly marked as primary SDK learning resource
    - Placed before official Soroban documentation

  - **Updated project structure** documentation:
    - Added `docs/SOROBAN_SDK_QUICK_REFERENCE.md` to file tree
    - Included all docs files (SETUP_GUIDE.md, contributing.md, diagrams/)

  #### 3. **Updated: `docs/contributing.md`**

  - **Added "Learn the SDK" section (Step 0):**
    - Positioned before prerequisites as the first step
    - Links directly to quick reference guide
    - Emphasizes guide as self-contained learning resource
    - Reduces dependency on external documentation

  ### Issue Requirements Met

  ✅ **Coverage of beginner-level patterns:**
  - Storage approaches (Map, Vec, Symbol as key)
  - Address and authentication patterns including `Address::require_auth()`
  - Contract invocation and cross-contract interactions
  - Event emission mechanics
  - Environment utilities (`env.ledger()`, `env.storage()`)
  - Common error patterns and panic scenarios

  ✅ **Content Organization:**
  - ✓ Organized by use case categories (authentication, storage, time, events)
  - ✓ Include verified code examples from actual PLEarn challenges
  - ✓ Reference official Soroban documentation for extended learning
  - ✓ Incorporate troubleshooting guidance for frequent SDK errors

  ✅ **Success Metrics:**
  - ✓ Coverage of all patterns in beginner-level challenges
  - ✓ Tested and accurate code samples (all from PLEarn)
  - ✓ Enable new contributors to resolve issues without consulting external Soroban documentation

  ### Files Changed

  README.md                           | 5 changes
  docs/SOROBAN_SDK_QUICK_REFERENCE.md | 689 lines (NEW)
  docs/contributing.md                | 12 changes
  ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  Total: 3 files, 706 insertions

  ### Testing & Verification

    - `challenges/beginner/01-hello-token/src/lib.rs`
    - `challenges/beginner/02-token-transfer/src/lib.rs`

  - ✅ Documentation structure reviewed for clarity

  ### Impact

author: goofmint
body:
fix #9

Implements Task 1.8: the undo/redo stack with transaction grouping and 750 ms typing coalescing (Req 5.4, design.md §7.1), following the CodeRabbit plan on the issue, adapted to the merged Task 1.7 `LineBuffer`/`Document`.

## What's included

### `packages/core/src/buffer/clock.ts` (new)
- `Clock { now(): number }` and `createSystemClock()` — the injectable time source the coalescing window needs, following the same `deps` conventions as `HostLog`/`StatusSink`; tests inject a fixed, advanceable fake.

### `packages/core/src/buffer/undoStack.ts` (new)
- `createUndoStack({ clock })` with independent undo/redo stacks and `TYPING_COALESCE_WINDOW_MS = 750`.
- `push` records a batch's inverse edits, `selectionsBefore`/`selectionsAfter`, an optional explicit `groupId` (transactions), and an optional `TypingCoalesceHint` for single-character non-newline inserts.
- Grouping: pushes sharing an explicit `groupId` merge into one entry. Typing coalescing merges only when the insert is a single character on the same line, exactly continues the previous insert, and lands within 750 ms — a newline, a cursor jump, the window expiring, or a transaction boundary starts a new entry.
- Every fresh push clears the redo stack; the pop-only `undo()`/`redo()` plus push-only `recordRedo()`/`recordUndo()` pairs let the document move entries between stacks without ever clearing redo history by construction.

### `packages/core/src/buffer/document.ts`
- `createDocument` now returns `CoreDocument` (extends the public `Document` — `packages/api` untouched) wired to an internal `UndoStack`; `clock` is injectable via `CreateDocumentOptions`.
- `applyEdits(edits, opts?)` accepts `{ undoGroup, selectionsBefore, selectionsAfter }` and records each batch with its computed coalescing hint. Readonly no-op, empty-batch early return, single `onDidChange` per call, and `dirtyRange`/`lineCountDelta` behavior are unchanged.
- `transaction(fn)` now really groups: a fresh `groupId` tags every `applyEdits` inside `fn` (nesting keeps the outer group; try/finally closes the group on exceptions), so a multi-edit operation undoes as one step.
- Internal `undo()`/`redo()` apply the stack's edits through the `LineBuffer` (bypassing the recording path so redo history survives), bump `version`, fire one `onDidChange`, and return the stored selection payload for the future editor layer. The inverses `LineBuffer.applyEdits` returns during undo become the redo edits, symmetrically.

### Barrels
- `buffer/index.ts` and `core/src/index.ts` extended with `Clock`, `createSystemClock`, `createUndoStack`, `UndoEntry`, `UndoStackDeps`, `CoreDocument`, and related types.

## Tests
- 14 unit tests for the stack: explicit-group merging, coalescing within/beyond 750 ms, newline and cursor-jump breaks, redo clearing, undo → redo → undo payload consistency.
- 10 document integration tests: transactions undo as a single step, undo/redo round-trips content and selections exactly, new edits clear redo, readonly stays guarded, and a fake clock verifies the coalescing boundary end-to-end.

`bun test`: 227 pass / 0 fail · `bun run lint`: clean · `bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean

Los dos últimos descartes cuyo motivo explicaba la brecha con una causa que nadie
midió. A diferencia del 4.1 y del 3.20, acá la comprobación NO los recupera — y
eso también es un resultado, siempre que quede medido en vez de contado.

**3.24 · crédito a la producción.** El motivo pedía una fuente concreta —«el cuadro
de crédito por destino económico del banco central, que no ingerimos»— y decía que
el indicador seguía abierto a ella. Se trajo: mensual desde 1996, trece destinos.
No cierra. Con el crédito como STOCK a diciembre sobre el PIB nominal —convención
declarada antes de mirar el resultado, la misma del 2.36— agricultura sola da
4,38%, agro+minas+manufactura 4,97% y los cinco productivos juntos 11,23%, contra
una base legal de 2,24%. Todos los destinos productivos por separado superan el
2,24% salvo minas y electricidad.

Y hay un argumento que no depende de elegir bien el agrupamiento: si el universo
de la ley fuera cualquier agregado de crédito bancario a la producción, la meta de
8% para 2015 ya estaría cumplida en la línea base, lo que vuelve incoherente la
trayectoria que la propia ley fija.

NO se eligió por cercanía, y queda escrito por qué: el barrido combinatorio sobre
trece destinos SÍ encuentra coincidencias —minas + electricidad + servicios
comunitarios da 2,31%, Δ 3,3%— y ninguna significa nada. Con trece sumandos
siempre hay una combinación cerca de cualquier número.

**2.33 · gasto público en salud.** Se probaron las siete variantes que publica el
emisor y ninguna se acerca a 1,4. La vía nacional tampoco alcanza: el portal de
datos abiertos publica ejecución presupuestaria desde 2016 y la base es de 2009.

**El guard que sale de los cuatro casos.** Un motivo puede explicar, pero si
explica con una causa que nadie midió, la causa se declara en
`hipotesis_sin_comprobar` y no en la prosa. Declarada es una lista de trabajo;
enterrada en el motivo es un indicador perdido — así el 4.1 y el 3.20 pasaron
meses descartados siendo medibles.

  · `hipotesis_abiertas()` computa qué reabrir, y `GET /{expediente}/hipotesis`
    lo sirve. Reemplaza leer motivos a mano con una expresión regular, que es
    como se encontraron estos tres y que envejece con cada motivo nuevo.
  · el guard persigue lo NO declarado, y excluye lo entrecomillado: los ocho
    descartes del PEFA citan la lengua hedgeada del propio anexo —«se podría
    cubrir RAZONABLEMENTE»— y eso es evidencia, no suposición nuestra.
  · una hipótesis abierta solo puede colgar de un DESCARTE. Con un binding
    verificado sería una cifra publicada sobre una suposición; para eso está
    `nota_comparabilidad`, que frena la promoción.

El motivo del 2.25 decía que el último valor «se parece» a la línea base; ahora
dice a cuánto queda (8,3%). Era una observación medida disfrazada de suposición.

Cobertura sin cambio: 33 de 90.

author: 0dian
body:
## 动机

用遥控器对着 Claude Desktop 或 ChatGPT 说完话之后，想往回翻看前面几轮对话，手上只有遥控器却做不到：把方向键映射成「上/下方向键」时，CGEvent 的方向键只会在输入框内部移动光标，对话区完全不动。结果是语音输入这一段体验是连贯的，一想回看历史就必须回到键盘鼠标，遥控器场景在这里断掉。

方向键在这类应用里滚不动内容并不是映射配置错了，而是事件类型本身不对——对话区响应的是滚轮事件，不是方向键。

## 改动摘要

按键映射新增 `scrollUp` / `scrollDown` 两个动作，改用 CGEvent 滚轮事件：

- `ButtonAction` 新增两个 case，归入「基础按键」分组，沿用既有连发白名单，按住时按既有 100ms 间隔连续滚动。
- `KeyboardInjector` 新增 `postScrollWheel`，每次滚动 3 行；正值滚向对话开头，即按上键看到更早的消息，与自然滚动方向的直觉一致。
- 滚轮事件是按事件位置分发的，所以先用 AX `focusedWindow` 定位前台窗口并取其中心；取不到时回退到 `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` 中该进程 layer 为 0 的最大普通窗口；仍取不到时才使用当前指针位置。
- 事件带既有的合成标记，且不经过 `KeyboardEventSuppressor` 的按键计数路径，避免影响 Fn 语音会话的按键统计。
- 中英文文案、自检与单测（方向与行数、窗口中心定位与回退、分组、连发、持久化标识符）同步补齐。
- 按 `AGENTS.md` 的要求同步更新了 `TODO.md` 对应条目，测试手册见 `Testing/RemoteScrollActions.md`。

## 真机验证证据

环境：macOS 26.5.0、小米 rc003 遥控器、SayAll 1.9.8 自构建。

- 上键 / 下键单击：Claude Desktop 与 ChatGPT 的前台窗口对话区正常滚动，方向符合预期（上键看到更早的消息）。
- 上键 / 下键按住：按既有 100ms 连发间隔连续滚动，没有卡顿或方向抖动。
- 滚轮事件落点：实测对准的是前台窗口中心，不是指针当时所在的位置，因此鼠标停在别的窗口上也不会滚错窗口。

## 测试状态

- `scripts/test.sh`：43/43 通过（含本 PR 新增的滚动动作自检项），其中的 `xcrun swift build` 一并通过。
- 新增的 Swift Testing 测试只做了编译验证，**未执行**：本机只有 Command Line Tools、没有 Xcode，缺少 `Testing` 模块，`swift test` 跑不起来。这部分需要在装有 Xcode 的机器或 CI 上执行。
- 上述真机验证覆盖 Claude Desktop 与 ChatGPT 两个前台窗口场景；`Testing/RemoteScrollActions.md` 中其余用例尚未逐条走完。

body:
## Summary

A feature-improvement pass over the `hwaro tool` subcommand family, closing the biggest capability/consistency gaps between sibling commands, plus one doctor check from the issue queue.

### Consistency & safety

- **export**: classified `HWARO_E_IO` failure instead of a bare `exit(1)`; `--json` per-file manifest; `--dry-run`; a warning (with count) when a re-export replaces pre-existing files.
- **import**: `--json` per-file manifest (`imported` / `overwritten` / `skipped`, bundle assets included) and `--dry-run` that resolves every destination — collision renames and skip decisions included — without writing.
- **convert**: `--dry-run` runs the full pipeline (dropped-comment warnings included) without rewriting any file.
- **unused-assets**: `-t/--templates-dir` so a non-default templates tree is scanned for references; an explicitly passed dir must exist (refuses instead of silently scanning zero templates and feeding false positives to `--delete`).
- **doctor**: `--json` now routes through `Runner.enable_json_mode!` like every sibling, so mid-run classified errors render as JSON payloads.

### New capabilities

- **list**: `--sort date|title|path`, `-r/--reverse`, `-n/--limit` (applied after sorting). Title ordering matches the template engine's `sort_by="title"` (`SortUtils.compare_by_title`) so CLI and rendered listings agree.
- **stats**: `--top N` replaces the hardcoded top-15 tag chart cap.
- **check-links**: `--ignore-url PATTERN` (case-insensitive substring with `*` wildcards, repeatable; matching links are never contacted) and `--allow-status CODES`; the JSON payload gains `skipped_external` (SSRF-guard skips were previously invisible to JSON consumers) and `ignored_count` (so an over-broad ignore pattern is distinguishable from a clean check).
- **validate**: `--strict` / `--max-warnings` mirroring doctor's exit policy (content errors exit 5, warning-driven gates exit 1).
- **agents-md `--write`**: the Site-Specific Instructions section of an existing AGENTS.md is preserved across regeneration, as the docs already promised; the marker constant lives on the template service, and a marker-less file is announced as a full replacement (prompt, or warning under `--force`) instead of silently losing content.
- **doctor**: new `image-processing-widths-empty` warning for an enabled `[image_processing]` with no `widths` (silent no-op).

### Docs

Fixes the long-standing `-c, --content` flag misspelling across six tool pages (en+ko; the flag is `--content-dir`), documents all new flags, adds the `--force` row the import options table omitted, and documents check-links' GET fallback, redirect follow, private-address skip, and unused-assets' real scan sources. All pages updated in English and Korean.

### Behavior changes to note

- `tool export` failures now exit 6 (`EXIT_IO`) with the standard `Error [HWARO_E_IO]` line instead of exit 1 with `Export failed:` — intentional alignment with every sibling tool command.
- `tool convert --json` payloads gain an additive `dry_run` key.
- `check-links --json` payloads gain additive `skipped_external` and `ignored_count` keys.

## Testing

- New unit specs (`spec/unit/tool_feature_improvements_spec.cr`, 9 examples) for dry-run/manifest/sorting semantics, including the pre-existing-symlink dry-run refusal and bundle-asset manifest rows.
- Paired warns/does-not-warn doctor specs for the widths check.
- 21 new functional CLI specs covering every new flag, error path, and the review-fix regressions.
- Adversarially reviewed (fresh multi-angle review); 8 of 10 confirmed findings fixed in the follow-up commit, the other 2 are the intentional behavior changes listed above. Two low-tier cleanups noted but deferred: validate/doctor `exit_code_for` duplication, and `skipped_external` classification by error-string sentinel.
- Full suite: 8016 examples, 0 failures. `crystal tool format --check` and ameba clean.

Closes #632

## Summary

- allow static DOM rich_rows to use the listing row own href when the row is an anchor
- configure UNDP global staff, PSA, internship, roster, and remote vacancies through the official jobs page and Oracle detail API
- configure 209 distinct UNDP individual consultancies with listing titles plus detail enrichment for office location, description, posting date, and contract type
- add localized company metadata and verified UNDP logo/icon assets

## Guided workflow evidence

The official UNDP careers estate was researched globally. The central jobs page exposed 107 links and is the canonical inventory for international and national staff, PSAs, internships, rosters, and home-based roles. The separate Individual Consultancies page exposed 209 distinct procurement notices.

The guided configuration path failed because each consultancy listing row is itself an anchor. DOM rich_rows rejected row href extraction, while detail-page Country labels varied by language and markup and produced only 2/10 locations. The JPO Service Centre page was intentionally excluded: static and browser access both returned HTTP 403, and its listing mixes UNDP positions with unrelated UN agencies without an agency-pure feed.

## Fix

The extractor already used the row node when link_selector was absent and failed closed when href or title was missing. This change removes the validation rule that prohibited that supported row-as-link path, documents it, and adds a regression test.

UNDP consultancies now use the self-linking row for canonical URL/title extraction. Detail enrichment reads the stable Office field for location, which passed 12/12 sampled notices including both rows whose listing location was blank. The global board uses the public Oracle HCM detail endpoint and returned clean title, description, location, and posting date data.

## Validation

- uv run ws validate
- uv run pytest tests/test_dom_pagination.py tests/test_inspect.py tests/test_compat.py (237 passed)
- uv run ruff check src/core/monitors/dom.py src/workspace/commands/help.py tests/test_dom_pagination.py
- git diff --check
- live consultancy extraction: 209 unique URLs; 12/12 detail samples clean
- direct encoded Oracle detail endpoint: HTTP 200 with title, description, location, and posting date

Environment note: the full crawler board dry-run could not start because the configured Postgres hostname did not resolve in this worktree; the live monitor and scraper components were exercised directly.

Closes #6994

author: elgansayer
body:
Closes #1287

## Summary
- keep the existing Joi schema as the canonical type/range validator while adding a raw pre-validation step before Joi defaults are applied
- fail production startup when required credentials are missing/blank or still contain known example/test placeholders
- validate service-appropriate URL schemes for frontend/app, Supabase, PostgreSQL, Redis, Centrifugo, LiveKit, Cloudflare R2, Apple/Google webhook audiences, and an optional LLM base URL
- wire NestJS `ConfigModule` through the new `validateEnvironment` bootstrap boundary
- make both root and backend `.env.example` inventories comprehensive, including previously undocumented TURN credentials and chat edit-window configuration
- add focused Jest regression coverage plus operator-facing rollout/rollback documentation

## Existing implementation reused
`backend/src/config/validation.schema.ts` and `ConfigModule.forRoot()` already existed on `main`. The gap was that many production-sensitive Joi fields had synthetic defaults intended for tests/local development, so a missing production secret could silently become a test credential. This PR preserves those development/test defaults but validates the raw production environment before defaults can mask an omission.

## Security / failure behavior
- configuration errors are fatal during bootstrap; the API does not serve traffic partially configured
- errors name only the affected environment variables/rules and never echo secret values
- production rejects known `test-*`, `change-me*`, `replace-with*`, Supabase example, and Stripe test placeholders for required keys
- no database/API/authentication contract changes and no persisted data changes

## Validation
GitHub Actions is the authoritative verification environment for this connector-authored branch. Added tests cover complete production startup, multiple missing secrets, placeholder credentials, malformed URLs, wrong URL schemes, Joi range validation, and preserved development/test defaults.

## Rollout
Populate every key in `PRODUCTION_REQUIRED_ENV_KEYS` in the production secret/config store before deploying. A missing or invalid value will intentionally keep the new instance unhealthy until configuration is corrected.

## Rollback
Revert this PR if the startup policy must be rolled back. Do not restore synthetic/test credentials in production. There is no schema migration or data rollback.

author: macabeus
body:
Meta-optimisation iteration 1: five findings from a supervisor pass over the round journals were
put through a hostile re-check. **Three survived, two were rejected, and two proposals turned out
to be already built or already done.** Nothing here can move a benchmark number: the diff is one
new git-only script, a PR-only CI job, console output in the harness, and prompt text.

Two of the supervisor's supporting claims did not check out and are corrected below, because both
were load-bearing for proposals I then dropped.

## What shipped

### `efe37c2` — a branch cannot merge an artifact older than the code it measures

`results.json` stamps `meta.asmlift.commit`, every published number reads from it, and nothing
mechanical checks the stamp is current. Verified counts, not the supervisor's:

* Round 2 produced **two** reviewer findings on it in one wave — the ship agent's own triage table
  records `6 (major) Artifact ten commits behind HEAD — CONFIRMED + fixed (dup of 3)`.
* Round 3 produced **two more**, one a CRITICAL (`stale by three behaviour-changing commits and
  two dataset rows`).
* **`match/switch-arms` is stale right now.** Artifact stamped `cb5b51b`; 9 later commits on that
  branch touch what it measures, two of them (`a2e58d8`, `6914e06`) change emitted C, and the two
  rows `bf74977` authored (`swdefmid`, `swjtorder`) are absent from it. Both reuse existing tags,
  so the whole offline suite is green on it.

`scripts/check-artifact-provenance.sh` is git-only and sub-second. It lists commits **this branch**
adds after the stamp that touch `packages/{core,cli,toolchains}/src`, `apps/benchmark/src`,
`apps/benchmark/dataset`. Commits the base gained meanwhile are excluded, so it never goes red
because main moved.

Run against three real refs, base `origin/main`:

| ref | result |
|---|---|
| `origin/match/switch-arms` | **FAIL**, exit 1 — 9 commits after `cb5b51b` |
| `origin/match/def-home` | OK, exit 0 — final tip, artifact was last |
| `origin/main` | UNKNOWN, exit 0 — squash-merged, stamp unreachable |

`packages/bench-schema` is deliberately **not** in the path list. The first version included it and
went red on `origin/match/def-home` for `248ba54`, which edits one definition's user-facing summary
and nothing else. A rendering-text change moves no row; including it would have made the check its
own expected-red.

The CI job is PR-only with `fetch-depth: 0` (the default depth-1 checkout cannot see the stamp at
all) and needs no pnpm and no toolchain. On this PR it ran in 14s and printed
`provenance: artifact stamp 0e4d191 is not an ancestor of HEAD — UNKNOWN, not checked` — correct,
since this branch's artifact is main's. To prove the CI *shape* also fails, I built the exact
topology GitHub checks out (`git commit-tree <switch-arms tree> -p origin/main -p
origin/match/switch-arms`, i.e. a `refs/pull/N/merge` ref) and ran the check against
`origin/main`'s sha: **exit 1, the same 9 commits, no commits from main leaking into the list**.

### `0e6cef4` — total the skipped rows on the tier line

`runner.ts:73` was the entire SKIP path: log, `continue`. Both round-2 agents that ran a full bench
paid for it in the same round — the implement agent relaunched five minutes in ("the harness
silently SKIPs 40 rows — a regression gate blind on a whole compiler"), and the ship agent re-ran
the tier after the same 40 `marioparty3` rows vanished. Each shard now prints its own tally and the
orchestrator totals them onto the per-tier line. Proved both directions:

```
ASMLIFT_AGBCC valid  ✓ synthetic: 1 results in 1.4s → results/synthetic.json
ASMLIFT_AGBCC bogus  [synthetic 0/8] SKIPPED 1/1 case(s): toolchain unavailable (agbcc)
                     ✓ synthetic: 0 results in 0.4s → … — ⚠ 1 row(s) SKIPPED, toolchain unavailable
```

I did **not** take the proposed "exit 2 unless `--allow-skips`". Skipping is a designed path with a
documented downstream guard (`toolchains.ts:56`: "An unavailable toolchain SKIPS its rows … and
stale-check's coverage guard keeps a skipping run from ever clobbering the dataset"), and a refusal
would break legitimate partial runs — including the cheap synthetic ladder the rounds actually use.
The defect was that 40 skips were *invisible*, not that they were *allowed*.

### `19d8262` — `/match-function`: the repro is a command, not a recollection

Three rules, ~17 lines, each from a defect these rounds produced.

**The flags are part of the number.** `match-function.md` never mentioned `--proto` at all — the
line that does lives in `attribute-function.md`, and round 2's ship agent only saw it by grepping
the sibling file. So this is a *missing* instruction, not an ignored one, which is why a prompt fix
is the right lever here. Round 2's implement agent ran LBG with `--proto`; the remediate and ship
agents each hand-composed their own and did not. The ship agent's runner calls
`decompileRanked(name, asm, target, obj, { backend, symbols, compile })` — no `prototypes` key.

**Never explain a discrepancy — re-run it.** That run gave 557 / 578 against a 547 baseline, and
PR #76 shipped both plus a reason for the gap: *"nothing pins the checkout's `build/` objects or
the symbols ELF between rounds"*. PR #74's merged body already said *"607 without it, 547 with it.
A ranked run without it tops out at 578"* — 578 is the documented no-proto number. Hard rule 5
(*numbers come from commands*) did not stop this, because a command **was** run. The missing rule is
the corollary, now rule 6.

**A sweep's configuration is part of its claim.** Round 2's architect: *"the branch's own
464-function validation could not see it because it was run with the project symbol map, under
which `addressCone` refuses every one of these loads … my no-symbol-map sweep of the identical
corpus finds 17 functions whose output changes, not 7, and one of them loses a byte-exact match."*
The branch learned it, PR #76 records it, the command did not — so the next round starts over.

## What I rejected

**A committed `scripts/rank-function.sh` that bakes the proto file.** Two reasons. (1) The durable
channel for that fact already exists, unmerged: `feat/config-prototypes` (`f0d6e29`,
*"feat(cli): tools.asmlift.prototypes, and refuse a malformed table"*) whose own message names this
exact problem — *"the only channel was `--proto` on the command line, which no published repro
script carries, so the fact was unstatable by the project that knows it"*. A shell wrapper would be
a third channel for the same fact and would rot the day that branch merges. (2) The rationale for
its progress-streaming half is false — see the corrections below.

**`scripts/probe-compile.sh`.** The premise ("agents retype the agbcc line and the copies differ in
ways that changed a round's verdict") is half-true: five agents did hand-roll a wrapper, and round
3's breaker really does use host `cpp -P -nostdinc` with a typedef prelude and no `-Wparentheses`.
But `-Wparentheses` is a diagnostic flag with no codegen effect, and no evidence in the transcripts
shows a *wrong compiler fact* coming out of any of them. The verdict-changing variance the finding
actually evidences is the **symbol-map configuration of the corpus sweep**, which is a different
thing and is what `19d8262` addresses. A shell reimplementation would also have to duplicate
`compileFromCommand`'s template substitution, i.e. introduce exactly the divergence complained of.

**`scripts/corpus-sweep.ts`, and splitting configurations between the two reviewers.** The
configuration rule belongs to the *implementer*, whose Phase 4 sweep is the one that was blind;
assigning it to reviewers finds it a wave later at best. One prompt line beats a new script nothing
depends on.

**Changing `features.test.ts` so the vocabulary check reads the dataset.** Rejected on two grounds.
The proposal as written *breaks the suite*: `authored` carries judgement tags only (asserted at
`features.test.ts:131`), so sourcing "every definition is carried" from

author: fabolivark
body:
## Summary

PR #160 merged with a `TEMP ORCA-280 diagnostic` marker still active in `tests/e2e/helpers/orca-app.ts:176` (disabled `auto` on `flushRendererRecoveryEvidenceQueue`), reopening the coverage gap for specs that launch their own `ElectronApplication` via `orca-restart.ts`/`paired-electron-client.ts`. This PR removes the marker and restores the coverage with a design that avoids the mechanism implicated in the regression, off current `origin/main`.

## What broke, on real evidence

`terminal-tab-close-restart-persistence.spec.ts:23` started throwing `selector_not_found` from `terminal.split` (`src/cli/runtime/client.ts:130`) — a completely unrelated subsystem — starting exactly at the commit that made `flushRendererRecoveryEvidenceQueue` an `auto: true` fixture:

| state | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| before `auto: true` | 0/2 fail |
| `auto: true` added | 2/2 fail |
| `auto` disabled (merged to main as TEMP) | 0/44 fail |

I ran my own isolated single-spec dispatches (both `auto` on and off) and both came back green — meaning the failure needs the full-shard context (many prior tests, `workers: 1`) to manifest at all, so my isolated tests don't independently confirm causation, but they don't contradict the shard-level A/B either.

**Mechanism: not found.** I read `fixtureRunner.js`'s `resolveParametersForFunction` — auto fixtures are collected and set up before any test-requested fixtures, and for a test requesting nothing else (`terminal-tab-close-restart-persistence.spec.ts`'s `async ({}, testInfo)`), the auto fixture became the *first and only* custom fixture ever instantiated for it. That's a real, first-of-its-kind structural change for that test, but I found no concrete pathway from Playwright's own-process fixture setup to an RPC race inside a separately-launched Electron subprocess's terminal-handle registry. Reporting this as "the fixture causes it, mechanism unknown" rather than inventing a story.

## The fix

Two options were on the table:
- Trust a status read inside the bypass helpers' own `dispose()` — not viable: a normal (non-soft) failed `expect()`/`expect.poll()` only `throw`s, so `testInfo.status` stays `'passed'` throughout the test's own `finally` block regardless of what `dispose()` does; there's no reliable status to read there for the general case.
- **A named fixture requested explicitly** — chosen. `flushRendererRecoveryEvidenceQueue` is now `{ scope: 'test' }`, not `auto`. 25 specs whose test bodies call `createRestartSession`/`launchPairedElectronClient` without also using `electronApp` now destructure it by name (`{ flushRendererRecoveryEvidenceQueue }`, with a `void` reference matching the existing `registerPostElectronShutdownCleanup` pattern) — 31 test signatures total. Only those tests pay for it; every other test's fixture graph is exactly what it was before any of this.

`electronApp`'s own fixture teardown (which already reliably sees the finalized test status) now calls a new `reportAndFlushRendererRecoveryEvidence(userDataDir, testInfo)` instead of reporting directly, so a test using `electronApp` *and* a second app via one of the bypass helpers still gets both evidence sources flushed.

**Known, separate, pre-existing gap** (not fixed here): `plugin-marketplace-content.spec.ts` and `plugin-startup-budget.spec.ts` import `test` directly from `@stablyai/playwright-test`, not `./helpers/orca-app`, so no fixture defined there — old or new — has ever reached them.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts tests/e2e/helpers/renderer-recovery-evidence.unit.test.ts` — 14/14 passing, including 2 new tests for `reportAndFlushRendererRecoveryEvidence`
- [x] Mutation-checked both new tests in both directions (dropped the flush call → failure-direction test caught it; removed the status gate → both passing-direction tests caught it)
- [x] `npm test` (full suite, foreground): `51879 passed | 109 skipped (51988)`
- [x] Built and ran locally against a real Electron app: `terminal-tab-close-restart-persistence.spec.ts` (3x), a spot-check across 8 of the 25 migrated spec files (19 tests list correctly, one run live end-to-end), plus two throwaway smoke specs proving both directions — a `createRestartSession`-only test reports nothing when it passes and exactly once when it fails; a test combining `electronApp` with a second `createRestartSession` launch reports both sources only on failure
- [x] `oxlint` clean on all changed files, no `max-lines` disables, no `any`, no leftover debug statements
- [x] Deleted the temporary `orca-280-diag-auto-enabled` branch used for the empirical mechanism test

author: rajatnagda45
body:
## Linked Issue

Closes #7068

## Description

Neptune Analytics' `topK.byEmbedding` (called by `search()` via `topKByEmbeddingWithFiltering`) returns the **squared Euclidean distance** as its `score` — lower means more similar, and the nearest/identical node scores `0.0`. This is documented by AWS, whose sample output shows the nearest node at `score: 0.0` and farther nodes at `24.0` / `25.0`:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune-analytics/latest/userguide/vectors.topK.byEmbedding.html

`_parse_query_responses` passed that value straight through as the similarity score, violating the `VectorStoreBase.search` contract (higher = more similar). As a result mem0's `score_and_rank` (default `threshold=0.1`, sorts descending):

- **drops the nearest matches** — distance ~0 becomes a score ~0, below the threshold;
- **ranks the farthest candidates first**.

So on a Neptune-backed `Memory`, `search()` returns results roughly farthest-first and silently discards the closest matches.

The fix converts the distance to similarity using the L2 formula the base class documents: `score = 1.0 / (1.0 + distance)` (monotonic, maps `[0, inf) -> (0, 1]`, nearest → highest). `get`/`list` (which return `score=None`) are unchanged.

This is the same class of fix already applied for pgvector (#6883), Milvus (#6933), the LangChain wrapper (#6884), Baidu (#6434) and Chroma. Unlike the euclidean-only cases (S3 Vectors #6546, Turbopuffer #6557), Neptune returns the distance **unconditionally** (no cosine path), so ranking is always inverted.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Refactor (no functional changes)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Breaking Changes

N/A — scores were previously unusable (raw distances). Callers relying on mem0's documented similarity contract now get correct ranking.

author: valzav
body:
Registers `herdr` as a Foreman backend beside `subagents` and `ao`, and closes the defects a review of that work found.

## Herdr backend

The controller runs inside the project's Herdr session and dispatches each worker as a fresh coding agent in a sibling pane of that session. Workers share the controller's checkout and canonical task branch; isolation comes from a fresh worker per dispatch and serial execution. Each role is pinned to a fixed harness, so every Review is cross-model.

- The inherited `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` is the session. A controller that exports a different socket or session name reads one session and spawns in another with no error from either.
- The controller lease is generational: `.foreman/controller.lock.<n>`, claimed with `ln`. A reclaimer claims `n+1` and never removes or moves the generation it observed, because no shell primitive removes a lock conditionally on it still being the one just read.
- Lease liveness tests the pane's recorded `agent_session` value. A pane outlives its agent and reports a null session at an ordinary shell, so a pane-existence test alone would hold a dead controller's lease forever.
- Release closes the accepted worker's own recorded pane and touches no Git state.

## Review gate

A passing code verdict routes straight to Landing, so the cross-mode pass exception is one-directional. Plan mode may pass while carrying a code-owned finding to the implementation head that can close it. Code mode returns `material findings` for every open P1 or P2 including Draft-owned ones, and names Draft so Forge returns `draft_required` before merge.

The `Verdict` section opens with one machine-readable line — `verdict: …; open: …; covered: …` — so the covered target and the carried findings are readable without parsing prose.

## Producer changes

- Draft inspects the baseline before writing a plan.
- Forge proves a negative-result instrument fires before trusting it.
- Cast asks for the tracker mode instead of defaulting to local, and states that changing mode after features exist requires migrating every `spec.md` mapping.

## Verification

`scripts/check-coordination-contracts.py`, its 29 static tests, and `scripts/build-skills-index.py --check` all pass. `claude plugin validate` passes with only the intentional no-version warning. The plugin loads under `--plugin-dir` in Claude Code and installs from the repository marketplace into an isolated Codex profile with all 11 skills cached. Every eval `files` path resolves and every rewritten fixture runs end to end.

Behavioral evals are declarations, not proof of behavior; the coordination check detects drift only.

author: joshes14
body:
…tick

WorldManager's five per-player announcer state maps (announceTicks, announceComponent, announceFadeTicks, announceFaction, lastSeenFaction) were plain HashMaps, mutated from the main-thread tick loop, the main-thread packet handler (onMove), and — critically — clearPlayerState, which is invoked from ServerPlayConnectionEvents.DISCONNECT. That Fabric event is not guaranteed to run on the main server thread: it fires from ServerCommonNetworkHandler.onDisconnect, which can be reached from the netty channel-inactive callback when a client's TCP connection drops. On a 4-player server after ~18.75 h uptime a disconnect eventually caught the tick loop mid-iteration of announceTicks, throwing CME from HashMap$HashIterator.nextNode and taking down the server tick.

- All five maps -> ConcurrentHashMap, matching the existing convention in TeleportRequestManager (same "per-player state cleared on DISCONNECT" pattern).
- lastSeenFaction and announceFaction put-sites converted to put-when-non-null / remove-when-null since ConcurrentHashMap rejects null values. Semantically equivalent -- callers already treated null-value and missing-entry identically via Objects.equals compare and null-tolerant buildFadeStep.
- Bump mod_version 3.4 -> 3.4.1.
- CHANGELOG entry documenting the crash, root cause, and mitigation.

Reentrancy ruled out: the tick loop only calls sendOverlayMessage (fire-and-forget packet) and safe iterator ops (entry.setValue, iterator.remove). No path from inside the loop back into announceTicks.put/remove.

Verification: ./gradlew build test -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL, all existing tests pass.

Fixes:
  java.util.ConcurrentModificationException
    at java.base/java.util.HashMap$HashIterator.nextNode(HashMap.java:1606)
    at io.icker.factions.core.WorldManager.lambda$register$0(WorldManager.java:44)

A subtraction ledger was the wrong instrument for this page's job: it isn't reconciling an account, it's saying where $35 million goes.

| | |
|---|---|
| **$35,000,000** | one-time 2026-27 appropriation *(full-width, cobalt)* |
| $24,240,308 | allocated directly to the 115 colleges |
| $1,000,000 | dedicated to the four noncredit campuses |
| $8,959,692 | statewide CPL projects and technology |
| $800,000 | two Chancellor's Office posts |

author: 0dian
body:
## 动机

把遥控器按键映射成「打开 Claude」或「打开 Codex」之后，真机上应用能被正常打开并置于前台，但输入框聚焦稳定失败：日志始终是

```
APP FOCUS failed bundle=com.anthropic.claudefordesktop method=accessibility reason=composer_not_found
```

对使用者来说，这正好卡在遥控器场景最关键的那一步——按一次键就该能开口说话，实际却要走过去用鼠标点一下输入框，语音输入的价值被抵消了大半。权限是齐全的（`input=true accessibility=true`，没有 `reason=not_trusted`），同一版本对非 Electron 目标的聚焦一切正常。

## 判定实验与根因

按 `AGENTS.md` 的 Bug 流程，先复现、再看日志、再定位根因：

开启 VoiceOver（Cmd+F5）后重按同一个按键：

- 旁白刚启动、辅助功能树尚未建好时，仍然失败；
- 数秒后再按，日志立刻变成 `APP FOCUS succeeded`，Claude Desktop 与 `com.openai.codex` 都成功。

这个实验把根因从「扫描算法找不到输入框」区分成了「树本身还不存在」，同时说明建树需要时间。

**根因**：Chromium / Electron 默认不为 web 内容构建辅助功能树，只有当辅助技术客户端主动声明自己时才会构建。VoiceOver 会去设置这个属性，无线麦从来没有声明过，所以 `focusComposer` 扫描到的只是一个没有 web 内容的空壳——重试多少次都不可能找到 composer。原有 8 × 200ms（1.4 秒）的重试窗口也短于真机上约 1~2 秒的建树耗时。

## 改动摘要

- `scheduleAccessibilityComposerFocus` 与自定义 APP 的 `recordedAccessibility` 路径，在每轮尝试开始处对目标进程的 `AXUIElement` 设置 `AXManualAccessibility = true`（Chromium / Electron 约定属性，幂等）。不认这个属性的应用返回 `attributeUnsupported`，静默忽略，不改变原有流程。
- 降级链：主属性返回 `attributeUnsupported` 时，对同一个 app element 改设标准的 `AXEnhancedUserInterface = true`。之所以不把它放在第一位——这个属性在部分 Electron 版本上有窗口变形与动画副作用，而 Electron 恰恰在第一步就成功、不会走到第二步；真正走降级路径的都是非 Chromium 外壳。顺序与取舍写在代码注释里。
- composer 重试窗口从 8 × 200ms（1.4 秒）放宽到 12 × 250ms（2.75 秒），覆盖真机观察到的建树耗时。自定义 APP 路径的时序保持不变，避免影响已验收行为。
- 新增日志 `APP FOCUS manual_accessibility bundle=<id> attempt=<n> result=<name>`，只在首次尝试和第一次建树成功时记录；走降级链时 `result` 前缀为 `fallback_enhanced_`，可以直接看出是哪个属性回答的。失败原因保持 `composer_not_found` 不变。
- 复现证据、日志结论、根因、修复与验证边界记录在 `Bugs/2026-08-22-electron-composer-focus-needs-manual-accessibility.md`，测试手册新增用例 4A（`Testing/CustomApplicationFocus.md`），`TODO.md` 对应条目同步更新。

## 真机验证证据

环境：macOS 26.5.0、小米 rc003 遥控器、SayAll 1.9.8 自构建，测试期间 VoiceOver 关闭、目标应用冷重启。

- **修复前**：权限齐全的前提下，`openClaude` / `openCodex` 稳定输出 `composer_not_found`。
- **判定实验**：开启 VoiceOver 后立刻 `APP FOCUS succeeded`，证实 Electron / WebKit 辅助树懒加载才是根因，而不是扫描算法有问题。
- **修复后 · Claude Desktop**：`APP FOCUS manual_accessibility ... result=success` → `APP FOCUS succeeded`，即时聚焦，**通过**。首轮修复对 Electron 完全生效。
- **修复后 · ChatGPT（`com.openai.codex`）**：结果与最初的预期不同，如实记录——该应用对两个属性都不支持，日志为 `result=fallback_enhanced_not_implemented`。但聚焦仍然成功，唤醒它懒加载的 web 内容树的是聚焦流程的**扫描本身**，而不是任何一个属性。由此产生的是一条时间窗边界：冷启动后的第一次按键可能在树建好之前用完 2.75 秒窗口而失败，之后的按键稳定成功。
- 该应用与其他非 Chromium 应用均未观察到窗口变形、缩放或异常动画；Claude Desktop 仍在第一步 `result=success`，不进入降级路径。

上述边界已记录在 Bugs 文档的「验证边界」中，并作为**已知边界（未修复）**明确标注：继续放宽窗口会拖长所有目标的失败路径，因此本次不改；如果真机反馈该场景常见，再单独评估按应用区分窗口或在扫描到空壳时提前重试。

## 关于本 PR 的第三个 commit

前两个 commit 是修复本体。第三个 commit（`补记 ChatGPT 降级路径的真机复验结果与冷启动时间窗边界`）是纯文档更新：原 Bugs 文档把 ChatGPT 的降级复验列为「待完成」并预期 `result=fallback_enhanced_success`，而真机复验的实际结果是两个属性都不支持。按仓库「每个 Bug 的验证边界都要记录到 `Bugs/`」的要求，把实测结果、真实成功路径和冷启动时间窗边界补记进去，并同步更正测试手册用例 4A 的期望值与自检数量。没有代码改动。

## 测试状态

- `scripts/test.sh`：42/42 通过，其中的 `xcrun swift build` 一并通过。（本分支不含滚动动作那一项自检，因此比同时带两个工作项的本地分支少 1 项。）
- 新增的 Swift Testing 测试（结果名映射、日志节流、重试窗口 ≥ 2 秒、降级链 token）只做了编译验证，**未执行**：本机只有 Command Line Tools、没有 Xcode，缺少 `Testing` 模块，`swift test` 跑不起来。这部分需要在装有 Xcode 的机器或 CI 上执行。
- 自动化不能证明 Electron 的真实建树时间、`AXManualAccessibility` 在各 Electron 版本上的行为，以及输入框最终是否真正获得焦点——这几项只有上面的真机验证能覆盖。
- 自定义 APP 路径（`recordedAccessibility`）本次未做真机验收，其时序刻意保持不变。

author: karodonghust
body:
## What changed

- add the Advisor-only `students.guardians.manage` capability and keep Founder/Admin read-only
- implement current guardian reads, privacy-safe guardian search, secondary relationship attach, and atomic primary-contact handoff
- add the PostgreSQL guardian relationship repository with tenant scoping, idempotency, audit/outbox writes, stale-version handling, and transactional rollback
- add the Student detail and guardian-management UI with explicit candidate selection, closed relationship vocabulary, retry-key lifecycle, responsive states, and capability-based controls
- add focused contract/unit coverage plus permanent PostgreSQL 17 HTTP and real-browser Local Dev gates
- close the CRM-01 local-only documentation status and add the CRM-02 implementation/acceptance record

## Why

Advisors need a complete local CRM workflow to reuse an existing Guardian across Students, attach that Guardian as a secondary relationship, and safely hand off the primary contact while preserving history. The workflow must remain tenant-isolated, idempotent, privacy-safe, and inaccessible to roles without the management capability.

## Impact

- Advisor can search and explicitly select an existing Guardian, attach a secondary relationship, and perform a version-checked primary handoff.
- Founder and Admin retain current relationship read access but cannot see management commands; direct write requests fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`.
- Two concurrent handoffs using the same expected version produce exactly one success and one `409 STALE_VERSION` with no loser-side effects.
- No database migration, migration manifest, or one-role generated baseline changed.

## Validation

- Node 22 TypeScript: pass
- targeted ESLint for CRM-02 owned files: pass
- CRM focused unit/UI tests: 21/21 pass
- architecture boundaries: 15/15 pass
- ENV-01A focused contract suite: 74/74 pass
- `pnpm test:crm-02-dev-http`: 1/1 pass on disposable PostgreSQL 17.10, current 28-file one-role baseline, Release1 synthetic seed, FORCE RLS, and real Next Dev HTTP
- `pnpm test:crm-02-dev-browser`: 1/1 pass with `stage=complete` using isolated Next Dev, system Chrome, and the same PostgreSQL contract
- shared diff/type/DTO/capability/idempotency/privacy review: pass
- `git diff --check`: pass

## Known verification boundary

- Production build was attempted with a deterministic local review identity but remained blocked before application compilation because the existing `next/font/google` Geist dependency could not reach Google Fonts, including outside the sandbox. This is not attributed to CRM-02 and is not reported as a passing build.
- Vercel Test: not run (unverified), per the accepted Local Dev delivery boundary.
- AWS Production: not run (unverified).

## Data and privacy

- tests use synthetic data only
- search terms and full contact details are not placed in URLs, logs, audit/outbox payloads, or error responses
- no secrets, local environment files, `PROJECT_PLAN.local.md`, migrations, or generated baseline assets are included

COALESCE(p.category, '')     -- ❌

invalid input value for enum scm.mfg_product_category: "" [22P02]

COALESCE(p.category::text, '')   -- ✅ 先 cast 再 coalesce

寄售是按单据类型分表的：`consignment_sales_order_items`、`consignment_delivery_order_items`、`purchase_consignment_order_items`。

body:
Tenth archivist deployment. Audited against `c4f6825` on a complete 748-commit history — the container's clone arrived shallow (196 commits) and every ancestry and guard result was re-derived after `git fetch --unshallow`.

## The headline is on the public site

`docs/how-it-works.html:58` reads "the first band is the **nine** public sources checked". The chart inlined at `:96` of the same page renders "**THE 10 SOURCES**" with ten chips. `:7`'s meta description says nine. Thirty-eight lines apart, on one screen, the prose contradicts the picture it introduces.

The chart is right: `src/sources.all_sources()` returns 10, `validate.mjs` exits 0 at "10 source chips", `README.md:56` says ten. The two "nine" strings are hand-written English in `scripts/site_templates/how_it_works.html.j2:3` and `:27`.

Live since `44550ca` (2026-08-17) — five days. That commit's message claimed "Every nine-sources surface moves to ten in the same change"; two did not. `check_site_sync.py` cannot catch it — template and built page agree, and both are wrong.

**Owner: site-experience.** Escalated, not edited.

## The finding against this seat

`agents/Claim Map.md`'s 2026-08-17 anchor block had already closed the source-count row: *"C12's source-count row is satisfied by that same commit (ten stated once, everywhere)."* Wrong twice — the row is **C11** (C12 is Model assignments), and it was **not** satisfied. The words came from `44550ca`'s commit message rather than from opening the four files C11 names.

**Rule adopted:** a commit message is a claim about a change, never a reading of the files after it; a claim-map row is closed only by re-reading every cell it names. Second form of the 2026-08-16 rule about guard exit codes.

Struck in place with the original wording quoted; C11 re-read cell by cell at `c4f6825`.

## Escalations to Emory — each re-measured, not inherited

| Thread | State |
|---|---|
| **D7** (new) | `METHODOLOGY.md:33` enumerates nine channels, omitting GDELT, and says Bing News is polled through **eight** queries where `src/sources/bing_news.py:23` defines **12** |
| **D8** (new) | `.claude/agents/site-experience.md:20` carries a second "Zero-cost" binding beside `systems-designer.md:17`, both falsified by `README.md:6` on 2026-08-08 |

| **D5** | Unchanged after nine days — eight of nine definitions still never name their seat's note |
| **F1** | **Day twenty-six**, same three counts a fourth time: `main` 37/21/37 vs `chore/operator-marks-2026-07-27` 40/38/40 |

## Fixed inside this seat's paths

- **`HANDOFF.md`** — sources table gains the `gdelt` row, a corrected `bing_news` row (12 queries), and a measured count naming all ten instances `all_sources()` returns, under a heading that claims "current reality".
- **`agents/obsidian-archivist.md:706`** — a `[[Workflow Threads]]` wikilink wrapped across a line break, so `build_graph --dry-run` listed this note as linking to a nonexistent note. Rewrapped.
- **Currency 4 failed → 1.** Registry, Claim Map, Workflow Threads and Change Log restamped to `c4f6825`. `STATE_OF_THE_ANSWER.md` left stale **by decision** — it is the analyst's living memory and the 2026-08-08 rule against restamping another seat's file governs.

- **`check_currency.py` on a shallow clone reported 7 failures, including three hard `FAIL`s for commits that exist** (`373cce6`, `9efafb0`, `ae42639`). After `git fetch --unshallow`: 4 failures, zero `FAIL`s. CI is unaffected — `pipeline-guards.yml:172` sets `fetch-depth: 0` — so the hazard is agent-session-only.
- **This every-3-days session ran six days after the last.** No 2026-08-19 record exists on any branch. A skipped session is silent by design (the emailer asks only "is anything unsent?"), so it reports nothing rather than a false all-clear. Flagged for a decision, not fixed unasked.

author: boingball
body:
## Summary

Pulls the PostScript backend from #17 (stale, based on commit `510fc08`, 12 merges behind main — predating the whole #29/#30 clamp/centering/AAN/PWG-preference chain) into current `main` so it can be tested against real PostScript hardware, without regressing anything shipped since.

**New**: `MP_ENGINE_POSTSCRIPT` (`driver/postscript_writer.c`/`.h`) — a minimal streaming PostScript Level 2 encoder wrapping the existing JPEG encoder's compressed output in ASCII85 + `DCTDecode`, for printers (e.g. Samsung C480W) that advertise `image/jpeg` over IPP but silently discard the job. It composes `MPJpegEncoder` directly, so the AAN fast-DCT work from #37 already speeds it up too.

## Conflict resolution

**Mechanical** (Makefile, `driver_core.c`'s engine-dispatch switches, `printertag.s`/`printertag_classic.s`): kept both sides' targets/objects/dependencies; the PostScript case slots into the same `MP_ENGINE_PWG`/`PDF`/`JPEG` pattern everywhere, including the width-clamp and `mp_job_write_row()` centering fixes from #34/#35 — both already engine-agnostic, no changes needed to cover PostScript correctly. Revision bumped to 27 (past both branches' rev26/rev20).

**The real work** (`src/MintPrintSettings.c`): both branches had independently rewritten `mintprint_test_page()` from the same pre-#29 ancestor — main via #29's private-ColorMap/synchronous-DoIO redesign, #17 via its own async/live-palette/small-PostScript-page redesign. Reconciled rather than mechanically picked a side:

- Kept #17's architecture: async `SendIO`+`WaitIO` (GUI stays responsive during Test Print), live Workbench-palette light/dark pen detection (fixes a toner-wasting grey-background bug on a real Samsung laser — a different instance of the same bug class #29 fixed differently), CPU/engine-name reporting, and PostScript's fixed small page size (4.5×6in via `SPECIAL_MILCOLS`/`MILROWS`, no `SPECIAL_CENTER` since the PostScript writer self-centers).
- For JPEG/PWG/PDF, kept **main's** explicit `DestCols`/`DestRows` computed from configured media instead of #17's `io_DestCols`/`DestRows=0` fallback: main's own code comment documents that leaving them at 0 was already tried and found broken on real hardware (~3113×3015px, unrelated to the configured `iso_a4_210x297mm` media). Reintroducing it would have silently undone that fix and broken the size the width-clamp (`mp_media_expected_width_px`) needs to compare against.
- `MP_ENGINE_MAX` 3→4, `driver_engine_explicit` (#36's PWG-preference tracking) preserved verbatim — that logic is string-based (`"pwg-raster"` lookup) and unaffected by the engine count/order change.

`media_size.c`/`.h`, `tests/test_media_size.c`, `config.c`, docs, the Aminet readme, and `windows_ipp_probe.py` all auto-merged cleanly.

## Test plan

- [x] `make test` (dpi/jpeg/media_size — unaffected by this merge) passes clean.
- [x] `make test-postscript` — host-builds the PostScript writer, generates a real `.ps` file, and validates it with Ghostscript (installed for this session): passes with no errors.
- [ ] Cross-compile with the m68k-amigaos toolchain (not available in this environment).
- [ ] Real hardware: confirm the PostScript engine on actual PostScript hardware (the point of landing this now).
- [ ] Real hardware: confirm JPEG/PWG/PDF are behaviourally unchanged after the merge (test page, width clamp, centering all still correct).
