author: cygmris
body:
## What this adds

An opt-in **Local AI** settings section, plus two entry points that turn messy text into clean Markdown using the user's own Ollama:

- **Command palette → "AI to Markdown"** — paste or drop a plain-text file, get a new note.
- **Editor toolbar ✨ / command palette → "Tidy the current note with AI"** — reformats the current note, or just the selection if there is one.

Requests go **straight from the browser to the user's own Ollama**. Note text never reaches the server. Nothing is enabled by default; the section is empty until a user configures it.

## Why the CSP change is unavoidable

The Worker runs at the edge and cannot reach a user's loopback address, so there is no server-side proxy option for this path. `connect-src` is widened to **exactly two hardcoded loopback endpoints** (`http://127.0.0.1:11434`, `http://localhost:11434`) and nothing else — no config value or user input is ever interpolated into that header.

## Two failure modes that shaped the design

**1. Ollama silently truncates over-long input.** When a prompt exceeds the context window, Ollama drops the front of it and the model then stops cleanly on the part it did see, reporting `finish_reason: "stop"`. Nothing in the API surfaces this. `detectLoss` therefore uses a second, independent heuristic — output far shorter than input on a first-turn conversion — and long input is chunked paragraph-first, then by line, then hard-cut.

**2. Offsets go stale while the model works.** With realtime sync on, the note can change underneath a long generation. A selection edit would then land in the wrong place and a whole-note edit would clobber the concurrent change — both silently. Writes carry the original text and are refused if it no longer matches, keeping the result on screen so it can be copied instead.

## Browser support, stated in the UI

- Safari blocks an HTTPS page from calling `http://localhost`, so this is Chrome/Firefox only. That limit is shown in the settings panel, not just in docs.
- Chrome 138+ additionally gates loopback access behind a permission prompt, and an **unanswered prompt leaves the request hanging rather than failing**. The connection test therefore carries its own 12s timeout and explains that specific case.

## Security

Note content is treated as untrusted data: the system prompt instructs the model to reformat rather than answer, and that instruction follows the user's UI language so weaker local models weight it properly. No new credentials, routes, or storage.

## Checks run

```
npm run typecheck      PASS
npm run i18n:check     PASS   (all new strings in both locales)
npm run comments:check PASS   (no comments added)
npm run test:unit      PASS   (138 tests)
npm run build          PASS
```

Assertions were reverse-verified: each implementation was broken in turn to confirm the matching test goes red, then restored.

**`npm run test:e2e` does not complete on my machine, and neither does it on an unmodified checkout of `main`** — wrangler crashes partway through with its own "please create an issue at workers-sdk" message and a note that 4.125.0 may fix it. I did not upgrade wrangler here since that would be an unrelated change to `package-lock.json`. Happy to re-run if you have a known-good version.

## Notes for review

- The default model string is whatever tag the user has locally; there is no bundled default that will work everywhere.
- `EditorToolbar.tsx` gains one button; the shared trigger logic lives in `features/ai/open-tidy.ts` so the palette and the toolbar cannot drift apart.
- No changes to `wrangler.toml`, persistence, sync, import/export, or backups.

author: pummelchen
body:
Sixteen commits. `main` had **five** failing CI jobs when this branch started; it now has **one**, and that one is pre-existing and untouched here.

## CI repairs

- **Compile Check** — `compile-check` gained a `libc` prerequisite in `47ff4f1` but the job was never updated. It needs `llvm-ar`, `meson`, `ninja` *and* the picolibc submodule; it had `clang lld` and no submodules.
- **ABI Contract** — `XAIOS_CAP_CREDENTIAL_READ` shipped in `syscall.h` but was never recorded in the frozen contract. Records a capability the kernel already enforces; widens nothing.
- **Hosted Engine & Model v2** — `make hosted-test` could not build on Linux. BearSSL `getentropy()` is hidden by glibc under `-std=c99`, and openbsd-compat `bcrypt_pbkdf.c` uses `__nonstring__`, unknown to clang before 21. macOS hid both.

## Local console

Three defects, all invisible to the existing gates because every interoperability suite drives XAIOS over SSH.

- **Output printed twice.** `klog_console_write` wrote each byte to the UART *and* into the capture buffer the shell then replayed. On the local console the UART is the terminal. Also stops publishing remote SSH command output on the physical serial port.
- **`xaiosctl` was unreachable.** `help` advertised it and `sysinfo`/`status` pointed users at it, but it had no dispatch entry — and it was `int main(void)`, a self-test harness, so registering it alone would have run the tests instead of the operation. It now takes arguments and forwards them to the control protocol under the observer role.
- **Six-digit console PIN** (`012345`), console-only, never accepted over SSH, and gated behind password auth so a key-only image stays key-only. Five failures now lock the prompt for 60s — `g_console_auth_failures` was previously counted and never acted on, so neither the PIN nor the password had any throttle.

## VMware Fusion

The Fusion window could be watched but not used: the framebuffer was a status panel that never echoed input or rendered output, and the serial port was write-only.

- **Framebuffer terminal** — after boot the display mirrors the console byte stream, with CSI parsing, wrapping and scrolling. Verified by reading the rendered pixels back on the real device.
- **USB keyboard** — two bugs. The control-endpoint ring was never rewound between devices, so everything past the first was unreachable; and the port-5 device is a composite HID whose interfaces are both `subclass 0 / protocol 0`, so the report descriptor is now used to identify a keyboard rather than binding a pointing device by mistake.
- **`XAIOS_FUSION_SERIAL=pipe`** for a bidirectional serial console.

## Storage and process ownership

- **Snapshot state could never persist.** `persistence` wrote to the default block device — the test image the launcher attaches with `snapshot=on`, so every write was discarded. `PERSISTENCE_SECTOR` (3000) sits just below `MFS_START_SECTOR` (3072); only the device binding was wrong.
- **MutableFS had no locking at all** while reachable from four vCPUs, on a kernel with no global syscall lock. Every entry point is now serialised.
- **`mutable_fs_write_fd` cleared a 256 KiB buffer on every call** — ~21 MiB of memset to write 3 KiB of audit log.
- **Process resources were keyed on a recycled pid.** One run issued and reaped pid 32 nineteen times, and every SSH child channel ran as `child=32`. VFS handles and sockets keyed on it, so any transient exiting released a live session's file handle. This was the FreeBSD gate's intermittent failure.

## FreeBSD gate

Two separate problems, both now fixed:

- The outbound budget was keyed on **guest** architecture (600s x86_64, 60s aarch64), which only holds on an ARM host. On an x86_64 runner the cross-emulated aarch64 guest got 60s. Now derived from the host/guest pairing; nothing that passes today gets less time.
- The gate produced **no guest-side evidence** — non-verbose builds silence klog after boot. It now captures kernel diagnostics, which is what named the ownership bug on the first failure after landing.

**The gate now passes in CI**, for the first time.

## Status

15 of 16 checks pass. **Core OS Aggregate RC** fails with exactly the same five items as `main` — `smmuv3 exited 2`, `nvme exited 2`, and three missing markers — verified unchanged across every commit on this branch.

Not addressed: those five items, and sustained parser fuzzing on the SSH stack and DNSSEC validator.

author: edicius2002
body:
The owner asked for narrower cards: per-week cards four across a row, per-month boxes three per row, and the fee cards at the bottom three per row as well.

## What was actually too wide

"Los cuadros de las barras por semana / por mes" turned out to be two different rules inside **`MoneyWeekChart`** — a grid of months (`.monthRow`) with a grid of week cards (`.weeks`) nested in it — not the `By week` / `By month` overview charts. Those were left alone, and it was verified rather than assumed: their SVG boxes measure 569.7px and 467.9px before and after, and the axis label set is byte-identical (`$0 $1k … $7.5k $10k`), so the known `formatAxisMoney` point-vs-comma inconsistency is neither touched nor made worse.

Measured in Chrome at 1536px CSS, root font 20px:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| month box | 549.6px, **2 per row** | 366.4px, **3 per row** |
| week card | 108.51px | 72.4px |
| July (4 weeks) | wrapped **3 + 1** | **4 on one row** |
| fee card | 1099.2px, **1 per row** | 356.4px, **3 per row** |
| Weeks panel | 1628px | 1233px |
| page | **2629px** | **2146px** |

**The old layout missed 4-across by 14.4px**: four clusters were 534.0px in a 519.6px box. The stylesheet's own comment claimed "a 4-week month fits in ~530px" — it did not, at the window it was written for.

Every one of the 18 figures on the page is byte-identical before and after. Gross still `$22.598,67`, five markers still make six segments, no fee moved.

## Two defects found on the way, both pre-existing

**The rule under a row of months was drawn in the wrong place.** `:nth-last-child(-n+2)` counts back from the end, so with five months in two columns it matched the fourth as well as the fifth — the rule under the second row was missing while a third row sat below it. Visible in today's archive. Now placed by where a row *starts*: `:nth-child(3n+1):nth-last-child(-n+3) ~`.

**The fee card's ledger escaped its own card below ~740px** — 24px outside, measured. A bare `minmax(13.5rem, 1fr)` floor that would not yield. Fixed with the house pattern `minmax(min(13.5rem, 100%), 1fr)`, which `Positions.module.css` already uses for the same reason, and pinned by a test.

## What stopped fitting — reported, not hidden

**A five-figure week does not fit.** The week card holds 64.4px inside its padding; nine characters at 0.56rem is 60.5px. Nine and not eight because `formatMoney` follows the reader's locale — the owner sees `$4272,50` (8) while `en-US` renders `$4,272.50` (9), and the card is sized for the longer. `$12,345.67` is eleven and would spill. The largest week today is $4,272.50 and the largest month $9,069.46.

**Nothing was rounded, truncated or abbreviated to avoid it.** The percentage pill and the date range wrap to a second line instead — `47.1% of` / `month`, `29/06–` / `05/07` — keeping every word and every decimal. Font sizes did come down: value 0.68 → 0.56rem, pill 0.52 → 0.48rem, range 0.72 → 0.6rem.

**The fee card had the opposite problem: a line, not a figure.** Range, week count and three metrics sat on one line needing 774px, and a third of a row gives 322.4px. That line was never narrowable, only wrappable, so the card is now the range on its own row over a three-line ledger. `Fee (under min)` is still written in full — 201.4px, the longest label there is, and the one the card is sized from. Measured headroom is fourteen characters against an archive whose largest segment is $6,451.32, so nothing here is near its limit.

## Breakpoints are derived, then deliberately overridden

All four fold points come from a measured card floor, not from typed numbers: week card 68.5px → cluster 82.5px → cell 329.9px → 1486.6 / 1116.6 / 766.7 / 601.8px of window. The fee card's own floor is 303px, which would allow 1375.8 and 1057.8.

**They were set to the month grid's 1486 / 1116 anyway**, because both grids live in the one Weeks panel and a window where the months have folded to two while the fee cards under them are still three reads as a bug. A test asserts the derived floors are ≤ the chosen thresholds — so the coupling always folds early and can never overflow — and that the two stylesheets' `@media` lists still agree.

Measured across 360 → 1920px, no horizontal overflow of card contents at any width. Below ~620px the page overflows, but that is the fixed 300px sidebar and pre-existing.

## One change outside the brief, flagged rather than slipped in

`GreenlightPage.module.css`: `.segmentsSlot { min-height: 8.5rem → 10rem }`. Two segments used to be two stacked cards (~161px); they are now one row of 176.1px plus margin = 196.1px, so the old reserve was 26px short — 26px of page moving under the cursor on the very click that creates the first marker, which is what that slot exists to prevent.

## Verification

**1675 → 1715 passing, 2 skipped unchanged** (106 → 110 files). +40, all in four new files; no existing test changed.

- `moneyWeekGrid.test.ts` (14) and `segmentGrid.test.ts` (11) read the *compiled* stylesheets and re-derive every width from the real 1099.2px list, check the widest rendered figure fits inside the card's padding, and re-derive all four breakpoints from the card floor — a number typed there that the arithmetic does not give goes red.
- `MoneyWeekChart.test.tsx` (7) and `SegmentSummary.test.tsx` (8) are the **first DOM coverage either component has ever had**.

**Verified by mutation, not just by being green:** a fourth column, the old padding, a 10rem ledger floor, and a moved breakpoint each turn the grid tests red.

## Left open

- The five-figure-week ceiling above; HANDOFF records it with the three ways out in cost order.
- The breakpoint coupling between the two grids is enforced only by a test, not by the stylesheets themselves.
- Greenlight's plan section is stale and was deliberately not fixed here: it says `Replace modes: all + current-month` where the code says `'all' | 'weeks'`, and ids **6.7 and 6.8 each appear twice**. Recorded in HANDOFF.

author: 0kaba0
body:
Fixes #1410. The field evidence named the cause precisely: the same error on every retry, down to the same local port (`47938`), while the socket no longer existed in `netstat` and IMAP/JMAP served the same user without trouble.

## The cause

`isConnectionError` decided by shape, not by cause:

```go
var opErr *net.OpError
if errors.As(err, &opErr) {
    return !opErr.Timeout()
}
```

A kernel `ETIMEDOUT` — TCP retransmission exhausted, the peer is gone — reports `Timeout() == true`. So the one error that most certainly means "this connection is dead" was the one excluded from reconnecting. Confirmed rather than assumed:

```
as OpError:               true
Timeout():                true
is ETIMEDOUT:             true
is os.ErrDeadlineExceeded: false
```

The exclusion was not wrong to exist — our own elapsed deadline also arrives as a timeout, and redialing on it would reconnect on every slow answer. The two are now separated by cause instead of by shape.

## Tests

`TestReconnectDecision` covers both sides, since a predicate that redials on everything is as broken as one that never does: kernel timeout → redial; our deadline → not; cancellation → not; peer closed / reset → redial; a malformed response → not.

`TestALookupSurvivesTheConnectionGoingAway` pins the end-to-end behaviour on the dead-socket shape a test can actually stage (the peer closing): the second lookup succeeds on a fresh connection instead of inheriting the corpse. The kernel timeout itself cannot be staged from a test — stated rather than faked.

## One line removed on the way

I first added an explicit `os.ErrDeadlineExceeded` case beside the cancellation check. The mutation that removed it changed no test result: that shape already failed the `Timeout()` test below. It was decoration that reads as logic, so it is gone and the reason is in the test comment.

Version 2.3.221 — same number as #1411; whichever merges second needs a re-bump, and I will do it on request.

author: jpalczewski
body:
Closes #35. Track B, first half.

## The bug

`search_fts` passed the user's text straight into `notes_fts MATCH :q`. FTS5 parses that operand as a query language, so ordinary prose raises `OperationalError` — **109 times in 30 days on production**, and the `except` swallowed it to `[]`. Hybrid search silently dropped to its vector leg on exactly the natural-language queries the tool is built for.

The failing inputs were not malformed; they were normal:

```
'poszukiwanie sensu, blokada twórcza, niedokończone projekty'
'<imię nazwisko> — kim jest, kontekst'
```

## The fix

`_to_fts_query` tokenizes on `\w+` (unicode-aware, so Polish diacritics survive) and quotes each token. A quoted token is an FTS5 string literal, so punctuation and the bare `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`/`NEAR` keywords lose their meaning. Tokens cannot contain `"` by construction, so no inner escaping is needed. Empty input returns `""` and the caller skips the query — an empty `MATCH` is itself a syntax error, which was a real production failure mode (`,,,`).

The `except` comment changed too. It used to describe a syntax error as "the common, expected case"; now any input is valid, so anything reaching it is a genuine DB problem and `search_fts_failed` means something again.

## Two decisions measurement forced

I first wrote this preserving implicit AND, on the reasoning that a syntax fix should not change recall. Measuring against the **real index** killed that. Note `notes_fts` is declared `tokenize='trigram'` (`db.py:82-90`), not the default `unicode61` — my first probe used the default and was measuring the wrong thing.

**Terms join with `OR`.** Against the trigram index, every sampled production query returns zero rows under AND:

| production query | raw | AND | OR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `poszukiwanie sensu, blokada twórcza…` | `OperationalError` | **0** | **2** |
| `<imię nazwisko> — kim jest, kontekst` | `OperationalError` | **0** | **2** |
| `molo promenada telefon wakacje rozmowa` | `OperationalError` | **0** | **1** |
| `<imię> z <miasto> — kim jest, kontekst` | `OperationalError` | **0** | **1** |

Quoting alone would have fixed the exception and restored nothing. OR is also the default for free-text input in [Lucene](https://lucene.apache.org/core/9_5_0/queryparser/org/apache/lucene/queryparser/flexible/standard/StandardQueryParser.html), [Elasticsearch](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/query/MatchQueryBuilder.java) and [Tantivy](https://docs.rs/tantivy/latest/tantivy/query/struct.QueryParser.html); the engines that default to AND ([Typesense](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/20), [Meilisearch](https://www.meilisearch.com/blog/matching-strategy)) pair it with automatic term relaxation. Bare AND with no relaxation is nobody's default.

Precision is left where it belongs: bm25 ranks documents matching more terms higher and [clamps IDF at zero](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html), so common words cannot invert a ranking, and the RRF fusion damps a weak candidate further.

**Tokens shorter than three characters are dropped.** A trigram index cannot represent them. They match nothing alone *and* zero an AND chain outright — `"Anna" AND "z" AND "Krakowa"` returns nothing where `"Anna" AND "Krakowa"` returns a row. Polish prose is full of them.

## Tests

`1121 passed`. 24 new, in `tests/repositories/test_chunk_search.py`:

- parametrised expression-building, incl. the comma case, `3-room-flat` (which produced `no such column: pokojowe`), bare `NOT`, unbalanced quote, parens, colon, Polish diacritics, sub-trigram tokens, and three empty-result inputs
- every query from a real `search_fts_failed` warning now returns a list rather than raising
- punctuation around a real term does not stop it matching
- an OR-recoverable prose query returns the row that AND would have dropped

`ruff` clean, `ty` unchanged from baseline (9 pre-existing, none in touched code).

## Not in this PR

The tokenizer question and recall tuning — measurement harness, Polish stopwords, suffix truncation, bm25 column weights, `remove_diacritics` — are a follow-up issue.

session: ship-ios-app

The first `bootstrap` run failed on `ASC_KEY_P8 has no BEGIN line`. The validator did its job — caught it in seconds rather than twenty minutes in — but bouncing the key back for a re-paste is the wrong response when the key is almost certainly fine and only differently shaped.

Apple hands out a PEM file, and every CI guide gives different advice about getting it into a secret, so the same key legitimately arrives four ways. All four are losslessly recoverable.

`scripts/normalize-asc-key.sh` now converts any of them to PEM before fastlane sees it, and prints which shape it found.

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| Raw PEM | `PEM` |
| Base64 of whole file | `base64-encoded PEM (decoded)` |
| Bare base64 body, markers stripped | `bare base64 body (markers restored)` |
| PEM flattened to one line | `PEM (line breaks rebuilt)` |
| PEM with stray blank lines | `PEM` |
| Empty / junk / header-only | rejected, with byte and line counts |

Verified against a real P-256 key by comparing **public-key fingerprints**, not merely by parsing succeeding — all five recoverable shapes yield a byte-identical key. Rejection messages describe what was found without ever printing the secret.

One bug worth recording: `fold(1)` emits no trailing newline, so the first attempt at re-wrapping a bare body put `-----END PRIVATE KEY-----` on the same line as the last of the base64. It failed to parse, which is how it surfaced.

## Intent
Refresh the desktop grant for an outside-workspace file when its cached grant expires, so an open file remains readable after the grant lifetime elapses.

Closes #3031

## Non-goals

- No change to server-side grant permissions or lifetime.
- No outside-workspace grants for remote runtimes.
- No grant request for files already inside the active workspace.

## Affected surfaces

- `packages/ui/src/lib/outsideFileGrants.ts` now keys grant and in-flight request state by runtime and path, renews grants before expiry, and coalesces concurrent requests.
- `packages/ui/src/components/views/FilesView.tsx` uses the renewal path for outside-workspace reads.
- `packages/ui/src/lib/desktop.ts` preserves the existing Electron bridge contract.
- Web, VS Code, hosted mobile, and remote runtimes do not mint local desktop grants.

## Repository guidance

| Guidance | Why it applies | How the change complies |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | Shared UI, runtime switching, and desktop boundary rules apply. | The change stays in shared UI and reuses the existing privileged Electron bridge without exposing new capabilities. |
| `openchamber-change-discipline` | The fix changes an external capability cache and failure behavior. | State is scoped by runtime and path, concurrent refreshes are coalesced, and the focused regression test covers expiry and switching. |
| `ui-api-decoupling` | The feature crosses the shared UI and runtime bridge boundary. | Runtime identity is resolved at call time, remote runtimes remain unsupported for local grants, and the existing bridge owns the native operation. |
| `desktop-shell` and `packages/electron/README.md` | Electron owns local filesystem authorization. | No renderer privilege was added; the existing `grantFileAccess` IPC path remains the only native grant entry point. |

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `bun test src/lib/outsideFileGrants.test.ts` | 1 pass |
| `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` | Pass |

## Visual evidence

No rendered UI changes. Grant renewal is transparent to the file editor and only changes the authorization data attached to outside-workspace file reads.

## Risks and failure behavior

- Grants are refreshed only for the local desktop runtime and the requested canonical path.
- Concurrent requests for the same runtime and path share one renewal request.
- Runtime switching invalidates a pending local result instead of reusing it for a remote runtime.
- Files inside the workspace keep the existing grant-free path.

## Summary
رفع نهایی مشکل «توی ساب وایرگارد دو سرور بود، فقط یکی نشون داده می‌شد».

با تست مستقیم لینک واقعی کاربر (`curl -A "v2rayNG/1.8.18" ".../sub/TOKEN"`) مشخص شد پنل asan-ps هر سرور رو با پارامتر `?host=N` روی همون لینک می‌ده:
- بدون پارامتر (یا `?host=1`) → سرور آلمان
- `?host=2` → سرور ترکیه
- `?host=3` → دوباره برمی‌گرده به همون آلمان (یعنی سرورها تموم شده)

یعنی پاسخ خامِ لینک، واقعاً و به‌طور مجزا فقط شامل یک سرور بود — فیکس‌های PR قبلی (پارس چند `[Peer]`/چند `[Interface]`) درست بودن ولی کافی نبودن، چون مشکل این بود که ربات اصلاً سراغ `?host=2` نمی‌رفت.

- روش تشخیص «تموم شدن سرورها» دقیقاً همون رفتاریه که پنل نشون داد: وقتی پاسخِ یک `host=N` با پاسخِ قبلی (یا پایه) عیناً یکی بشه، متوقف می‌شه.
- برای ساب‌های غیروایرگارد (اکثر کاربرها) هیچ درخواست اضافه‌ای زده نمی‌شه — فقط وقتی پاسخِ پایه واقعاً wg-quick باشه این منطق فعال می‌شه.
- حداکثر تا `host=12` امتحان می‌شه تا در بدترین حالت (پنلی که هیچ‌وقت واقعاً تکرار نمی‌شه) حلقه‌ی طولانی/کند نشه.
- هم روی مسیر اصلی استخراج (`extractSubscription`، استفاده‌شده در `sub_refresh.php` و کش) و هم مسیر موازیِ اولیه‌ی ارسال لینک/بروزرسانی (`fetchSubAndHeaderParallel` در `bot.php`) اعمال شده.

body:
## What

This companion improves the exact PR-head implementation of the new constructor-bridging feature (`ConstructorGenerator`, `NewTransformer.transform(IrMethod, ConstructorGenerator)`, `Dex2Asm.insertConstructors`) that handles Dalvik bytecode invoking `<init>` on an ancestor class further up the hierarchy than the direct superclass (illegal on the JVM, so dex2jar must synthesize bridging constructors on the intermediate classes and rewrite the skip-level call).

### Behavior lock (added tests, no production change)
- `ConstructorGeneratorTest` (dex-ir): 8 unit tests covering `add`/`isEmpty`/`enterClass`/`leaveClass`/`getCurrentParentClass`/`entries`, idempotent re-add, the mismatch exception (with old/new base), distinct-parameter-type entries, and `ConstructorPair` equals/hashCode.
- `Dex2AsmSuperConstructorBridgingTest` (dex-translator): 5 integration tests built from hand-written smali for a 3-level class hierarchy (`BaseBase` -> `Base` -> `Sub`) where `Sub`'s constructor calls `BaseBase`'s constructor directly. Runs the real `Dex2Asm.convertDex` pipeline end to end and asserts the synthesized bridging constructor, the rewritten skip-level call, ASM-verifiable output bytecode, the no-op case when every call already targets its direct superclass, and the exact `RuntimeException` message when an ancestor class cannot be resolved from the dex file.

Both test classes pass unmodified against the original PR-head production code (`behavior_baseline`) and again after the edits below (`behavior_candidate`), with the identical command.

### Cleanup
- Reverted 4 `System.err.println` workaround messages and the `NO_CODE_MASK` constant in `Dex2Asm.java` from an inconsistent trailing-operator/misaligned continuation format (incidental reformatting noise introduced by this PR) back to the file's existing leading-operator continuation convention. No functional change; identical resulting strings/values.

### Performance
- `Dex2Asm.insertConstructors` previously re-scanned the entire `DexClassNode` list with `stream().filter().findFirst()` for every ancestor-hierarchy step of every constructor-bridging entry (O(entries * hierarchyDepth * classCount)). Replaced with one `O(classCount)` name-to-class map (built with `putIfAbsent` to preserve `findFirst()`'s 'first match in list order' semantics, including for duplicate class names) and `O(1)` lookups thereafter. The exact exception type, message, and throw site for a missing ancestor class are preserved, proven by a dedicated characterization test.
- Measured on a synthetic worst-case workload (5000 classes in one inheritance chain, 300 bridging entries, 6-level walks): deterministic scan/lookup operations drop from 4,503,540 to 6,800; wall-clock median drops from ~25.8ms to ~0.20ms per call (7 timed batches each, same process).

### Modernization
Not applicable: the PR's changed files do not reference or pin any JDK/framework/plugin/dependency version.

## Verification
- `./gradlew :dex-ir:test :dex-translator:test --tests "*ConstructorGeneratorTest*" --tests "*Dex2AsmSuperConstructorBridgingTest*"` — pass, 13/13, identical before and after.
- `./gradlew clean :dex-ir:test :dex-translator:test :dex-tools:test :d2j-smali:test` — pass, 601/601 across all affected modules, 0 failures/errors.
- `./gradlew compileJava compileTestJava` — whole project compiles cleanly.

## Limitations
- The performance workload is synthetic and run outside the Gradle test JVM; real-world dex files with fewer bridging entries will show a smaller absolute wall-clock delta, though the algorithmic-complexity reduction and preserved exception behavior are proven directly against the production code path.
- No modernization opportunity was in scope for this PR's changed files.

author: vjovanov
body:
A run stops being live before it has recorded anything. `_run_locks` drops when `run_command` returns; the exit code is stamped a frame later, from the process exit path in `main` that is the only place the code is knowable. Both waits read the descriptor inside that gap:

- **`rhei attach --wait`** found no status on a run that had exited 0 and reported *"recorded no exit status, so it did not end on its own"* — failing exactly the CI step `<§>FS-rhei-run-headless.5.3` exists to pass. The JSON follower has the wider window of the two: it stops on the `run_finished` *record* plus one 150 ms drain, while the run is still writing its closing files. That is what went red on main — `attach_json_follows_a_run_it_did_not_start_and_exits_with_its_code` on the ubuntu runner of [the CI run for #83](https://github.com/vjovanov/rhei/actions/runs/32578420341), which passed on macOS and Windows and passes 6/6 locally.
- **`rhei stop --wait`** printed "It recorded no exit status." for a run that stamped a moment later. It only misprints — it never lied about an exit code — but it is the same read in the same gap.

## What changed

- The liveness loop in `wait_for_run_end` is extracted as `poll_until_run_ends`, and the JSON `--wait` path now calls it too: `run_finished` ends the run *loop*, not the process.
- `settled_end` re-reads the descriptor until the exit status lands, bounded by the existing `UNDECIDED_GRACE`. Long enough for an ordinary exit path, short enough that a run killed outright — which never stamps anything — is still reported as one that recorded nothing.
- `stop --wait` reuses it, which also filters its re-read by run id: a successor run's descriptor was never this run's result.

## Verification

- `the_wait_gives_a_late_exit_stamp_time_to_land` pins it: a stamp written three polls behind the wait. Reverting `settled_end` to a bare read fails it.
- `attach_wait_fails_for_a_run_that_recorded_no_exit_status` still fails a `SIGKILL`ed run, now after waiting out the grace.
- Both e2e tests pass 5/5 in a row; full workspace suite green (242 integration tests, was 241 passed + 1 failed).

author: os-zhuang
body:
Fixes #10945

`SchemaRegistry.resolveObjectKey` answered the short-name direction by walking **every** key of `objectContributors` and calling `parseFQN` on each. It is reached from seven call sites — `getObject` among them — so a kernel boot that registers N objects and resolves O(N) names did O(N²) string work.

The consequence was a silence, not a failure: boot got slower purely by an environment accumulating metadata, and once bootstrap outgrew the request waiter every request answered `kernel_warming` and the environment could never be opened, with no error anywhere. Refs objectstack-ai/cloud#1555.

## The change

`resolveObjectKey` now reads a short-name to FQN index `Map` maintained beside `objectContributors`.

Both containers are mutated only through two private choke points — `openObjectEntry` / `closeObjectEntry` — so they cannot drift apart by construction rather than by discipline. After this change `objectContributors.set` / `.delete` appear **only** inside those two methods, plus the paired `.clear()` in `reset()`. A future caller cannot add a contributor list and forget the index half.

Resolution is deliberately unchanged. The index array holds the same members in the same order as the list the scan built, so:

- an ambiguous short name still resolves to the **first** key registered under it,
- the ambiguity warning still fires and still names every match, in registry order,
- the legacy `ns__name` fallback and the explicit-full-key form still work.

## Behaviour change check (dispatch Zone 2, item 2)

The pre-fix scan returned `matches[0]`, i.e. first-registered-wins for an ambiguous bare name. An index could as easily have become last-writer-wins with nothing failing, so **that is not asserted by hand** — the pin re-implements the old loop as an oracle and asserts exact equivalence with it across **all 24 permutations** of a name set mixing a plain key, two legacy keys colliding on one short name, and a plain key colliding with a legacy one. Any future drift in which FQN wins reds there.

Net: no observable behaviour change, and the winner is now pinned rather than incidental.

## Verification

Three-leg ablation, with the mutation confirmed on disk at every leg by marker counts (not by an editor's exit code):

| leg | `objectKeysByShortName` occurrences | full-registry scan present | new pin file |
|---|---|---|---|
| fixed (HEAD) | 10 | 1 (`getAllObjects`, legitimate) | 12 passed |
| ablated (`registry.ts` from `origin/main`) | 0 | 2 (the scan is back) | **7 failed / 5 passed** |
| restored | 10 | 1 | 12 passed |

No rebuild is involved in that ablation and none is owed: the pin imports its subject as `./registry.js`, a same-package relative specifier, which never resolves through package `exports` and therefore never reads `dist/`. Independent proof that vitest read the edited source: the structural assertions compare `objectKeysByShortName`, a field that exists only in this diff and in no built artifact, and they pass.

Measured on this container, resolving one name per registered object (32,000 lookups over 4,000 objects vs 4,000 over 500):

| registry | big window | scaling ratio at 8x input |
|---|---|---|
| full-registry scan | 4,888 ms | **62.5x** (8x input, 64x cost — quadratic) |
| short-name index | 2.3 ms | **5.7x** |

The scaling pin asserts a ceiling of 30x, placed between the two measured populations (~2.7x above the worst healthy sample, ~2x below the ablated one) rather than close to either.

⚠️ The card's own evidence rig lives in `objectstack-ai/cloud` (`scripts/dev-local/bootstrap-curve.mjs`) and was **not** re-run — it is not reachable from this container. The numbers above are the local scaling substitute, which triage named as an acceptable alternative.

## Gates

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test` — 228 files / 4034 tests passed, at the final commit.
`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` — exit 0.

18 gate families green, derived from the actual changed paths with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (which named five the dispatch list did not: `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:type-check-debt`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:where-matcher`).

`check:type-check-debt` is the one family not run in its CI form — its `--re-measure` needs the whole ledgered dependency closure built. It is probed directly instead, which answers the only question this diff can move: tsc over objectql **with tests included** reports **0** diagnostics naming the new test file and **0** naming `registry.ts`. The probe's total (355) is the ledger's 354 plus exactly one `TS6059` rootDir diagnostic, which is an artifact of probing through the package's own `rootDir: src` config rather than the gate's generated project — the same one the ledger note records leaving when it went 355 to 354.

Repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's run. Locally it is narrowed to the two changed files and the narrowing is measured, not assumed: population taken from eslint's own config, file count read from `--format json` (2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings), and the config declares no `parserOptions.project` — type-aware linting is off, so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch.

author: bearyjd
body:
## Summary

B4 of the body-composition intake track — the most substantially reworked package in this whole effort. See `docs/prp/01-plan.md` §B4 and `docs/prp/00-design.md` §3.7 for the full design and the review history behind it.

## Background: why this got bigger than planned

The original dedup design was select-then-push-then-insert with no transaction. The devil's-advocate review demonstrated that two concurrent identical POSTs both see "no duplicate" and both write — the *exact* outcome dedup exists to prevent, reproducible with a single uvicorn worker via plain asyncio interleaving. A follow-up verification pass then caught that the first fix only covered the insert path, not the enrichment path (two composition-bearing POSTs matching one stored row would race the same way, one sub-case over), and that the proposed mitigation for holding the Garmin call inside the transaction ("give it a timeout") named a mechanism that doesn't exist in the pinned `garminconnect` version.

## Changes

- `vitalforge-weight/app.py` — the route now runs `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, `SELECT`s for a duplicate match (`±50g` weight, `60s` window via `julianday()`, not string comparison), and writes inside the same transaction — `INSERT` for a new weigh-in, or `UPDATE` the `NULL` composition columns for an enriching duplicate. The Garmin push happens **after** `COMMIT`, outside any lock, then a final `UPDATE` records the sync outcome. This reverses today's push-before-write ordering for *every* request, not just duplicates — a smaller, second behavior change riding along with the concurrency fix.
- `shared/database.py` — additive index on `weight_log(timestamp)` for the dedup lookup.
- `tests/test_dedup.py` — 12 tests: the three sub-cases (collapse/enrich/conflict), the ±50g boundary (including exactly 50g, which the original design left ambiguous), the 600s real-weigh-ins case, and the response shape contract.
- `tests/test_dedup_concurrency.py` — 5 tests, the ones that would have caught the original break: two concurrent identical POSTs → one row, one Garmin push; two concurrent enrichment POSTs → one update, one push; and a direct proof that a concurrent writer is never blocked by an in-flight Garmin push (confirms the lock genuinely doesn't span the network call).

## Testing

- `ruff check .` → clean
- `pytest -q` → 193 passed, 3 deselected (176 existing + 17 new)
- `pytest -q -m playwright` → 3 passed, unaffected (the weight-logging smoke test exercises the new route end-to-end)

## Related Issues

Depends on #6, #7, #8 (B1, B2, B3, all merged). Does not depend on the B3 live checkpoint (that gates B5, not this).

author: hf7y
body:
NO-DECISION: a drift witness that compared against a branch nobody ships, and two files still routing readers to a deleted script; both tested, both reversible

## E1 — the witness preferred the wrong branch

`bin/tests/carry-drift.test.sh` resolved its bashified side as
`for c in bashified origin/bashified` — **local first.**

A dev checkout's local `bashified` is whatever that clone last fetched, and
`bashified` is a **machine-cut branch**. On 2026-08-22 this clone's copy was not
merely 8 commits stale, it had **diverged** — `git fetch origin bashified:bashified`
was rejected non-fast-forward — and the suite reported **4 drifts against a
branch nobody ships**.

The false-red is the cheap direction. The inverse — a stale local branch
reporting **clean** while the shipped branch has drifted — is this repo's
recurring genre and is the one that costs something.

It now fetches `origin/bashified` and prefers it, falls back to a local branch
only when no remote ref resolves at all, and **says so on the line** when it
does.

One consequence worth knowing: a carry must now be **pushed** to be seen. This
PR demonstrates both halves — 16/2 with the carry committed but unpushed, 18/0
once pushed. CI, which has no local branch, was always in the pushed case.

## E3 — two dangling references #511 left behind

`bin/claim-drift.sh` was deleted 2026-08-22 and two surviving files still sent a
reader to it:

- **`.claude/commands/cloture.md`** told an agent to *run* `claim-drift --convention`
  and `claim-drift <n>` — a brief instructing an agent to execute a command that
  does not exist.
- **`bin/lib/body-grammar.sh:3`** named it as one of its two readers.

Both now point at the grammar itself and at `gh-sign`, which is what actually
enforces it at the write.

`cloture.md`'s replacement names the **real gap** rather than asserting a
permanent absence — *"`gh-sign` refuses a bad body AT THE WRITE; a body edited
afterward is not re-read by anything, so read it yourself."* That stays true
whether or not a post-write checker is ever added, which the first draft
("there is no after-the-fact checker") would not have.

## The carry rides this push

`commands/cloture.md` and `bin/lib/body-grammar.sh` are both rows in
`bin/lib/carries.tsv`, so the `bashified` carry is in the same push, not a later
one (#526 / scheduler#222). Without it this suite is **16/2** — which is the
guard doing its job, and is shown above.

## Verified

- `bash bin/tests/carry-drift.test.sh` — 18 passed, 0 failed (16/2 without the carry)
- `bash bin/shellcheck-lint.sh` — 90 files, 9 baselined, no new findings
- `bash bin/run-suites.sh bin/tests/*.test.sh` — 36 suites green

<!-- DEFERRED -->
- none
<!-- /DEFERRED -->

<!-- DELIVERS -->
- none
<!-- /DELIVERS -->

Docs only — records your two decisions and unblocks the last two Phase 8 tickets.

**Q-0040 — reactivation.** *Ownership of the deletion decides who may undo it.* A maker restores a product **they** deleted; an admin-deleted product is **admin-only** and the maker is told why (a platform removal is a moderation decision, not self-service).
- No new column needed: `Auditable.DeactivatedBy` already stamps the acting user on every soft delete, so "who deleted this" is a comparison, not a migration.
- The **category** half of your answer (maker proposes, admin approves, invisible until approved) is **already ticketed as T-0163** — delegated there rather than duplicated.

**Q-0041 — order escape hatches.** Your answer today supplied the **time bound**; your confirmed decision of **2026-06-03** (recorded in `sprint-7.md`) had already supplied the **roles**. They compose exactly, so nothing is left to guess:

| Actor | From | Window | Money |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer | `PendingPayment` only | — | nothing moved, no refund |
| Maker ("refuses") | `Paid` only | **2 days from `PaidAt`** | refund via existing `RefundOrder` |
| Admin | any state | — | unchanged (T-0107) |

- **Explicitly not granted:** customer cancellation of a *paid* order — on made-to-order goods that returns money after production may have started. Recorded as a deliberate exclusion, not an oversight.
- The 2-day window lands in `CountryConfiguration`, not a hard-coded constant (ADR 0004), so it's tunable without a deploy.
- **No state-machine change:** `Order.Cancel` already accepts `PendingPayment | Paid | Accepted` — both tickets are command layer + refund wiring + UI.

Both tickets are now `ready` with full Given/When/Then AC, including the negative paths (past-window refusal with a pinned `IClock`, cross-tenant not-found, re-run idempotency with no second refund).

author: jmgilman
body:
Adopts the reusable release unit in `meigma/release`, pinned to
`0dee66ff6c4cc7e28d7bb65e97a37d701e0eff4a` (v0.1.17), and retires this
repository's bespoke release and attestation workflows.

## What a release produces after this change

One canonical set of binaries feeds every channel:

- GitHub Release: 6 archives (darwin/linux `tar.gz`, windows `zip`; amd64 and arm64), signed and notarized macOS binaries, signed DEB/RPM/APK for linux amd64 and arm64, one SPDX SBOM per archive and package, `checksums.txt` plus a keyless Cosign bundle.
- `ghcr.io/componere/incusos-builder` for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, digest-pinned, with provenance and per-platform SBOM attestations.
- A cask pull request against `componere/homebrew-tap`.
- A manifest pull request against `componere/scoop-bucket`.
- A native package publication request to `componere/pkgs`, which publishes to `https://pkgs.componere.dev`.

## Windows support

`internal/update` did not compile for Windows: `statfsFree` used
`golang.org/x/sys/unix`, which has no `Statfs` there. The release contract
requires Windows `amd64` and `arm64` binaries, so free space now has a
platform-split implementation — `space_unix.go` keeps the statfs path and
`space_windows.go` uses `GetDiskFreeSpaceEx`, whose quota-adjusted result needs
no block arithmetic. All six targets compile and `internal/update` tests pass.

## melange no longer compiles anything

`release-cli image build` stages the GoReleaser binary as `application` and
writes the release version into a vars file, so the image and the release
assets are the same bytes. The `go/build` pipeline is gone; reintroducing it
would produce a second, unattested binary. `security-scan.yml` and the
`image-local` mise task were updated to stage a binary the same way.

Two schema corrections fell out of this: melange rejects `vendor`, `homepage`,
and `maintainer` under `package:`, and `apko.yaml` must not hardcode
`org.opencontainers.image.version` because the image verifier compares the
injected version and revision against the release being built.

## Verification performed before opening this PR

- All six `GOOS`/`GOARCH` targets build; `internal/update` tests pass; lint and format are clean.
- `goreleaser check` validates the config.
- A full offline stage run produced 6 archives, 6 native packages, 12 SBOMs, `checksums.txt`, the cask, and the Scoop manifest.
- Native signing was exercised with throwaway keys in the exact formats the release uses. The APK signature segment is named `.SIGN.RSA.incusos-builder-apk-001.rsa.pub`, matching `apk_key.published` in the `componere/pkgs` policy, and the RPM carries an RSA signature.
- `mise run image-local` built the image from the rewritten melange and apko configs. `docker run --rm incusos-builder:dev --version` printed the banner, and `docker inspect` reported user `65532` and entrypoint `/usr/bin/incusos-builder` — the two values the image verifier requires.

## Publication is disabled in this commit

All five publish inputs are `false`. This merge is the rehearsal configuration:
the first tag exercises the complete build and leaves a draft. Publication is
enabled in a separate reviewed commit.

author: arasz
body:
@dotnet-engineer

## Root cause

`ModelDownloadPlanner.PoolingDecision` (`src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Embedding/Download/ModelDownloadPlanner.cs:345-366`)
returns from the `1_Pooling/config.json` branch before it ever consults the `OnnxGraphProbe?`
parameter. For `BAAI/bge-m3` the graph publishes `token_embeddings` (rank 3, real token-level) AND
a distinct `sentence_embedding` output (rank 2, already pooled) beside `1_Pooling/config.json`'s
CLS flags — the planner trusts the flags and writes `pooling.mode: cls`. It only matches the
checked-in oracle (`tests/AiRaccoon.Tests/Resources/ManifestFixtures/bge-m3.full.json`, which
asserts `model-output`) because CLS happens to reproduce bge-m3's own baked pooled vector — a
model whose baked output is not CLS-pooled would get a silently wrong manifest.

This is distinct from #470/#475 (merged): that fix covers a graph whose **sole** output is
already rank-2-pooled, using the real ONNX Runtime rank (`IOnnxSmokeTester.Verify` /
`OnnxOutputRanks`) measured **after** download. #459 is the bge-m3 shape — a **second**,
distinctly-named pooled output beside a real rank-3 token-level one — and #475 states rank-3
graphs are left untouched, so this case was still open.

## The fix

`PoolingDecision`'s `1_Pooling/config.json` branch now also checks whether the graph probe
(`probe.OutputNames`) already exposes a second, distinctly-named pooled output — the exact same
name-based heuristic (`SelectEmbeddingOutput`/`SelectTokenEmbeddingsOutput`) the pre-existing D11
placeholder branch (no `1_Pooling` present) already used. When it does, the plan returns
`pooling.mode: model-output` with provenance `onnx-graph` (matching #475's vocabulary) instead of
the sentence-transformers flags. `EmbeddingOutput`/`TokenEmbeddingsOutput` were already populated
from the graph's output names independent of pooling mode, so no further change was needed there.
The sentence-transformers flags stay the fallback when the graph shows no second pooled output —
pinned by a dedicated negative-control test.

This deliberately reuses the existing pre-download protobuf probe (`OnnxGraphProbe`, names only)
rather than adding a second rank-determination mechanism alongside #475's ORT-based one — the two
signals (name-based at plan time, rank-based post-download via `IOnnxSmokeTester`) serve different
moments in the download pipeline and neither needed touching to close this gap.

## RED → GREEN

```
Pooling_GraphBakedOutput_OutranksSentenceTransformersFlags
  RED   plan.PoolingMode should be PoolingMode.ModelOutput but was PoolingMode.Cls
PoolingLayoutInRepo_DoesNotShadowTheModelConfig
  RED   result.Plan.PoolingMode should be PoolingMode.ModelOutput but was PoolingMode.Cls
```

Fix commit follows this draft.

## Files

- `src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Embedding/Download/ModelDownloadPlanner.cs`
- `tests/AiRaccoon.Tests/Unit/Embedding/Download/ModelDownloadPlannerTests.cs`
- `tests/AiRaccoon.Tests/Unit/Embedding/Download/ModelDownloadServiceTests.cs` (a pre-existing
  integration-level test pinned the buggy behaviour at the `ModelDownloadService` level via the
  fake bge-m3 repo's default two-output graph; its assertions are corrected alongside the fix)

Closes #459

## Description

Moves the concurrent SSE send test away from Catch2 assertions inside scheduler-worker coroutines. The server, sender, and reader coroutines now return structured observations and captured exceptions; the test thread performs assertions after requesting cleanup, shutting down the scheduler, and confirming joinable root frames are destroyed.

author: david-driscoll
body:
Drains `secrets/shared/*` — 146 flat paths — into a layout that says where each credential is used. Decisions are recorded per-path in [`docs/openbao-shared-secrets-reorg.md`](docs/openbao-shared-secrets-reorg.md) and encoded in [`scripts/bao-reorg/plan.ts`](scripts/bao-reorg/plan.ts).

```
clusters/<key>/apps/<app>/<leaf>   scoped to one site
third-party-tokens/<vendor>/<x>    credentials someone else issues
apps/<app>/<x>                     infrastructure this repo operates
docker/apps/<app>/<x>              things every Dockge host runs
retired/<slug>                     parked, pending deletion
```

`shared/` was never meant to be flat — the vault repo's `PLAN.md` §A specifies this grouping. What shipped was `op-to-bao`'s **default** rule, `shared/<slug>`, because `mapping.yaml` was reviewed for path collisions rather than for grouping. This is that layout, finished.

## ⚠️ Do not merge yet — the data has not moved

`bao-reorg --verify` currently reports **all 162 destinations missing**. Every consumer in this diff points at a path that does not exist. The copy runs first:

| | |
|---|---|
| 1 | Widen the `eso-*` policies — **phase 3 only**, root ceremony |
| 2 | `bao-reorg --phase N --apply --copy` — writes destinations, **keeps sources** |
| 3 | Merge this |
| 4 | Reconcile; every ExternalSecret `SecretSynced` |
| 5 | `bao-reorg --phase N --apply` — reaps the sources |

Step 2 must use `--copy`. A move destroys the source the moment it verifies, and the window between that and the merge is a live cluster reconciling manifests that still name the old path.

Step 5 is not optional either: two paths holding one credential is the drift this removes, and nothing tells you which one a rotation updated.

## Phase 3 needs a root ceremony

`eso-<cluster>` grants `secrets/data/shared/*` and `secrets/data/clusters/*` and nothing else. A trailing `*` is a prefix glob spanning `/`, so everything under `clusters/` is already in policy — that is phases 2 and 4. Phase 3 introduces `third-party-tokens/`, `apps/` and `docker/`, which **no ESO policy grants**.

Running it early does not fail at write time — the `pulumi` AppRole holds `secrets/*` and writes happily. It fails an hour later as ~30 ExternalSecrets flip to `SecretSyncedError`, with nothing in the diff to point at. So `--phase 3` refuses without `--policies-widened`; `--preflight` prints the HCL for the vault repo's `equestria-init.sh`.

If you would rather skip the ceremony entirely, nesting these as `shared/third-party-tokens/…` costs nothing and needs no policy change.

## What reading the live server changed

Of 146 paths, only **69 are referenced anywhere in this repo**. The other 77 are all still at version 1 with `updated_time` 2026-08-08 — written once by `op-to-bao --apply`, never read since: retired apps (lldap, zitadel, seafile, harbor, homarr, outline, vikunja, warpgate…), SGC-era infrastructure, and one path with zero data fields.

Draining `shared/` is mostly a deletion job. 60 go to `retired/` (parking is one `bao-move` from undo; a destroy is not), 17 are destroyed outright.

## Two amendments to the reviewed worksheet

**`shared/eris-ssh-key` was marked RETIRE and is live.** The retirement rested on "its only consumer left with SGC". It did not — namespace `stargate-command` runs *on equestria*; the workloads were folded in and only the name survived. `home-assistant-ssh` is SecretSynced and mounted at `helmrelease.yaml:212`. Now a move. Every other retirement was checked the same way and holds.

**The two GitHub tokens were right as called.** `stacks/vault/KubernetesGithubAppToken.ts` mints `kube-system/github-token` from the App and emberstack reflects it everywhere. Dynacat takes it as a `secretKeyRef` env var, the nine Pulumi Stack CRs read `github-token`/`token` directly, and `pulumi-operator-github` is deleted. A static PAT and a GitHub App were two credentials for the same access, and only one of them expires on its own.

## Notable

- **`resolveBaoPath` no longer derives `shared/<slug>` from a 1Password title.** That rule now yields a well-formed path that cannot exist, failing at read time rather than at the call site. `TITLE_PATHS` is exhaustive; an unlisted title is an error naming itself.
- **`media-management-secrets`** was 19 fields read by six ExternalSecrets across two namespaces. Split per app, with the field renamed `<app>_apikey` → `apikey` — the path already says which app. `spike-management-credentials` is reassembled from the pieces so the five `*arr` `secretKeyRef`s did not have to move in the same change.
- **`scripts/bao-reorg/run.sh`** exists because `mise run vals-run` deadlocks mid-migration: it resolves every `ref+` in the environment in one pass, and `.config/mise.toml` names three of the moving paths. It is how you get credentials to run the migration, and the migration is what creates the paths it wants. `run.sh` resolves only the AppRole, from SOPS.
- **`docker/alpha-site/prometheus-exporters` removed** (its `adguard-home` credential retires with it). Deleting a Dockge stack directory does not stop the container — needs `ssh alpha-site 'docker rm -f adguard-exporter'` after the Pulumi run.
- **`stargate-command/secrets/media-management.yaml` deleted** — no manifest and no pod in that namespace references the Secret it produced.
- Two dead dynacat extracts dropped (celestia/luna PBS backup users; the rewritten keys were never templated).

## Second commit: `scripts/op-to-bao/` deleted

Independent of the above, and separable. `ee5238c4` removed that script's `mapping.ts`, `mapping.test.ts` and 5350-line `mapping.yaml` after the migration finished, but left four files behind — and **both survivors that contain code import the deleted module**, so neither can run. `bao.ts`'s own comment says it "gets deleted with the rest of op-to-bao after Phase 11", and Phase 11 has happened.

Its `baoSlug`/`oidcBaoPath`/`pbsBaoPath`/`dockgeBaoPath` assertions move to `components/bao.test.ts`, beside what they test, extended to cover `dockgeBaoPath` which had none. The parity half died with `mapping.ts` — there is no second implementation left to diverge from.

One gap recorded rather than hidden: `BaoClient`'s wire behaviour was covered by stub-server tests in `mapping.test.ts` and is now covered nowhere.

## Verification

- `hk check --all` green — `flate` renders 355 Flux resources, plus `eso-values-lint`, `yamllint`, `shellcheck`, `typos`, `biome`
- 92/92 tests pass
- Typecheck identical to `main` (8 pre-existing errors, none introduced)
- All four phases dry-run clean against live OpenBao: phase 1 **81 ok**, phase 2 **30 ok**, phase 3 **34 ok**, phase 4 **17 fields, 0 failed**
- 130 references rewritten across 74 files, all from `plan.ts`

> *"i love the onboarding just center the questions one by one"*

The list rendered **all three steps at once**. Two of them were always things the reader couldn''t act on yet — and a step you can''t do is a step you have to read past to find the one you can. Fixes the stale-image bug: a screenshot re-cropped over its own filename kept
rendering at its original size, and reopening the document did not clear it.

## Cause

`resolve_image_source` handed the editor an `ImageSource::Resource(Resource::Path(..))`
for every local image. gpui resolves that through the **app-level** asset cache
(`App::loading_assets`), which is keyed on a hash of the path and has no eviction
path at all — `remove_asset` is the only way out, and nothing in the markdown path
ever called it. So the bitmap decoded on first render was served for the life of the
process, and reopening the document could not help because the cache outlives the
document. Renaming the file worked around it only because a new path is a new key.

## Fix

Each editor now owns a `RetainAllImageCache`, and local images resolve to an
`ImageSource::Custom` that reads through it. Owning the cache is what makes
eviction possible: when the project reports a changed image file, live preview
drops that path from the cache and notifies, and the next draw re-decodes it.
`RetainAllImageCache::remove` also releases the sprite-atlas entry, which the
app-level cache has no way to do, and the cache dies with the editor — so closing
a document now frees every image it decoded, where before they were retained for
the whole session.

Routing through `resolve_image_source` rather than through the `img` element means
both paths are covered: standalone image widgets and `![[embeds]]`, and images the
`MarkdownElement` renderer resolves inside other blocks.

## Not covered

- Images outside any worktree get no filesystem events, so they still go stale.
- A destination spelled with `..` resolves to a path that will not string-match the
  worktree's own absolute path, so eviction misses it. Normalizing lexically would
  fix that but changes meaning under symlinked directories, so I left it alone
  rather than trade a working case for an edge case.

## Tests

`test_rewriting_an_image_in_place_reloads_it` draws a real image through the resolved
source, rewrites the file at different dimensions, and asserts the drawn bitmap is
**still** the old one until the path is evicted — so it reproduces the bug first and
then pins the fix, rather than passing vacuously. `cargo nextest run -p markdown_live_preview`
is 46/46; `cargo check -p zed` builds.

Release Notes:

- Fixed a markdown image continuing to render its old version after the file was overwritten in place

author: cipher813
body:
## What & why

`alpha-engine-config-I7309` gates re-enabling `pit_parity` on the weekly SF behind two recorded blockers. This PR addresses both — and **re-measures the second one, which was mis-attributed**.

### Blocker 2 — "the walk-forward pass places ZERO orders". It does not.

I7309 records the smoke slice's `pit_status: no_orders` as a property of the walk-forward pass. Measured against S3 instead:

- `backtest/2026-07-31/pit_parity.json` carries the walk-forward child's own log tail at the moment it was killed — `Simulation: 1995/1995 dates (100% coverage), 2489 orders`, then `Sweep combo 5/60 done in 272.5s`.
- `backtest/2026-08-07/pit_parity.json` carries live `ORDER REDUCE SCHW/BLDR/USB/ARE/CYTK` lines from the same pass.

The production walk-forward pass trades. What produced zero orders is the **`smoke-pit-parity` fixture**, and the cause is arithmetic, not sizing:

| | value |
|---|---|
| `smoke-pit-parity` → `predictor_backtest.max_trading_days` | 60 |
| canonical `_WF_DEFAULTS["min_train"]` | 504 |
| trading dates needed before `build_walk_forward_folds` emits its first fold | **514** |

`build_walk_forward_folds` initialises `fold_start_idx = min_train` and loops `while fold_start_idx < n`, so on a 60-date axis the body never executes. Zero folds → `predictions_by_date == {}` → `build_signals_by_date` iterates an empty date list → the simulation loop runs zero dates → `no_orders`, whose note read *"No ENTER signals passed risk rules during the simulation period"*. Verified by construction: `min_trading_dates_for_one_fold(**_WF_DEFAULTS) == 514`; a 2500-date axis (production) builds 95 folds.

Every step was silent. The one guard that would have spoken —

```python
if folds and n_test_dates_scored == 0:      # gated on `folds`
    logger.error("... ZERO test dates scored ...")
```

— cannot fire when the fold list is *empty*, which is precisely the case. The look-ahead pass runs `walk_forward=False`, a single pass over all dates, which is why `current_status: ok` on the identical fixture. That asymmetry was read as a sizing asymmetry for three weeks.

**Fixes:**

1. `run_walk_forward_inference` **raises** on zero folds, naming the axis it got, the fold parameters, and the axis length required — the last derived from the builder itself (`synthetic/pit_folds.min_trading_dates_for_one_fold`) so it cannot drift from the scheme it describes.
2. `smoke-pit-parity` gains `predictor_backtest.walk_forward_params` (`test_window 5 / min_train 10 / purge 2 / embargo 1`) scaled to its own 30–60-day slice, so it builds ≥1 fold and genuinely exercises the PIT path. Not a weakening: `purge` still separates train-end from test-start, and this path scores with the **deterministic momentum baseline** (no booster is refit), so `min_train` here governs only how much un-scored warm-up is skipped.
3. `_run_simulation_loop` returns a new `no_dates` status when `dates_expected == 0`, instead of borrowing `no_orders`'s sentence about the risk rules. `no_orders` is unchanged and still tolerated in production (config#7252); an empty *input* just stops being reported in the vocabulary of the *strategy*. `reporter._section_predictor_backtest` renders it as "Not measured".

`tests/test_predictor_backtest_walk_forward.py::test_no_folds_yields_empty_predictions` asserted the opposite premise — *"folds==0 is a benign short-history case, not a failure"*. That codified belief is what let the failure hide, so it is replaced (`test_no_folds_aborts_the_pass`) with the reasoning recorded in the docstring.

### Blocker 1 — two asymptotically different workloads under one ceiling

The issue's own framing is the answer. Under the single `_PIT_PARITY_PASS_TIMEOUT = 2700` the look-ahead pass runs ONE simulation (measured 922 s), while the walk-forward pass with `pit_parity_sweep` set runs one full simulation **per combo** — 60 × 272.5 s ≈ 16,350 s.

**Decision: bound the sweep, do not raise the ceiling.** The pass already carries a deadline (`_pass_deadline_epoch`, injected by `_run_predictor_pass_isolated`), and its *other* long loop — the walk-forward fold loop — has been self-deadlining since config#7199. The sweep combo loop was the one still unbounded. `analysis/param_sweep._run_combos` now asks the same question before each combo (`remaining − reserve ≥ p90(observed combos)`), stops early, and returns the combos it finished as a labelled PARTIAL. With both loops self-deadlining the 2700 s ceiling becomes a true backstop rather than the mechanism, and the pass always publishes something.

**What I would need to measure to know the bound is right** — and therefore what the change emits into `sweep_df.attrs`:

- `combo_p90_s` — the per-combo cost this run actually observed. It is what the *next* run's affordability arithmetic uses, and it is the number that decides whether the seeded `SWEEP_FIRST_COMBO_ESTIMATE_S = 300` (the measured 2026-07-31 cost, rounded up) is still right.
- `n_combos_run` / `n_combos_planned` / `n_combos_skipped_for_budget` / `sweep_budget_stopped` — the coverage actually achieved.

A pass that is *persistently* short needs a bigger **budget**, not a bigger ceiling — and that is only decidable once both numbers reach the artifact instead of a log tail. Two consecutive runs with `sweep_budget_stopped: true` is the trigger to raise the budget or cut the grid; a single stop is the mechanism working. Raising the ceiling first would make an observational stage the longest thing in the weekly pipeline and would still be a guess.

`sweep`'s 50 %-completion gate is corrected in the same change: it computed `n_total − n_failed`, an identity that only held while every planned combo produced a row. A truncated sweep would otherwise have reported a short run as fully successful.

### Shared primitive, not a copy

`deadline_budget.py` lifts the config#7199 self-deadlining primitive (`deadline_remaining_s` / `safe_remaining` / `p90` / `next_unit_affordable`) out of `synthetic/predictor_backtest.py` on its **second in-repo adoption**, per `policy-shared-code`. `predictor_backtest`'s `_deadline_remaining_s` / `_safe_remaining` / `_p90` / `_next_fold_affordable` are now thin bindings of it to the `[walk_forward]` tag and constants — same surface, same tests, one implementation. It stays repo-local rather than going to `nousergon-lib`; lift it there on the first adoption outside this repo.

## SOTA choice and delta

- **Fail loud on the degeneracy rather than special-casing the fixture.** The fixture fix alone would have made the smoke green while leaving the class — any future short axis — silent. The raise is the part that survives the class; the fixture change is what keeps it green today. No delta.
- **Bound the workload rather than the wall.** Self-deadlining loops that publish PARTIAL are the shape config#7199 already established here; a raised ceiling is the expedient alternative and is not taken. **Delta:** a budget-stopped sweep covers fewer combos, so the CSCV PBO it feeds rests on a smaller combo set. That is a labelled, measured reduction in coverage instead of an unlabelled total loss, and the labels are what make the budget correctable.
- **`min_trading_dates_for_one_fold` calls the builder rather than re-deriving its index arithmetic.** A hardcoded 514 would drift the first time the fold scheme changes. No delta.

## Out of scope, and what remains on I7309

- **`alpha-engine-config-I7222` needs no further code.** Its root cause (both `replay_for_dates` paths passed `atr_by_ticker=None`, collapsing `atr_map` to `{}` so the first ENTER aborted — `EOG`/`GD` were merely alphabetically unlucky) was fixed by `crucible-backtester#668`, merged 2026-08-14; the per-ticker ATR-coverage bounding and its structural guards are on `main` (`tests/test_parity_replay_atr_contract.py`). Its detector also already exists and is working — the evaluator's backtester tile grades `vectorized_vs_consolidated_parity` RED whenever `parity_report.json` is not `data_state: ok`, which

author: nikomann1
body:
End-to-end skeleton of the trip photo picker, built to validate the save-to-Photos path on a real iPhone before any scoring work starts. **Scoring is a deliberate placeholder** — `lib/scoring.ts` returns a random ~10% subset.

Merging this puts the app on `main` so Vercel can deploy it (set **Root Directory** to `photo-picker` on import).

## What is here

- **Upload screen** — multi-file image input, tested with 20–30 photos.
- **Placeholder selection** — `lib/scoring.ts` splits per-photo scoring from selection, so real blur/duplicate/aesthetic logic can replace `scorePhoto` without touching the route or the UI.
- **Review screen** — grid of the selected photos.
- **Save to Photos** — `navigator.share` with a `files` array, plus download-attribute anchor links as a fallback.
- **Server upload path** — `POST /api/upload` stores photos in a per-session temp directory with a `meta.json` alongside; `/api/photos/...` serves them back. Off by default behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_TO_SERVER=1` (see below).

## Two decisions worth reviewing

**Photos stay in the browser.** The picked `File` objects go into IndexedDB, the grid renders them from object URLs, and the share hands those same `File` objects to `navigator.share`. This started as a deployability fix — server-side temp storage assumes a persistent filesystem, which serverless hosting does not provide, so batched uploads and later image fetches could land on different instances — but it is also the better shape for this milestone: Safari requires `navigator.share()` to be called while the user gesture is still live, and with the files already in hand there is nothing to await before the call. Milestone 2 decides whether real scoring runs server-side (which needs the pixels up there) or in-browser via WASM; the server path is kept working behind a flag so both doors stay open.

**`allowedDevOrigins` in `next.config.ts`.** The Next dev server returns 403 for `/_next/*` requests from non-allowlisted hosts. Loading the app from a phone is exactly that case, and the failure is silent-looking: the HTML arrives, every JS chunk 403s, the page never hydrates, and the file picker just does nothing. The config allowlists private IP ranges, `*.local`, the machine's detected addresses, and common tunnel hostnames.

## Verification

Driven against a production build in a mobile-emulated browser, over both loopback and LAN origins:

- 22 photos in, 2 selected, thumbnails render from blob URLs
- `navigator.share` receives real `image/jpeg` `File` objects with correct names and byte sizes
- `share()` confirmed to run synchronously inside the click task — the iOS constraint above
- reloading `/review` restores the batch from IndexedDB
- download fallback renders when Web Share with files is unavailable
- missing and unknown sessions handled
- server path re-checked with the flag on: 5 batched POSTs per upload, stored and scored

Build and typecheck are clean.

**Not verified:** real iOS Safari and the actual share sheet — no device available in the session, so the share call was exercised against a stub. Whether iOS offers "Save N Images" for a multi-file share is what the on-device test answers.

## Not in scope yet

Real scoring, HEIC handling, auth, and 500-photo batches (20–30 is the tested range).

body:
## Summary

Backlog of 11 requested features/fixes for the Secure Signal Admin dashboard, built via brainstorming-driven decomposition.

**New features**
- Admin invite-user flow (`inviteUserByEmail` + dialog on Users page)
- Google sign-in on login/signup
- Per-incident staff↔rider messaging (new `incident_messages` table + RLS + realtime chat panel on the monitor page)
- AI chatbot widget (Anthropic Claude, site-wide, bottom-right) — degrades gracefully with a clear message until `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set
- Password field eye-icon show/hide toggle

**Real bugs found and fixed while implementing the above**
- `middleware.ts` never listed `/` as a public route, so anonymous visitors were bounced to `/login` before ever seeing the marketing page — this is why "How It Works" / "Features" looked broken; they were simply unreachable.
- FCM ping/stop endpoints queried an empty `notifications` table instead of `devices.fcm_id`, which is where the mobile app actually writes tokens. Also fixed a `text` vs `uuid` `device_id` mismatch in the stop endpoint. (Verified live against a real device — token lookup now succeeds; actual delivery is still blocked by a Firebase-project/sender-ID mismatch between this backend and the mobile app's build, which needs a Firebase-console fix outside this repo.)
- The authenticated dashboard shell was a fixed `240px + 1fr` CSS grid with no mobile breakpoint, breaking every authenticated page on small screens. Rebuilt as a slide-in drawer (`AuthedShell`).
- CSP (from an earlier hardening pass) was blocking legitimate Supabase Storage profile photos — added to `img-src`.

## Test plan
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `next build` clean, zero warnings
- [x] Verified live in-browser: eye-icon toggle, Google OAuth button reaches provider redirect, FCM token lookup against a real device, messaging send/realtime/reload round-trip, chatbot graceful degradation, mobile drawer open/close with no horizontal overflow across incidents/users/monitor pages, `/` now returns 200 anonymously while `/admin/*` stays protected
- [ ] Manual: confirm password-reset email delivery (Supabase dashboard SMTP/redirect config, not verifiable from this repo)
- [ ] Manual: align Firebase project between mobile app and this backend's service account for actual push delivery

Four badges under the tagline, plus a line in the install section pointing at the project page.

```
[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/listenr?logo=pypi&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/listenr/)
[![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/listenr?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/listenr/)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/pypi/l/listenr)](https://github.com/Rebreda/listenr/blob/main/LICENSE)
[![Tests](https://github.com/Rebreda/listenr/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Rebreda/listenr/actions/workflows/tests.yml)
```

Version, Pythons and license are read live from PyPI, so they stay right on their own instead of going stale the next time you tag. The tests badge points at the workflow that now gates the release.

The install section also gains a short note that it is on PyPI, needs 3.11+, and that fine-tuning and the importers are behind extras. That is the first question someone has after seeing a 20-package core install.

## Verified

All four resolve with real content:

| Badge | Renders |
|---|---|
| PyPI | `pypi: v0.1.0` |
| Python | `python: 3.11 \| 3.12 \| 3.13` |
| License | `license: MPL-2.0` |
| Tests | `Tests - passing` |

Ran the README through `readme_renderer` the way PyPI does. All four images survive the HTML sanitizer, so the badges show on the project page and not just on GitHub. `twine check --strict` passes on both artifacts.

author: sm06224
body:
#300 段③ で組み込みアプリが**既定で別窓**になったので、この穴は
「多重タブを使う人だけ」の話ではなくなりました ── **本文を書いている隣で、
別窓のカレンダーが同じノートに日付を書く**、が普通の動線になります。

---

## 🔴 まず severity を測り直しました(issue の前提が 1 つ間違っていた)

動線レビューも、#178 も、私の最初のコメントも「別窓の書込が**黙って消える**」と
書いていました。⚠ **実物の worker で窓 2 枚の物語を通したら、消えていませんでした。**

`COMMIT_EDIT` は既存ノートで `checkpoint: true` なので、worker が履歴へ積むのは
`old.body` = **ディスク上の値 = 別窓の版**です(`maintainChain`)。つまり:

> **上書きはされる。しかし消えてはいない ── 履歴から戻せる。**

⚠ しかも **1 稿目の fixture は前提から間違って**いて、その場で落ちました
(新規行には `old` が無いので `maintainChain` が呼ばれない)──
**読むより測るほうが速い**の実例です。この筋は
`tests/adapter/storage-worker.test.ts` に常設しました。

## だから直したのは「黙っていること」

推薦していた 2 つとも、**要らなくなりました**:

| 案 | なぜ落としたか |
|---|---|
| 楽観検査で**断る** | user が**打った字を捨てさせる**ことになる。#300 が戻そうとしている動線と逆 |
| `updatedAt` の突合 | `UPSERT_SQL` は `datetime('now')` = **秒粒度**。「1 秒以内に重なる」という**当の場面**で素通りする |
| 本文 hash の突合 | **要らなかった** ── 印を立てる仕組み(`diskAhead`)は**既に在り**、足りなかったのは他タブの書込が**そこへ届いていない**ことだけ |

入れたものは 3 つです:

1. **`REMOTE_BODY_CHANGED`** ── 他タブ / 他窓の書込を編集中のタブが受けて
   `diskAhead` を立てる。⚠ **下書きには 1 バイトも触りません**。
   ⚠ `BODY_PERSISTED`(**自分**の ack)とは**別の口**にしています ── 混ぜると
   自分の書込でも印が立ちます
2. **`remote-change.ts`** ── 「誰に聞きに行くか」の判断(編集中でなければ何もしない /
   自分のノートでなければ本文を読みに行かない)。`main.ts` は配線だけ
3. **`COMMIT_EDIT`**:重なっていたら ① `checkpoint` を**強制**
   (新規ノートの初回 commit だけは本当に消えるので、断り文を本当にする)
   ② **画面に理由と戻し方を出す**

🔑 **last-write-wins は覆していません**(P3-6a review #4 の判断のまま)──
user が打った字を、別の窓の都合で捨てさせないためです。
変えたのは **残るかどうか**と**黙るかどうか**の 2 つだけです。

## 確かめたこと

- **変異試験 11 件すべて KILLED**。⚠ うち 1 件(`checkpoint` の強制)は
  **1 稿目の test が空振りしていた**のを変異試験が教えました ── 普通のノートは
  `checkpoint` がどのみち true なので、強制を外しても緑でした。
  **普通なら false になる形**(新規ノートの初回 commit)で見る形に書き直しています
- **実ブラウザで窓 2 枚**を通す smoke を足しました
  (`tests/smoke/window-overlap.smoke.spec.ts`)── タイルから 2 枚目の窓を開き、
  そこで日付を付け、本体で保存して**理由が出ること**と**打った字が残ること**を見ます。
  ⚠ 空振りでないことも変異(理由を出さない)を当てて確かめました ── **KILLED**
- unit **4241 緑** / `typecheck` / `lint` / **フル smoke 199 緑**(5.1 分)

## ⚠ 残す「覆る条件」

- 断りの頻度が高くて煩わしいと実機で分かったら、per-lid ロックへの従属(重い側)へ
- 履歴の保持は **100 版**(`REVISION_KEEP_LATEST`)── その先まで編集が続くと
  上書きされた版は落ちます。**「必ず戻せる」ではなく「100 版のうちは戻せる」**です
  (お知らせにもマニュアルにも「必ず」とは書いていません)

body: Release-lane remediation for the @hasna/emails@1.4.6 release candidate. The ship-latest wave (#856) bumped apps/emails/package.json pins to @hasna/contracts@0.13.4 and @hasna/domains@0.0.43 but did not refresh the per-app bun.lock, which still pinned 0.13.3 / 0.0.42. The Docker-context install (`bun install --production --frozen-lockfile` with package.json + bun.lock only) fails with "lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen" — measured from a clean dir, rc=1.
