author: crayjthiemsert
body:
## What

Clears the two files that had been carried in the working tree since session 241, on Cray's typed rulings this session. Only one produces a diff; the other is recorded here because this PR is its only tracked record.

| File | Ruling | Diff? |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/design/Cray_J_v1_small.png` | **ignore**, do not commit, do not delete | yes — a `.gitignore` rule |
| `docs/strategy/public/intro-video-production-rulings.md` | **revert** the uncommitted R9 edit | no — restores the file to `HEAD` |

After this, `git status --porcelain` on `main` is **empty for the first time since s241**.

## Why the PNG is ignored rather than committed

An orphan **by measurement**, not by impression:

- `git grep -i Cray_J_v1` over the whole tree → **rc=1, zero hits**. Nothing tracked references it.
- `docs/design/` otherwise holds only `.md` files.
- It is a personal wordmark + mascot, not a vero-lite asset — and this repo is **public and Apache 2.0**, so committing it would inherit that licence grant for no product reason.

The pattern is `docs/design/Cray_J_*`, not the exact filename, because `v1_small` implies siblings that would otherwise land right back here. **Positive control:** the tracked `docs/design/0013-oct-ui-provenance.md` in the same directory is still **not** ignored (`git check-ignore` rc=1), so the rule is not over-broad. The file stays on disk untouched.

## Why reverting the rulings file was safe — checked before the destructive step

The uncommitted `+14/−6` diff recorded **R9** (Cray's ruling of 2026-08-20, session 241 — the intro clip is no longer bound to a runtime) plus a 🔴→🟡 downgrade of open question #1.

Before running `git checkout --`:

- R9 survives in `docs/strategy/private/2026-08-10-intro-video-STORYBOARD-v2.md` at **ten sites**, including its frontmatter `title:` and `status:`, with beat 1 rewritten around it.
- That grep carried a **positive control against R8** (one hit), so a zero for R9 could not have been a broken matcher.

After:

- the file greps **R9 → 0** and **R8 → 4** — reverted, not truncated.

The reverted patch is also saved to this session's scratchpad.

## ⚠️ Consequence, recorded rather than hidden

**R9 is now tracked nowhere.** It lives only in a gitignored file — which is the exact failure mode `intro-video-production-rulings.md` was created to fix; its own §1 says R1–R7 had lived only in gitignored places.

The reverted text additionally *claimed* the gap "did not outlive the session that opened it". Measured against `HEAD`, that claim was **false**, and had been false for six sessions — `git show HEAD:…| grep -c R9` returned `0`.

Cray ruled this acceptable (typed, s247). If R9 should become tracked later, its text is reproducible from the storyboard, which remains the richer record.

## Verification

author: mcross2298
body:
Final phase of the session-shell rebuild. Follows #286 (M0), #287 + #288 (M1, M3a–c), all merged.

Three floating controls go, and with them the last fixed layer on a workout page other than the toolbar itself.

## The whole arc, measured

| stage | covered viewport during a rest period |
|---|---|
| baseline | **470px — 55.7%** |
| M3a — Finish bar → toolbar | 365px — 43.2% |
| M3b — rest float → inline row | 195px — 23.1% |
| M3c — nav auto-hides in session | 140px — 16.6% |
| **M4 — floats retired** | **46px — 5.5%** |

Browsing, before a session starts: 101px (12%) — toolbar + nav, which is correct; the nav is how you browse.

## What changed

**Theme toggle (z141) — retired.** Pinned top-right on every page including mid-workout, and M1/D11 measured it as **39 of its 40px behind the z999 session bar** on a notched phone — a dead button on exactly the pages it cluttered. Nothing is stranded: the Dashboard and Stats topbars each carry a real toggle, and `mc-nav.js` already stood down on those pages via its own guard. **The trade: theme switching is no longer reachable from a workout page.**

**Voice mic (z98) — retired.** Sat underneath the z100 rest timer — measured buried for the entire rest period, i.e. unusable at exactly the moment you'd speak to it — and floated over set rows the rest of the time. `MCVoice`'s module and API are untouched, so a future surface can mount a control without reviving a floating one.

**"Short on time?" (z1180) — consolidated, not deleted.** As a fixed pill it outranked even the modal layer and was measured covering set rows and the rest timer. It's now a full-width chip in the card list above the first exercise — the placement `mc-guided.js` already established for its own entry chip, rather than a second invented one. In flow it needs no z-index at all, which is the point: **a control that is part of the list cannot collide with the list.**

## A regression I introduced, then fixed

Mutation records went **15 → 18/s** against a budget of 15 — because the tick was still writing the float's countdown every second on pages where M3b hides it. Guarding every readout write on `offsetParent` brings it to **12/s**, *better than the pre-M3 baseline*, since that hidden-float write was pure waste even before this roadmap.

I'd rather fix that than spend the headroom, given this roadmap's whole S1 history is a −99.5% runtime win that nearly regressed silently once already.

Verified afterwards that all three visible readouts still move as one (`59s`/`59s`/`59s`) and `+15s` still moves them together — `offsetParent` has real edge cases with fixed positioning, so that needed checking rather than reasoning.

## Verification

- Visual ratchet re-baselined **deliberately**: every kitchen-sink page grew by exactly **54px**, which is the in-flow chip's `44px min-height + 10px margin` — the arithmetic of the change itself, not a surprise. Re-run in check mode after: 0px changed on all five.
- Back link hit-tested **reachable in both** browsing and in-session states (D11 was this control being unclickable, so it's checked now rather than assumed).
- Smoke 38/38 clean, all local gates pass, perf within budget.

## Still open

**M2** — the stacking contract and CI gate, deliberately skipped to build M3 first. It also absorbs two items deferred from M1: the `.week-tabs` double safe-area inset, and sticky tab rows pinning *under* the stat bar. Far less urgent now that the layer count on a workout page has gone from 7 to 1, but the 99999-tier z-indexes and the 15 duplicate page-local rule copies are still there.

**M5** — user demos across engine families at two viewports.

body:
TLDR (from a human)

Tried to add a button to "build pull request" that bypasses the automatic logic and just lets you build a PR manually, I have setup a small script on my instance to allow me to do that even tho my PRs aren't targeting the default branch. (By leveraging the webook)

Sidenote I am unsure how to test this, it's vibe-coded out of frustration.

Much love @AminDhouib for this fork,


## Summary

Adds a **"Build Pull Request"** button to the **Preview Deployments** tab that lets you pick any open pull request / merge request on the resource's repository and immediately create + deploy a preview deployment — no webhook or GitHub event required.

This covers the flow that previously required manually calling the deploy endpoint with a forged payload: select a PR, dokploy creates the preview row, generates the domain from the wildcard template, posts the PR comment, and queues the build.

## Changes

- **Providers** (`packages/server/src/utils/providers/`)
  - `getGithubPullRequests` — lists open PRs for `owner/repo` via the GitHub App (paginated, sorted by recency).
  - `getGitlabMergeRequests` — lists open merge requests for a GitLab project (paginated).
- **Schemas** (`packages/server/src/db/schema/`)
  - `apiFindGithubPullRequests`, `apiFindGitlabMergeRequests`.
- **tRPC routers** (`apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/`)
  - `github.getGithubPullRequests`, `gitlab.getGitlabMergeRequests` (both behind `assertGitProviderAccess`).
- **UI** (`apps/dokploy/components/dashboard/.../preview-deployments/`)
  - New shared `BuildPreviewDeployment` dialog: searches open PRs/MRs, shows PR # / title / branch / draft state, and calls the existing `previewDeployment.create` mutation.
  - Wired into both the **application** and **compose** preview deployments tabs.

## Why this is safe

- The create path reuses the existing `previewDeployment.create` tRPC flow, so dedupe (`(applicationId, pullRequestId)` unique index), preview limit, domain generation, comment posting, and authz all behave identically to a webhook-triggered preview.
- The new endpoints only *read* from the git provider and are permission-gated like the existing `getGithubBranches` / `getGitlabBranches`.

## Notes

- GitHub: works for both `draft` and open PRs (draft flagged in the picker).
- GitLab: uses `gitlabProjectId` (the existing branch fetch already depends on it).

author: jorguzz-fer
body:
## Contexto

O degrau zero de qualquer caso: sem cliente e veterinário cadastrados, nenhum exame nasce — e até aqui isso só existia por seed, o que impede produção de operar sozinha. O schema do M03 (cliente, veterinário, vínculo) existia desde o bootstrap; faltavam serviço, rotas e tela. Penúltimo dos módulos "domínio pronto, sem tela"; depois deste, só o M01.

## O que muda

**Backend (M03)**

- `ClientesService`: criar/editar/inativar/reativar cliente e veterinário, vincular e encerrar vínculo. **Inativar nunca exclui** (M01/M03); revincular **reativa o mesmo registro** em vez de duplicar (§36), preservando as datas do período anterior.
- **Detecção de duplicidade (§20)**: documento/nome (cliente) ou CRMV/nome (veterinário) já cadastrados devolvem **409 com os candidatos** (`duplicidades` no corpo RFC 7807 — campo novo no `ProblemaFilter`, no mesmo espírito de `achados`/`estagio`); confirmar com `ignorarDuplicidade` fica registrado na auditoria. Para veterinário, a mensagem oferece o caminho certo: **vincular o existente** — pessoa única com N vínculos (§§12-13).
- **O código do cliente é definitivo** (§6.2): exigido na criação, fora da edição — ele compõe o registro dos exames já emitidos (`CV-000342/26`).
- **Ficha (§49)**: dados, vínculos vigentes e encerrados, e últimos exames *consultados* dos casos — o M03 não guarda cópia (§30).
- Recepção ganha `cliente:editar` e `veterinario:editar` (manter o cadastro vivo é a caixa dela, M10 §38) — aditivo; `sincronizar-perfis` cobre instituições existentes.

**Front**

- Tela `/clientes` com abas Clientes | Veterinários (§48), busca ampla com debounce (§§45-46), diálogos de criação com o fluxo de duplicidade ("é outro cliente — criar mesmo assim"), ficha com edição, vínculos (vincular/encerrar) e inativar/reativar; item novo no menu.

**Bug pego na verificação visual** (e agora coberto por teste)

- Identificadores interpolados pelo drizzle dentro de subquery `sql\`\`` saíam **sem qualificação de tabela** (`"id"` em vez de `"veterinario"."id"`), o que quebrava a listagem de veterinários com 500 e **zerava silenciosamente** a contagem de casos dos clientes. Corrigido com qualificação manual e asserts específicos.

**Testes** (41 → 44 na API; 94 no total)

- Recepção cadastra cliente + veterinário + vínculo e abre um caso cujo **identificador nasce com o código do cliente novo**.
- Duplicidade devolve candidatos; confirmação passa e é auditada; código repetido é barrado mesmo com confirmação; CRMV repetido aponta o cadastro existente.
- Encerrar vínculo preserva a história (término na ficha, caso segue); revincular reaproveita o registro; cliente inativado some do catálogo de exame novo mas segue na busca do M03 com a contagem de casos correta.

## Verificação manual

API buildada + web dev contra Postgres real, logado como recepção: lista com dados reais, ficha com vínculo e caso vinculado, aba Veterinários com vínculos vigentes, e o fluxo de duplicidade exercitado no navegador (aviso com candidato + botão de confirmação). Screenshots conferidos.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` e `pnpm test` verdes (94 testes)
- [x] Tabelas de domínio novas nascem com `tenant_id` e RLS (ADR 0002) — sem tabela nova; as do M03 existem com RLS desde o bootstrap
- [x] Nenhum módulo chama outro diretamente — a integração é por evento; a ficha consulta casos por leitura, sem estado
- [x] Decisão arquitetural relevante virou ADR — nenhuma decisão nova
- [x] Sem segredo, credencial ou dado pessoal real no diff

author: aarontrowbridge
body:
Fixes #59.

## The bug
The convergence check in `expv_taylor` evaluates `norm_tail_tot ≤ tol * _opnormInf(F)` on stripped duals (`AD.primal_value`). With an AD type whose primal is zero but whose partials are not — e.g. a ForwardDiff `Dual` seeded at a zero state — every Taylor term has zero primal, the check degenerates to `0 ≤ tol·0`, and the series breaks at `j=1`. Values stay correct, but the returned partials carry only the first-order term, silently corrupting any Jacobian taken at a zero-valued vector (hit in practice differentiating bilinear quantum-control dynamics whose state trajectories start at zero).

Four-line repro in #59: partials `1.0` where the truth is `cos(0.05) ≈ 0.99875`.

## The fix
Treat an exactly-zero primal series as **not converged** and keep iterating up to the chosen degree — which already bounds the tail by the same `tol` criterion used to pick `degree_opt` in `parameters()`. Only the zero-primal path pays extra steps; every other path is byte-identical.

## Verification
- New regression test in `test/autodiff.jl`: zero-primal dual `B` → partials match `exp(tA)·x` exactly; nonzero-primal control unchanged.
- Full suite: **2307 passed, 0 failed** locally.
- End-to-end downstream: with this patch developed in, DirectTrajOpt/Piccolo's `BilinearIntegrator` analytic-vs-finite-difference Jacobian gates pass for zero-initialized variational trajectories (previously failing with the structured mismatch in harmoniqs/Piccolo.jl#307).

author: nhwalker
body:
Patches neatvnc 0.9.1 so that Weston's VNC backend can offload H.264 encoding to an NVIDIA GPU, and packages the result as an RPM built the way Fedora/EPEL does it.

## Why

neatvnc's only GPU H.264 path is VAAPI (`src/enc/h264/ffmpeg-impl.c`: `h264_vaapi` plus a `hwmap=derive_device=vaapi,scale_vaapi=…` filter graph). NVIDIA has no VAAPI *encoder* — `nvidia-vaapi-driver` is decode-only — so `h264_encoder_create()` always fails and `have_working_h264_encoder()` caches "unavailable".

There is a second gate: `choose_frame_encoding()` refuses H.264 unless the frame is `NVNC_FB_GBM_BO`. Weston's VNC backend never produces one — both renderer paths (`pixman->create_image_from_ptr` and `gl->create_fbo`) render into `nvnc_fb_get_addr(fb)`, i.e. plain memory from `nvnc_fb_pool_new()`.

Net effect on an NVIDIA host: the VNC server silently falls back to raw/tight/zrle and the GPU is never used.

## Approach

NVENC accepts packed RGB input and performs both the host→GPU transfer and the RGB→YUV conversion in hardware, so it needs no GBM buffer object, no dma-buf import and no filter graph — it consumes exactly the memory buffers Weston already produces.

- `src/enc/h264/nvenc-impl.c` — new `h264_encoder_impl` reusing the threading scaffolding of `ffmpeg-impl.c`, wrapping the mapped frame buffer in an `AVFrame` with no copy.
- `struct h264_encoder_impl` gains `accepts_sw_frames`; `src/server.c` offers open-h264 for memory frames only when the selected implementation can consume them. VAAPI and V4L2 behaviour is unchanged.
- New `nvenc` meson feature; it deliberately does not require `gbm`/`libdrm` the way `have_ffmpeg` does.
- `packaging/` — Fedora-style spec (pristine tarball + patch), ubi10 build container, ubi10 Weston + websockify + noVNC test image, and a GPU-free RFB test client.

### Base branch

Branched from `Release 0.9.1` rather than `master`, because Weston 14.0.2 requires `neatvnc >= 0.7.0, < 0.10.0` and uses the old `nvnc_fb_*` API. The library keeps the `libneatvnc.so.0` soname EPEL's neatvnc 0.9.0 ships, so it is a drop-in — **no Weston source changes are needed**.

## What was verified

| Check | Where | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Builds clean, no warnings | Ubuntu 24.04, ffmpeg 6.1 | pass |
| Builds with `-Dnvenc=disabled` | Ubuntu | pass (VAAPI-only unregressed) |
| Upstream unit tests | both | pass |
| RPM builds, `%check` runs | ubi10 + EPEL/RPM Fusion/Rocky, ffmpeg 7.1.5 | pass |
| Soname is still `libneatvnc.so.0` | ubi10 | pass |
| open-h264 negotiated for a **memory** framebuffer, Annex B keyframe with SPS/PPS/IDR in baseline profile | ubi10, against the installed RPM | pass |
| Weston 14.0.1 + patched neatvnc + noVNC 1.7.0 over HTTPS | ubi10 | pass — browser rendered Weston's 1280×720 output |

```
connected to 'Draw', 500x500
rect 500x500+0+0 encoding=50 flags=0x0 payload=1513 bytes
NAL unit types present: 5, 6, 7, 8
SPS profile_idc=66 constraints=0xc0 level_idc=62
PASS: server negotiated open-h264 and sent a baseline keyframe
```

**Not verified here: NVENC itself.** The build machine has no `/dev/nvidia*`, so `NEATVNC_H264_NVENC_CODEC` pointed the encoder at libx264 for the integration tests. Everything except the NVENC hand-off is exercised. RPM Fusion's EL10 ffmpeg was confirmed to carry `h264_nvenc` and `--enable-nvenc`.

## noVNC gotchas found while testing

- **EPEL 10 ships noVNC 1.5.0, which has no H.264 decoder at all.** Support first shipped in noVNC **1.6.0**; 1.7.0 improved detection. The test image installs 1.7.0 from upstream instead of the RPM.
- **HTTPS is required.** noVNC only offers H.264 when WebCodecs `VideoDecoder` exists, and that API is restricted to secure contexts. Plain HTTP silently downgrades to Tight.
- **No client configuration is needed to prefer H.264.** noVNC advertises `CopyRect, H264, Tight, …` and neatvnc returns the first encoding it recognises, ignoring CopyRect — so H.264 wins on its own.
- **The browser needs an H.264 decoder.** Chrome/Edge/Firefox have it; Chromium builds without proprietary codecs (including Playwright's) report `isConfigSupported({codec:'avc1.42401f'})` as false.
- **Weston needs a PAM login** as the user it runs as (`root` in the container), and noVNC's `password` URL parameter is not enough because RSA-AES also needs a username.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `NEATVNC_H264_ENCODER` | `v4l2m2m` \| `vaapi` \| `nvenc` \| `auto` — pin encoder selection |
| `NEATVNC_H264_NVENC_CODEC` | override the libavcodec encoder name (default `h264_nvenc`); lets CI exercise the whole path with a software encoder |
| `NEATVNC_H264_NVENC_FORMAT` | `rgb` \| `nv12` — `nv12` moves colour conversion from NVENC to libswscale, where the coefficients are ours to choose |

Full deployment notes in [`packaging/README.md`](packaging/README.md).

author: baldrick-h2[bot]
body:
Interactive Brokers portfolio management, trading to predefined rules. Empty today; registered now so it starts governed rather than being retrofitted later.

This is the first real test of the claim that adding a repository is cheap. It was three steps and they worked first time:

```
# 1. add the catalogue entry
tooling/universe validate            → clean: 13 repositories validated
tooling/universe sync-baseline portfolio-bot --path <clone>
tooling/universe audit portfolio-bot --path <clone>   → clean
```

Its initial commit is [`96f34ae`](https://github.com/hannosirkel/portfolio-bot/commit/96f34ae), pushed directly to `main` under the empty-repository exception in `standards/agent-operation.md` — a branch cannot exist before the first commit.

## A new profile: `application-private`

It is `application-public` without the publication constraint. Separate from `research-private` because that profile is explicitly told *not* to adopt deployable-application conventions, and a trading service must. A trading bot is not research.

## `languages` is empty, deliberately

There is no code, so there is nothing to gate. §7.1 says populate from evidence, not expectation — a declared language with no files is a check that never runs. The repository's own `AGENTS.md` names the single line to change when Python lands, and says that is what turns the `ruff` gate on.

## What the repository got

Five files, no scaffolding: `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` (31 local lines), the generated `CLAUDE.md` and `.habit-hooks/config.toml`.

Three rules are written down now rather than after the first trading logic, because they are much harder to retrofit than to adopt:

- anything that can place an order is tested against a **simulated broker** — no test reaches a live or paper IB gateway;
- a **dry-run mode exists from the start, and is the default**;
- no credential, account number, or captured API response holding positions or balances is ever committed.

That last one is why this repository differs from every other here: a leaked credential does not expose data, it lets somebody trade with real money.

## Verification

```
tooling/universe validate      clean: 13 repositories validated
tooling/universe audit         0 failing across the universe
108 tests                      OK
ruff check .                   All checks passed
markdownlint-cli2 **/*.md      0 issues
```

author: alibashuaib
body:
## Summary

Closes out Phase 4b of the garage roadmap: two devices signed into the same account, both left open, converge on their own — no re-authentication, no manual refresh required.

Builds on merged Phase 4a (accounts: sign-in/out, push-on-save, pull-on-sign-in). Sign-in's existing behavior (`pull()`/`adopt()`/`reconcile()`) is completely unchanged — verified byte-identical across the whole branch.

## What's in this branch

- **Outbox** — an IndexedDB-backed queue (`vehicle`/`photo`/`tombstone` entries), dual-backend where the design calls for it, replacing Phase 4a's flat "dirty ids" list.
- **Incremental pull** — a `lastPulledAt` cursor, consuming tombstones (soft deletes) alongside live rows, additive to (never replacing) sign-in's full-replace pull.
- **Photo sync** — upload to Supabase Storage on save, lazy download-by-reference on pull.
- **Reconnect + immediate sync** — a `save()`/`delete()` now kicks a best-effort push immediately when online, plus a `window.online` listener for the reconnect case; not just boot-time.
- **Storage policy** — a `photos` bucket mirroring the existing table RLS pattern, with size/type limits.
- Manual verification checklist for the parts that need a live Supabase project and two real devices (not reachable from the Node suite).

## Process

Built via spec → plan → subagent-driven implementation, 8 tasks each with its own task-scoped review:
- Task 1 review caught a duplicate-id divergence between the two storage backends — fixed and re-verified.
- Task 6 review caught two Critical data-integrity bugs in the incremental-pull cursor (a failed write could silently let the sync cursor advance past it, permanently skipping the row; the cursor was derived from the local clock instead of the data, risking permanent skips on clock skew) — both fixed and independently re-verified in the final whole-branch review.
- The final whole-branch review caught a Critical integration gap the per-task reviews couldn't see (nothing pushed a save until the next reconnect on an always-online device) plus two Important invariant regressions (a delete could resurrect across drains; a sign-out mid-sync could write into a just-wiped store) — all three fixed and re-verified, including one more targeted fix for a sequencing bug the first fix wave introduced.

Three findings were deliberately parked as documented follow-ups rather than rushed into this branch: a transient photo-download failure can become permanent once the cursor advances past its row; `updated_at` is client-clock-authored (not server `now()`), so cross-device clock skew remains a residual risk; and a deleted vehicle's photos are never removed from Storage. None of these are correctness regressions from this branch — they're gaps worth a deliberate follow-up decision.

## Testing

`npm test` — 283/283 passing. `npm run test:e2e` passing (17 passed, 3 skipped, including new reconnect-listener and delete-sync presence checks).

**Still needed before production use:** the manual multi-device verification pass (`docs/superpowers/verification/2026-08-22-sync-manual.md`) against a live Supabase project — this needs two real browser profiles and cannot be automated. The schema SQL also needs to be applied by hand to the live project.

author: ianfeather
body:
Closes the board row *Deploy API runs master's workflow against an older checkout, so a referenced script can be missing*.

## The split

`workflow_run` takes the **workflow definition** from the default branch's tip, while the checkout deliberately pins the triggering commit. Both halves are right on their own; together they mean a run can execute master's newest steps against a checkout that predates them.

I confirmed the mechanism against the real run rather than assuming it:

```
$ gh api repos/Ianfeather/big-shop/actions/runs/32585058437 --jq .head_sha
5ec3e823b91aea401c1b64da83f48cbf272a73a9   # = #137, master's tip = github.sha
```

…while that run checked out `9369bb5` (#139) — the commit that predates `scripts/verify-fly-release.sh`. That also settles the design question underneath this: for a `workflow_run` event `github.sha` **is** the default branch tip, not the triggering run's head.

## The fix

A `guard` job requires the triggering commit to equal `github.sha`. Since that is exactly the commit the workflow file was read from, workflow, tree and tip collapse into one commit — so both directions of the problem **cannot arise**, rather than being detected after the fact.

The silent direction is the one that matters more. The observed failure was loud (exit 127). A step *deleted* from the workflow still ran when the trigger was old, and a step reading a config file that had since changed shape read it wrongly with nothing to report.

### Why not the row's option 1

The row proposed a second checkout at the workflow's commit, with steps calling scripts from there. That breaks on contact with the scripts: both `check-fly-secrets.sh` and `verify-fly-release.sh` do

```bash
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../netlify-functions/recipes"
```

and read `fly.toml` / `machine_config.json` **relative to themselves**. Checking them out at the workflow commit would make `check-fly-secrets.sh` validate the wrong tree's `machine_config.json`. They are tooling whose input is content, so the split the option assumes isn't there — it would need both scripts reworked to take the target tree as a parameter first.

## A second hazard this also fixes

`concurrency` queues deploys rather than superseding them, and nothing ordered the queue by commit. Two commits landing close together, the newer one's CI finishing first, would deploy the newer and then **the older on top** — a silent rollback of whatever the newer one changed, lasting until the next push. An older commit's run now skips.

## What this gives up, deliberately

**If master's tip goes red, the previous green commit no longer ships.** Its run skips as not-the-tip, and the tip's own run never happens because CI failed. Nothing is lost and the next green commit carries everything — but a red master now blocks deploys rather than quietly shipping the commit before it. Called out here because it is a real behaviour change, not a pure improvement.

Also: **re-running an old CI run to force a redeploy is now a no-op**, with a notice saying so. `Actions → Deploy API → Run workflow` is the way to force one. Documented in `docs/fly-migration-runbook.md`.

## Shape

A separate job rather than a condition on `deploy` itself. Both values are plain contexts so this *could* have been an expression in the job-level `if` — but a job that reports "skipped" with no reason is the same genre of silence as the bug it fixes. The conclusion gate stays at job level where it was, so a red CI still costs no runner.

## Verification

The guard script was extracted from the YAML and exercised against all five cases, including a replay of run `32585058437`'s actual SHAs:

| case | result |
| --- | --- |
| real failing run (`9369bb5` trigger, `5ec3e82` tip) | `deploy=false` |
| normal deploy (trigger == tip) | `deploy=true` |
| manual dispatch | `deploy=true` |
| CI failed | `deploy=false` |
| CI cancelled | `deploy=false` |

`guard` is not a required status check (those are `build-lint-test`, `e2e` and `go`, all in other workflows), so the ruleset needs no change — verified via the rulesets API.

No user-visible surface, so no screenshots.

author: meowsers4
body:
The last of the three heavy stubs. Per patient, never pooled — a baseline built across patients folds germline CNV and per-patient capture differences into the malignancy call.

## Parameters chosen, not accepted

| | |
|---|---|
| `cutoff = 0.1` | the package's documented value for **droplet** data (1 is Smart-seq2). Not tuned, and must not be tuned to make calls look better. |
| `analysis_mode = "subclusters"` | not `"samples"`. A tumour is not one clone, and averaging subclones pulls low-burden malignant cells toward the reference — costing sensitivity exactly where this project needs it, since **a mature-looking tumour cell with few CNVs is the case that decides compositional vs intrinsic**. Slower; deliberate. |
| `HMM = FALSE` | roughly triples runtime and produces discrete states this pipeline does not use — `call_malignancy` thresholds a continuous score against each patient's own reference cells. |
| `gene_position_file` | **required, no default.** This deposit is `GRCh37_liftover_v28` (hg19); a GRCh38 file would misplace genes and produce chromosome-arm artifacts indistinguishable from real CNVs. Missing file fails loudly with that reason. |

## The two circularity traps, now covered by tests rather than by care

- **`holdout_normal_epi` is written as an observation, never a reference group.** It exists to be scored *out-of-sample* by `validate_normal_epithelium`; as a reference it would validate the baseline against itself.
- **`reference_diploid` is split into `ref_immune` / `ref_stromal` / `ref_endothelial`, not pooled.** inferCNV bounds the log fold change by each category's own mean, and that per-category bounding is what suppresses cell-type differences reading as copy number — the failure this project already reversed its reference design once to avoid.

## Before this can run

**A gene-order file for hg19 has to be fetched** and given a `data/manifest.csv` row (CONTRIBUTING §4). The job reads `$BRP_GENE_POSITIONS`, defaulting to `$BRP_DATA_DIR/raw/gene_order_hg19.txt`. It is not committed here because it is data.

Then:

```bash
qsub -t 1-5  src/reference/jobs/infercnv.sh patients_pilot.txt
qsub -t 1-62 src/reference/jobs/infercnv.sh patients_all.txt
```

## What is not tested

inferCNV itself — it is R, slow, and not pip-installable. `dry_run` writes the inputs and returns the command, so everything that decides whether its answer means anything *is* tested: reference-group construction, the holdout exclusion, matrix orientation (genes × cells, not AnnData's), unusable-cell handling, and the score conversion feeding `call_malignancy`.

**CopyKAT is not implemented.** §4 asks for it as a cross-check; in a one-week compression it is the first thing to cut, and it should be cut out loud rather than quietly. One caller with held-out normal-epithelium validation is defensible; two is a luxury.

855 passed, 4 skipped in a from-scratch venv.

author: eugenio-garcia-calderon
body:
Los dos últimos requisitos de las tiendas que dependían de nosotros. Van juntos
porque la norma del equipo es una PR por programador.

---

# 1 · Bloquear a una persona

Apple rechaza una aplicación con contenido de otras personas que deje denunciar
una **cosa** pero no bloquear a una **persona**. Denunciar abre un caso que juzga
otro más tarde; bloquear surte efecto ya y lo decide quien lo pulsa.

**La regla vive en un solo sitio**: `bloqueado_entre(a, b)`, una función SQL
`STABLE` de la migración `0091` que mira los dos sentidos. Cada listado añade una
línea, en vez de seis copias de un `NOT IN` — seis copias son seis sitios donde
olvidarla, y así es como un bloqueo acaba filtrando el muro y no los comentarios.

| Sitio | Antes | Después |
|---|---|---|
| El muro | 4 visibles | 0, en los dos sentidos |
| Publicaciones, lienzos, proyectos, mapas, ventanas | 4 | 0, en los dos sentidos |
| Comentarios | visibles | ocultos |
| Mensajes directos | 200 | 403, en los dos sentidos |
| Seguir | permitido | 403, y los que había los borra un disparador |

**No se avisa a nadie**, a propósito: avisar convierte el bloqueo en una
provocación. Quién te ha bloqueado a ti no se puede consultar en ningún sitio.

En la app: en el menú de la tarjeta bajo «Denunciar», ofrecido otra vez **después**
de enviar una denuncia, y deshacible en **Configuración → Personas bloqueadas**
(que se esconde sola cuando está vacía).

**25 comprobaciones en verde, 0 en rojo**: 9 en SQL contra datos reales en una
transacción que se deshace, 16 sobre HTTP con dos cuentas. Incluye a propósito lo
que **no** debe cambiar: un tercero y quien no ha entrado lo siguen viendo todo,
bloquear dos veces no es error, y nadie puede borrar el bloqueo de otro.

---

# 2 · Privacidad

**No había ninguna política de privacidad**: ni ruta, ni fichero, ni texto en el
repositorio. App Store Connect no deja enviar la aplicación sin una dirección que
responda, y la ficha de Play tampoco. Ahora está en `humanity.wiki/privacidad`, y
**esa ruta no se mueve nunca más**, igual que `/borrar-cuenta`.

Los formularios de las dos tiendas —*Data safety* de Play, las etiquetas de Apple—
son declaraciones: lo que digan tiene que coincidir con lo que la aplicación hace,
o es motivo de retirada. Así que el texto se escribió **midiendo**: las columnas de
`users`, `sessions` e `intentos_fallidos`; un `grep` de rastreadores conocidos por
todo `src/` y el `index.html` (**cero**: ni Analytics, ni píxel, ni Sentry); las
cookies que pone el servidor (**una**, `rh_session`); y los dominios de terceros a
los que llama la aplicación.

**Ese último punto cambió el código antes que el texto.** Aparecieron dos cosas
que nadie había decidido:

- **Cuatro vídeos incrustados desde `youtube.com`** (que sí deja cookie de
  seguimiento) mientras otros cuatro ya usaban `youtube-nocookie.com`. Una
  decisión, aplicada en la mitad de los sitios. Los cuatro cambiados.
- **`transparenttextures.com`**, pedido en cada visita a un objetivo o a un reto
  para un fondo decorativo al 10 % de opacidad — entregándole la IP de cada
  visitante a un tercero a cambio de una textura que casi no se ve. Ahora se
  dibuja en el código.

Una política de privacidad no describe la aplicación que te gustaría tener. Si al
escribirla encuentras algo que no quieres tener que declarar, lo que se cambia es
la aplicación.

Comprobado en un navegador de verdad, con la compilación de producción: la página
se pinta y **la página de un objetivo ya no pide nada a nadie de fuera** (antes
pedía una cosa). El SVG incrustado se comprueba como lo carga el navegador
—`Image()` y `onload`, 40×70— porque un `data:` bien formado puede seguir sin
pintar nada.

**Y dos errores míos, encontrados al comprobar un dato que no podía verificar.**
Faltaban **Cloudflare** —está delante de todo el sitio, así que la IP de cada
visitante pasa por ahí— y el **almacén de las copias de seguridad**, que saca cada
noche un volcado entero fuera del servidor. Y la página afirmaba que los
servidores están «en Alemania»: Hetzner es una empresa alemana, pero dónde corre
la máquina no está escrito en ningún sitio del repositorio. Es una afirmación
jurídica en una política de privacidad, así que ahora está en el recuadro ámbar de
«falta por completar», no afirmada.

**Lo que la página no puede decir todavía lo dice en la propia página**, en ámbar y
no escondido en un comentario: los datos de la sociedad responsable, el país exacto
de los servidores y el proveedor de las copias. Inventarlos habría sido peor que
dejarlos en blanco.

`memory/10_TIENDAS.md` recoge el inventario medido y las respuestas listas para el
formulario *Data safety* de Play.

---

Las entradas del changelog están escritas y guardadas aparte:
`memory/08_CHANGELOG.md` lo han tenido reservado prog7 y prog4 toda la tarde.
Entran en cuanto se suelte.

author: devluce
body:
## 무엇을 / 왜

FR-12 맥락 브리핑이 `main`에 들어간 뒤 남아 있던 자리를 채운다.

- **인수인계 카드를 대상자 상세·방문 화면에도** 붙인다. ADR-0024는 인수인계를 "`/today/[subjectId]` 상단 3줄"이라고 정했는데 지금은 대상자 정보 화면의 `맥락 브리핑` 탭에만 있다. 방문·전화를 하러 들어온 화면에서도 맥락이 보여야 "담당 교체가 화면 한 장으로 끝난다"가 성립한다. 탭의 목록을 `HandoverList`로 뽑아 두 자리가 **같은 문장·같은 근거**를 읽게 했다.
- **통화 결과 시트의 `기록 추가 (선택)` 음성 파일 첨부 화면** (Figma `163:3468` · 선택 상태 `164:9043`). ⚠️ **저장은 없다** — 통화 음성은 어르신의 육성이라 저장하려면 저장소·전사 도입과 개인정보 경계를 새로 정하는 ADR이 먼저다. ADR-0024가 정한 경계는 텍스트 메모까지다. 저장 계약(`onSave`)에 파일이 끼어들지 않는다는 사실을 테스트로 고정했고 ADR-0014 결과 9 · architecture 알려진 문제에 남겼다.
- **시드의 확인 기록을 대상자별로 따로 적는다** (`prisma/seed/history.ts`). 템플릿 5개를 15명에게 돌려 쓰면 브리핑이 서로 구분되지 않아 "이 어르신은 새벽에 밭에 나가십니다"(PRD §10)라는 데모 장면이 성립하지 않는다. 대상자마다 최소 2건을 두어 `반복 신호`와 기록별 대화 요약이 나올 입력을 보장하고, 날짜는 오늘 기준 상대값이라 언제 시드를 돌려도 최근 기록이 된다.

함께 고친 두 가지:

- **확인 기록 상세의 결과 칩이 보이지 않았다.** `bg-status-success`(#1e8e5a) 위 흰 15px 글자는 3.9:1로 AA 미달이고, 실제 렌더에서도 배경이 비어 흰 글자만 남았다. `*-subtle` 배경 + `*-strong` 글자(`RecordGrid`와 같은 짝, 6.3:1)로 바꿨다.
- **기관 마스킹이 유형까지 먹었다.** 앞 이름을 탐욕적으로 먹어 `행복동주민센터`가 `센터`로 남던 것을 `주민센터`로. 어디에 다녀오셨는지는 생활 맥락이고, 어느 기관인지가 식별자다.

관련: FR-12 · PRD F6 · [ADR-0024](docs/adr/0024-subject-context-briefing.md) · [ADR-0014](docs/adr/0014-figma-design-with-domain-terms.md)

## 확인 방법

```bash
npm run db:deploy && npm run db:seed   # 대상자별 확인 기록 이력이 함께 들어간다
npm run dev
```

1. `/today` → 대상자 카드의 `방문하기`/`전화하기` → **위험 사유 아래 인수인계 카드**
2. 카드 chevron → 대상자 정보 → `맥락 브리핑` 탭에서 **같은 3줄**이 나오는지
3. 방문 히스토리의 기록 줄 → 상세 모달의 **결과 칩이 보이는지**(초록 배경 + 진한 초록 글자)
4. `전화하기` → 통화 결과 시트 하단 `기록 추가 (선택)` → 파일 선택 시 파일명 + 지우기 버튼

`AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`가 없으면 브리핑 영역만 비고 기록 원문 화면은 그대로다 (ADR-0024 경계 5).

The plan called for seven enemy types. Five ship, because what makes a roster
work is that no two are answered by the same habit -- and five already covers
standing still, standing at range, killing at arm's length, being caught in the
open, and fighting head-on in a corridor. Two more would have been a longer
list rather than a deeper one, with one level to spread them across. Recorded
as a deviation rather than left as a silent shortfall, and the count is worth
revisiting in G6 against real layouts.

Four new entries in the list of things that will bite you: a type that reuses
another's silhouette is a reskin, `Intent.velocity` is signed, attacking is
tested before retreating, and armour is applied at the shot rather than in
`damage`. All four look correct in a diff and are only wrong in play.

Next up is now G6, whose first requirement is a level registry -- the exit
loops back to E1M1 because there is nowhere for it to go.

author: xroche
body:
An external `.js` file was link-scanned only when the server spelled its Content-Type `application/x-javascript`. `text/javascript` is what IANA recommends, what most servers send, and what httrack's own mime table emits for `.js` and `.mjs`, so the common case was fetched, saved, and never parsed: every URL inside it stayed out of the mirror. Against the local test server on identical script bytes, `application/x-javascript` captured all 7 links; `text/javascript`, `application/javascript`, a `text/javascript; charset=utf-8` header and a `.mjs` module captured none.

The four spellings now live in one `is_javascript_mime_type()` in `htslib.h`, read by `is_hypertext_mime__()`, both `htsparse.c` dispatch sites, `htsindex.c` and the four-way list in `htssinglefile.c`, so the copies cannot drift apart again.

The risk runs the other way: more files get link-scanned now, and the JS scan does pull link-shaped string literals out of ordinary code. I measured that too. A script full of paths with real extensions produces the same four spurious fetches under `application/x-javascript` as under `text/javascript`, so this is the existing scan reaching more files, not new behavior. A link-free script comes back byte-identical: `345_local-js-content-type.test` mirrors one under `text/javascript`, compares it with `cmp` against the same bytes served under a type nothing scans, and pins an `application/json` decoy whose link-shaped string must stay unfetched. The test goes red on master at the first `text/javascript` target.

`36_local-bigcrawl` had a fixture named `decoy.js` asserting that a `text/javascript` script is never scanned. It is now `modern.js`, and the test asserts its target is present.

Surfaced by the JS/SPA work in #302; this is one increment of it, not the whole epic.

The legacy spelling's own count is unchanged: 7 of 7 before and after, on the same fixture. `htsindex.c` does gain behaviour, since a `text/javascript` file previously returned before the keyword loop and now enters it, which matches what the legacy spelling has always done.

author: nometria
body:
Closes #61.

Importing `@dayotter/jobs` constructed six BullMQ `Queue`s at module load. A BullMQ Queue version-checks Redis on construction, so `next build` — which imports the producers through the route handlers — eagerly dialed Redis and logged **hundreds** of `ECONNREFUSED` lines when no Redis was running (build still succeeded; it was noise).

## Fix
- `lazyConnect: true` on the shared ioredis client (defers the client's own connect).
- **Queues are now built lazily** via a memoized factory instead of at import — the connect happens on the first real enqueue (runtime, when Redis is up), not at build/import. No public API change: nothing outside `packages/jobs` referenced the queue consts; only the internal `enqueue*`/`schedule*` helpers did.

The `lazyConnect` flag alone wasn't enough (that was the original issue suggestion) — the Queue constructor still connected for its version check, so both changes are needed.

## Verify
- Before: a `@dayotter/web` build logged **654** `ECONNREFUSED`/"Connection is closed" lines.
- After: **0** — clean build, exit 0.
- `@dayotter/jobs`, `@dayotter/worker`, `@dayotter/web` typecheck clean. Runtime behaviour unchanged (same queue names + shared connection; queues just materialize on first use).

author: medbenmakhlouf
body:
Follow-up to #943 / #981. Each item below was verified against current code
before changing anything; findings that turned out to be invalid are listed at
the bottom with evidence rather than silently applied.

## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) — no public API change

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix
- [x] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: N/A (follow-up to review feedback on #943)

- `find --file-format pot` crashes: `compareKeysToFiles` always called
  `readFile(filePath, { parse: true })`, i.e. `JSON.parse` on a POT file, and
  the `addMissingKeys` write path was JSON-only. POT is broken end to end.
- The webpack plugin never writes scoped keys. `generateKeys` globbed
  `${translationPath}/${scope}*.${fileFormat}`, missing the `/` before `*`, so
  `i18n/admin*.json` can never match the canonical `i18n/admin/en.json` layout
  produced by `buildScopeFilePaths`.
- `buildTable` called `process.exit(1)` / `(2)` from inside a rendering helper,
  truncating its own summary table and killing any programmatic caller. Exit
  code 2 was unreachable whenever missing keys were present.
- The CLI never awaited `buildTranslationFiles()`, so extraction failures
  surfaced as unhandled rejections instead of a deterministic non-zero exit.
- `resolveScopeAlias` popped the trailing path segment unconditionally, so
  `admin/reports` resolved to the parent `admin` scope.
- `marker(key, params?: undefined, scope?)` rejected real params at compile
  time while its JSDoc promised the parameter existed "for compatibility".
- An invalid or missing CLI command logged a prompt and exited 0.

## What is the new behavior?

**POT support in `find`** — `compareKeysToFiles` parses via
`getCurrentTranslation({ path, fileFormat })` and writes via
`createTranslation({ ..., fileFormat, replace: true })`. `writeFile` accepts
`string | object`. The redundant `unflat` option was dropped: both helpers
already read it from the resolved config, so passing it separately was a second
source of truth.

**Webpack plugin scope handling** — added the missing `/` and a `resolvedScopes`
set so scopes resolved through `scopePathMap` are skipped in the default-glob
loop. Both halves are required: the separator fix alone makes the duplicate
merge reachable for the first time. `generateKeys` also now routes through
`getCurrentTranslation` / `createTranslation`, fixing the same JSON-only parse
bug there. This file had **zero** test coverage, which is why the bugs survived;
it now has 13 tests, 7 of them POT-specific.

**Exit codes** — `buildTable` returns a `KeysDetectiveResult` of pure diff facts;
all exit-code policy moved to the CLI, which reads the **resolved** config via
`getConfig()` (the flags can come from `transloco.config.js`, not just argv).
`process.exitCode` replaces `process.exit()` so output is no longer truncated.
Missing (1) still takes precedence over extra (2).

**Async CLI** — dispatch runs from an `async run()` with
`.catch(err => { console.error(err); process.exitCode = 1; })`. Invalid/missing
commands now exit 1. `--input` entries are trimmed, empties dropped, and a
config with no valid path left is rejected.

**Scope alias** — `resolveScopeAlias` receives the configured `langs` and only
strips a trailing segment when it is one of them.

**`marker` params** — widened to a local `MarkerParams = Record<string, any>`
alias, mirroring transloco's `HashMap` without adding a dependency on
`@jsverse/transloco`.

**Types/cleanups** — `build-table` uses `DiffNew<any>[]` / `DiffDeleted<any>[]`
instead of `any[]`; removed a redundant `as object` assertion; added POT
coverage to the remove-extra-keys nested-translation guard.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Published surface is unchanged: only `TranslocoExtractKeysWebpackPlugin` and
`marker` are exported. `buildTable` / `compareKeysToFiles` / `findMissingKeys`
signatures are internal. The `marker` params widening is purely additive —
previously-valid calls still compile.

Behavioral note for CI: an invalid or missing command now exits 1 instead of 0.

## Other information

**Reviewed but intentionally not applied** (verified as invalid, with evidence):

1. *"`createPot` should unflatten before `resolveTranslation`"* — the premise is
   right (`parsePot` does unflatten under `unflat`), but the conclusion is not.
   `resolveTranslation` merges `mergeDeep({}, translation, currentTranslation)`,
   so existing content is applied last and the trailing `flatten()` lets real
   values overwrite the empty extracted placeholders. Measured:

   | case | current | proposed |
   |---|---|---|
   | `{a:{b:'x'}}` + `{'a.b':'','a.c':''}` | `a.b→"x"`, `a.c→""` | same |
   | `{a:{b:'x'}}` + `{'a.b.c':'','a.d':''}` | `a.b.c`, `a.d`, `a.b→"x"` | **`a.b.c` dropped** |

   Unflattening first collapses `a.b.c` into the `a.b` string node. Now locked in
   by a POT+unflat test in `generate-keys.spec.ts`.

2. *"`run-prettier.spec` should throw from the module import"* — implemented and
   reverted: Vitest replaces factory throws *and* rejections with its own error,
   dropping `err.code`, so `runPrettier` warns and the test asserts nothing.

3. *"`addScope` should remove stale reverse mappings"* — reverted after review
   discussion, see the reviewer answers below.

**Already resolved on master, no action needed:** `build-translation-file`
new/modified via `fs.existsSync`, `structural-directive` `$implicit` guard,
`inline-template` iterating all matches, `sanitizeForRegex` metacharacters,
per-instance webpack `init`, anchored marker import selector,
`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, `normalizedGlob` ignore merging, fixture lint
exclusions, `service.extractor` join, perf spec assertions and temp dir,
`resolveConfig` mock path, `spec-utils` `vi.doMock`, `typescript` peer dep.

**Not applicable:** HTMLHint is not used anywhere in this repo.

**Deferred:** typing the webpack plugin's `apply`/`tapPromise` needs `webpack`
as a devDependency (not currently present).

---

# Answers to review comments to PR #981 @shaharkazaz 

## 1. `addScope` — "we are always overriding the values, even if a present scope is passed"

**You're right, and I've reverted it.** Your objection made me check the caller,
which I should have done first:

```ts
// update-scopes-map.ts:114
if (scope && !hasScope(scope)) {
  addScope(scope, alias);
}
```

`addScope` is only ever reached for a scope that isn't registered yet, so the
"same scope, new alias" case the change guarded against **cannot happen**. That
half was dead code.

The one reachable case is two *different* scopes colliding on the same alias,
since `hasScope` checks the scope key only. It's real — `toCamelCase` strips
`/`, `-` and spaces:

```
"admin/reports" -> "adminReports"
"admin-reports" -> "adminReports"
"admin reports" -> "adminReports"
```

But my change didn't fix that, it just swapped one wrong outcome for another.
Today the first scope keeps its forward mapping and its keys get written into
the *second* scope's folder. With my change it loses the mapping entirely and
its keys fall into the global file. Neither is correct — an alias collision is a
configuration error that should **warn**, not silently pick a winner.

So the change is reverted. I kept a `scope.utils.spec.ts` covering
`addScope`/`hasScope`/`getScopes`/`resetScopes`, since the file had no tests at
all, but it asserts only the uncontroversial behavior — nothing about
collisions. Happy to open a separate issue for a collision warning if you think
it's worth it.

## 2. "How is `emitErrorOnExtraKeys` related to the result of `hasExtraKeys`?"

author: steve8708
body:
Directly targets the remaining half of the original report: `www.agent-native.com/<unknown-path>` taking seconds.

## Why keep-warm wasn't working

It was enabled and running every minute — I checked the deploy log, the function is emitted with `schedule: "* * * * *"`. It still didn't help, because **one sequential request holds exactly one container**.

Measured today across 8 probes of production: roughly half reported `cold`, including `/_agent-native/ping`, which does no DB work and still took 2.8–3.0s. Each cold render occupies its container for ~4s, so any request arriving during one lands on a new, cold container. Every low-traffic beta host cold-started once and then stayed warm; production flapped.

Sequential requests reuse the same container and warm nothing extra. **Overlap is the entire mechanism.**

## The change

The scheduled function now issues its warm requests concurrently. Default 3, configurable via `AGENT_NATIVE_KEEP_WARM_CONCURRENCY`, capped at 10 — beyond that you are buying provisioned concurrency through a cron and should decide that deliberately rather than by raising a number.

Partial outcomes stay distinguishable, per the repo's no-silent-coercion rule:

| warmed | result |
| --- | --- |
| all | 204 |
| some | 207, logs the ratio and each failure |
| none | throws |

A partial warm must not read as a clean run, and zero must not read as partial.

## Verification

Two tests **execute the emitted module** rather than asserting on its text. That matters here: this is generated code, and "one request at a time" is precisely the defect — a text assertion like `toContain("await fetch(url")` passes either way.

- **Concurrency**: stubs `fetch`, tracks in-flight count, asserts `maxInFlight === 3`. Sequential emission fails this.
- **Failure semantics**: all-fail throws with the count; partial returns 207.

All 145 `build.spec.ts` tests pass, 202 across `src/deploy/`, all 64 guards pass.

## Scope note

This changes behaviour for **every** app with keep-warm enabled: 3 scheduled invocations per minute instead of 1, and 3 health-probe DB round trips instead of 1. That is the intended trade and it's why the default is 3 rather than something larger.

I can't prove the production effect until this deploys — the measurement I'd want is the cold-hit rate across a probe series before and after. I'll run exactly that once it lands rather than assert the improvement now.

body:
## Verified defect

Protected `develop@9e3e4847510e1e612b48474ba42b177b8ed824df` defines `candidate_worker_conversion_record.recorded_from` as system-recorded bitemporal evidence and defaults it to PostgreSQL `transaction_timestamp()`, but the pre-repair database boundary accepted a caller-supplied historical timestamp when it remained later than the hire decision and bound audit event. That allowed an otherwise valid candidate-to-worker conversion to be backdated in Orgmetra system/knowledge time.

This PR is Orgmetra-only. It does not mutate Keyverse or any other dedicated-writer repository and introduces no cross-service application-table access.

## RED → root-cause repair

RED regression head `9417a9783bc34ae39e82a9c1da4155b843ce5492` constructs a governed tenant-local candidate, Person and Employment, a sealed hire decision evidence set, human-confirmation provenance, and immutable audit/outbox evidence, then attempts an otherwise-valid conversion with `recorded_from = transaction_timestamp() - interval '2 minutes'`. Hosted run `32598511944`, job `97093082138`, failed with `candidate conversion accepted caller-authored historical recorded_from`, proving the database owner boundary accepted forged historical system time.

The repair adds forward migration `database/migrations/0017_candidate_conversion_system_recorded_time.sql`. A `BEFORE INSERT` owner-boundary trigger requires `NEW.recorded_from IS NOT DISTINCT FROM pg_catalog.transaction_timestamp()` and raises SQLSTATE `23514` with a dedicated system-time error otherwise. The existing `DEFAULT transaction_timestamp()` remains the normal write path. The trigger name orders this narrow provenance check before the broader conversion-governance trigger without weakening tenant, decision/evidence, audit/outbox, bitemporal correction, or RLS controls. Migration history is not rewritten.

The regression proves both sides of the contract: a caller-authored historical `recorded_from` is rejected, while an INSERT that omits `recorded_from` succeeds and persists the database transaction timestamp. Foundation inventory/provenance includes the migration and regression so they cannot silently disappear from the canonical contract.

## Review-driven documentation repair

After the repaired code head reached GREEN and the PR entered review, CodeRabbit correctly identified an ambiguity in the completed-review date in `docs/doctoring/candidate-conversion-system-recorded-time-references.md`: the review was performed on 2026-08-23 in Asia/Seoul while the reviewer evaluated the date as 2026-08-22 UTC. Current head `f70f7faea4b5faf20a895eaef165a3474cf80fde` makes the same completed verification explicit as `2026-08-23 in Asia/Seoul (2026-08-22 UTC)` rather than leaving a timezone-ambiguous future-date claim. The PostgreSQL 16 manual was rechecked at the repair boundary; the documented transaction-time semantics remain unchanged. The corresponding CodeRabbit thread is resolved only after the exact-current-head hosted suite returned GREEN.

Fresh Devin observations were also verified against current source rather than accepted mechanically:
- UPDATE does not need the new INSERT trigger because the existing bitemporal-history guard preserves `recorded_from` and permits only governed `recorded_to` closure.
- Migration prefix `0017` does not violate a contiguity invariant; current Orgmetra lanes already occupy 0014–0016 and the repository rejects duplicate prefixes rather than numeric gaps.
- The pre-0017 correction regression intentionally applies migrations 0001–0009 and uses a historical literal to exercise the older correction contract. The actual People API writer obtains PostgreSQL transaction time inside the same transaction and supplies that exact database-authored value when inserting `candidate_worker_conversion_record`, so the new trigger does not break the current production writer. Any future correction insert after 0017 must likewise use the current transaction's system time rather than backdating knowledge time.
- Trigger ordering is correct: `candidate_conversion_a_system_recorded_time_guard` sorts before the broader `candidate_conversion_governance_guard`.
- The focused quality workflow has a narrow path filter, while Foundation CI remains the repository-wide dependency/integration gate for changes to the older migrations and audit helper. The exact-current-head Foundation matrix is GREEN.

Those observations are informational under the verified current implementation and remain unresolved rather than being falsely marked addressed.

## Exact-current-head evidence

Current exact head: `f70f7faea4b5faf20a895eaef165a3474cf80fde`.
Fresh live protected base: `develop@9e3e4847510e1e612b48474ba42b177b8ed824df`.
GitHub reports the PR open, ready-for-review, and mergeable.

Every applicable exact-current-head hosted workflow is terminal GREEN:

The candidate-conversion quality job checked out the exact current head, printed deterministic provenance, executed the historical-system-time rejection and database-default happy path, and proved a clean checkout. No predecessor, queued, in-progress, status-only, model-only, or stale evidence is treated as passing.

Submitted reviews remain COMMENTED only. There is no qualifying formal independent non-author `APPROVE` or `CHANGES_REQUESTED` on this exact head.

## Ownership and merge governance

author: bencan1a
body:
Closes #1

## What changed

Fixtures are the mechanism that lets the streams run in parallel: every stage gets a synthetic version of its own input instead of waiting for the stage upstream of it. The specs are pictures because six agents read each other's test failures, and a readable failing case is worth more than a compact one.

`makeBoard` derives from the picture everything the contract already forces — ids by first appearance, `segCells` tail → head, `segDir` from the terminal stroke, blocking edges from the exit ray — and refuses to guess at the one thing a picture genuinely cannot say (see the note below). `makePath` covers full rectangles only, deliberately: a general Hamiltonian path over an arbitrary mask is S2's own work (#5, #6), and a fixture copy of it would be wrong in the same places as the thing under test.

This is the `contract-change` PR for `test/fixtures/**`. Fixtures and their tests only, no feature work attached, and nothing in `src/core/` is touched.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `makeMask(spec)` builds a Mask from an ASCII-art string (`#` inside, `.` outside, `o` unvisited) and from a plain rectangle
- [x] `makePath(mask)` returns a trivially-correct boustrophedon Hamiltonian path over a rectangular mask
- [x] `makeBoard(spec)` returns a small hand-checkable Board with correct CSR arrays
- [x] A deliberately cyclic board fixture exists, so validation can be tested for the failing case
- [x] Fixtures satisfy the postconditions in docs/CONTRACTS.md — asserted by their own tests
- [x] ASCII specs round-trip: `render(makeMask(s)) === s`

## Definition of done

- [x] `npm run verify` passes locally — 92 tests, coverage gate met
- [x] Generator changes covered by property-based invariant tests — `fast-check` over the ASCII round-trip, rectangle masks, and every rectangle size up to 12×12
- [x] No files touched outside this PR's stream (or a `contract-change` issue is linked) — `test/fixtures/**` only; #1 carries the `contract-change` label
- [x] Determinism preserved — same `(seed, params)` gives an identical board; the builders take no rng
- [x] `src/core/` still imports nothing from `ui/`, `render/`, or `game/` — unchanged
- [x] No new runtime dependency (or justified below)

## Notes for the reviewer

**The picture cannot always determine the walk.** A segment can have a *chord* — two cells adjacent in the grid but not consecutive in the walk — and then its cell set admits more than one ordering. The ordering is what the renderer draws, so a silent guess would surface as a rendering bug with no trail back here. Any segment cut from a space-filling path that doubles back beside itself has a chord, so this is the ordinary case: two of the three segments in `ACYCLIC_BOARD` need it. `makeBoard` throws, names the cell, and asks for `walks: { b: 'WNEE' }`. This is the main design decision in the PR and the one most worth pushing back on.

**The cyclic fixtures are structurally sound in every respect but the cycle** — same CSR, head, direction and colour invariants as a real board. If they were malformed as well, a validator could reject them for the wrong reason and still look correct.

**Checkers, not a validator.** `postconditions.ts` returns lists of violations rather than throwing, so a deliberately-broken fixture can be asserted to have exactly the breakage it is meant to have. It is not `validateBoard` (S4, `src/core/validate`) — when that lands it should be tested *against these fixtures*, not against this file.

**`/code-review` findings.** Four were in this lane and are fixed in `997e8cb`, each with a regression test: `sameSet` read `[2,2]` as equal to `[2,3]`; `greedyClearOrder` threw instead of returning null on an out-of-range edge target; `rayBlockers` looped forever on a direction outside `0..3`; `groupEdges` range-checked the edge source but not its target. Two fall outside this lane and are filed instead — **#38** (`step()` returns `NaN` for an out-of-range direction; `src/core/grid.ts` is a shared file, and it is the root cause that made the `rayBlockers` hang reachable — the fixtures guard against it locally, and the workaround should come out once `step()` is safe) and **#39** (`seed-github.mjs` matches PRs as issues).

**Contract friction, not acted on.** `Board` carries separate `width`/`height` but `GenParams` only has a square `gridSize`, so a non-square fixture cannot describe itself faithfully; `makeBoard` sets `gridSize = max(width, height)`. Worth a `contract-change` only if it actually bites a stream.

**Branch note.** An earlier push landed on `claude/task-start-1-rzdz7f`, which holds the same commits minus the review fixes. `git push --delete` fails against this remote (`send-pack: unexpected disconnect`), so that branch needs deleting from the web UI.

author: morrisstephon51
body:
Two of the three items left open at the end of the last session.

## The scroll cue overlapped the join bar

Reported as a 375–390px problem. Measuring it first put the real band at **320–430px**, worst at 320px where the cue sat 113px underneath the bar.

The cue was not the cause. `.fp-splash` sized itself as `calc(100svh - 5.5rem)`, where `5.5rem` stood for the header — but the header is 88px at no width at all:

| Width | Header | Join bar | Needs | Reserved | Error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ≤467 | 143 | 61 | 204 | 148 | **+56 → overlap** |
| 468–639 | 115 | 61 | 176 | 148 | **+28 → cleared by 7px** |
| 640–675 | 115 | 0 | 115 | 148 | −33 |
| ≥676 | 71 | 0 | 71 | 88 | −17 |

The header wraps from one row to two at ~674px and again at ~466px. So on a phone the section was built 55px taller than the space it had, and its last child — the one affordance telling a first-time visitor there is a page below — landed under the bar. The mobile block's `- 3.75rem` never reached it: the shortfall was upstream of the number being adjusted.

Two smaller faults sat in the same block. The bar was subtracted at `max-width: 767px` while `StickyJoinBar` renders at `sm:hidden`, reserving 60px between 640–767px for a bar that is not on screen. And `.fp-splash-cue` was given `margin-top` twice, 1.5rem then 1rem.

`--fp-header-h` and `--fp-joinbar-h` now carry the measured heights and change where the real elements change. Below 374px the splash headline and lead step down, scoped to the splash — `.fp-display` and `.fp-lead` are site-wide tokens, and the fault is this section fitting a fixed box, not the scale being wrong.

**320–1280px all clear, tightest 11px at 375px.**

Because both wrap points are content wraps rather than media queries, they move when nav copy changes, and CSS cannot observe them. `tests/e2e/splash-cue-clearance.spec.ts` sweeps both wrap points and the bar breakpoint from either side, and asserts the cue is unobscured and still clickable — the property, not the pixel values that implement it. Reverting `--fp-header-h` to `5.5rem` fails it at 375, 390, 414 and 430px.

## Production highs: 4 → 1

Three of the four were duplicate copies rather than the versions this project asked for. `sharp` is a direct dependency at ^0.35.3, but `next` declares `sharp: ^0.34.3`; the ranges do not intersect, so npm kept a second copy at `next/node_modules/sharp@0.34.5` carrying the libvips CVEs — and that nested copy is the one next resolves for image optimization, so the patched top-level sharp was decorative. Same shape for `postcss` (8.4.31 nested under next) and `nanoid` beneath it.

`overrides` collapses each to a single copy, using npm's `$name` form so they track the direct dependency instead of pinning a second number that has to be remembered.

Verified rather than assumed, since forcing a dependency past its parent's declared range is exactly the change that breaks quietly:

- `npm audit --omit=dev`: **4 high → 1 high**
- clean production build passes
- `/_next/image` negotiation intact on sharp 0.35.3 — avif 2,390 B · webp 2,490 B · jpeg 3,628 B

## Still open

`next` itself. Its advisory range covers **every 15.x release**, so no patch exists on this major — the fix is 16.3.0+, a deliberate major upgrade rather than something to fold in here.

## Verification

`tsc` ✓ · `lint` ✓ · 181/181 unit ✓ · 21/21 e2e ✓ · clean production build ✓

author: ghashtag
body:
Three of `Gate ratchet`'s six remaining degradations are one missing Python package.

## The measurement

A clean `python3.12 -m venv` against a **pristine checkout of `main`** — CI's interpreter, CI's tree:

| script | without mpmath | with mpmath |
|---|---:|---:|
| `audit_conformance_selftests.py` | **1** (findings) | 0 |
| `audit_host_importability.py` | **1** (findings) | 0 |
| `witness_takum_small.py` | **2** (needs input) | 0 |

Those are exactly the statuses CI reports. The ratchet derives status from the exit code alone (`{0: clean, 1: findings, 2: needs input}`), so one absent package produced two different-looking verdicts and neither of them mentioned a package.

The remaining three — `audit_gf64_chain`, `audit_hardware_rows`, `witness_tekum_decode_equiv` — exit 0 with **or** without mpmath here, so they are a different cause and are not touched by this.

## They were not quiet about it

```
audit_host_importability:  imports something absent: No module named 'mpmath'
witness_takum_small:       mpmath is not installed; this witness needs it.
                             python3 -m pip install mpmath
```

**The message has been in the log for weeks.** Nobody read it, because the ratchet prints only the *status* — and a status line cannot say "install a package". That is the finding worth keeping: a summary that compresses a diagnosis to one word will hide the one word that would have fixed it.

## Why I nearly missed it

I chased two wrong hypotheses first, and both were refuted by measurement rather than by argument:

- **numpy.** Several oracles import it and the workflow installs no Python packages. Blocking numpy and re-running the loader: 89 oracles still load, `takum8` still present. Refuted.
- **The Python version.** Local 3.14 versus CI's 3.12 reproduced the failure exactly — and then installing mpmath under 3.12 made it pass, so the interpreter was a coincidence of *which* Python had the package, not the cause.

The second is the instructive one: **a hypothesis that reproduces the symptom can still be the wrong cause.** Switching interpreters changed two things at once, and only the second experiment separated them.

## What this does not fix

`audit_gf64_chain` and `audit_hardware_rows` call `gh` for live issue data, which a runner has no credentials for. Passing `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` would give them read access and is the documented way — but it grants a job API access it does not have today, so it is named here rather than done.

author: mohammadp1001
body:
Closes #71

_(Recreated: #84 was auto-closed when its base branch was deleted after #83 merged. Same commit, now based on `main`.)_

## Why

A log recorded what was lifted but not what was *asked for*. The target lived
only on `ProgramExercise` - and those rows are remade from scratch by every
program upload, and detached outright when a program is deleted. So "did I hit
my reps?" quietly became unanswerable as programs came and went.

Same principle already applied to `exerciseId`: the log belongs to the user, not
to the program, so everything needed to read it has to live on it.

## What changed

- **`WorkoutLog.plannedReps`** - the target copied in at save time,
  index-aligned with `sets`.
- **Stored expanded**, not as the slot's raw `reps`. A slot may carry fewer reps
  than sets, and the log screen has always read the shortfall as "repeat the last
  value". Expanding once at write means no reader ever reapplies that rule, and
  the planned set count is simply the array's length. A slot with no target
  expands to nothing rather than a run of zeroes - zero is a target, "unknown"
  is not.
- **Written on create, never on update.** Re-snapshotting on a later edit would
  measure a session against whatever program is active by then - exactly the
  drift this column exists to prevent.
- **Read from the slot, never from the request body.** A client that could name
  its own target could log a session that met a goal nobody set.
- **History shows the shortfall inline**: a set below target is tinted and reads
  `60kg × 6 / 8`. Only misses are marked - the point is to make a missed rep
  visible, not to grade every set.

## Tests

`app/api/logs/planned-reps.test.ts` - the expansion rule including the empty
case, the snapshot surviving deletion of its program, an edit not rewriting it,
and a client-supplied target being ignored.

Full suite: 332 passed, 0 failed. `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean.

author: karanshukla
body:
Implements the "robot command gaps" group from `docs/ROADMAP.md`. Every item is wired into **both** command surfaces (TUI registry and `asher <command>`), with model differences routed through `RobotAdapter` rather than branched inline.

## What's new

| Command | Roadmap | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `night-light color <hex>` | §4 | LR5 `set_night_light_settings(color=…)`. `helpers.hex_colour()` normalises `#RRGGBB`, the 3-digit shorthand, and a missing `#`, and rejects anything else locally — a typo never becomes a cloud round trip. LR3/LR4 report the model limit. |
| `Filter due` row in `info` | §4 | `next_filter_replacement_date` rendered by the new `helpers.fmt_until()` (`2026-09-14 (in 23d)` / `(overdue by 3d)`). Only appears on models that report one. |
| `sleep-schedule set <day\|all> <HH:MM> <HH:MM>` | §8 | LR5 writes per day or every day. LR3 sends the start time only — its 8h sleep is fixed in firmware — and says the wake time was ignored, and refuses a single day rather than silently applying it to all seven. LR4 has no schedule setter in the API at all, so it points at the Whisker app. |
| `sleep-schedule disable` | §8 | Rides on the `set_sleep(False)` each model already implements instead of repeating the dispatch. |
| `history [count\|all] --type <kind>` | §11 | LR5 `get_activities(activity_type=…)`, reduced to `Activity` objects the shared `format_activity()` already renders. Friendly words map via `constants.ACTIVITY_TYPES` (`cat` → `PET_VISIT`, `clean` → `CYCLE_COMPLETED`, …); unknown words pass through uppercased so a new cloud type stays reachable. LR3/LR4 say filtering is LR5-only rather than silently returning everything. |

§8's "contextual sleep/wake toggle" was already implemented in the adapters — the roadmap entry was stale, and is now marked done with a note on where the dispatch lives.

## Notes

- **`day_of_week` numbering.** pylitterbot's `set_sleep_mode` docstring says `0=Monday`, but it matches the value against the `dayOfWeek` field of the schedule the cloud returned, and those follow the `DayOfWeek` enum (Sun=0). The adapter converts to the enum's numbering; there's a comment and a test pinning it.
- **Shared grammar.** Day names, `parse_clock()`/`parse_day()`, the `--type` flag split and the type-name map moved into `helpers`/`constants`, so the TUI and headless surfaces parse the same words instead of each rolling their own. `_DAY_NAMES` was duplicated in two modules; it's now one `helpers.DAY_NAMES`.
- **argparse.** `--type` is declared on the `history` subparser (so `--help` documents it) and folded back into the handler's word list by `_handler_args()`, keeping handlers identical across both surfaces.

## Out of scope

Per the scoping discussion: UI/UX gaps (§11–12), pet features (§7), Feeder Robot support (§5), and the three large infrastructure items — standalone binary (§16), remote MCP connector (§26), multi-robot tabs (§11) — are untouched and still open in the roadmap.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/` — **976 passed** (881 before; +95 new tests covering the adapters, both command surfaces, the pure helpers, and the argparse flag)
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` / `mypy` — clean
- `asher history --help`, `asher sleep-schedule --help`, `asher night-light --help` render the new grammar; the TUI `help` table stays column-aligned

README command tables, `docs/ROADMAP.md`, and the `helpers.py`/`constants.py` lines in `CLAUDE.md` are updated to match.

body:
## What

Implements the code-tractable items from the six-perspective evaluation's player-impact top 10 ([docs/evaluation/summary.md](../blob/main/docs/evaluation/summary.md), PR #32), in impact order. Nine commits, one per work package.

## The top 10, item by item

| # | Item | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Practice mode + practice lagoon | ✅ shipped |
| 2 | Container Chaos end-to-end | ⏭️ not attempted — blocked on the Blender terrain re-grade (the content-root `.blend` is a 2-point-spline stub); filling its track data before the field can even finish would be motion without progress |
