| 10 | Score the finish | ✅ shipped |

Plus from the per-discipline lists: lobby connect time-box (Net #6), README two-tab-probe correction (Net #5), boost ignition voice so the wave chord stays reserved (Audio #4), master limiter + shared noise buffer (Audio #6), catalog honesty pins (GD #9), and CI least-privilege + SHA pins (Sec #2/#3 — the security review's "cheapest real win").

## Highlights

**Practice mode (summary #1, per the 2026-08-22 maintainer decision).** A 4th PRACTICE tile (pre-focused with a NEW HERE? badge until `tutorialCompleted` latches), the practice screen offering the coached First Run plus the new **practice lagoon** — an asset-light JSON venue (loads on any unhydrated clone) whose loop lays the skills out in ride order: throttle/cruise straight → heavy rolling-swell LAUNCH lane → TRICK table → TUCK rollers → a 345 m drift sweep sized for SMT+. An 8-beat station script rides the new per-track `script-catalog` (sandbar First Run byte-identical), with new `notifyTuck` / best-launch-quality director channels. It commits as `?race=1&track=practice-lagoon&tutorial=1&ai=0` — zero new boot plumbing. The venue doubles as the standing hard-rule-2 dev-test scene; `tests/e2e/practice-lagoon.spec.ts` boots it and clears the first two beats with real input.

**Takeoff grader sign bug (found implementing #3).** `TAKEOFF_IDEAL_PITCH_RAD` shipped as `+0.24`, but in the codebase's pitch convention (`asin(-fwd.y)`, positive = nose DOWN — verified against `quatRotate` and the thrust code's `fwd.y > 0` = climbing) that graded a 14° *dive* off the lip as the perfect pop, and a proper nose-up pop as ~0. Masked because the takeoff verdict was cosmetic-only — the exact gap the economy fix closes, which is how it surfaced. Now `-0.24`, with the convention documented at `pitchAngleFromQuat` and a quat-path regression pin.

**Jump economy.** The landing edge pays a landing-dominant combined jump score (0.65/0.35): perfect jump = 0.75 meter (out-earning one SMT in gained speed-time, pinned both ways in unit tests), clean jumps auto-vent a 1.5×/1.2 s BoostEffect burst (pad merge semantics) so the reward lands without the extra button press. A single jump still pays under one UMT — drift keeps corner identity; wave tracks out-earn through repetition. ⚠️ Numbers were chosen against the drift-tiers math, not playtested — this wants a headed feel pass.

**AI wave mastery.** Rivals now shape takeoffs into the graded pop band (closed-loop hold), pitch landings toward the surface tangent (pure `decideAILandingPitch`, using the normal the existing `sampleSurface` call already returns), and spend the meter on straights (`decideAIVent`, releasing into drift-worthy corners). Difficulty-gated with the existing Infinity/zero short-circuits: Casual stays out, Standard demonstrates, Hard is the role model.

**Audio pass.** Positional one-shots (distance gain half-volume at 40 m + pan; weapon spawns eid-diffed so same-frame multi-drops stop collapsing into one sound and each gets a position), a 2-voice rival engine pool, dedicated countdown ladder, position-aware finish stinger (win/podium/finish/DNF; TT celebrates a new all-time best), a cup fanfare on the `?podium` scene (which now installs the soundtrack radio — it previously had no audio engine at all), a boost ignition voice so `wavePump`'s chord again means "you read the water", a master-bus limiter, and one shared noise buffer replacing per-shot AudioBuffer allocation. `tools/convert-music.mjs` gained two-pass EBU R128 loudnorm (−14 LUFS / −1.5 dBTP, linear mode); all 14 opus files were regenerated locally.

**Multiplayer honesty.** Snapshot positions int16→int32 behind new tag `0x03` (the ±327.67 m fuse the encoder's own comment warned about is defused; legacy `0x02` still decodes; the relay is passthrough, no relay change; old clients warn-and-drop unknown tags). Pickups no longer spawn in MP rooms — items were per-tab fiction ("I hit him and nothing happened"); revert the one-line gate when M10.13 puts combat events on the wire. The lobby connect is time-boxed at 10 s with a can't-reach-the-relay explainer (dev builds name `pnpm party:dev`), and ESC finally appears in the footer keys.

**Trust surfaces.** Mayday Bay's card said 1 lap while the JSON runs 3 — fixed, and `catalog-consistency` now pins card laps === JSON `lapsToFinish` for every venue with a JSON twin, plus a test banning cut-mechanic (anti-grav) copy in live catalog data (Liberty's set-piece re-worded per its track doc). `track-themes.md`'s real-world-place lock carries a superseded note for the fictional-city pivot. README no longer claims the two-tab probe "is not yet automated".

## Test plan

All gates run locally on this branch (hydrated clone):
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` — exit 0 (1,381 warnings; main's baseline is 1,358, the +23 are the blessed `noNonNullAssertion` class in new code)
- [x] `pnpm test` — **1506 passed** (155 files; +55 new tests: launch-grade economy pins, AI wave-mastery helpers, practice venue/station pins, script catalog, director tuck/launch channels, snapshot v2 + legacy decode, spatial audio, catalog consistency)

- [x] **Headed Playwright** (hard rule 2, `E2E_PORT=5307`): practice-lagoon boot + coached-session spec, both practice menu commits, the full 23-spec menu suite, m9-audio (one boot-timing flake, passed on retry with zero console errors)
- [x] Two-tab `m10-11-state-sync`: the race-lock + convergence tests pass through the new codec; the "lobby cohort" test fails **identically on clean `main` on this machine** (start-barrier timeout — pre-existing environmental issue with that spec's self-launched browsers, not this change)
- [x] `pnpm gen:music` re-run end-to-end (two-pass loudnorm verified on all 14 tracks)

## Notes for the reviewer

- **Feel numbers need a headed pass**: jump payout weights/scales, clean-jump burst, AI landing gains (`landingPitchGain` 2.2/3.5), vent thresholds (0.9/0.55), rival engine level (0.045), spatial ref distance (40 m). All chosen from the constants math, flagged inline as tune-with-playtest.

The first release to reach the candidate gate got there through plan, full verification, **three image builds**, the manifest and a drafted tag — then every step of the gate failed on:

```

```

## The same trap, second visit

[#81](https://github.com/0feklevy/cebu/pull/81) fixed the workspace-relative *JSON* paths in this job and added a test for them. **Nobody checked the `cd`s.** All five said `cd podcast-saas/deploy`, which under `defaults.run.working-directory: podcast-saas` resolves to `podcast-saas/podcast-saas/deploy`.

The gate failed closed and the deploy was correctly skipped — which is the system working. It still cost twenty minutes of builds to learn something a string check catches, so the new guard is written against **every job that inherits the default**, not against this one: the trap belongs to the workflow, not to a job.

## And the mask that masked nothing

The gate generates a throwaway RSA key so the backend's Firebase parser has something syntactically real to chew on, and masks it with `::add-mask::$key`.

`::add-mask::` registers **one exact string** and replaces it where it appears contiguously. A PEM is multi-line, and the runner prints a step's `env:` block across lines — so the mask matched nothing and the entire key appeared in the failing run's log, directly beneath a comment of mine asserting that *"a PEM appearing unmasked in a build log is a pattern worth never establishing"*.

**That key is generated per job and authenticates nothing, so nothing leaked.** The pattern is what is fixed: the same code holding a real credential would have leaked it, and the comment would still have said it was safe. Each *line* is registered now, which is what actually replaces a multi-line value.

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| the repo-root `cd` comes back | 1 failed |
| the blob mask comes back | 1 failed |

body:
The CSS, fonts and markup in this repo were a 2014 snapshot of Cayman, produced
by GitHub's old automatic page generator and carried here ever since with no way
to pick up fixes. Cayman is now a Jekyll theme at
[pages-themes/cayman](https://github.com/pages-themes/cayman), so this replaces
the snapshot with a pinned reference to it.

* `index.html` becomes `index.md`, content unchanged from #10.
* The three vendored stylesheets go. 82 insertions against 895 deletions.
* Pinned at `v0.2.0` rather than floating, so the site cannot change appearance
  without a commit here.

Worth being clear about what this does not buy. Upstream has had no release
since July 2021, so this is about sitting on a maintained base rather than
gaining features, and Cayman still has no dark mode. The page should look the
same.

## Two things to check after merging

I could not build this locally. There is no Jekyll toolchain on this machine and
the system Ruby is 2.6, so the first real build is the one GitHub Pages runs.

1. **Watch the Pages build.** Adding `_config.yml` switches this repo from being
   served as static files to being built by Jekyll, and a build failure is the
   risk. Pages currently reports `build_type: legacy` serving from `main`, which
   includes `jekyll-remote-theme`.
2. **Check `/version` still works.** The application's update check fetches it:

   ```
   curl https://www.tvrenamer.org/version
   ```

   It must return a bare version number, currently `1.0`. `version.html` carries
   no front matter, so Jekyll copies it through untouched, as it does the
   `downloads`, `issues` and `source` redirect pages. That is worth confirming
   rather than assuming, since breaking it silently disables update checks for
   every install.

author: davimoraisdev
body:
## Bloco 5b — order-service consome `payment.captured`

Fecha a integração payment ↔ order. O 5a fez o payment **produzir** o evento;
aqui o order **consome** e leva o pedido a `PAGO`.

### A decisão que organiza o bloco

O TECH_DEBT dizia "no padrão do notification-service", que reivindica o evento no
Redis antes de processar. **Não foi adotado**, e o motivo não é preferência.

Marca de idempotência e efeito precisam commitar juntos. Em dois armazenamentos
independentes não existe "juntos": um dos dois é o primeiro, e existe um instante
entre eles. Com o Redis primeiro, um crash nesse instante deixa a marca gravada e o
efeito não — a redentrega lê "duplicata", dá `ack`, e **o pedido fica `PENDENTE`
para sempre, sem erro, sem log e sem DLQ**.

O notification usa Redis porque o efeito dele é enviar e-mail, que não tem
transação para participar. Ali é a melhor opção disponível, não a melhor opção em
geral. O efeito do order é escrita no Postgres, então marca e efeito cabem na mesma
transação e o instante intermediário deixa de existir. O order também não tem
`ioredis` nas dependências — adotar o padrão de lá significaria adicionar
infraestrutura para obter uma garantia pior.

### O invariante

**Linha no inbox existe se e somente se o efeito aconteceu.**

Isso obriga um detalhe que é fácil errar: desfechos que vão para a DLQ e não
produzem efeito — pedido inexistente, valor divergente — precisam **desfazer** o
insert do inbox, não commitá-lo. Como o insert é a primeira operação da transação,
isso é feito lançando um erro de controle (`SemEfeito`) traduzido do lado de fora.
Commitar a marca de um evento sem efeito reintroduziria exatamente o buraco do
parágrafo anterior, dentro de um banco só.

### Binding estrito, não `payment.*`

Com binding largo, `payment.refunded` chegaria aqui sem handler e as duas saídas
seriam ruins: `ack`-e-ignora é perda silenciosa, DLQ empilha operação normal numa
fila de erro.

Com binding em `payment.captured` o evento simplesmente não roteia — e o publisher
do payment tem `mandatory` + `basic.return` desde o 5a, então ele fica `PENDING` e
logado na origem. Falha visível em quem publica é melhor que silêncio em quem
consome.

### Divergência deliberada do notification-service

O notification faz `connection.on('close') → process.exit(1)`. Correto para um
worker puro: reiniciar é a recuperação.

O order serve a API de pedidos. Matar o HTTP porque o RabbitMQ caiu troca
degradação parcial (eventos atrasam) por indisponibilidade total (ninguém cria
pedido). O consumidor loga, agenda reconexão e o Express segue atendendo.

### Refatoração necessária

`updateOrderStatus` abria a própria `$transaction`. O miolo foi extraído para
`aplicarTransicao(tx, ...)`, e `updateOrderStatus` virou o embrulho — assinatura e
comportamento inalterados, validados pelos 137 testes existentes sem nenhuma
alteração neles. O consumidor abre a *sua* transação e chama `aplicarTransicao` com
o mesmo `tx`.

Efeito colateral bom: a transição para `PAGO` enfileira `order.status_changed` na
mesma transação, então o notification é avisado sem código novo.

### Tabela de decisões

| Situação | Ação | Motivo |
|---|---|---|
| Reentrega do mesmo evento | `ack` | `@unique` do inbox aborta tudo; efeito não repete |
| Payload inválido | `nack-dlq` | Retry nunca conserta JSON quebrado |
| Pedido inexistente | `nack-dlq` | O payment só emite captura para pedido consultado antes |
| Pedido já `PAGO`/`ENVIADO`/`ENTREGUE` | `ack` | Efeito já aconteceu; `ENVIADO → PAGO` nunca vira válido, requeue seria loop |
| Pedido `CANCELADO` | `ack` + `PendingCompensation` | Dinheiro capturado exige estorno, não retry |
| Falha do banco | `nack-requeue` | Indisponibilidade momentânea não pode custar o evento |
| Routing key fora do binding | `nack-dlq` | Binding é estrito; outra key é topologia adulterada |
| Valor divergente | `nack-dlq` | Violação de contrato entre serviços; exige olho humano |

### Detalhes que valem review

- **`P2002` não é uma coisa só.** Pode vir do `@unique` do inbox (duplicata real →
  `ack`) ou do unique parcial de `pending_compensations` (corrida → precisa
  reprocessar). Só o primeiro vira duplicata; qualquer outro é relançado e vira
  requeue. `P2002` desconhecido cai no lado conservador.
- **`findFirst` antes de criar a compensação, em vez de `create` com `catch`
  P2002.** Em Postgres, erro dentro de transação envenena a transação inteira: o
  `catch` daria a ilusão de ter tratado enquanto o próximo statement falharia. O
  padrão create-e-trata existe em `registrarCompensacaoPendente`, mas lá o `create`
  é solo, fora de transação.
- **Dead-letter declarada antes da fila principal.** Argumentos de fila durável são
  imutáveis; apontar para uma DLX inexistente faria mensagens rejeitadas sumirem, e
  corrigir depois exigiria recriar a fila.
- **`changedBy` é fixo (`'payment-service'`), nunca lido do payload.** Aceitar a
  autoria da mensagem deixaria quem publica no exchange escolher quem assina a
  trilha de auditoria.
- **Comparação de valor com aritmética `Decimal`, não `Number(total) * 100`.** Ponto
  flutuante transformaria divergência de contrato em falha intermitente.

### Verificação

- `npm test` — 143 testes, 12 suítes, verdes
- `npm run test:integration` — 45 testes, 5 suítes, verdes
- `npm run build` e `npx tsc --noEmit` — limpos
- **Bateria de 10 sabotagens** com a árvore commitada: todas derrubaram o alvo
  exato, nenhuma passou vazia, `git status --porcelain` vazio ao fim de cada uma.
  Inclui T1 (falsificar o `eventId` → só o G2 cai, provando que a dedupe vem da
  constraint) e T3-bis (trocar o `throw` por `return` mantendo a detecção → só o G6
  cai, isolando o rollback da detecção).

### Declarado como NÃO coberto

- O laço de reconexão e o `consume` não têm teste — mesma natureza da dívida já
  registrada para `startOutboxRelay`/`stopOutboxRelay`.
- **A discriminação do `P2002` não tem teste.** Confirmado pela sabotagem T5: aceitar
  qualquer `P2002` como duplicata não derruba nada. Registrado no TECH_DEBT antes de
  rodar a bateria, não depois.
- O payload de `payment.captured` não tem campo `type`, então a checagem cruzada
  `type` × routing key que o notification faz não existe aqui. O binding estrito faz
  o papel. Adicionar `type` é mudança no payment-service — Fase 10.

### Fora de escopo

Correção do publisher do order-service (achados 4.2/4.4/4.5 do 5a) — PR próprio, já
registrado. Teste com RabbitMQ real — Bloco 8.

author: vadi2
body:
#### Brief overview of PR changes/additions

- `phpTable()`'s `__newindex` now tests `self[key] == nil` rather than `not self[key]` to decide whether a key is new.
- Assigning `nil` to a key that never existed no longer registers one.

#### Motivation for adding to Mudlet

`not self[key]` is true for a stored `false` as well as for an absent key, so overwriting a `false` appended a second copy of that key to the order list. `pairs()` then yielded it twice, and the delete branch - which only removes one entry - could never clear it.

#### Other info (issues closed, discussion etc)

Closes #10137.

**Test case:** `t = phpTable({flag = false}); t.flag = true` then iterate `t:pairs()` - `flag` appears once, and `t.flag = nil` removes it. Three new `Other_spec` cases cover it; all three fail if `Other.lua` is reverted.

author: utkarshnigam1221
body:
Follow-up to #246. That PR made a re-check settle an abandoned payment, and it works
for new ones — verified in dev. It does not repair the orders that were already stuck
before it shipped, and clicking Check Payment on them still leaves the list showing
PENDING however many times you click.

## Why the already-stuck ones are different

Their payment record is already terminal. The webhook, as it behaved before #246,
settled the payment to FAILED and never touched the order. So `reconcile` calls
`HandlePaymentFailure`, `resolvePayment` sees FAILED — not in `{INITIATED, PENDING}` —
reports it already-processed and returns before anything reaches the order. A new
abandoned checkout leaves the payment INITIATED, the handler runs, and
`failOrderPayment` writes the order. Hence one works and the other cannot.

This is confirmed against prod (read-only). Two orders show the pattern, and the
timing is what identifies it:

| order | lines | reserved | released | gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `29d63752…2ef4` | 3 | 18:38:22.833Z | 18:53:26.449Z | 15.1 min |
| `d7a7c69f…6686` | 1 | 18:34:40.714Z | 18:49:55.914Z | 15.3 min |

Both released at the 15-minute mark, which is PhonePe's Standard Checkout order
expiry, not a human cancelling. No COMMIT rows, and `source_id` is empty on every
RELEASE so no refund was involved. Every other caller of `ReleaseOrderStock` is
either an immediate rollback measured in seconds or an admin action — and both admin
paths were themselves broken that day, Cancel Order 400ing on the missing reason and
the dropdown not offering CANCELLED. The expiry webhook is the only path left.

Worth stating plainly: **no stock was leaked.** All four affected products currently
read `reserved_qty = 0, available_qty = 3`. The old failure path released correctly.
The only damage is the order's stale copy of the payment status.

## The change

`CheckProviderStatus` converges the order itself after reconciling, instead of
assuming a handler did it. Only the two outcomes the gateway reports are mapped —
refund statuses belong to the refund flow, and a payment still in flight has nothing
to copy. It writes only on a real difference, so re-checking an order that already
agrees touches nothing.

Confined to the re-check, which is the admin explicitly asking for the record to be
made right. Relaxing `resolvePayment` would have repaired these too, but it would
also let a replayed webhook re-emit `payment_outcome` and double-count it.

`order.Status` is still left alone. These stay PENDING with a FAILED payment, and
cancelling them remains a decision rather than a side effect.

## After deploying

Click Check Payment once on each stuck order and the payment column flips to FAILED.
It is retroactive, not forward-only.

Note the orders list renders two badges. The **Payment** column is what this fixes;
the **Order Status** column stays PENDING by design.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./internal/...` — all pass. `TestCheckProviderStatus` now covers five
      cases, including `repairs an order the old failure path left behind` (payment
      already FAILED, order stale → order written, no stock released because the old
      path already did) and `writes nothing when payment and order already agree`.
- [x] `POSTGRES_DSN=… CI=1 go test ./internal/repository/postgres/` — pass.
- [x] `golangci-lint run internal/...` — 0 issues.
- [x] Prod inspected read-only: three `SELECT`s, no writes.
- [x] Not yet exercised against live PhonePe.

author: jphutchins
body:
Closes #179. Replaces #212, which carried the same flip plus two mechanisms that are now tracked separately — see **Scope** below.

## The question dissolves rather than being answered

#179 asked whether an outdated inline review can be resolved from the pipeline. It can't — GitHub exposes no API to resolve a review thread, and the pipeline's only lever is to **minimize** the previous round's comments. On a PR that iterates, superseded threads accumulate on the diff and nothing the reviewer does retires them.

An inline thread is a human-only surface a later round can neither revise nor resolve. The sticky is one comment each round rewrites in place. So the sticky is the surface that can stay true, and the default flips.

## `inline` is render-only

It reaches exactly two decisions — what `buildInlineComments` produces, and which `InlineDisposition` the sticky renders — and **gates no API call**:

| | `inline: false` (new default) | `inline: true` |
|---|---|---|
| sticky | lists every visible finding | lists the strays; in-diff ones are on the diff |
| review object | **posted**, body-only | **posted**, with `comments[]` |
| prior reviews dismissed | yes | yes |
| stale threads minimized | yes | yes |

The review object is always posted: it's the trail from the PR to the sticky and to the run (#204), and the run is what will carry the whole review in its summary (#205). Body-only is a shape `post()` already supported (#43).

Because dismiss and minimize run unconditionally, flipping a repo to the new default also clears the threads its previous rounds left on the diff — the closest thing to "resolving" them the API allows.

Two deliberate omissions: the findings heading drops its `outside the diff` qualifier, which no longer describes anything, and there is **no** "inline is off" banner — it's the default mode, and announcing a default on every review forever is noise.

## One default, not two

The CLI flag and the workflow input are both off, `--inline` the single opt-in. The opt-in is probed against `post --help`, because `CODE_REVIEW_VERSION` pins the **published** CLI: between this merging and the next release it names a CLI that has never heard of the flag, and citty ignores an unknown option silently rather than failing. The probe is anchored on a terminator so `--inline-template` can't satisfy it.

## Scope: what I removed, and why

Earlier revisions (#212) also carried a comment-size shed and a breadcrumb-failure tolerance. Both were added in response to review findings *about this change* — and over four rounds they generated more findings than they closed, while the flip itself stayed untouched:

```
0.13 → 1.77 → 1.00 → 0.32 → 1.51 → 3.25
```

The last round's three minors were all in that machinery, including one at likelihood 1.0 (a test assertion that could never match). That's churn, not convergence, so they're out of this PR:

- the size shed → **#214**, which also notes that **#217** drops the ~32KB embedded blob from the sticky and lands in the same release. That removes far more size pressure than the shed recovered, so designing the shed before #217 was the wrong order.
- the breadcrumb-failure tolerance → **#223**, since it's a pre-existing robustness gap this change merely made more prominent.

What's left is 238 lines including tests, against 548 before, with `post.ts` at +55 instead of +284.

> [!WARNING]
> **LLM Disclosure**
>
> This pull request was authored by claude-opus-5[1m] on behalf of @JPHutchins, implementing the `inline=false` default she decided on. She corrected an earlier revision where I had made the review object conditional on the flag; the render-only framing above is hers.

author: protonicwave
body:
## What changed

The cash/card toggle on the Today console is gone. The full width **Add trip** button is now two halves, **Add cash** and **Add card**, so the payment method is the button he presses rather than a setting he has to set first.

- New `AddTripActions` component, built by mapping `FARE_PAYMENT_METHODS` and reading `PAYMENT_META`, so no method name is written as a literal and a third method would need only the domain constant. It composes `ui/Button`, so the amber gradient, the pressed transform and the disabled treatment keep exactly one definition.
- The method is an argument, never state. `TodayScreen` no longer holds a `method`, and `PaymentToggle.tsx`, `lastMethod.ts` and the `taxi:lastMethod` storage key are deleted outright, along with the `.pay-zone` / `.pay-seg` / `.pay-seg-btn` / `.pay-cap` rules.
- After a save the row shows a green confirmation naming the method that landed. It is a covering layer, so both halves stay mounted and keyboard focus is never dropped, and it is hidden from assistive technology because the existing toast already announces the save.
- The amount row was a three column grid balancing the toggle on its right. With nothing left to balance it is now simply the centred readout.

## Why

The toggle was two 34 x 30px icon buttons, under the 44px touch floor and the smallest targets on a screen full of large ones, with the method word carried only by a 9px caption. Growing them was not an option: Today is a fixed one screen tab and the keypad tray's 250px floor means every pixel the toggle gained came off the keys. Splitting the action instead turns two taps into one and takes the target from roughly 1,000px2 to roughly 9,000px2.

## The trade-off

Today a wrong toggle tap is harmless until Add is pressed. After this change a wrong tap saves the wrong method straight away. That is mitigated rather than denied: the halves are separated by a gap, the confirmation names what was actually recorded, and the edit sheet keeps its roomy **Paid by** chips so a mistake stays a one tap fix. A confirm step would have given back the tap this change exists to remove, so there isn't one.

Nothing downstream moves: `paymentMethod` on the fare, the trip tags, the Stats split, the Firestore rules and legacy fares with no method are all untouched.

## Verified

Measured in Chrome against a build of `main` for comparison, at 320, 375 and 390 wide:

- **Height budget.** The save row is 59.5px, byte for byte the single Add button's own box. The minimum viewport height at which the console does not scroll is 772px both before and after, so the change adds no height at all. An earlier revision was 3.19px taller and is fixed in this branch.
- **Render count.** One React commit per digit typed, the same as before.
- **Themes.** Light and dark against every accent preset and a custom hue. The halves stay the primary colour in all twelve and never pick up the category accent; they compute identically to the button they replace.
- **Motion and input.** Pressed transform fires, the confirmation animates in and clears after 900ms, the animation is dropped under reduced motion by the existing global rule, tab order runs left to right and Enter activates.
- **Offline.** With the network down the fare still records its method, the confirmation still names it, and no failure toast appears.
- **Bundle.** Smaller, not larger: the app chunk goes 133.01 to 132.70 kB and the stylesheet 69.98 to 69.90 kB, because the deleted toggle and storage module outweigh the new component.
- Lint clean, build clean, 452 tests green.

Still to check on the driver's phone: the real feel of the two halves in the cradle, and whether the gap between them is enough to make a mis-tap rare.

author: sedoglia
body:
v4.5.6 is published, but nothing at the top of either README led to it: the version badge linked to the repository root — where the reader already is.

## What changed

- The **version badge** now links to `releases/latest`.
- A line under the intro paragraph points at the same place, naming what is there: the `.mcpb` bundle, the release notes and the `.sha256` to verify the download.

```
📦 Ultima release: v4.5.6 — bundle .mcpb pronto da installare, con le note
   di rilascio e il file .sha256 per verificarlo.
```

## Why `releases/latest` and not `releases/tag/v4.5.6`

Same reason v4.3.1 moved the download links there: a hardcoded tag goes stale at the next release, and nobody notices until someone downloads a bundle two versions old. `releases/latest` currently 302s to `releases/download/v4.5.6/…` and will keep following the newest release on its own.

Only the version *named in the text* has to move at release time, next to the badge that already carried it.

## And since that adds a sixth place the version is written down

The release section of both READMEs now lists every one of them — `package.json`, `manifest.json`, `SERVER_VERSION` in `src/utils/constants.ts` (the one sent in the MCP handshake), and the badge plus the release line in each README — and says explicitly that the download links are *not* among them, so nobody "helpfully" pins those to a tag later.

body:
Workflow run 32602436759 (Issue #106) failed at the "Push Branch and Open Pull Request" step: `git push origin HEAD:agent-exec/106` was rejected as non-fast-forward, aborting the job before a PR could be opened.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/agent-02-execute.yml`** — "Push Branch and Open Pull Request" now force-pushes the `agent-exec/<issue>` branch instead of a plain push.

## Root Cause

"Create Working Branch" always rebuilds `agent-exec/<issue>` from scratch via `git checkout -B` at the start of every run — it never carries forward remote history. When an earlier run for the same Issue had pushed that branch and then failed before `gh pr create` succeeded, the remote branch retained unrelated commits. The next run's plain push was then rejected as non-fast-forward.

The branch is single-purpose and disposable by design, and the guard step earlier in the job already confirms no PR exists for it before this point runs, so force-pushing is safe.

author: coinerd
body:
W3 of v1.00.13 (#886) — request lifecycle ownership: headers, cleanup, structured failures (RL-5/RL-6/RL-7).

## What
- **Structured failure context** (`llm/http-helpers.rkt`): `build-network-failure-context` (kind / http-status / redacted response-headers / parsed retry-after-ms). Response headers are REDACTED to the retry-relevant subset (`Retry-After`, `x-ratelimit-*`) — authorization/cookie values never reach failure metadata or logs.
- **`parse-retry-after-header`**: delta-seconds AND HTTP-date forms. The date parser is timezone-free (civil-calendar conversion — `find-seconds` is locale-dependent) with a deterministic `#:now-ms` clock seam; past dates clamp to 0.
- **Deterministic port ownership** (RL-6): `make-provider-http-request` closes every response port exactly once — success, status-check failure, read timeout, request timeout (cleanup passed to the request-timeout wrapper), cancellation (dynamic-wind post-thunk). Provider errors from status checkers are re-raised with the structured context attached.
- **`current-provider-http-sendrecv`**: injectable HTTP boundary for the cleanup-contract tests.
- **Retry consumes structure, not strings** (RL-7): `structured-retry-after-ms` (auto-retry) reads the context hash only; `with-auto-retry` no longer feeds the exception message to `parse-retry-after`. `provider-error-context` accessor exported from provider-errors.
- Duration contracts widened `exact-positive-integer?` → `positive?` (matches downstream wrappers; enables sub-second test durations).
- **Tests**: failure-context (429/Retry-After fixture, redaction, HTTP-date) and response-cleanup (close-once matrix across success/status-raise/read-timeout/request-timeout/cancel) suites promoted green; heartbeat contract split to `test-stream-liveness-classification.rkt` (@not-test until W4).

## Evidence
14 focused suites green: context, cleanup, http-helpers, auto-retry, adaptive-retry, retry-telemetry, stream, openai, anthropic, azure, gemini, policy, conformance, partial-result-preservation. Fast gate green (after arch-parameter registration of the new injection seam).

Closes #9473 (+ subs #9474–#9477). Plan §6 W3.

author: davidmenggx
body:
Functions on a `LowCardinality` column already run over the dictionary instead of over the rows. If every dictionary key gives the same answer, then so does every row, so the result is now returned as a `ColumnConst` and `WHERE` and `PREWHERE` drop or keep the whole block at once. Headers are computed by running the same functions on an empty block, so no constant is produced there (it would be taken for a real one).

`FilterDescription::preprocessFilterColumn` also unwraps `LowCardinality` inside a constant before expanding it, so building the filter no longer touches every row either.

`isConstant` now returns `1` for such expressions.

Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115296

author: 404khai
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Android Google registration flow that was incorrectly surfacing `Google sign-in was canceled`, and consolidates the backend into this repository as a monorepo.

## What changed

- Moved the complete NestJS/Prisma backend into `Keihatsu-API/` as tracked monorepo content.
- Removed the nested API repository metadata so `Keihatsu-API/` no longer has an independent Git origin.
- Made Google Sign-In initialization a single awaited operation before authentication.
- Allow the Google server client ID to be supplied through `GOOGLE_SERVER_CLIENT_ID` for builds without generated Firebase configuration.
- Added clearer diagnostics for cancellation, provider/client configuration failures, token exchange failures, and backend responses.
- Made the API base URL configurable through `API_BASE_URL` for device and deployment builds.
- Included the Prisma migration history required by the Google-authenticated user flow.

## Root cause and configuration

The debug APK signing certificate SHA-1 was missing from the Firebase Android app, so Google Play services returned a cancellation-like result before an account could be selected. The debug SHA-1 was registered in Firebase and the generated local `google-services.json` was refreshed. The release/upload SHA-1 remains registered as well; generated Firebase configuration is intentionally not committed.

The backend database also had unapplied Prisma migrations. Running `npx prisma migrate deploy` applied all 10 migrations before retrying registration.

## Verification

- Built a clean debug APK successfully with `flutter build apk --debug`.
- `dart analyze lib/providers/auth_provider.dart` passes with no issues.
- Tested on a physical Android device: the Google account chooser and consent flow completed successfully.
- `POST /auth/google` returned HTTP 201.
- The authenticated user was created in PostgreSQL and the app navigated to the authenticated Explore screen.
- The API migration status is up to date.

## Notes for deployment

Register every Android signing certificate used by each Firebase build variant, keep the correct web OAuth client ID in the Firebase configuration, and run `npx prisma migrate deploy` against the deployment database before enabling Google registration.

author: zhen-miao
body:
## Problem
Hyphenated words like `fifth-largest`, `35-year-old`, `city-owned` were annotated as uncommon at every level — the compound isn't in the 10k common-word list even though every part is — and the card then read *"No dictionary entry found"* because the dictionary API has no entry for them. In today's feed, 265 of 356 distinct hyphenated tokens were this kind of transparent compound.

## Changes (`index.html`)
- **Skip compositional compounds**: a hyphenated word is ignored when every part is an everyday word at the reader's level, a number word, or a known prefix (`hardParts()`); words with a genuinely uncommon part (`post-pandemic`, `singer-songwriter`) are still annotated. Strings with more than 3 parts are ignored.
- **New `COMPOUNDS` glossary**: 226 common hyphenated words with learner definitions and part of speech (`high-profile`, `trade-off`, `much-needed`, `market-rate`, `transit-oriented`, `rank-and-file`, `stop-gap`, …) plus suffix patterns (`-free`, `-friendly`, `-rich`, `-driven`, `-fold`). Optional `lv` tag: `b1` shows only at B1–B2, `b2` hides at C1+, untagged shows everywhere. Level-hidden entries never resurface through auto-detection.
- **Dictionary fallback for hyphenated words**: try the closed-up spelling (`co-worker` → `coworker`), then explain part by part — *post- (= after) + pandemic — "pandemic" means: …*. Also fixes double-click lookups on hyphenated words.
- Existing idioms gain hyphenated spellings (`ramp-up`, `wrap-up`, `kick-off`, `stand-off`, `lay-off`, `ground-breaking`); glossary matches leave at least two of the 9 slots for uncommon single words; matched variants (`crackdown`) no longer reappear as separate words; `lemmas()` maps `largest`→`large`, `fortified`→`fortify`.

## Verification
Script extracted and run headlessly in Node (`node --check` + a `vm` harness with stubbed DOM/storage/fetch): the `fifth-largest` case, level filtering, fallback formatting, and a full pass over all 80 articles in `feed.json` at each level with zero compositional compounds surviving. Not yet checked in a real browser.

author: jamesatintegratnio
body:
The two gate bugs the local proving ground surfaced. Both found on a real podinfo `6.7.0 → 6.14.1` bump, and both buried the actual change under full-set churn.

## Before

```
**Added (5)**
- `Deployment/podinfo in podinfo-tenant`
- `Pod/podinfo-grpc-test-lxlnc in podinfo-tenant`
- `Pod/podinfo-jwt-test-485zk in podinfo-tenant`
- `Pod/podinfo-service-test-cujfl in podinfo-tenant`
- `Service/podinfo in podinfo-tenant`

**Removed (5)**
- `Deployment/podinfo`
- `Pod/podinfo-grpc-test-4p5ep`
  …
```

## After

```
**Changed (2)**
- `Deployment/podinfo in podinfo-tenant`
- `Service/podinfo in podinfo-tenant`
```

## Namespace

Whether a chart stamps `metadata.namespace` **varies between versions of the same chart**. Verified directly:

```
podinfo 6.7.0    Deployment podinfo-tenant   ns=(unset)
podinfo 6.14.1   Deployment podinfo-tenant   ns=default
```

The object identity keys on namespace, so every resource read as one removal plus one addition. Passing `--namespace` doesn't help — helm can't add a field a template never declares.

A namespaced resource without the field lands in the Application's destination namespace when ArgoCD applies it, so that is now its identity and both renders agree. A render with no destination — the committed-manifests path — still invents nothing, so a `ClusterRole` doesn't acquire a namespace it never had. Both cases are tested.

## Helm test hooks

Never applied by a sync, and the one place charts routinely generate a random name, so all three of podinfo's test pods appeared as added *and* removed on every render. Only `test`, `test-success` and `test-failure` are excluded — `pre-install` and `post-upgrade` hooks **are** applied by ArgoCD and are still reported. Tested both ways.

Note the annotation is emitted quoted (`"helm.sh/hook": test-success`), which is why a first pass looking for it missed it.

## Verification

- Three new tests, each failing before the fix
- `go vet ./... && go test ./...` green
- Extraction test passes
- End-to-end against the real chart, output above

author: martinebene
body:
## Work Package

WP-013 - Finalización inconclusa, pérdida de quórum y cierre de sesión con votación pendiente

## Agente implementador

- Herramienta/agente utilizado: Codex.
- Modelo efectivo verificable de la sesión: `gpt-5.6-sol`.

## Qué cambió

- Se encapsuló la transición final e irreversible a `CERRADA + INCONCLUSA` sobre la misma instancia `Votacion`.
- Se agregó el motivo manual normalizado e inmutable, separado de las causas institucionales.
- Se implementó exclusivamente `POST /api/v1/votaciones/{id}/finalizacion`, con body estricto, respuesta 204 y protección contra comandos obsoletos por id.
- La tecla 9 evalúa pérdida de quórum antes que completitud. Si ambas condiciones aparecen con el mismo retiro, prevalece `PERDIDA_QUORUM`.
- `DELETE /api/v1/sesion` resuelve primero una votación `EN_CURSO` o `EMPATADA` como `INCONCLUSA`; el empate conserva fecha de cierre y votos.
- Los tres recorridos comparten un helper interno que no readquiere el lock y respeta `VALIDAR -> CONSTRUIR -> AUDITAR -> MUTAR -> LIBERAR`.
- Se conservaron los estados técnicos `CERRADA + resultado=None` fuera de recovery.
- Se alinearon contratos, reglas, casos de uso, modelo, auditoría y criterios de aceptación autorizados.

## Explicación para principiantes

Una votación tiene dos conceptos distintos: el estado de recepción (`EN_CURSO` o `CERRADA`) y el resultado institucional. WP-013 cubre situaciones en las que la recepción termina sin consolidar una mayoría ordinaria, por eso la entidad queda cerrada y su resultado es `INCONCLUSA`.

El flujo principal funciona así:

1. el servicio entra al único `EjecutorMutaciones`, que serializa comandos concurrentes;
2. valida el estado global, la misma referencia activa y, en el comando HTTP, el id exacto;
3. construye y persiste el evento institucional en los CSV con `flush` y `fsync`;
4. solo después modifica la misma instancia `Votacion` y libera `votacion_activa`;
5. si la auditoría falla, no se ejecutan las mutaciones posteriores y el writer queda en fallo cerrado.

En presencia hay dos hechos: primero se audita y aplica la nueva presencia; después se evalúa la votación. Esa segunda evaluación comprueba quórum antes que completitud para impedir que un retiro que deja al cuerpo sin quórum calcule por error una mayoría. Si falla el evento derivado, la presencia ya durable no se revierte.

Al cerrar sesión, la finalización de la votación y el cierre de sesión ocurren bajo una sola adquisición del lock. Si la votación estaba empatada, una primitiva de dominio específica cambia solamente `EMPATADA -> INCONCLUSA`; no existe un setter libre y la finalización manual no puede usar esa transición.

Orden sugerido de lectura:

1. `dominio/votacion.py` para las transiciones protegidas;
2. `servicios/finalizacion_votacion.py` para el orden auditoría/mutación común;
3. `servicios/votacion.py`, `servicios/entrada.py` y `servicios/sesion.py` para los tres disparadores;
4. `api/votaciones.py` y `api/errores.py` para el contrato HTTP;
5. `test_finalizacion_inconclusa.py` y `test_api_votaciones.py` para escenarios y carreras.

Para comprobarlo se pueden ejecutar los comandos globales informados en “Pruebas ejecutadas”. Las pruebas de concurrencia no dependen del orden casual de `asyncio.gather`: encolan operaciones sobre el mismo ejecutor y liberan explícitamente cada adquisición.

## Qué no cambió

- No se implementaron desempate ni voto presidencial, recovery, reapertura, edición de votos, tecla 7, frontends, SSE, bridge, persistencia ni WP-014.
- No se modificaron PLAN, WP-013 ni DEC-008/010/011.
- No se agregaron dependencias.

## Estilo y documentación del código

- [x] Los identificadores propios nuevos están escritos en español, salvo nombres impuestos por lenguaje/framework/librerías/contratos externos.
- [x] Los identificadores en español evitan tildes y `ñ` y respetan las convenciones del lenguaje.
- [x] Clases, funciones y flujos no triviales están documentados/comentados abundantemente en español con finalidad pedagógica.

- Nuxt MCP: No necesario; no hubo cambios frontend ni comportamiento específico de Nuxt.

author: brzzdev
body:
## What changed

`perch <TAB>` now offers every branch the command will actually take at that
position, including branches that exist only on the remote. The picker has
always listed those and `perch <name>` has always checked them out, but the
completions derived their list with `git branch`, which cannot see them.

The list comes from the binary, via a hidden `--complete` at each position —
`perch --complete`, `perch br --complete`, `perch wt --complete`, and after a
`--` — joining the `perch wt rm --complete` that #95 added. Each subtracts the
words its own dispatcher arm eats before it reads a branch name.

## Why

Closes #96. "Which branches complete here" had five implementations: the
`br|wt` and `ls|rm|list|remove` lists in each of the three completion files,
plus `dispatch`/`dispatch_wt` in `src/main.rs` and `go_there_argument` in
`src/app.rs` — the last of which carried a comment asking a human to keep it in
step with the first. Adding a fourth verb meant editing five files, and
forgetting one of the three shells failed silently.

The word that selects a verb is now part of declaring the verb — on `Verb` and
a new `wt::Subverb`, via a `spelled!` macro that generates the parsing from the
same list. That declaration is what the dispatcher reads and what the
completions subtract, so there is no second list for a fourth verb to be
missing from.

## Things to look out for

**A shell-injection hole closed on the way through.** Review caught that the
bash completion built candidates with `compgen -W`, which expands its word list
before matching. Git permits `$`, backticks and `${IFS}` in a ref name, so a
branch called `$(touch${IFS}/tmp/x)` executed on TAB — and, once inserted
unescaped, again on the Enter after it. Both halves are fixed and pinned by a
regression test. The sink predates this branch, but it used to see only names
you had created yourself; offering remote-only branches is what makes the name
attacker-chosen, so it belongs here. zsh and fish were never affected.

**`perch <TAB>` gets longer.** Remote-only branches are now offered, flat, in
one list. #96 left this open ("worth deciding whether remote-only branches
belong there at all"); the call was to include them, since a name the command
accepts but never completes is the gap the issue leads with. A fresh clone of a
busy repo will have a lot of them.

**`--` answers `--complete`.** The first draft had the shells ask
`perch br --complete` for their post-`--` list, reasoning that `br` eats nothing
so its list is the unfiltered one. That is a pun, not a fact: the day `br`
gained a subverb, every `--` arm in all three shells would start filtering the
escape hatch that exists to reach exactly those words — silently, and inverted
from what the user typed `--` to ask for. So `--` now answers for itself. Git
refuses a branch name beginning with `-`, so `perch -- --complete` could never
have reached a real branch.

#96 originally put all `--` handling out of scope, and review flagged this as
going past that boundary. The boundary was the thing that was wrong: the
post-`--` list is a fifth copy of the derivation the issue exists to remove, not
settled per-shell work. #96 has been amended to say so — the list is in scope,
the per-shell logic deciding *where* a `--` still leaves a branch to read stays
out.

**A second TAB kept narrowing after the injection fix.** Escaping candidates for
insertion costs the word on the command line its identity with the name, so
where several share a prefix the next TAB arrives with `$cur` already escaped —
`feat\&` for `feat&one` and `feat&two` — which no raw name starts with. Review
caught it; `$cur` is now matched against both spellings. Confirmed on a live
pty: before, the second TAB rang the bell and offered nothing.

**~17 ms slower per TAB on the most common path** (measured, release build, best
of 3 × 200: `git branch` 5.0 ms → `perch --complete` 22.7 ms). Four `git` forks
where the shell previously ran one, on a keypress that gets hit constantly. Well
under the ~100 ms perceptual threshold, but a bigger regression than #95's
+2.5 ms and on a far hotter path. A single `git for-each-ref refs/heads
refs/remotes/<remote>` carrying `%(HEAD)` and `%(upstream:remotename)` would
answer the whole thing in one fork (~8 ms) — I left it out as a `git.rs` rewrite
beyond this refactor, and can file it as a follow-up.

**A verb's word is now part of declaring the verb.** Review found that the
first draft kept a hand-maintained `Verb::ALL` beside an exhaustive `spelling`
match, and that omitting a new verb from it compiled clean, passed the suite,
and silently left its word offered as a branch — the very drift #96 exists to
kill. A small `spelled!` macro now generates `parse` from the variant
declaration, so there is no second list to be missing from.

**`app::Verb` is now `pub`.** It was `pub(crate)`; `main.rs` is a separate crate
and needs to parse through it. Nothing else about it changed.

**fish is unverified.** fish isn't installed on this machine, so
`completions/perch.fish` has had no live exercise — only a read-through against
the zsh and bash versions, which were both verified end to end.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test` — all pass, 0 fail
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo doc --no-deps` — same warning count as `main` (the intra-doc links
      to private items that the first draft added are gone)
- [x] New integration tests assert the offered set at each of the four
      positions, and that a remote-only branch is offered
- [x] Verified live in zsh and bash against a scratch repo carrying branches
      named `br`, `wt`, `ls`, `rm`, `list`, `remove`, `feat/x` and one
      remote-only — both shells agree at every position, and `wt rm` still
      offers worktree names
- [x] Injection verified end to end on a pty against bash 3.2.57 and 5.3.15:
      before the fix TAB alone created the payload file; after it, TAB inserts

author: dees-bot
body:
## What this is

The Q21 lens-hardening campaign closed on 2026-08-22 — all 40 lenses now carry hardened eval suites and `qwen3.5:4b` is floor-of-record for every one of them. That leaves **Q22 as the only item on the decisions log's "genuinely still open (undecided)" list**, so this PR takes it up.

It adds a **design-only, build-owner-gated** proposal (`docs/executing-cited-checks.md`) that works Q22 from question to a decision-ready fix. It is the shape-first artifact requested before the suite is touched — the analog of D16's design-approved / build-deferred split. **No shipped behavior changes.**

## The gap

Three measured instances (#215, #216, #253) where the atlas selected the right lens, named the exact governing rule, and cleared the change anyway — each caught by an external reviewer minutes later. Lens selection was never the failure; the *execution* of the named check was. The doc also states what the synthesizer's existing steps 6/7 already cover (uncertainty), so the fix doesn't duplicate them — Q22's failure is the *confident-and-wrong* case.

## What the doc proposes

- **Two mechanisms.** M1 — a cheap standing-dispute check (scan the PR's existing threads before affirming a claim; catches #253 alone). M2 — a falsification attempt on affirmatively-applied rules, scoped to greppable claim classes (the #216 absolutes shape).
- **A home.** `synthesizing-review-findings`, as a discipline step — one edit reaches both the standalone skill and each collapsed entrypoint's `reference/synthesis.md` via the generator. Rejects the per-entrypoint `tool-evidence.md` and new-shared-file alternatives, with reasons.
- **Dispositions** for every open sub-question: self-review specificity (M1 is worth building regardless; M2's necessity waits on a non-self-authored instance), the review-transcript eval shape (evaluated separately from the 40 lenses), and the ceremony budget.
- **A reversible, evidence-gated two-phase build** — Phase 1 (M1 + meta-review eval seed) recommended for approval first; Phase 2 (M2) deferred and gated on evidence.

Also links the proposal from the Q22 section in `open-questions.md`.

## Verification

- `python -m tooling.cli drift` → clean (docs-only change; no skills or manifest touched).
- `pytest tests/` → 403 passed.

## Asks of the reviewer

This is a decision, not a merge-and-forget: approve/amend/defer Phase 1, and weigh in on whether M2's home and scope are right before it's built.

author: vadi2
body:
#### Brief overview of PR changes/additions

- A version component too large for an `int` makes the version unreadable rather than silently becoming 0.
- The regexp anchors with `\A`/`\z` instead of `^`/`$`, which also matched around a trailing newline.
- Build metadata has to carry at least one identifier, so `1.2.3+` is a typo rather than a version.

#### Motivation for adding to Mudlet

`toInt()` reads an out-of-range component back as 0, which sorted the highest version there is *below* every other one - and whichever side of the comparison it landed on got the update decision backwards. An unreadable version is honest: `Release::operator<` already falls back to comparing dates, which is what PTB builds rely on.

#### Other info (issues closed, discussion etc)

Closes #10066.

Release versions come from GitHub's `tag_name`, so no shipped version string is affected by the tighter anchors - `4.22.0` and `4.22.0-ptb-2026-08-08-7c6b5a49` both still parse.

**Test case:** covered by three new `SemVerTest` cases; all three fail if `SemVer.cpp` is reverted.

body:
### Security Enhancement: Security Headers Middleware & Information Disclosure Protection

- **Severity:** ENHANCEMENT
- **Vulnerability:** Unset security HTTP headers and Express framework banner (`X-Powered-By`) disclosure.
- **Impact:** Attackers could identify technology stack details (`Express`) and exploit missing browser defense-in-depth headers (MIME sniffing, clickjacking, XSS reflection in legacy browsers).
- **Fix:** 
  1. Disabled `X-Powered-By` header using `app.disable('x-powered-by')`.
  2. Created custom security middleware `server/middleware/security.js` setting `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, `X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block`, and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.
- **Verification:** Verified via test request that `X-Powered-By` header is omitted and all specified security response headers are returned correctly.

author: arshbibhaw
body:
## Description:
**Summary**
This PR prepares the backend for live production deployment on Render and Supabase. It resolves several hardcoded configuration issues that were preventing the app from booting in a non-local environment, causing database connection failures, and blocking frontend communication.

**Key Changes:**
- **Added Production Server:** Added `gunicorn` to `requirements.txt` to support the required Render build and start commands.
- **Dynamic CORS Implementation:** Removed the hardcoded `localhost:3000` from `main.py`. The `CORSMiddleware` now dynamically parses the `CORS_ORIGINS` environment variable to support Vercel preview and production domains.
- **Database URL Fallback:** Removed the hardcoded `sqlite:///` string in `config.py` that was overriding environment variables. It now correctly falls back to `os.getenv("DATABASE_URL")` to allow Render to inject the Supabase Postgres string.
- **Alembic Password Parsing Fix:** Updated `alembic/env.py` to properly escape `%` characters. This prevents Python's `configparser` from crashing with an interpolation error when parsing URL-encoded database passwords (e.g., `%40` instead of `@`).
- **Configuration Cleanup:** Removed an accidental shadow config file (`app/core/__init__.py`) that contained a UTF-16 BOM, which was causing `alembic upgrade head` to crash with a unicode decode error.

**Impact:**
Once this is merged into `main`, Render will automatically trigger a new deployment, successfully install `gunicorn`, connect to the Supabase Transaction Pooler, and expose the API securely to the Next.js Vercel frontend.

author: francescoa27122
body:
**Apple only, decided today. Windows deferred.**

The macOS failure is the worse one: *"Nox is damaged and can't be opened"* reads as a broken download rather than an unsigned app, and the fix is a terminal command most people will not run. Windows at least offers a click-through — and an *OV* certificate would not remove even that immediately, since SmartScreen reputation accrues with downloads. Recorded in the 1.0 bar row so it is not re-litigated.

**Nothing changes until the secrets exist.** An absent certificate builds ad-hoc exactly as today, and an unset GitHub secret arrives as an empty string, which counts as absent.

## What's wired

Six secrets beside the updater's two. The bundler imports the certificate itself from `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` — read out of `tauri-bundler`'s `macos/sign.rs`, whose `keychain()` delegates to `tauri_macos_sign::Keychain::with_certificate` — so there is **no `security create-keychain` step here**, unlike the manual example in Tauri's own CI docs, and `KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD` is unused. Two Tauri doc pages disagree on this; the source settled it.

`tauri.conf.json` is untouched on purpose: `bundle.macOS.hardenedRuntime` already defaults to `true` and notarization requires it, while an unknown key there would fail at tag time with nothing local to catch it. The default is the safer place to stand.

## The guard, and the trap it exists for

Mirrors the updater's *"half a keypair signs updates that nothing can verify"*.

**Signing without notarizing is the trap.** Gatekeeper still stops the app — a milder dialog than *"damaged"*, but still a click-through — so the release notes would promise a clean first launch that does not happen, and nothing would say so. Apple requires notarization for a Developer ID Application certificate, so a certificate without the notarization secrets **fails the build** rather than shipping the half that does not work.

## Verification

Nothing here can be tested by a normal CI run — the release workflow fires only on a tag, and no build has a certificate. So:

- **The YAML was parsed** and the step order and `if: runner.os == 'macOS'` condition confirmed programmatically.
- **The guard was extracted from the workflow and run**, rather than read. Four states, all four as intended:
  - nothing set → passes, prints the ad-hoc path
  - certificate only → fails, names all five missing secrets
  - certificate + password + identity, no notarization → fails, names the three
  - all six → passes
  - plus empty-string secrets, which is what an unset GitHub secret actually becomes → treated as absent
- `npm test` 1885 passed, `npm run check` 964 files 0 errors, `npm run build` green.

**The first tagged release with real secrets is still the first real test**, exactly as it was for the updater. The runbook makes that a `-rc` prerelease on purpose — the gate already accepts `v0.9.0-rc1` against version `0.9.0` — so a dry run costs a draft rather than a bad release.

## Install docs deliberately unchanged

`README.md:38-53`, the workflow's `releaseBody`, and the roadmap row all still promise the `xattr` command, because that is still true. The spec lists all three as the thing to change once a signed release exists — the same call 0.5.1 made when it softened the macOS paragraph only after signing worked.

## The human half

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-apple-signing-design.md` — enrolment, CSR, certificate, export, the six secrets, the dry run, and what to verify with `codesign`, `spctl` and `stapler` rather than trusting the absence of a dialog. It also flags, once, that an **individual** Developer ID puts your legal name in every binary you ship, readable with `codesign -dv` — a decision made at enrolment and awkward to undo.

author: kriskit
body:
Closes #27.

Upstream was already HTTP/1.1, entirely by accident: Go's transport only negotiates h2 when `DialContext` is nil and `ForceAttemptHTTP2` is unset, and we set `DialContext` for corporate-proxy CONNECT tunnels. The comment above that line says nothing about protocol negotiation, so anyone tidying the transport could switch every upstream request onto one multiplexed connection.

That matters here specifically: the traffic is long-lived SSE completions, many at once when subagents fan out. Multiplexed onto one h2 connection, a few live streams exhaust the stream budget and a trivial request waits behind them.

Now explicit, with a test.

## The test needed two assertions, and the reason is the interesting part

The obvious live-protocol check turns out not to cover the second regression. Go disables auto-h2 whenever **any** of `TLSClientConfig`, `Dial` or `DialContext` is non-nil — and the test has to pin `RootCAs` to trust its self-signed upstream, which is itself enough to force h1. So nil'ing `DialContext` left the round-trip assertion green.

There is therefore a construction-level assertion alongside it. Plants, run independently:

| Plant | Result |
|---|---|
| `ForceAttemptHTTP2: true` | `upstream saw protocol "HTTP/2.0", want HTTP/1.1` |
| `DialContext` removed | `Transport.DialContext is nil, want egress.DialContext` |

The live assertion alone provably cannot catch the second — which is worth knowing, because it is the one a refactor is more likely to cause.

The upstream reports the protocol *it* observed via a response header: the httptest server the client talks to is a separate plaintext connection and says nothing about the proxy→upstream leg.

No README change — internal transport behaviour, no user-visible surface (noted per CONTRIBUTING.md rather than skipped silently).

author: francoisldaigneault
body:
Fleet parity: the same two Speed indicators land in `pi-config`, `governance`
and `.github` today. This is the `governance` half; no code is touched.

## Why the wall-clock target had to go

A duration target in seconds goes red whenever tests are added, which directly
contradicts the `Green tests` indicator of this same file - one line rewards
what the other punishes. `pi-config` hit it first: 42 tests added to close
three silent data losses took its suite from 72 to 114 while the cost per test
moved from 53 ms to 55 ms, and the axis turned red for a job well done.

`Test suite duration` becomes two indicators:

| Indicator | Current | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Median cost per test | 7 ms (2.05 s / 287 cases) | < 60 ms |
| Test suite duration (feedback-loop ceiling) | 2.05 s (262 tests) | < 10 s |

Cost per test catches a real slowdown - a sleep, a fixture that grew, a timeout
actually waited on - and stays green when the suite legitimately grows. The
ceiling protects the edit-run loop, which is what the old target was really
defending.

## Measured here, not copied

11 warm runs: median **2.05 s**, range 2.03 to 2.42 s. The old row carried
`2.41 s`, a single reading that sat near the top of that range - which is the
point of the second measurement note below.

Three notes now travel with the rows, and they are the substance of the change:

- `uv run pytest -q` carries `--cov` through `addopts`. Measured here:
  **2.05 s with, 1.30 s without**, so about **37%** of this speed reading pays
  for the coverage gate. Without that, the figure is not reproducible by anyone
  else. The share differs per repository - `pi-config` measures about 21% - so
  each file states its own.
- The figure is a **median over warm runs**, never a single reading.
- The dating convention merged today is respected: the readings are read by
  hand, so they carry their date.

## On the headroom

7 ms against a 60 ms ceiling is a lot of room, and that is deliberate: the
targets are the same across the fleet so a suite is compared with its siblings
rather than with its own past size. It is a guardrail holding, not a target set
too low. If it never moves it can be tightened later - this file says so itself.

## Note

Merging this puts the release PR #53 `BEHIND` (it is `CLEAN` while this one is
merely open). #53 has not been touched, and unblocking it is a
`gh pr update-branch`, never a local rebase.

author: marco308
body:
## What and why

Refs [#99](https://github.com/marco308/meals/issues/99) — **deliberately not `Closes`**, see the blocker below.

A household already said which tier it was on. It now says **until when**, **where that came from**, and **what was agreed**, and `limits.effective_tier` is the only thing that reads any of it.

**Lapsing is derived, never written back**, and that is the load-bearing choice. Past its expiry plus `ENTITLEMENT_GRACE_DAYS` (14) a household reads as `free`; nothing rewrites `tier`, so §5's promise holds by construction rather than by a job remembering to keep it — nothing deleted, everything readable, plan usable, shopping list working, export free. It also makes renewing one column rather than a reconstruction, and keeps the record of what somebody was on through the weeks they lapsed. **A null `paid_until` never expires**, which is every self-hosted household, so a server that sells nothing sees none of this.

**Comp tooling comes first**, because you comp people in week one and a spreadsheet is not a source of truth. `python -m app.entitlements` comps, extends, revokes and lists, most urgent at the top — a command on the box like `app/provision.py`, not an endpoint. Extending an active year adds to its end so renewing early costs nothing; extending a lapsed one starts from today so nobody pays for the weeks they could not grow.

**The founding price is defended, not just stored.** `grant` refuses to overwrite an existing price and says why; `revoke` keeps it, so coming back costs what it always did.

**Dunning** is `python -m app.dunning` from cron: one before expiry, one after (at expiry, where the news is still actionable, not at the end of grace where it is only a complaint). Each marked once, both marks cleared when the expiry moves, and a relay failure marks nothing so the next run retries. No SMTP is not an error.

## The blocker: no merchant of record has been chosen

The issue says **"Decide which before writing the webhook"**, and nothing in the repo names one — `08-freemium.md` §7 says only "a merchant of record rather than raw Stripe", and PR #114 just shipped a privacy section stating no processor exists. Paddle and Lemon Squeezy differ in their signature header, their event names and their payload shape, so writing it now would be guessing at all three.

So **the webhook and its failure alert are not here.** Everything above is processor-independent and is exactly what that webhook will call: `entitlements.grant` / `extend` / `revoke`, with `entitlement_source` taking the processor's name where `comp` goes today. Tell me which one and it is a focused follow-up.

Also not here, and also from the issue's own text: **email verification and reaping abandoned free households**, which the issue itself calls prerequisites for opening `REGISTRATION_ENABLED` rather than parts of this. And **StoreKit**, explicitly out of scope.

## One thing I chose not to do

`GET /limits` could report `paid_until` and the entitlement state, and it would be additive. I left it out because [#100](https://github.com/marco308/meals/issues/100) is specifically about keeping commerce out of the iOS app, and where a renewal date is allowed to surface feels like that issue's call rather than this one's.

## Checklist

- [x] **API contract stayed additive** — no endpoint or response field changed at all.
- [x] **Model change has a migration** — `74e2494dfabf`, five nullable columns, chained onto the single head, up/down/up verified. Autogenerate also proposed re-creating `ck_meal_recipe_scale`; that already exists in `c4f2a8b19d63` and is a SQLite-reflection false positive, so it is excluded with a comment saying so.
- [x] **Shopping-list quantities still derive from `ListItemSource`** — n/a, untouched.
- [x] **Every new query filters on `household_id`** — n/a: the operator commands are whole-server by design, like the usage gauges, and read no household content.
- [x] **Skill/prompt pack updated** — n/a, nothing an assistant drives changed.
- [x] **New 4xx strings say what to do instead** — no new 4xx. `EntitlementError` carries the same shape of sentence for the operator, e.g. refusing a reprice names the stored price and points at §6.

The export's column guard from #97 caught the five new columns immediately and they are now recorded as excluded with the reason: this deployment's bookkeeping about a household means nothing on the box it is moving to.

author: gumptionthomas
body:
CLAUDE.md asserted that per-key VALUE is discarded. That rested on two things, and neither was a test:

- Keychron's `per_key_rgb.c`, which is the **shared** tree rather than this pad's build.
- One accident: an early Lights Out used `DARK = (0, 0, 0)` and the board came up white.

The accident is weaker than it reads. `(0, 0, 0)` is also `s=0`, so white is what you get whether v is **replaced** or merely **clamped to a floor** — and a floor would mean `v=128` is genuinely dimmer than `v=255`, which nobody would have spotted.

## Measured

Three frames on the pad, hue and saturation constant within each so the only variable is `v`:

| frame | result |
|---|---|
| blue ladder, `v` 0→255 down the rows, `s=255` | flat |
| the same ladder at `s=0`, where brightness shows most | flat |
| alternating rows of `v=255` and `v=0` | indistinguishable |

Flat everywhere excludes the clamp — a floor would have left the top of the ladder graded.

## And one new fact

**The array stores `v` faithfully.** The ladder reads back exactly as written, so the discard happens at render, not at write. That is why this was never noticed: every write this codebase makes uses `v=255`, so there was nothing to see.

Documentation only — no code change, 99 tests unaffected.

author: kunwar-axilio
body:
## Context for a reviewer with zero context

The DCP reconnect + cursor-resume work (axilio PRs #1935–#1938; platform-go #17; platform-python #41) gives every socket a survivable-drop contract: meaningful close codes, an opt-in cursor so a reconnect resumes where the client left off, an in-band resync signal for the expired-window case, and idempotency keys so re-sending the one in-flight command is safe. The product bar set in that design: a customer on our SDKs never writes reconnect logic, and a customer on a raw WebSocket gets a contract "small enough to wrap in an afternoon" — which requires the contract to actually be documented. This page is that document (the design doc's Contract section, public-safe).

## What changed

- New `api-reference/dcp/reconnect.mdx`: close-code table (retry vs stop, including `4409` control-held), reconnect HTTP-status semantics (`403` = session over, terminal), opt-in cursor checkpoints (`resume=1`, the `Axilio.cursor` / `CURSOR` frames on the two sockets), reattach parameters, at-least-once semantics, retention-window behavior and the resync signal, `idempotencyKey` usage for mutating input, and the five-point client checklist (duplicate tolerance, monotonic request ids, close classification, handshake replay, no client pings).
- Added to the DCP nav group (between raw-usage and reference) and cross-linked from raw-usage's next-step cards.
- Written per WRITING_GUIDE (payoff-first, second person, bold-led bullets, next-step cards) and public-safe: behaviorally accurate retention windows ("roughly two minutes / ~100 frames") without internal storage or stream-key detail, no ticket references.

## Notes

- Publish after the server contract deploys to production (axilio #1935/#1936) so the page never describes behavior a customer can't reach; the SDK PRs' "built in" claim also lands with their releases.
- The untracked local analysis files in this repo's working tree are deliberately not part of this PR.

| `mostrador.html` | la cooperativa, en una tablet | clara, alto contraste, botones de 56px |
| `pantalla.html` | colgada junto a la cooperativa | números gigantes, nada más |
| `medidor.html` | Carlos, para el reporte STEAM | cifras, gráfica y CSV |

Son opuestas **a propósito**: el alumno la ve en un pasillo con el teléfono en la mano; la cooperativa la usa con las manos ocupadas y con sol pegando. Ninguna toca los datos directamente — todas hablan con `nucleo.js`.

## Las tres decisiones que sostienen todo

**1 · El motor de datos es un adaptador nuestro** (regla §2 de la casa). Hoy corre el local: `localStorage` + `BroadcastChannel`, sin cuenta de nadie, sin internet, sin costo. El hueco del servidor ya está escrito para que el día que la escuela lo autorice sea conectar y no rehacer. El límite queda dicho con todas sus letras en el LEEME: sirve para la demostración y para operar desde una tablet, no para doscientos teléfonos hablando entre sí.

**2 · La fila se ordena en un solo lugar** — `colaOrdenada()`, regla 4 del catálogo. No es "primero en llegar": lo que ya está en la plancha no se reordena, los anticipados entran primero, **quien lleve esperando más de N turnos se vuelve intocable**, y sólo entonces lo rápido primero. Sin ese tope, atender primero lo rápido deja sin comer al que pidió el plato fuerte.

**3 · Cero datos de más.** Nombre de pila y grupo. Sin apellidos, sin correo, sin contraseña, sin fotos de alumnos. Cientos de menores sin una base de datos de menores. Dos reglas están en el código, no en un documento: la pantalla pública muestra números y nunca nombres, y la deuda de un alumno no aparece en ninguna pantalla que vea otro alumno.

## Nada se detiene si algo falla

| Si se cae… | Qué pasa |
|---|---|
| el internet | el motor local no lo usa. Se pide igual |
| la notificación | el turno se ve en pantalla, y la señora sigue gritando números |
| la app entera | el mostrador congela la lista y la imprime. Se despacha en papel |

## Verificado

**42 pruebas propias** que corren solas al cargar cada pantalla, y una corrida de punta a punta con tres pestañas abiertas al mismo tiempo:

```
✓ el alumno recibe turno
✓ el pedido llega al mostrador sin recargar nada
✓ la pantalla pública muestra el turno 1
✓ la pantalla pública NO muestra el nombre
✓ al alumno le llega "ya está" solo
✓ el alumno ve que quedó entregado
✓ el medidor registró que alguien alcanzó
De punta a punta: 7/7 · sin errores en ninguna pantalla
```

Más: ningún objetivo táctil por debajo de 44px en las cuatro, sin desborde horizontal en teléfono de 390px ni en tablet de 834px.

## Lo que falta, y por qué

| Qué | Por qué no está |
|---|---|
| El motor de servidor | necesita permiso de la escuela. El hueco ya está escrito |
| Pago desde la app | marcado por Carlos como "más adelante"; el ticket ya contempla "pagado en línea" |
| La notificación en iPhone | sólo llega con la app instalada en la pantalla de inicio. **Falta probarlo en un iPhone real antes de prometerlo** |
| Fotos del menú | las sube la cooperativa desde su pantalla; mientras, cada categoría tiene color e ícono |

body:
## 概要

Issue #65「電子帳簿保存法対応確認」のチェックを実施し、結果と決定を ADR 0002 として記録しました。

**結論: カシャケイボは電子帳簿保存法の適用対象外であり、対応は行わない (「電帳法対応」を謳わない)。**

Closes #65

## 変更点

- `documents/adr/0002-denshi-choubo-hozon-hou-out-of-scope.md` を新規作成

チェックの内容 (詳細は ADR 本文):

1. **適用対象外の根拠**: 電子帳簿保存法の保存義務者は事業者 (納税者) 側であり、個人の家計の記録を目的とする本アプリには保存義務自体が生じない。ストアメタデータ (fastlane/metadata)・利用規約 (docs/Terms.md)・アプリ内文言 (lib/ 全体) を grep で実測し、電帳法対応・経費精算・確定申告を訴求する記載が無いことを確認。利用規約は前文・第14条4項で税務・会計助言を目的としないことを明示済み
2. **仮に対応を謳う場合の未充足点の記録**: 訂正削除履歴なし (R2 画像はユーザーが自由に削除・上書き可能)、タイムスタンプなし、画質要件 (200dpi 相当以上・RGB 256階調以上) の担保なし、検索要件 (取引年月日・金額・取引先) の保証なし。要件の出典は国税庁の電子帳簿等保存制度特設サイト ( https://www.nta.go.jp/law/joho-zeikaishaku/sonota/jirei/tokusetsu/index.htm )
3. **将来への制約**: design_handoff_kashakeibo/README.md にある CSV エクスポート文言案「確定申告・経費精算に」は、実装時に集計データの書き出しの範囲の表現に留める (原本保存の代替と誤認させない)。事業者向け機能を出す場合は本 ADR を Supersede して再評価する

## 動作確認

ドキュメント (ADR) のみの追加で、コード・設定の変更はありません。build_runner / analyze / test / ビルドは対象外のため実行していません。電話番号の差分点検 (`--staged` / `--unpushed`) は検出 0 件・exit 0 を確認済みです。

補足 (任意のフォローアップ情報): 利用規約に「電子帳簿保存法の要件を満たす保存を提供しない」旨の明示文を追加するかは依頼範囲外のため本 PR には含めていません。必要なら別途対応します。

## 人間が確認

なし

author: jfogelman
body:
The points ending sorted survivors by score and took the first. **`Array.sort` is stable**, so an exact tie handed the game to whoever came first in player order -- the Horde, every time -- and then logged that they were *"declared ahead on points"*. The one line in the game capable of stating something false.

Measured over 36 games it never fired (closest: 4 points apart), so this is about **being correct, not common**. A human playing deliberately to the limit will reach it long before two AIs do.

## Where a draw lives

`winner` is `number | null` and **null already meant "still playing"**, read that way in a dozen places -- so widening `winner` would have touched every read. Instead `isOver(state)` answers the question those places were actually asking, and a drawn game keeps `winner` null while recording `victory: draw`. The `winner` clause inside `isOver` carries saves from before endings were recorded at all.

## The screen

Copes with having nobody to name: **"Nobody has won"**, both sides exactly level, and a line about the result being declared a technicality and everyone going home. It reaches for **one picture rather than one per faction** -- a draw is the only ending where both sides belong in the frame.

That picture is prompted in ART_PROMPTS but not yet drawn, so **missing art now removes itself** rather than leaving a broken-image icon in the middle of the ending. Verified both ways: the draw drops its image cleanly, the points ending keeps its own.

Also fixes "after 1 turns".

276 tests pass (3 new).

## What

`dhs_mdns` now installs Apple Bonjour on win11 **unattended**: stage
`BonjourPSSetup.exe` (LFS guard), carve the embedded CAB at the `MSCF`
header whose `cbCabinet` fits the file, `expand -F:*`, install the core
`Bonjour64.msi` with `msiexec /qn /norestart` (win_package, idempotent by
product code), keep "Bonjour Service" running/automatic. The opt-in
silent flag and the "operator installs at the console" notice are gone.
testbed.md mDNS section updated.

Closes #797 (completes #784, epic #780).

## Why

Owner: Ansible must install Bonjour, not the operator. Root cause from
the MSI log of the earlier failures: Apple's bootstrapper bundles six
MSIs and in silent mode installs only `BonjourPS64.msi` (Print Services),
which fails 1603 / hangs with *"Bonjour Print Services requires Bonjour
2.0 or newer ... install the Bonjour core package first"*. dhs needs only
the core.

## How

- `tasks/windows.yml`: `win_shell` carve+expand (`creates:
  <extract_dir>\Bonjour64.msi`), `win_package` MSI `/qn /norestart`,
  `win_service`.
- `defaults/main.yml`: `dhs_mdns_bonjour_extract_dir`, flag removed.
- Verified by hand first on win11: cabinet @ offset 90848, cbCabinet
  5228595 (= the bootstrapper log's "Total length of cabinet file"),
  msiexec exit 0 in ~10 s, dnssd.dll present, service Running/Auto.

`fleet-converge.yml -l win11` twice — posted as a comment below when the
